artists.b: Kunstniku perekond opteerus 1920 Eestisse. A. Hoidre õppis 1933-1937 Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis graafikat, lõpetas Riigi kõrgema kunstikooli 1941. Samal aastal mobiliseeriti Punaarmesse, võttis osa lahingutest ja oli kunstnike rindebrigaadis. 1944-1982 oli ERKI (EKA) õppejõud.
artists.ben: The artist's family opted for Estonia in 1920. A. Hoidre studied graphic art at the State School of Applied Arts in 1933-1937, graduated from the State Higher Art School in 1941. In the same year he was mobilised into the Red Army, took part in battles and was in the artists' front brigade. From 1944-1982 he was a lecturer at ERKI (EKA).

artists.b: Õppis 1913-1917 Ants Laikmaa ateljeekoolis Tallinnas, 1917-1918 kuulus Noorte Kunstnikkude Ühingusse "Vikerla". Kuulus Eesti Kunstnikkude Rühma 1920.aastate lõpul. 1928 oli Pariisis, 1931 esines Helsingis, Soome Kunstnike Ühingu aastanäitusel.
artists.ben: Studied 1913-1917 at Ants Laikmaa's studio school in Tallinn, 1917-1918 belonged to the Young Artists' Union "Vikerla". Belonged to the Estonian Artists' Group in the late 1920s. In 1928 was in Paris, in 1931 exhibited in Helsinki, at the annual exhibition of the Finnish Artists' Union.

artists.b:
Priidu Aavik sündis kooliõpetaja Eduard Aaviku üheksalapselise pere viienda lapsena.1914 asus perekond Tallinna, 1917 koliti Hagerisse Maidla mõisa. Priidu Aavik õppis Hageri kihelkonnakoolis. 1918. aastal ema suri ja P. Aavik asus elama Kernu valda Haiba külla perekond Kruuside juurde, 17-aastaselt kolis Tallinna.

P. Aavik õppis kunsti Ants Laikmaa ateljeekoolis, 1934 astus Kõrgemasse Kunstikooli Pallas, kus õppis Nikolai Triigi ja Ado Vabbe käe all kuni 1938. Seejärel asutas oma stuudio, 1939 tegi reisi Pariisi, kuid oli sõja puhkemisel sunnitud tagasi pöörduma. 1941. aasta suvel mobiliseeriti Aavik Punaarmeesse. Ta võttis osa lahingutest Tallinna ja Leningradi lähistel, hiljem siirdus Jaroslavli, kus oli üks Jaroslavli eesti kunstnike kollektiivi ja Eesti Nõukogude Kunstnike Liidu asutajaid.

Eestisse naasnult töötas ta aastatel 1944–1946 Tartu Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi direktori kohusetäitjana, 1945–1947 oli Eesti Nõukogude Kunstnike Liidu juhatuse esimehees ja 1947–1948 Tallinna Kunstifondi esimehees. 1951–1953 oli ta Üleliidulise Põllumajandusnäituse Eesti paviljoni peakunstnik ja 1954–1962 Eesti NSV Rahvamajandusnäituse peakunstnik. 1962-1965 viibis kahel pikemal Atlandi ookeani retkel, kuuludes Tallinna kalalaevastiku baasi (esimene Põhja-Atlandil, teine lõunas, käidi ka Lääne-Aafrikas)
artists.ben:
Priidu Aavik was born as the fifth child in the nine-child family of the schoolteacher Eduard Aavik. In 1914 the family moved to Tallinn, and in 1917 relocated to Maidla Manor in Hageri. Priidu Aavik studied at the Hageri parish school. In 1918 his mother died, and P. Aavik went to live with the Kruus family in Haiba village, Kernu Parish; at the age of 17 he moved to Tallinn.

P. Aavik studied art at Ants Laikmaa's studio school; in 1934 he entered the Pallas Higher Art School, where he studied under Nikolai Triik and Ado Vabbe until 1938. He then founded his own studio; in 1939 he made a trip to Paris but was forced to return upon the outbreak of war. In the summer of 1941 Aavik was mobilised into the Red Army. He took part in battles near Tallinn and Leningrad, later moving to Yaroslavl, where he was one of the founders of the collective of Estonian artists in Yaroslavl and of the Estonian Soviet Artists' Union.

After returning to Estonia, he worked from 1944 to 1946 as acting director of the Tartu State Art Institute, from 1945 to 1947 as chairman of the board of the Estonian Soviet Artists' Union, and from 1947 to 1948 as chairman of the Tallinn Art Fund. From 1951 to 1953 he was chief artist of the Estonian pavilion at the All-Union Agricultural Exhibition, and from 1954 to 1962 chief artist of the Estonian SSR National Economy Exhibition. From 1962 to 1965 he took part in two longer Atlantic Ocean voyages, belonging to the base of the Tallinn fishing fleet (the first in the North Atlantic, the second in the south, also visiting West Africa).

artists.b: Sündinud 12.11.1855, Paldiski lähistel, Uuga-Rätsepal; surnud 26.06.1929. Haridus: 1876–1879 vabakuulaja Peterburi Kunstide Akadeemias; 1873 Peterburis Bollhageni ja Šutovi töökojas; 1870–1873 Tallinnas tisler Bergi juures.

Andres Adamsoni vastus:"Sirje on minu ema, kes täna (28.09.2021) saab juhtumisi 81, ja Võidu 18-8 oli meie aadress Kärdlas, 1963?-1972. Ema on ka praegu Kassaris, ma lähen sünnipäevale alles tagantjärele, pühapäeval, näitan talle seda pilti ja küsin, kumma oma see on. Taseme (puudumise) tõttu eeldan, et tema oma. Ka emal oli nimelt korralik kunstianne, ka tema pidi minema ERKIsse, kuid nende abielludes isa juba oli seal ja elati nii kitsastes oludes, et kahe pereliikme üheaegne õppimine oli raskendatud. Lükkus ja lõpuks jäigi. Isa autorluses kahtlen seepärast, et Rannapaargu sai valmis millal?, vist 1966, ta oli siis juba 28, koolid selja taga, ma ei tahaks uskuda nii kehva tehnilist taset, ta sai hiljem ju Balti akvarellibiennaalidelt medaleid jne. Ka allkiri pole tema käega kirjutet (ei sarnane küll ka ema omale) ja oma aadressi ei kirjutanuks ta mitte mingil juhul pildi juurde. Isa käest kahjuks üle küsida ei saa."
artists.ben: Andres Adamson's reply: "Sirje is my mother, who today (28.09.2021) happens to turn 81, and Võidu 18-8 was our address in Kärdla, 1963?-1972. My mother is also currently in Kassari, I'm only going to the birthday afterwards, on Sunday, I'll show her this picture and ask whose it is. Because of the (lack of) level, I assume it's hers. My mother indeed had a proper artistic talent too, she was also supposed to go to ERKI, but by the time they married my father was already there, and they lived in such cramped conditions that two family members studying at the same time was difficult. It was postponed and in the end never happened. I doubt my father's authorship because when was Rannapaargu finished?, probably 1966, he was already 28 then, schools behind him, I wouldn't want to believe such a poor technical level, he later won medals at the Baltic Watercolour Biennials etc. Also the signature is not written in his hand (though it doesn't resemble my mother's either), and he would never under any circumstances have written his own address next to a picture. Unfortunately I can no longer ask my father."

artists.b: Õppis kunsti 1923-1924 Charlottenburgi kunsttööstuskoolis Berliinis ja F. Colarossi, P. Ransoni ning Montparnasse'i vabaakadeemiates Pariisis. Ta õpetajad olid Charles Guerin, Roger Bissiere, Moise Kisling, Andre Lhote, Vassili Šuhhajev. Elas kuni 1932 Prantsusmaal, Hispaanias jm, 1933-1934 Kreekas. II ms ajal, 1941, evakueeriti NSVL tagalasse, kus oli Jaroslavlis asutatud eesti kunstnike liidu juht. 1945-1949 oli Tallinna Riikliku Tarbekunsti Instituudi direktor. 1951 langes nõukogude repressioonide alla. 1983 asutati Adamson-Ericu Muuseum Tallinnas.

Grigori (Georg) Tõnisson sündis Pärnus gümnaasiumi kojamehe pojana. 1911 trükiti tema maastikuvinjetid ning vested Postimehe lisas Sädemed, peagi ilmusid ta karikatuurid ajalehtedes Kilk ja Meie Tallinna Ajaleht. 1913 asus elama Tallinna ja tööle ajakirja Leek. 1915 mobiliseeriti tsaariarmeesse, langes 1915 Saksa sõjavangi. 1918 tuli tagasi Tallinna ja asutas koos Hendrik Saarega (Kivilombi Ints) pilkekunsti ajakirja "Sipelgas" (ilmus 15 nr), mille juures Gori oli nii proosa- kui pildiautor (puulõikes). Alates 1920 oli ajalehe Vaba Maa toimetuse liige, 1938 Rahvalehe toimetuse liige. 1941 Gori arreteeriti, pärast vabanemist töötas ta ajalehtede Rahva Hääl ning Sirp ja Vasar juures. Saksa okupatsiooni ajal oli kaks korda vangis, kunstniku surmaaeg on 7.10.1944, selle põhjus (enesetapp?) on jäänud lahendamata. Maetud Tallinna Siselinna kalmistule.
artists.ben: Grigori (Georg) Tõnisson was born in Pärnu as the son of a grammar school caretaker. In 1911 his landscape vignettes and stories were printed in the Postimees supplement Sädemed, and soon his caricatures appeared in the newspapers Kilk and Meie Tallinna Ajaleht. In 1913 he moved to Tallinn and began working for the magazine Leek. In 1915 he was mobilised into the Tsarist army, and in 1915 he was taken prisoner of war by the Germans. In 1918 he returned to Tallinn and, together with Hendrik Saar (Kivilombi Ints), founded the satirical art magazine "Sipelgas" (15 issues were published), for which Gori was both a prose and picture author (in woodcut). From 1920 he was a member of the editorial board of the newspaper Vaba Maa, and in 1938 a member of the editorial board of Rahvaleht. In 1941 Gori was arrested; after his release he worked at the newspapers Rahva Hääl and Sirp ja Vasar. During the German occupation he was imprisoned twice; the artist's date of death is 7.10.1944, the cause of which (suicide?) remains unresolved. He is buried at the Tallinn Siselinna cemetery.

artists.b: Kunstiharidus - 1918.a. R. Lepiku eraateljee. 1919.a. astus kunstikooli "Pallas". 1926.a. omandas joonistusõpetaja kutse. 1931.a. astus uuesti kunstikooli "Pallas". 1931/1932.a. N. Triigi ateljees, lõpetas maali erialal 1932.a.
artists.ben: Art education - 1918 R. Lepik's private studio. In 1919 entered the art school "Pallas". In 1926 obtained the qualification of drawing teacher. In 1931 entered the art school "Pallas" again. In 1931/1932 in N. Triik's studio, graduated in painting in 1932.

artists.b: Alates 1920.aastast töötas joonistusõpetajana Tallinnas. Liitus Eesti Kunstnikkude Rühmaga 1925, 1927 reis Berliini ja Pariisi. 1928 esines "Suur-Berliini kunstinäitusel" koos Blumenfeldti, Histi, Laarmani ja Olviga.
artists.ben: From 1920 worked as a drawing teacher in Tallinn. Joined the Estonian Artists' Group in 1925, in 1927 travelled to Berlin and Paris. In 1928 exhibited at the "Great Berlin Art Exhibition" together with Blumenfeldt, Hiist, Laarman and Olvi.

artists.b: Oli 1932-44 Tallinna Töölisteatri kostüümikunstnik ja näitleja, 1944-46 Noorsooteatri kostüümialajuhataja, 1940-50 ühtlasi Tallinna Rkl. Tarbekunsti Inst-i õppejõud, 1950. aastail töötas portselanimaalijana, hiljem olnud vabakunstnik. ENSV tnl. kunstnik (1969).
artists.ben: He was costume designer and actor at the Tallinn Workers' Theatre in 1932-44, head of the costume department at the Youth Theatre in 1944-46, and at the same time a teacher at the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art in 1940-50; in the 1950s he worked as a porcelain painter, later became a freelance artist. Merited Artist of the ESSR (1969).

artists.b: 1938. - 1941.a. Riigi Kõrgema Kunstikooli aiakujunduskursuste õppejõud. 1943.aastast kuulus Jaroslavli eesti kunstnike kollektiivi NSVL-i tagalas. 1944.aaastast ERKI õppejõud. 1957. - 1962.a. ENSV Kunstnike Liidu esimees.
artists.ben: 1938-1941 lecturer at the garden design courses of the State Higher Art School. From 1943 belonged to the collective of Estonian artists in Yaroslavl in the rear of the USSR. From 1944 lecturer at ERKI. 1957-1962 chairman of the ESSR Artists' Union.

artists.b: Marina Aleksejeva (sündinud 18. mail 1971) on eesti kunstnik, kes on tuntud oma joonistuste ja kollaažide poolest. Ta lõpetas Tartu Ülikooli maaliosakonna 1995. aastal ning kaitses magistritöö samas ülikoolis 2016. aastal. Alates 1992. aastast on ta osalenud mitmetel näitustel nii Eestis kui ka rahvusvaheliselt. Lisaks kunstiloomingule töötab Aleksejeva õpetajana Tartu Kunstikoolis ja Tartu Lastekunstikoolis.
artists.ben: Marina Aleksejeva (born 18 May 1971) is an Estonian artist known for her drawings and collages. She graduated from the painting department of the University of Tartu in 1995 and defended her master's thesis at the same university in 2016. Since 1992 she has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and internationally. In addition to her artistic work, Aleksejeva works as a teacher at the Tartu Art School and the Tartu Art School for Children.

artists.b: Sündinud 28.06.1966, Põltsamaa; surnud 31.12.2019. Haridus: 1993 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia Tartu osakond; 1988 Tartu Kunstikool.
artists.ben: Born 28.06.1966, Põltsamaa; died 31.12.2019. Education: 1993 Estonian Academy of Arts, Tartu department; 1988 Tartu Art School.

artists.b: Vano Allsalu (1967) jõuliselt ekspressiivse käekirja ja isi- kupärase värvimaailmaga loomingu teemadering ulatub loodusstiihiatest meeleseisundite ja mütoloogiliste konstruktsioonideni. See puudutab intiimselt isiklikku, aga pakub ka tõlgendusi kultuurilisel ja sotsiaalsel väljal toimuvast. Allsalu on lõpetanud Eesti Kunstiakadeemia maali eriala (1991) ning töötanud õppejõuna Tartu Ülikoolis, Eesti Kunstiakadeemias ja Sally Stuudios; aastatel 2013–2025 oli ta Eesti Kunstnike Liidu presi- dent ja asepresident. Ta on osalenud aktiivselt näitustel, pälvinud mitmeid tunnustusi ning tema teosed kuuluvad paljudesse muuseumi- ja erakogudesse. Ta on Eesti Maalikunstnike Liidu ja Tartu Kunstnike Liidu liige ning Eesti Kunstnike Liidu auliige.
artists.ben: Vano Allsalu's (1967) work, with its forcefully expressive style and distinctive colour world, spans a range of themes from natural elements to states of mind and mythological constructions. It touches on the intimately personal, but also offers interpretations of what is happening in the cultural and social sphere. Allsalu graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in painting (1991) and has worked as a lecturer at the University of Tartu, the Estonian Academy of Arts and Sally Stuudios; in 2013–2025 he was president and vice-president of the Estonian Artists' Association. He has actively participated in exhibitions, received numerous accolades, and his works belong to many museum and private collections. He is a member of the Estonian Painters' Association and the Tartu Artists' Association, and an honorary member of the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.wdesc: Austrian painter, etcher and art educator (1860-1897)

artists.b: On lõpetanud Tallinna ülikooli kunstiosakonna. Pärast seda jätkas kunstiõpinguid Aasias. Ta õppis Tais Rajamangala ülikoolis maalikunsti, Lõuna-Koreas Kyonghees Souli rahvusülikoolis kujutavat kunsti ja lõpetas magistrantuuri Hongiki ülikoolis Soulis.
artists.ben: Graduated from the art department of Tallinn University. Afterwards continued art studies in Asia. He studied painting in Thailand at Rajamangala University, fine art in South Korea at Kyung Hee University and Seoul National University, and completed a master's degree at Hongik University in Seoul.

artists.b: 1966. usaldati talle tulekahjus osaliselt hävinud Tartu Ülikooli peahoone restaureerimisprojekti koostamine koos mahukate uuringutega. Hilisemas perioodis tegeles vanema kiviarhitektuuri uurimisega, peamiselt linnustega. A-tel 1977-93 valmisid konserveerimis-restaureerimisprojektid Kuressaare, Haapsalu, Paide, Porkuni ja Virtsu linnuste kohta. Tulemused võtab kokku 1993. a. ilmunud mahukas „Eesti keskaegsed linnused“.
artists.ben: In 1966 he was entrusted with drawing up the restoration project, together with extensive research, for the main building of the University of Tartu, which had been partly destroyed by fire. In the later period he studied older stone architecture, mainly castles. In the years 1977-93 conservation-restoration projects were completed for the castles of Kuressaare, Haapsalu, Paide, Porkuni and Virtsu. The results are summarised in the extensive book "Eesti keskaegsed linnused" ["Estonian Medieval Castles"], published in 1993.

artists.b: 1980-ndatest veetis enamuse suvedest Haapsalus maalides ja joonistades, ateljee asus Võnnu tänaval. Projekteeris Haapsalu ja Uuemõisa piiril asuva Aiandus-Mesindusseltsi maja. Sellesse ajajärku kuulub ka romantilises võtmes kuivnõela tehnikas sari Haapsalu ajaloost, millest nii mõnigi leidis omaniku Kivilille Galerii näitus-müükide kaudu.
artists.ben: From the 1980s he spent most of his summers painting and drawing in Haapsalu, his studio was located on Võnnu Street. He designed the building of the Gardening-Beekeeping Society located on the border of Haapsalu and Uuemõisa. This period also includes a series in a romantic vein done in the drypoint technique on the history of Haapsalu, several of which found an owner through the exhibition-sales of the Kivilill Gallery.

artists.b: Sündinud 04.01.1960, Tallinn. Haridus: 1984 Tartu Ülikool, kunstiajalugu; 1978 Tõnis Vindi stuudio.
artists.ben:
Siim-Tanel Annus (1960) is considered the first and one of the most significant performance artists in Estonia, although in the last two decades he has been working more in printmaking, painting and photography. Together with Jaan Toomik and Raol Kurvitz, Annus was among the first artists to represent Estonia at the Venice Biennale in 1997. In his work, Annus is looking for an ideal world and aims to give the audience the opportunity to rise above the everyday.

Siim-Tanel Annus began his career as an artist in 1976, when his early prints were exhibited at a Soviet avant-garde exhibition in the US and at the Rijeka International Drawing Bienniale. Unlike most artists at the time, Annus did not receive a traditional art education, instead he studied at Tõnis Vint's semi-underground studio and later art history in University of Tartu. In the 1980s Annus began doing performance art in his garden, inspired by the avant-garde apartment exhibitions in St Petersburg and Moscow. The best known of these exhibitions is “Läbimised” (The Transition, 1987), presented together with Ariel Lagle's original music. During the performance Annus conducted various fire rituals, while being clothed in a white dress and wearing a crown. The performance concluded with the artist passing through a gate of fire on a wheeled base while blindfolded. “Läbimised” even drew the attention of the Militsiya and Annus was interrogated together with the television crew. Annus' work, originally concerned with themes of universality, became intertwined with political reality, amplified by Perestroika and Estonia regaining its independence, elevating Annus to the status of prophet in retrospect.

In 1997 Estonia participated in the Venice Biennale for the first time ever and the Estonian Cultural Endowment chose Siim-Tanel Annus, Jaan Toomik and Raoul Kurvitz to create performances and installations on the Giardini embankment (at the time a pavilion was not rented for the exhibit). Annus created his piece based on a motif he had used in his previous work and transformed it into a sculptural three-dimensional object for his Venice performance, essentially staging its birth through his performance.

Today, the artist no longer works with performance, the medium that won him wider recognition, and is now mainly interested in painting and printmaking, returning to the preferred media of his youth in a way. In the 2010s he exhibited acrylic paintings “Raha ja poeesia” (Money and Poetry) as part of his solo show in Tallinn Art Hall, depicting magnified banknotes used in 20th century in Estonia. The.

artists.b: Õppis 1908-1913 kunsti Peterburis, Kunstide Edendamise Seltsi koolis (õpetajad N. Roerich, I. Bilibin jt), täiendas end Viinis ja Münchenis. Oli 1920-1925 Tallinnas Riigi Kunsttööstuskooli õppejõud ja 1926-1930 Tartus Pallase õppejõud. 1944 lahkus Eestis Saksamaale, 1949 asus USA-sse.
artists.ben: He studied art in Petersburg 1908-1913 at the school of the Society for the Encouragement of the Arts (teachers N. Roerich, I. Bilibin, and others), and continued his education in Vienna and Munich. He was a lecturer at the State School of Arts and Crafts in Tallinn 1920-1925 and a lecturer at Pallas in Tartu 1926-1930. In 1944 he left Estonia for Germany, in 1949 he moved to the USA.

artists.b: Õppis Moskva Maali-, raid- ja ehituskunstikoolis (1877-1883  V. Perovi ja 1886-1888 V. Polenovi juures ning ka V. J. Makovski) ning Peterburi KA (1884-1886 Wenigi ja Tšistjakovi juures). Sai 1885 ja 1887 suure hõbemedali AK-s ja 1909 Münchenis rahvusvahelises kunstinäitusel kuldmedali.
artists.ben: He studied at the Moscow School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture (1877-1883 under V. Perov and 1886-1888 under V. Polenov and also V. J. Makovsky) and at the Petersburg Academy of Arts (1884-1886 under Wenig and Chistyakov). He received a large silver medal at the Academy of Arts in 1885 and 1887, and a gold medal at the international art exhibition in Munich in 1909.

artists.b: Töötas Tallinna Metallitoodete Tehase kunstnikuna ja 1968–1969 Tallinnfilmi lavastuskunstnikuna; aastast 1969 vabakunstnik. Eesti NSV teeneline kunstnik (1988). Aastast 1969 Eesti kunstnike liidu liige. 1996. aastal oli ta Tartu Ülikooli vabade kunstide professor. Kuulus rühmitusse ANK'64.
artists.ben: He worked as an artist at the Tallinn Metal Products Factory and in 1968–1969 as a production designer at Tallinnfilm; from 1969 a freelance artist. Merited Artist of the Estonian SSR (1988). Member of the Estonian Artists' Union from 1969. In 1996 he was professor of liberal arts at the University of Tartu. A member of the group ANK'64.

artists.wdesc: Estonian stage artist, painter, and singer (born 1957)
Estonian painter and sculptor residing in Germany (born 1964)
Estonian athletics competitor, sports journalist and caricaturist (1915-1984)

artists.b: Läti kunstnik Martins Kruklis, sündinud 1972, kunstnikunimega Tif Bitmap. Tallinna XII graafikatriennaalil esines kolme digitaaltrükis teosega "Sõnum Tif Bitmapilt". Võitis Balteco eripreemia ja Eesti Kunstimuuseumi ostupreemia.
artists.ben: Latvian artist Martins Kruklis, born 1972, artist name Tif Bitmap. At the XII Tallinn Print Triennial he presented three works in digital print titled "A Message from Tif Bitmap". Won the Balteco special prize and the Art Museum of Estonia purchase prize.

artists.b: Sündis Järvamaal Koerus, 1907-1915 elas Narvas, 1915-1921 Venemaal Omskis. Tuli 1921 Eestisse tagasi, 1923-1935 õppis Tartus Pallases. Lõpetas graafikuna. 1937-1941 oli abielus Kaarel Liimandiga. 1937 õppereis Pariisi. 1940 kunstnike liidu org-toimkonna liige, "juunikommunist". 1940-1941 Tartu K. Mäe-nimelise kunstikooli õppejõud. 1941-1944 viibis Nõukogude Liidu tagalas, 1942 Jaroslavlis. Alates 1946 vabakunstnik Tallinnas.
artists.ben: Born in Koeru, Järva County, lived in Narva 1907-1915, in Omsk, Russia 1915-1921. Returned to Estonia in 1921, studied at Pallas in Tartu 1923-1935. Graduated as a graphic artist. 1937-1941 married to Kaarel Liimand. 1937 study trip to Paris. 1940 member of the organisational committee of the artists' union, a "June communist". 1940-1941 lecturer at the Tartu K. Mägi-name Art School. 1941-1944 stayed in the rear of the Soviet Union, in Jaroslavl in 1942. From 1946 freelance artist in Tallinn.

cit: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

artists.b: Sündis Riias kaupmehe pojana. Õppis Dresdeni kunstiakadeemias. Pärast õppereisi Itaaliasse, kus sihtles B. thorwaldseniga ja J. A. Kochiga, saabus 1829 Riiga tagasi. 1832 asus Dresdenisse, kus pärast teist Itaalia-reisi sai 1843 akadeemia õppejõuks ja 1846 professoriks. Elu lõpupoole tegeles teadusega (Liivimaa ajalugu, loodusteadused jne).1836 maalis C. D. Friedrichi portree, 1833 Riia Toomkiriku altarimaali jm altarimaale Läti kirikutele. Oli viljakas portretist.
artists.ben: Born in Riga as the son of a merchant. Studied at the Dresden Academy of Arts. After a study trip to Italy, where he associated with B. Thorwaldsen and J. A. Koch, he returned to Riga in 1829. In 1832 he moved to Dresden, where, after a second trip to Italy, he became a lecturer at the academy in 1843 and a professor in 1846. Towards the end of his life he engaged in scholarship (the history of Livonia, natural sciences, etc.). In 1836 he painted a portrait of C. D. Friedrich, in 1833 the altarpiece of Riga Cathedral and other altarpieces for churches in Latvia. He was a prolific portraitist.

artists.b: Ajalehe "Izvestia" enamnõutavate kaupade konkursi laureaat, üleliidulise rahvamajandusnäituse hõbe- ja kuldmedal dekoratiivse kanga "Gobelään" ja supellina eest (Moskva), Tšutkihhi nim. NSVL e preemia (1987.a.),  NSVL Kergetööstuse Ministeerium diplom.
artists.ben: Laureate of the newspaper "Izvestia" competition for most sought-after goods, silver and gold medal of the All-Union National Economy Exhibition for the decorative fabric "Gobelään" and bath towel (Moscow), USSR Tšutkihh named prize (1987), USSR Ministry of Light Industry diploma.

artists.b: Tema loomingu olulisemateks mõjutajateks olid Mantegna tööd ning Antonella da Messina poolt Veneetsia maalikunsti toodud Madalmaade kunsti elemendid. Neile tuginedes lõi Bellini oma isikupärase stiili, milles mängib olulist osa soe ja helendav valgus ning loomulik rahulik atmosfäär.
artists.ben: The most important influences on his work were the works of Mantegna and the elements of Netherlandish art brought to Venetian painting by Antonella da Messina. Building on these, Bellini created his own distinctive style, in which warm and luminous light and a natural, calm atmosphere play an important role.

artists.b: Kuna leidis tunnustust ka õukonnas, määrati vastutusrikastesse ametitesse. Nii oli ta Peterburi Vene Muuseumi esimene koguhoidja (alates 1895) ja Kaubanduse ja manufaktuuride Departemangu (hilisema ministeeriumi) kunstiosakonna inspektor.
artists.ben: As he also found recognition at court, he was appointed to positions of great responsibility. Thus he was the first curator of the Russian Museum in St. Petersburg (from 1895) and inspector of the art department of the Department of Trade and Manufactures (later the Ministry).

artists.b: Kunstialast algõpetust sai gümnaasiumis käies prof. Lipharti juures Peterburis; 1923 - 1926 Müncheni Akadeemias Janki ja Zügeli juures. Seejärel vabakunstnik Revalis. 1941 - 1945 Dresdenis, II MS järel Griesbachis (Bayer); Langeoogis ja Weeneris.
artists.ben: He received his initial art education while attending gymnasium under Prof. Liphart in Petersburg; 1923–1926 at the Munich Academy under Jank and Zügel. Thereafter a freelance artist in Reval. 1941–1945 in Dresden, after WWII in Griesbach (Bavaria); in Langeoog and in Wien.

artists.b: Laulja (bariton); ETL 1945;1930 Pärnu poeglaste gümnaasium; 1938 TK (A. Arderi kl.); Oli 1938-39 Viini Volksoper'i, 1942-1943 Kasseli Riigiooperi ning 1940-41 ja 1944-1988 "Estonia" solist; töötas alates 1940 vaheaegadega TK õppejõuna; aastast 1947 professor; esines väljaspool Eestit; tuntud oli ka kammer-ja oratooriumilauljana; esines ka filmis ja temast tehtud mitmed filmid; esikoht Viinis rahvusvahelisel lauljate võistlusel 1938; ENSV tnl. kunstnik 1945; ENSV rahvakunstnik 1952; NSVL rahvakunstnik 1954; Nõukogude Eesti preemia 1949, 1959, 1967; A-st 1993 tegutseb Estonia Seltsi juures lauluõppurite toetuseks tema nim. fond ning peetakse lauluvõistlusi.
artists.ben: Singer (baritone); ETL 1945; 1930 Pärnu Boys' Gymnasium; 1938 TK (A. Arder's class); was a soloist of the Vienna Volksoper in 1938–39, of the Kassel State Opera in 1942–1943, and of "Estonia" in 1940–41 and 1944–1988; worked from 1940, with interruptions, as a lecturer at TK; professor from 1947; performed outside Estonia; was also known as a chamber and oratorio singer; also appeared in film, and several films were made about him; first place at the international singing competition in Vienna in 1938; Honoured Artist of the ESSR 1945; People's Artist of the ESSR 1952; People's Artist of the USSR 1954; Soviet Estonian Prize in 1949, 1959, 1967; since 1993 a fund named after him has operated at the Estonia Society to support voice students, and singing competitions are held.

artists.b: Tema loomingut märkas Napoleon ja seetõttu sai ta 1794 ekspertide grupi juhuks, kes pidid välja Hispaania Madalmaades (nüüd Belgia) välja valima kunstiteosed, mida saadetakse pariisi. Samades ülesannetes tegutses ta ka Itaalias.
artists.ben: His work was noticed by Napoleon, and as a result in 1794 he became the head of a group of experts who were to select works of art in the Spanish Netherlands (now Belgium) to be sent to Paris. He carried out the same tasks in Italy as well.

artists.wdesc: Serbian painter, lawyer, journalist, and poet

artists.b: 1934. aastal alustas ta kunstiõpinguid graafik Aleksei Kravtšenko stuudios. 1936. aastast õppis Leningradis Ülevenemaalise Kunstiakadeemia kõrgemas kunstikoolis (praegu Peterburi I. E. Repini nimeline akadeemiline maali-, skulptuuri- ja arhitektuuriinstituut).
artists.ben: In 1934 he began his art studies in the studio of the graphic artist Aleksei Kravtšenko. From 1936 he studied at the Higher Art School of the All-Russian Academy of Arts in Leningrad (now the I. E. Repin Saint Petersburg Academic Institute of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture).

artists.b: Reisid Sakasamaale, Ungarisse, Kaukaasiasse. 1894 - 1915 tegutses Riias maalija, illustraatori ja kunstiõpetajana. Suured tellimused ka keiser Aleksander III - lt (pastellportree). 1915 - 1917 prof. Moskvasee evakueeritud Riia polütehnikumis. 1918 - Riias, 1919 - Berliinis, alates aastast 1923 vaheldumisi Berliinis ja Gollnowis (Pommer). Personaalnäitused Dresdenis, Berliinis ja Riias.
artists.ben: Travels to Germany, Hungary, the Caucasus. 1894–1915 worked in Riga as a painter, illustrator and art teacher. Also received large commissions from Emperor Alexander III (a pastel portrait). 1915–1917 professor at the Riga Polytechnic Institute evacuated to Moscow. 1918 in Riga, 1919 in Berlin, from 1923 alternately in Berlin and Gollnow (Pomerania). Solo exhibitions in Dresden, Berlin and Riga.

artists.b: Marju Bormeister (s. 1945 Tallinnas) lõpetas Eesti Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi maalikunstnikuna 1985. a. Kunstnike järeltulijana on ta elanud pool elust Tallinna Kunstihoones, sattudes varakult tärpentiini-lõhnalisse värvide maailma. Maalida meeldib Bormeistrile eelkõige loodust ning selles leiduvaid erinevaid pinnastruktuure. Bormeister naudib tehnikana eriti monotüüpiat.
artists.ben: Marju Bormeister (b. 1945 in Tallinn) graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute as a painter in 1985. As a descendant of artists, she has lived half her life in the Tallinn Art Hall, encountering early on the turpentine-scented world of paints. Bormeister especially likes to paint nature and the various surface structures found in it. As a technique, Bormeister particularly enjoys monotype.

artists.b: Baleriin, ballettmeister, balletipedagoog; ENL 1940; ETL 1959; lõpet. Tallinna vene gümnaasiumi; tantsu õppis 1921-25 E. Litvinova stuudios; 1928-29 Berliinis V. Gsovsky; 1932 Pariisis O. Preobrazenskaja juures ja 1934-36 Riias ja 1943-44 Moskva koreograafiakoolis; Esines Riias ja Stockholmis, oli 1925-30 Antverpenis Flaami Kuningliku Ooperiteatri balletisolist, seejärel Kesk-Euroopas; oli 1933-35 Liepaja ooperiteatri ballettmeister ja solist; 1937 Pariisi kabaree Folies Bergére tantsupedagoog ning esines 1938 H. Flemingi trupiga Itaalias; oli 1940-41 "Estonia" balletipedagoog ja lavastaja ning samas 1944-51 balletijuht ja ballettmeister, kuulus ERKA-sse; algatas TKK rajamise, oli 1946-48 ja 1951-65 selle direktor, a-ni 1966 klassikalise tantsu õpetaja; ENSV tnl. kultuuritegelane 1959; Nõukogude Eesti preemia 1948.
artists.ben: Ballerina, ballet master, ballet pedagogue; ENL 1940; ETL 1959; graduated from the Tallinn Russian Gymnasium; studied dance in 1921-25 at E. Litvinova's studio; in 1928-29 in Berlin with V. Gsovsky; in 1932 in Paris with O. Preobrazhenskaya and in 1934-36 in Riga and in 1943-44 at the Moscow choreography school; performed in Riga and Stockholm, was in 1925-30 a ballet soloist at the Flemish Royal Opera Theatre in Antwerp, then in Central Europe; was in 1933-35 ballet master and soloist of the Liepāja Opera Theatre; in 1937 a dance teacher at the Paris cabaret Folies Bergère and performed in 1938 with H. Fleming's troupe in Italy; was in 1940-41 ballet pedagogue and director at "Estonia" and there also in 1944-51 ballet director and ballet master, was a member of ERKA; initiated the founding of TKK, was its director in 1946-48 and 1951-65, and until 1966 a teacher of classical dance; Honoured Cultural Worker of the ESSR 1959; Soviet Estonian Prize 1948.

artists.b: Töötas Venemaal alates 1750. aastate lõpust. Oli kunstniku ja restauraatori L. C. Pfandzelti abiline, mh. Tsarskoje Selo dekoratiivmaalingute teostamisel. Hiljem töötas iseseisvalt portretisti ja kopistina, säilinud on mitu tema koopiat Peeter III, Katariina II ja troonipärija Pavel Petrovitði (Paul I) portreedest. Maalis kõrgete riigiametnike ja sõjaväelaste portreid, tegi eskiise M. V. Lomonossovi mosaiigitöökoja jaoks.
artists.ben: Worked in Russia from the late 1750s. Was an assistant to the artist and restorer L. C. Pfandzelt, among other things in the execution of decorative paintings at Tsarskoye Selo. Later worked independently as a portraitist and copyist; several of his copies of portraits of Peter III, Catherine II and the heir to the throne Pavel Petrovich (Paul I) have survived. Painted portraits of high state officials and military men, made sketches for M. V. Lomonosov's mosaic workshop.

artists.b: C. F. C. Buddeus sündis Tüüringis, Gothas, arvatavasti prantsuse päritolu perekonnas. Õppis filantropiinis ja töötas koduõpetajana. Pärast 1809 oli koduõpetaja Saaremaal, Pihkva ja Peterburi kubermangus, hiljemalt 1825 asus Tallinna, kus abiellus veinikaupmees Hartmuthi tütrega. Elas Kopli poolsaarel. Eestis viibides tegeles palju joonistamisega. Suri Gothas.
artists.ben: C. F. C. Buddeus was born in Gotha, Thuringia, presumably into a family of French origin. He studied at a philanthropinum and worked as a private tutor. After 1809 he was a private tutor in Saaremaa, in the Pskov and St Petersburg governorates, and by 1825 at the latest he settled in Tallinn, where he married the daughter of the wine merchant Hartmuth. He lived on the Kopli peninsula. While in Estonia he engaged much in drawing. He died in Gotha.

artists.b: 1907 - 1912 õppis Riia kunstikoolis Th. Krausi, V. Purvitise ja J. Rosenthali juures. Lõpetas preemiaga. 1912 - 1916 õppis edasi Peterburi Kunstide Akadeemias. Edasi Tartus vabakunstnik; 1922. aastast alates õppis graafikat Dresdeni KA-s.
artists.ben: 1907-1912 studied at the Riga Art School under Th. Kraus, V. Purvitis and J. Rosenthal. Graduated with a prize. 1912-1916 continued studies at the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. Afterwards a freelance artist in Tartu; from 1922 studied graphic art at the Dresden Academy of Arts.

artists.b: Paul ja Karl Burman on meie kultuuriloos huvitav näide sellest, kuidas toona hääbuva baltisaksa kultuuri esindajad kohanesid ja sulandusid tormiliselt arenevasse rahvuslikku kunstiellu. Ta alustas kunstniku karjääri Eestimaal ajal, mil baltisaksa kunstielu oli hääbumas ja tähtsust minetamas. Paul kuulus oma kultuurilistelt tõekspidamistelt ja keele kasutuselt kindlalt baltisaksa ringkonda. Õpingud ja lapsepõlvekodu sidusid teda ka vene kultuuriga. Kunstniku perekonnal olid baltisaksa juured ning tihedad sidemeid Venemaaga. Paul Burman ei omandanud eesti keelt kuni surmani, kuigi lävis eluajal paljude eesti kunstnikega. Tema looming arenes aga seesmise loogika ja impulsside ajel ning sellel puudus tihedam side eesti kunsti üldiste suundumustega.
artists.ben: Paul and Karl Burman are an interesting example in our cultural history of how representatives of the then-declining Baltic German culture adapted to and blended into a rapidly developing national art scene. He began his career as an artist in Estonia at a time when Baltic German artistic life was fading and losing significance. Paul, in his cultural convictions and use of language, firmly belonged to the Baltic German circle. His studies and childhood home also connected him with Russian culture. The artist's family had Baltic German roots and close ties with Russia. Paul Burman never learned the Estonian language until his death, although during his lifetime he associated with many Estonian artists. His work, however, developed under the influence of inner logic and impulses and had no closer connection with the general trends of Estonian art.

artists.b: Varaseid balti ksülograafe. Lõpetas Tartu kreiskooli, õppis F. L. von Maydelli puugravüüritöökojas Tartus ja vabakuulajana Peterburi kunstiakadeemias. Avas Peterburis Vassili saarel puugravüüritöökoja, mis varustas illustratsioonidega ajalehti, kalendreid jne.

L. von Maydell's wood engraving workshop in Tartu and as a visiting student at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Arts. Opened a wood engraving workshop on Vasilyevsky Island in Saint Petersburg, which supplied illustrations for newspapers, calendars, etc.

artists.b: Esines näitustel Peterburis ja Moskvas kunstnike ühingu "Novoe Obšestvo" näitustel ning Mir Isskustva, Obšestvo Nezavissimõh salongides. Esines ka Kiievis, Helsingis, Riias, Roomas ja Veneetsias. Hiljem Tallinnas, Tartus, Lübeckis ja Köningsbergis. Osales kunstnikkude ühingu ARS ja EKKKÜ ning Kultuurkapitali korraldatud näitustel. Oli Eesti Akadeemiliste Kutseõiguslike Kunstnikkude Koondise liige ja Helsingi Vene Kunstnikkude Ühingu liige.
artists.ben: He exhibited at exhibitions in Saint Petersburg and Moscow at the exhibitions of the artists' association "Novoe Obšestvo" and in the salons Mir Isskustva and Obšestvo Nezavissimõh. He also exhibited in Kiev, Helsinki, Riga, Rome and Venice. Later in Tallinn, Tartu, Lübeck and Königsberg. He took part in exhibitions organized by the artists' associations ARS and EKKKÜ and by the Cultural Endowment. He was a member of the Estonian Academic Association of Professional Artists (Eesti Akadeemiliste Kutseõiguslike Kunstnikkude Koondis) and of the Helsinki Russian Artists' Union.

artists.b: Keskel naisterahvas valgetes riietes, paljajalu, pruunikas sall õlgadel. Ta on sirutanud käed paremale, tütarlapse poole, kes tema põske silitab. Neiu piha ümbert hoiab kinni noormees, kes teise käega paremale, taamal seisvale purjekale osutab. Vasakult poolt tulevad joostes vanem mees ja naine.
artists.ben: In the middle a woman in white clothing, barefoot, with a brownish shawl on her shoulders. She has stretched out her arms to the right, towards a girl, who strokes her cheek. A young man holds the girl around the waist, and with his other hand points to the right, towards a sailboat standing further away. From the left an older man and a woman come running.

artists.b: Sündis 1799 Viljandis rätsepa Friedrich Burchard Dörbecki ja poolatarist ema Helena (Rakosnik) pojana. Õppis graafikat Peterburis Friedrich Neyeri juures, oli riigi väärtpaberite teksti graveerija. Dörbecki esimene abielu kestis august-oktoober 1819. Elas 1820-23 Riias, kus graveeris visiitkaarte ja portreid. 1822 tegi akvatinta eestlasest K. J. Petersonist. 1823 abiellus Riias uuesti ja läks Berliini, kus tegutses menuka karikaturistina (kirjastaja Gropius). Litosarjad: Berliner Witze, Berliner Redensarten (1830), Album Academicum (1832), jt. Berliinis graveeris Dörbeck Lutheri, Calvini jt portreed. 1823 sündis tütar Olga Helene ja 1827 poeg Roman Anastasius. 1830 suri teine naine Jakobine. 1831 abiellus kunstnik kolmandat korda. 1832 sündis poeg Franz. Tuberkuloosihaigena pöördus Dörbeck koos Olga ja Romaniga 1835 tagasi Viljandisse. Suri Viljandis. Riia maantee kalmistul avatud talle mälestuskivi.
artists.ben: He was born in 1799 in Viljandi, the son of the tailor Friedrich Burchard Dörbeck and his mother Helena (Rakosnik), who was of Polish descent. He studied graphic art in St. Petersburg under Friedrich Neyer, and was an engraver of texts for state securities. Dörbeck's first marriage lasted from August to October 1819. In 1820–23 he lived in Riga, where he engraved visiting cards and portraits. In 1822 he made an aquatint of the Estonian K. J. Peterson. In 1823 he remarried in Riga and moved to Berlin, where he worked as a successful caricaturist (publisher Gropius). Lithograph series: Berliner Witze, Berliner Redensarten (1830), Album Academicum (1832), etc. In Berlin Dörbeck engraved portraits of Luther, Calvin and others. In 1823 his daughter Olga Helene was born, and in 1827 his son Roman Anastasius. In 1830 his second wife Jakobine died. In 1831 the artist married for the third time. In 1832 his son Franz was born. Suffering from tuberculosis, Dörbeck returned with Olga and Roman to Viljandi in 1835. He died in Viljandi. A memorial stone was unveiled to him at the Riia maantee cemetery.

artists.b: Sündinud 26.03.1934, Järvamaa, Võhmuta. Haridus: 1959 Eesti NSV Riiklik Kunstiinstituut, graafika.

artists.ben:
Sirja-Liisa Eelma (1973) is a conceptual painter, whose visual language is characterised by minimalist structures. She often works with repeating and slowly changing images in order to analyse themes like lack of intimacy, the physical experience of pause, silence, and delineating the visible and the invisible. Eelma’s practice relies on the mutual impact of the time factor and the spatial context in painting, her works evoke contemplation and meditative quietness. Eelma’s colours are extremely nuanced, sensitive in gradation and mostly pastel.

She started her career as an artist in the second half of the 1990s. In her early years, Eelma focused on the playful juxtaposition of letters and shapes. At the show “Õ><Ö” (2006, Tallinn City Gallery) she displayed a series that offered proof of a theorem regarding the alikeness of the letters Õ and Ö; the exhibition “Everyday vocabulary” (2006, Hobusepea Gallery) combined elements of different sign systems to create a new coherence. Since the late 2000s she has increasingly focused on the process of painting, letting herself be guided by the flow of time, the pleasure and solitude of painting a repeating image.

The exhibition and the series of paintings titled “Secret Matter” (2003, Hobusepea Gallery) centred on the hidden or perceptible objects as well as expectations and fears related to their environment. Eelma continued working with these ideas in the show “There is Nothing” (2012, Draakon Gallery), where all the exhibited paintings depicted curtains. The anxious repetition of the image of curtains expressed a tension, whereas the title of the show evoked a safe environment. Repetitive motifs were also the central element in the exhibition “The Waiting Room” (2014, Hobusepea Gallery), where the artist showed similar views of interiors and, drawing parallels between the similarity of the gallery space and the depicted waiting room, created an installation of a-space-within-a-space.

The series of paintings “Emptying Field of Meaning” (2014) was the first time a slowly changing symmetrical repetition of an abstract geometrical shape appeared in Eelma’s work. The idea of the series was to create a pause in the contemporary information overload, above all, for the painter herself but also for the viewer.

artists.b: Sirje Eelma (s. 1950 Tallinnas) kunsti põhiliseks lähteallikas on loodus. Tema jaoks on oluline graafika trükiprotsess ning väljendusvahendite sisemistest võimalustest tekkivad nüansid. Summutatud koloriit toob hästi esile teose sisemise helenduse ja erinevate faktuuride kontrastid. Viited äratuntavatele motiividele on põimunud elegantse vormikeelega, piltide salapärane tehniline mitmekihilisus loob mängulisi ruumilisi assotsiatsioone ja hoiab koos positiivset meeleolu.
artists.ben: Sirje Eelma's (b. 1950 in Tallinn) main source of art is nature. For her, the printmaking process of graphic art and the nuances arising from the internal possibilities of the means of expression are important. The subdued colouring brings out well the inner glow of the work and the contrasts of different textures. References to recognisable motifs are intertwined with an elegant formal language, the mysterious technical multilayeredness of the images creates playful spatial associations and holds together a positive mood.

artists.b: Aastatel 1972–1977 töötas ta Eesti Telefilmi joonisfilmigrupis kunstnik-kopeerijana. 1977. aastal alustas õpinguid ERKI-s, lõpetas 1983. aastal maalikunstnik-pedagoogina. Näitustel osalemist alustas 1982. Aastatel 1983–1984 töötas Tallinfilmi joonisfilmis kunstnik-maalijana. Aastatel 1984–1989 kunstiliste eriainete õpetajana Tallinna Kergetööstustehnikumis. Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liigea Eher 1989. aastast. Teoseid Eesti Kunstimuuseumi, Tartu Kunstimuuseumi, Venemaa kultuuriministeeriumi, Tretjakovi galerii, Alma-Ata Kunstimuuseumi ja Kasahstani Uzhgorodi kunstimuuseumi kogudesse ning erakogudesse.
artists.ben: From 1972 to 1977 he worked as an artist-copyist in the animated film group of Eesti Telefilm. In 1977 he began studies at ERKI, graduating in 1983 as a painter-pedagogue. He began participating in exhibitions in 1982. From 1983 to 1984 he worked as an artist-painter at Tallinnfilm's animated film studio. From 1984 to 1989 he was a teacher of artistic special subjects at Tallinna Kergetööstustehnikum. Member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1989. Works are held in the collections of the Art Museum of Estonia, the Tartu Art Museum, the Ministry of Culture of Russia, the Tretyakov Gallery, the Alma-Ata Art Museum and the Uzhgorod Art Museum in Kazakhstan, as well as in private collections.

artists.b: EINMANN, Eduard (1913, Kullamaa – 1982, Tallinn). Einmanni looming on jagatav perioodideks. 1950. aastatel lõi ta natuuritruid tööliste, talupoegade, teadlaste ja kunstiinimeste portreejoonistusi, 1960. aastate töödes on märgatav stiliseeriv joon, 1970. aastatel pöördus kunstnik tagasi realistlikku portree- ja maastikumaali juurde. Kunsti õppis Einmann Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis ja Riigi Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis, kus lõpetas dekoratsioonimaali eriala. II maailmasõja ajal kuulus ta Jaroslavi eesti kunstnike kollektiivi. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/.

Arhitekt, TÜ kasvandik (tehnikateaduskond 1935-1936), Helsingi ülikool arhitektuur 1937-1940, Müncheni Tehnokaülikool arhitektuur 1942-1944, Ontario Kunstikolledž (Torontos) keraamika 1982-1992, Baieri Rahandusministeeriumi ehitusosakonna arhitekt 1945-1948, Rootsi 1948, Kanadasse 1949, Toronto ülikooli arhitektuuri õppejõud, ühtlasi eraarhitekt 1949-1982, Taani Kuningliku Kunstiakadeemia külalisprofessor 1964, professor emeritus 1982.
artists.ben: Architect, graduate of the University of Tartu (Faculty of Technology 1935-1936), University of Helsinki architecture 1937-1940, Munich Technical University architecture 1942-1944, Ontario College of Art (Toronto) ceramics 1982-1992, architect at the Bavarian Ministry of Finance's construction department 1945-1948, Sweden 1948, to Canada 1949, lecturer of architecture at the University of Toronto, also private architect 1949-1982, visiting professor at the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts 1964, professor emeritus 1982.

artists.b: Maal on olnud rektor Toomas Asseri kabinetis 2021-2024. Universitas Tartuensis 2021 nr 6 lk 11: Koroonaaja saabudes otsustas rektor Toomas Asser viia oma tööruumist välja suure musta kapi, mida ta nimetab masendavaks. Vabanenud seinapinda valis ta kaunistama Jaan Elkeni 1978. aastal valminud maali „Kusagil Eestis“, mis kuulub ülikooli kunstimuuseumi kogusse. „Ma ei tea, mida see uuele põlvkonnale ütleb, aga siin on väga palju tähenduslikke asju. Üleval on näiteks „KG“ ehk KGB, ja siis on näha suunamuutusi – et midagi Eestis muutub,“ kirjeldab rektor maali vaadates.
artists.ben: The painting was in Rector Toomas Asser's office from 2021-2024. Universitas Tartuensis 2021 no. 6, p. 11: With the arrival of the coronavirus period, Rector Toomas Asser decided to remove a large black cabinet from his office, which he calls depressing. To decorate the freed-up wall space, he chose Jaan Elken's 1978 painting "Kusagil Eestis", which belongs to the collection of the university's art museum. "I don't know what it says to the new generation, but there are a lot of meaningful things here. Up there, for example, is 'KG', that is, KGB, and then you can see changes of direction - that something is changing in Estonia," the rector describes while looking at the painting.

artists.b: Eesti Raadioamatööride Ühingu liige, esimesi eesti raadioamatööre. 1930. a-te teisel poolel oli Aleksander Rähni töökoda Tallinna üks tuntumaid raadioparandustöökodasid. Veel tegeles A. Rähn raadioaparaatide erikonstruktsioonide, amatööride kontrollimise, supervastuvõtjate häälestamise, ristmähiste kerimisega.
artists.ben: A member of the Estonian Society of Radio Amateurs, one of the first Estonian radio amateurs. In the second half of the 1930s Aleksander Rähn's workshop was one of the best-known radio repair workshops in Tallinn. A. Rähn also worked on special constructions of radio apparatus, testing of amateurs, tuning of super receivers, and winding cross coils.

artists.b: 1891 - 1914 eriart Riias. I MS - sõjaväearst vene armees. 1919 - 1924 Saksamaal. 1924. aastast Tallinas ja Tartus kultuuri, teaduse ja kirjanduse alal tegev. Selle kõrval tegeles maaliga. Personaalnäitused Tartus, Rakveres ja Tallinnas.
artists.ben: 1891–1914 specialised in Riga. World War I – military doctor in the Russian army. 1919–1924 in Germany. From 1924 active in Tallinn and Tartu in the fields of culture, science and literature. Alongside this he also engaged in painting. Solo exhibitions in Tartu, Rakvere and Tallinn.

Eike Eplik (1982) is a sculptor and installation artist. She uses nature motifs for constructing narrative, utilises the gallery space from floor to ceiling, works with sculpting techniques from classic plaster casting to paper and wood assemblage and found objects. The processes in her art are partly subconscious and not always fully explainable. When preparing exhibitions Eplik relies on improvisation – to the extent material allows, of course.

One of Eplik's first exhibitions, “The girl who loved everything” (2012) is inspired by the Hungarian writer Ervin Lázár's fairytale “The seven-headed fairy”. The animals in the fairytale-like

created in the exhibition are cartoonish, many of them freaks, chimeras combined of multiple plants and animals, conglomerates frozen into weird compositions.

The exhibition “Some of the birds flew on their backs” (2015) played around with creating compositions of portrait paintings and still lifes, emphasising the perishable and temporal nature of the subject. This existential theme was further developed with the show “Beauty salon” (2017), where the artist explored the construction of beauty and its fleeting and unnatural core. Unlike her previous exhibitions, “Natural” (2018) foregrounded a mechanical-therapeutic way of making art – the artist exhibited installations-sculptures that imitated organic and natural forms in various stages of abstraction.

artists.b: Albert Eskel (1922–1975) rakendas 1960. aastail äratuntavalt isikupärast modernistlikku vormikõnet nii portreedes, figuraalsetes kompositsioonides kui ka monumentaalloomingus. Suur osa tema praegustest pronksskulptuuridest on viidud väärismaterjali alles pärast autori surma. Portreeloomingut, mis valati pronksi juba autori eluajal, iseloomustab pinnatöötluse varjundirikkus ning hea materjali võimaluste taju. Ta on enamasti lõiganud portreed väga madalalt, kaelaosa välistades, jättes modelleeringu ajuti taotluslikult robustseks. Figuraalsete kompositsioonide hulgas on ajastumärgilisi muusikateemalisi kompositsioone, millest osa lahendatud ka jämedakoelises šamotis. Kogu tema 1960. aastate loomingut iseloomustab jõulise väljenduslikkuse taotlus, vorm on lakooniline ja tähelepanuväärselt monumentaalse üldmõjuga. Monumentidest tuntakse enim Eduard Vilde monumenti Tallinnas (1965), ta on loonud aga ka rea mälestustahvleid ja hauasambaid.
artists.ben: Albert Eskel (1922–1975) applied a recognisably distinctive modernist formal language in the 1960s, both in portraits, figural compositions and monumental work. A large part of his bronze sculptures existing today were only cast in the precious material after the author's death. His portrait work, which was cast in bronze already during the author's lifetime, is characterised by a rich nuance of surface treatment and a good sense of the possibilities of the material. He has mostly cut the portraits very low, excluding the neck area, leaving the modelling occasionally deliberately rough. Among the figural compositions there are music-themed compositions marking the era, some of which are also executed in coarse-textured chamotte. All his work of the 1960s is characterised by a striving for forceful expressiveness, the form is laconic and remarkably monumental in overall effect. Among his monuments, the best known is the monument to Eduard Vilde in Tallinn (1965), but he has also created a series of memorial plaques and gravestones.

artists.b:
Sündis Tallinnas inseneri perekonnas.Ta lõpetas koos tulevase abikaasa Albert Eskeli ning mitme teise oma põlvkonna tuntud kunstnikuga 1948. aastal Tallinna Riikliku Tarbekunstiinstituudi, ent diplomit talle poliitilistel põhjustel ei antud. Tema isa Raiu Mullari oli silmapaistev vabadussõdalane ning vend Rünno Mullari, andekas matemaatik, saadeti okupatsioonivõimude poolt vangilaagrisse.

Aastail 1948–1952 töötas Juta Eskel mitmes Tallinna koolis joonistusõpetajana, 1952–1957 sai ta kunstnikuna tööd kunstitoodete kombinaadis.
artists.ben:
Born in Tallinn into an engineer's family. In 1948 she graduated, together with her future husband Albert Eskel and several other well-known artists of her generation, from the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art, but was not given a diploma for political reasons. Her father Raiu Mullari was a prominent Estonian War of Independence veteran, and her brother Rünno Mullari, a talented mathematician, was sent to a prison camp by the occupying authorities.

In 1948-1952 Juta Eskel worked as a drawing teacher in several schools in Tallinn, in 1952-1957 she found work as an artist at the Art Products Combine.

artists.b: Eesti näitleja, õppis 1918–24 Tallinna Linna Poeglaste Reaalgümnaasiumis ja 1924–25 Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis (Günther Reindorffi graafikaklassis). Õppinud laulu Armanda degli Abbati ja Helmi Eineri juures. Võeti 1925 Estonia õpperühma, töötas 1925–41 (tegi kaasa ka operetis) ja 1947–49 Estonias, 1947 Rakvere Teatris, 1949–65 Draamateatris ning 1966–83 Noorsooteatris; 1941–46 oli väljasaadetuna Solikamskis. Mänginud kuuldemängudes (Tolstoi Elav laip, 1956; Cronini Tsitadell, 1956; Büchneri Dantoni surm, 1963), telelavastustes (Hauseri Valge veri, 1959; Gruszezneski Suur Bobby, 1962; Dürrenmatti Meteoor, 1969; Bunini Öisel merel, 1977) ja rohkem kui 30 filmis (Päikese lapsed, 1932, Theodor Lutsu stuudio; Pöördel, 1957, Põrgupõhja uus Vanapagan, 1964, Indrek, 1975, Kõrboja peremees, 1979, kõik Tallinnfilm; Jäljed lumel, 1955, Vaikne hooaeg, 1968, mõlemad Lenfilm; Nõukogude Liidu suursaadik, 1969, Mosfilm; Kolme katku vahel, 1970, Eesti Telefilm). Oli tuntud ka maalijana ja enne Teist maailmasõda meeleolulauljana. Mälestusteraamat Näitleja on ajastu lühikroonika (1986). Temast on filmid Ants Eskola (1968, Eesti Telefilm) ja Ants Eskola: olla või mitte olla (2008, režissöör Kristjan Paul Virve). Tema vanglakirjad on publitseeritud raamatus Härra Ants. Ants Eskola kirjad Hugo Laurile Solikamski vangilaagrist (2005, koostanud Irja Vaher).
artists.ben: Estonian actor, studied 1918–24 at the Tallinn Municipal Boys' Secondary School and 1924–25 at the State School of Arts and Crafts (in Günther Reindorff’s graphic art class). Studied singing under Armanda degli Abbati and Helmi Einer. Was admitted in 1925 to the Estonia study group, worked 1925–41 (also performed in operetta) and 1947–49 at Estonia, in 1947 at Rakvere Theatre, 1949–65 at the Drama Theatre and 1966–83 at the Youth Theatre; from 1941–46 was deported to Solikamsk. Performed in radio plays (Tolstoy’s The Living Corpse, 1956; Cronin’s The Citadel, 1956; Büchner’s Danton’s Death, 1963), television productions (Hauser’s White Blood, 1959; Gruszecki’s Big Bobby, 1962; Dürrenmatt’s The Meteor, 1969; Bunin’s On the Night Sea, 1977) and in more than 30 films (Children of the Sun, 1932, Theodor Luts’s studio; Pöördel, 1957, The New Devil of Hell's Bottom, 1964, Indrek, 1975, The Master of Kõrboja, 1979, all Tallinnfilm; Traces in the Snow, 1955, The Quiet Season, 1968, both Lenfilm; Ambassador of the Soviet Union, 1969, Mosfilm; Between Three Plagues, 1970, Eesti Telefilm). Was also known as a painter and, before World War II, as a mood singer. Memoir book Näitleja on ajastu lühikroonika (1986). Films have been made about him: Ants Eskola (1968, Eesti Telefilm) and Ants Eskola: olla või mitte olla (2008, director Kristjan Paul Virve). His prison letters have been published in the book Härra Ants. Ants Eskola kirjad Hugo Laurile Solikamski vangilaagrist (2005, compiled by Irja Vaher).

artists.b: Õppis Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis Pallas maali- ja mööblikunsti (1926–1932). Pärast Pallase lõpetamist tegutses vabakunstnikuna Tartus, kus pidas aastatel 1934–1937 legendaarset kultuurirahva kohvikut "Ko-Ko-Ko. Pärast sõda aastatel 1945–1947 töötas ta Tartu 1. keskkoolis joonistusõpetajana ning aastatel 1947–1950 Kunstifondi Tartu büroo esimehena. Hiljem tegi illustratsioone ERM-i väljaannetele ja ajakirjadele ning loonud karikatuure. Oli aastast 1932 Eesti Kujutavate Kunstnikkude Keskühingu liige ning aastast 1945 Eesti NSV Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: He studied painting and furniture art at the Pallas Higher Art School (1926–1932). After graduating from Pallas he worked as a freelance artist in Tartu, where between 1934 and 1937 he ran the legendary café for cultural figures, "Ko-Ko-Ko". After the war, between 1945 and 1947, he worked as a drawing teacher at Tartu 1st Secondary School, and from 1947 to 1950 as chairman of the Tartu bureau of the Art Fund. Later he made illustrations for ERM publications and magazines and created caricatures. He was a member of the Central Union of Estonian Visual Artists from 1932 and a member of the Estonian SSR Artists' Union from 1945.

Kadi Estland (1973) is a textile artist by education and her feminist work relies on the method of critical deconstruction. One of the focal points of Estland's work is the relationship between the individual and the system – she tells stories about vulnerable people in the contemporary world. By combining expensive and cheap materials or vernacular with high culture quotes, Estland creates emotional works that highlight the processes of reproduction of the patriarchy.

Since the beginning of the 2000s Kadi Estland’s (official name Kadi Soosalu) feminist work has shaped contemporary Estonian art and during that period she worked both individually and as part of collectives such as Valie Export Society, The Elfriede Jelinek School of English Language and Feminismiehitaja. These collectives focused on articulating women's rights and possibilities in Estonia at the end of the 1990s and in the beginning of the 2000s. Estland is also the founder and manager of the artist-run-space Nancy Nakamura Ideederiiul (Tallinn, 2013–2015), and free clothing store and community centre Suburbia Kopopola (with Minna Hint, Tallinn, 2015).

One of Estland's earliest appearances was together with Ele Praks and Helen Lehismets at the exhibition “Töötud armastajad” (Unemployed Lovers, 1999) at the Tallinn Art Hall Gallery. The exhibited set of embroidered pieces titled “Kuidas elatakse Ameerikas?” (How do they live in America?) evoked autobiographical narratives, where the artist's notes and comments played an important role, alluding to the possibility of other kinds of experiences. Through the personal nature of Estland's embroidery the work also acquired a political meaning and her conscious decision to use craft techniques was guided by an ideological principle.

In 1999 Estland founded the collective Valie Export Society together with Killu Sukmit and Mari Laanemets, borrowing its name from the Australian feminist artist Valie Export. With performances in public spaces the artists recreated Valie Export's artistic interventions, adapting them to the cultural context of the newly independent Estonia. For example, during the intervention “Homomeeter II” (a remake of Valie Export's “Homo Meter II”, 1976) the artists walked the streets of Tallinn, each with a loaf of bread attached to their stomach, offering slices of bread to passers-by. In “From the Portfolio of Doggishness” (2000) the members of the group walked around Tallinn with the art critic Hanno Soans tied to a leash (a reference to Valie Export's work “Aus der Mappe der Hundigkeit”, 1968).

artists.b: Haridus: 2007–2009 Goldsmiths College, MFA Art Practice; 2005–2007 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, interdistsiplinaarsed kunstid MA; 2004 Kent Institute of Art and Design, Suurbritannia, vahetusõpilane vabade kunstide teaduskonnas; 2001–2005 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, maal BA; 2000–2001 Non Grata Academia, performance.
artists.ben:
Merike Estna (1980) is an artist working in the space of expanded painting, with many of her works transcending the boundaries of the canvas to encompass different environments, objects, and bodies. Estna’s work intertwines repetitive patterns and mythological motifs. She references history, literature and myths, linking them to contemporary themes and personal stories. In recent years, the artist’s work has been strongly influenced by the culture of Mexico, where she has lived and worked since 2022.

Estna began her creative journey in the early 2000s with photorealistic and pop-inspired paintings and collages. Her early works feature hyper-sexualised female nudes, assertive men, and naive children, depicting a neoliberal consumer society. While studying at Goldsmiths College in London, the artist changed her mode of expression, and in 2012 began to reimagine the meaning of painting. As a result, her works include stage sets, benches, tiled floors, curtains, household items, clothing, and food and drink, inviting the viewer to experience them with their senses: her artworks can be touched, worn, or tasted. Estna first addressed the expanded boundaries of painting in her solo exhibition

at the Kumu Art Museum (2014), where canvases became spatial installations and painting principles were applied to various objects such as books, clothing, etc.

Since 2016, Estna has become increasingly interested in traditional craft techniques. Expanding the medium of painting, she has used ceramics, woven carpets and other textiles, making them carry personal stories and cultural messages (.

artists.b: Sündinud 02.07.1974, Budapest, Ungari. Haridus: 2003 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, fotograafia MA; 2001 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, graafika BA.
artists.ben:
Dénes Farkas (1974) is a Hungarian-Estonian photo and installation artist, focusing on the critique of visual representation, the relationship of image and text, and the role of social predetermination in individual experiences.

Even when Farkas' work includes people, the human figure is rarely seen. Only one of his earlier series, “Portraits of women” (2002–2003) depicted real people. With his next series “15 portraits” (2004) the artist stepped away from depicting people only to portray them through their refrigerators instead.

Farkas also has a keen interest in architecture, and so one of his most characteristic motifs is paper models of everyday situations. In his series “Superstructure“ (2009) and “How the fuck are you tonight” (2009), based on post-structural theory, Farkas photographed paper chairs, tables, sofas and other human-made objects and environments, placing them in compositions conveying social structures.

In 2013 Farkas represented Estonia at the 55th Venice Biennale with the exhibition “Evident in Advance”. At the centre of Farkas' installation was a library of 10 000 books; additionally, symbolic spaces for working with books, such as an archive, class room, and home were created. The audience was invited to explore the spaces with books and locate new spheres of meaning. As a labyrinth of language, translation and interpretation, “Evident in Advance” illustrated the quest for knowledge and the inevitable failure of trying to explain everything.

artists.b: Baltisaksa graafik, maalija ning apteeker. Sündis šveitsi päritoluga apteekri ning Limbaži raehärra pojana, ta ema oli kohaliku pastori tütar. 1828 sooritas Gehlhaar Tartu ülikooli juures apteekriabilise ja 1828, eksternina, proviisori eksami. 1834 sai ta oma isa apteegi omanikuks Limbažis. Arvatavasti õppis Tartu ülikooli joonistuskoolis C. A. Senffi juures, kuid oli kunstnikuna valdavalt iseõppija. 1828 andis Tallinnas välja esimese akvatintatehnikas vaategraafika sarja, mille kirjastaja oli Georg Eggers. Sarjas oli kolm T. Gehlhaari enda joonistatud vaadet, kuus lehte reprodutseerisid Johannes Hau guaššmaale ja kolm gravüüri vahendasid Karl Ferdinand von Kügelgeni seepiajoonistusi või maale. 1832/33 ilmus T. Gehlhaari koostatud/teostatud ja G. Eggersi kaubastatud, kuid anonüümselt ilmunud 12 lehest koosnev nn tušimaneeris akvatintasari. 1833–35 tegi Gehlhaar ka üksiklehtedena Tallinna ja selle ümbruse vaateid, samuti 1835 akvatintatehnikas Riia vaadete sarja. U 1840 litografeeris Georg Friedrich Schlater Tartus värviliselt 12-lehelise T. Gehlhaari etnograafilise sarja „Iseloomulikke stseene Eesti- ja Liivimaa talupoegade elust”. U 1850 teostas T. Gehlhaar 10 litograafiast koosneva Tallinna vaadete sarja (kirjastaja F. Kluge) jt üksiklehti (litograaf F. J. Tempeltey). T. Gehlhaari on loonud ka õli- ja guaššmaale.
artists.ben: A Baltic German printmaker, painter and pharmacist. He was born as the son of a pharmacist of Swiss origin who was also a town councillor of Limbaži; his mother was the daughter of a local pastor. In 1828 Gehlhaar passed the examination for pharmacist's assistant at the University of Tartu, and in 1828, as an external candidate, the examination for pharmacist. In 1834 he became the owner of his father's pharmacy in Limbaži. He presumably studied at the drawing school of the University of Tartu under C. A. Senff, but as an artist he was mainly self-taught. In 1828 he published in Tallinn the first series of view prints in aquatint technique, published by Georg Eggers. The series included three views drawn by T. Gehlhaar himself, six sheets reproduced gouache paintings by Johannes Hau, and three engravings rendered sepia drawings or paintings by Karl Ferdinand von Kügelgen. In 1832/33 there appeared, compiled/executed by T. Gehlhaar and marketed by G. Eggers but published anonymously, a series of 12 sheets in the so-called ink-manner aquatint technique. In 1833–35 Gehlhaar also made individual sheets with views of Tallinn and its surroundings, as well as, in 1835, a series of views of Riga in aquatint technique. Around 1840 Georg Friedrich Schlater lithographed in colour in Tartu T. Gehlhaar's 12-sheet ethnographic series "Characteristic Scenes from the Life of the Peasants of Estonia and Livonia". Around 1850 T. Gehlhaar executed a series of 10 lithographs of views of Tallinn (publisher F. Kluge) and other individual sheets (lithographer F. J. Tempeltey). T. Gehlhaar has also created oil and gouache paintings.

artists.wdesc: Italian engraver active in Antwerp and France (1520-1582)

artists.b: 1901 - 1903 esimesed kunstiõpingud Gabriele Edelmanni juures Liibaris, umb. 1904 - Wieni Naiskunstnike Akadeemias, 1904 - 1908 Müncheni naiskunstnike ühingu juures asuvas Naisakadeemias prof. Max Feldbauer ja Franz Marci juures. Samuti tarbekunsti v. Debschitze ja prof. v. Berlepschi juures.
artists.ben: 1901–1903 first art studies under Gabriele Edelmann in Liibar, c. 1904 at the Vienna Women Artists' Academy, 1904–1908 at the Women's Academy attached to the Munich Women Artists' Association under Prof. Max Feldbauer and Franz Marc. Also applied art under v. Debschitz and Prof. v. Berlepsch.

artists.b: Painter and video artist of the precarious artist's life, in deadpan Russian-Estonian.
artists.ben:
Alexei Gordin (1989) is mainly known as a painter, however, he also works with photography, video and performance. Using black humour, Gordin draws attention to the absurdity of the (art) world and alienation, highlighting issues like inequality and the difficulties of marginalised groups. Gordin's work is influenced by caricatures and combines text and pictures, referring to comics and meme culture.

Gordin began exhibiting at the beginning of the 2010s. In his solo show “March 1989. August 2014” (Tallinn City Gallery, 2014), Gordin looked at the hidden side of post-soviet societies and its palpable presence in Eastern Europe today, using the medium of photography. Raised in Tomsk, Russia, he has applied his experience in many of his works to make visible what it is like to live in a transitional society. Another well known work is “Artist picking through the trash” (Y-gallery, 2014), where he analysed the relationship of making art and poverty. Artworks he created during the project were funded by money the artist earned by collecting empty bottles. He also documented it on video, suggesting this could be an alternative way to fund culture.

In the 2015 solo exhibition “Forever not ready” at Draakoni gallery, Gordin presented paintings that could be interpreted as an ironic commentary on the functioning of the art world. He continued with the same theme in several of his painting series presented at solo exhibitions “Art Is Not Just Fun Anymore” (Tartu Art House, 2017) and “I remained silent” (Kogo Gallery, 2018). In his work Gordin creates caricatures of the art world, with its galleries, fairs and white cubes, where artists are often the underdogs. The atmosphere of the works is often depressing, and the characters alienated from society, the frustrating images are accompanied by text akin to comic strips.

In 2019 Gordin exhibited his so-called second hand paintings at the culture club Tempel in Pärnu. The artist used old paintings and added ironic messages that once again played with stereotypes of the art world. By using found paintings the artist questions the value of artworks and the mechanisms of the art world.

artists.b: Greenberg oli eesti maalikunstnik, kelle ajastu kunstisuundi järgiv looming läbis pika stiililise arengu. 1920. aastate lõpul valminud maalid on ekspressiivsed, väljenduslikkust lisava  krobelise tekstuuriga.  1930. aastatel oli Greenberg mõjutatud art deco’st, milles värvikäsitlus rõhutab vormide plastilisust. Sama aastakümne keskpaigas helenes Greenbergi koloriit impressionismi mõjutusel ning teda hakkas köitma teatrimaailm – näitlejate omapärane võlu ja naiste poeetilise nukrusega tepitud sarm. II maailmasõja ajal lisandusid tema loomingusse mure, leina ja traagika, mille väljendamiseks kasutas kunstnik klassikalisi lahendusi. Kunstihariduse omandas Greenberg Tallinnas Ants Laikmaa ateljeekoolis, Berliinis kunsttööstuskooli õhtukursustel, Münchenis A. Ažbe kunstikoolis, H. Groeberi ateljees ning Müncheni Kunstiakadeemias. Hiljem töötas õppejõuna Jaan Koorti nimelises Riigi Rakenduskunsti Koolis ja Tallinna Riiklikus Tarbekunsti Instituudis.
artists.ben: Greenberg was an Estonian painter whose work, following the artistic trends of the era, underwent a long stylistic development. The paintings created at the end of the 1920s are expressive, with a rough texture that adds expressiveness. In the 1930s Greenberg was influenced by art deco, in which the treatment of colour emphasises the plasticity of forms. In the middle of the same decade Greenberg's colouring lightened under the influence of impressionism, and he became fascinated by the world of theatre – the peculiar charm of actors and the charm of women quilted with poetic melancholy. During World War II, worry, grief and tragedy were added to his work, which the artist expressed using classical solutions. Greenberg received his art education at Ants Laikmaa's studio school in Tallinn, at the evening courses of the school of applied arts in Berlin, at A. Ažbe's art school in Munich, in H. Groeber's studio, and at the Munich Academy of Art. Later he worked as a lecturer at the Jaan Koort State School of Applied Art and at the Tallinn State Art Institute.

artists.b: Kunstihariduse sai isa, Stuttgardi õukonnakunstniku ja Ludwigsburgi maaligalerii hoidja Johann Friedrich Groothi juures. Töötas Dresdenis, Danzigis ja Prahas. Tuli Eestimaa kindralkuberneri W. von Loewendaeli kutsel Tallinna ja siirdus siit edasi Peterburi, kus temast sai õukonnakunstnik valitsejanna Anna Leopoldovna ja pärast 1741. a. keisrinna Jelizaveta Petrovna juures. Osales 1742 koos L. Caravaque'i ja I. Vinjakoviga Moskvas Jelizaveta kroonimispidustuste dekoreerimisel. Oli alates 1743 keiserliku kunstikogu hoidja ja restauraator, tegeles ka selle täiendamisega. Alates 1743. a. töötas Venemaal ka tema vend, animalist Johann Friedrich Grooth (1717-1801).
artists.ben: He received his art education from his father, the Stuttgart court artist and keeper of the Ludwigsburg painting gallery, Johann Friedrich Grooth. He worked in Dresden, Danzig and Prague. He came to Tallinn at the invitation of the Governor-General of Estland, W. von Loewendael, and moved on from there to St. Petersburg, where he became court artist to Regent Anna Leopoldovna and, after 1741, to Empress Yelizaveta Petrovna. In 1742, together with L. Caravaque and I. Vishnyakov, he took part in decorating Moscow for Yelizaveta's coronation festivities. From 1743 he was keeper and restorer of the imperial art collection, and was also involved in expanding it. From 1743 his brother, the animal painter Johann Friedrich Grooth (1717-1801), also worked in Russia.

artists.b: Akstratehnika - see tehnika leiutati Viljandis. Akstrakunsti viljelemist alustati 1970. a. II poolel A. Grossi juhendamisel nn. "Akstra" stuudios. Akstratehnika oli A. Grossi enda välja mõeldud. Tehnika peamisteks komponentideks oli emailvärv (kunstniku omavalmistatud koostisega, mida ta teistele ei avaldanud) ja lahjendatud bituumen. Heledat emailvärvi ja tumedat bituumenit kasutati siiditrüki põhimõttel, kuid siidiraami asemel oli trafarett. Need osad, mis trafareti alla ei jäänud, tuli kinni katta, pulverisaatori abil emailvärviga üle lasta ja siis emailvärv omakorda bituumeniseguga üle katta. Tulemuseks oli süsimust plaat. Edasi tuli oodata reaktsiooni, mis sarnanes foto ilmutamisega. Need kohad, mis olid kinni kaetud, läksid tumedaks, bituumeni alla jäänud hele emailvärv hakkas omakorda reageerima – bituumenist läbi pressima, aegamisi moodustus reaktsiooni tulemusena soovitud pilt. Selletaolise tehnika tulemuseks oli akvarellilaadne ebamääraste ja teravate piirjoontega veidi saladuslik maal. Seda tehnikat sai teostada kahe värviga.
artists.ben: The Akstra technique - this technique was invented in Viljandi. The cultivation of Akstra art began in the second half of the 1970s under the guidance of A. Gross in the so-called "Akstra" studio. The Akstra technique was A. Gross's own invention. The main components of the technique were enamel paint (of a composition made by the artist himself, which he did not reveal to others) and diluted bitumen. Light enamel paint and dark bitumen were used on the principle of silkscreen printing, but instead of a silk frame a stencil was used. The parts that did not fall under the stencil had to be covered over, sprayed over with enamel paint using an atomiser, and then the enamel paint in turn had to be covered over with the bitumen mixture. The result was a pitch-black plate. Next one had to wait for a reaction, which resembled the developing of a photograph. The places that had been covered turned dark, while the light enamel paint left under the bitumen began, in turn, to react - pressing through the bitumen, and gradually, as a result of the reaction, the desired image was formed. The result of this kind of technique was a somewhat mysterious, watercolour-like painting with vague and sharp outlines. This technique could be executed with two colours.

artists.b: Kunstnik Albert Gulk sündis 1969. aastal Antslas. Lõpetas 1996. aastal Tartu Ülikooli maaliosakonna. On töötanud Tartu Lastekunstikoolis õpetajana, hetkel vabakutseline. Osaleb näitustel alates 1988. aastast. Samal aastal asutas koos Ilmar Kruusamäe, Peeter Alliku ja Priit Pangsepaga Tartus Kursi koolkonna. Kuulub Eesti Kunstnike Liitu alates 1995. aastast. Albert Gulki töid iseloomustab isikupärane joonistuslaad, kus ta juhindub monumentaalkunsti ja pannooliku esituslaadi reeglitest. Kunstiteadlane Eha Komissarov on öelnud, et Gulki töötamislaadi kindlus ja veenvus tõstsid ta koheselt eesti joonistuse esiridadesse. Albert Gulki algupärast taidurlikkust toonitab fakt, et kunstnik ei kasuta oma joonistustes modelli ega foto abi ja toetub üksnes oma visuaalse mälu kujunditele.
artists.ben: Artist Albert Gulk was born in 1969 in Antsla. In 1996 he graduated from the painting department of the University of Tartu. He has worked as a teacher at the Tartu Children's Art School, currently a freelance artist. He has taken part in exhibitions since 1988. In the same year, together with Ilmar Kruusamäe, Peeter Allik and Priit Pangsepp, he founded the Kursi school in Tartu. He has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1995. Albert Gulk's works are characterised by a distinctive drawing style, in which he follows the rules of monumental art and the panel-like manner of presentation. Art historian Eha Komissarov has said that the certainty and conviction of Gulk's working manner immediately raised him into the front ranks of Estonian drawing. Albert Gulk's original artistry is underlined by the fact that the artist uses neither a model nor the help of a photograph in his drawings, relying solely on the images of his visual memory.

artists.b: Põgenes ööl vastu 19.09.1944 koos 12 kaaslasega sakslastelt varastatud päästepaadiga aerutades Rootsi. Pärast seda külastas esmakordselt Kuressaaret mais 1986, seejärel veel 1991. Eestis käis ka 1970 ja 1977.
artists.ben: He fled on the night of 19.09.1944 together with 12 companions to Sweden, rowing a rescue boat stolen from the Germans. Afterwards he first visited Kuressaare in May 1986, then again in 1991. He also visited Estonia in 1970 and 1977.

artists.b: Voldemar HAAS (1898, Tori – 1982, Tallinn) oli eesti teatrikunstnik ja pedagoog, kes on eesti lavakujundust rikastanud paljude tehniliste uuendustega (ringhorisont, projektsiooni- ja pilveaparaadid). Oli 1920. aastatel viljakas maastiku- ja 1970. aastatel linnavaatemaalija. Kunstihariduse omandas Haas Ado Vabbe ja Konrad Mägi juures Pallase kunstikoolis ning Tartu Ülikoolis joonistusõpetaja erialal. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
artists.ben: Voldemar HAAS (1898, Tori – 1982, Tallinn) was an Estonian theatre artist and pedagogue who enriched Estonian stage design with many technical innovations (cyclorama horizon, projection and cloud apparatuses). He was a prolific landscape painter in the 1920s and a painter of cityscapes in the 1970s. Haas received his art education under Ado Vabbe and Konrad Mägi at the Pallas Art School and studied drawing pedagogy at the University of Tartu. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.

artists.b: 1912 astus Tallinna Eesti Kunstiseltsi joonistuskursustele, mis nimetati 1914. aastal Tallinna Kunsttööstuskooliks, õppis ka Nikolai Triigi ateljeekoolis kuni 1917. aastani, mil mobiliseeriti sõjaväkke. 1916 sai temast Eesti Kunstiseltsi liige ning 1917 kunstirühmituse Vikerla liige. Aastatel 1918–1921 töötas ta Paldiski reaalgümnaasiumis joonistusõpetajana. 1920. aastal asus Haavamägi elama Haapsallu, kus töötas Läänemaa ühisgümnaasiumis joonistus- ja kunstiajaloo õpetajana ning seejärel vabakutselise kunstnikuna.
artists.wdesc: Estonian sculptor, painter and graphic artist (1891-1964)
artists.ben: In 1912 he entered the drawing courses of the Estonian Art Society in Tallinn, which in 1914 were renamed the Tallinn School of Applied Art, and also studied at Nikolai Triik's studio school until 1917, when he was mobilised into the army.
