In 1916 he became a member of the Estonian Art Society, and in 1917 a member of the art group Vikerla. In 1918–1921 he worked as a drawing teacher at the Paldiski Realgymnasium. In 1920 Haavamägi settled in Haapsalu, where he worked as a teacher of drawing and art history at the Läänemaa joint gymnasium, and thereafter as a freelance artist.

artists.b: A. M. Hagen sündis Vijciemsis Liivimaal (tänap. Läti) mõisarentniku pojana. Õppis Cesise kreiskoolis ja Karl August Senffi ateljees Tartus (olles ka abiline), reisis 1820-1823 Saksamaal ja Šveitsis. 1826 oli kubermangugümnaasiumi ja 1826-1832 tütarlaste gümnaasiumi kunstiõpetaja ning 1838-1851 Tartu ülikooli joonistuskooli juhataja. Vene keisri tellimusel tegi sarja Soome saarte vaatemaale (C.D. Friedrichi mõjudega), sai 1837 Peterburi kunstiakadeemia liikme ja vabakunstniku nimetuse. Läks pensionile 1851, aga alates 1855 tegeles fotograafiaga Tartus.
artists.ben: A. M. Hagen was born in Vijciems in Livonia (present-day Latvia) as the son of a manor leaseholder. He studied at the Cēsis district school and in Karl August Senff's studio in Tartu (also working as his assistant), and travelled to Germany and Switzerland in 1820–1823. In 1826 he was an art teacher at the provincial gymnasium and in 1826–1832 at the girls' gymnasium, and in 1838–1851 he headed the drawing school of the University of Tartu. Commissioned by the Russian Emperor, he made a series of views of the Finnish islands (with influences of C. D. Friedrich), and in 1837 received the title of member and free artist of the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. He retired in 1851, but from 1855 engaged in photography in Tartu.

artists.b: Sündinud 27.10.1824, Tartumaa; surnud 20.10.1902.
artists.ben: Born 27.10.1824, Tartumaa; died 20.10.1902.

artists.b: 1955 valmis täisfiguur tollasest primaballeriinist Helmi Puurist. Ka järgnevatel aastakümnetel pühendus Erika Haggi peamiselt eesti kultuuriisiksuste portreteerimisele. Tema loomingust meenuvad põhjamaisest graniidist August Jansen, Heino Eller, Tiit Kuusik ning Georg Otsa juubeliaastal 1977 Estonia fuajees avatud graniitbüst. Samuti on ta portreteerinud nimekaid sportlasi. Portreeloomingu kõrval huvitas skulptorit ka dekoratiivne žanr. Tema dekoratiivloomingust võiks esmalt nimetada Tallinna Kunstihoone esist haljasala kaunistavat tumedat graniittorsot “Meremehe pruut”.
artists.ben: In 1955 he completed a full-figure statue of the then prima ballerina Helmi Puur. In the following decades, too, Erika Haggi dedicated herself mainly to portraying Estonian cultural figures. From her oeuvre one recalls the Nordic-granite works August Jansen, Heino Eller, Tiit Kuusik, and the granite bust of Georg Ots unveiled in the foyer of Estonia in his jubilee year 1977. She has also portrayed well-known athletes. Alongside portraiture, the sculptor was also interested in the decorative genre. Among her decorative works, one might first mention the dark granite torso "The Sailor's Bride", which adorns the green area in front of the Tallinn Art Hall.

artists.b: 1928 siirdus Halliste Tallinna, kus töötas aasta jagu Jaan Koorti ateljees, õppides seal keraamikat ning pronksivalu. Koorti juurest lahkudes hakkas Halliste elatist teenima mööblidetailide valmistamise ning klaverivabrikule ornamentide graveerimisega. Oli Eesti Muuseumi Ühingu, Eesti Kujutavate Kunstnikkude Keskühingu juhatuse liige, Kujutava Kunsti Sihtkapitali Valitsuse liige ning Tallinna Kunstihoone ehituskomisjoni ning juhatuse liige. 1930. aastatel avanes kunstnikul võimalus täiendada end reisidega Venemaale, Soome, Itaaliasse, Prantsusmaale ja Saksamaale. II maailmasõja ajal elas kunstnik tagasitõmbununa, suviti viibis ta koos abikaasaga Pupastveres. Pärast sõja lõppu töötas skuptor mõnda aega Riikliku Kunstimuuseumi restauraatorina. Sõjajärgsed aastad olid kunstniku loomingus kõige viljakamad, põhiliseks töökohaks oli ateljee Lauristini tänavas Tallinnas.
artists.ben: In 1928 Halliste moved to Tallinn, where he worked for a year in Jaan Koort's studio, studying ceramics and bronze casting there. After leaving Koort he began earning his living by making furniture parts and engraving ornaments for a piano factory. He was a board member of the Estonian Museum Society, of the Central Union of Estonian Fine Artists, a member of the Board of the Fine Arts Foundation, and a member of the building committee and board of the Tallinn Art Hall. In the 1930s the artist had the opportunity to further his training through trips to Russia, Finland, Italy, France and Germany. During World War II the artist lived withdrawn from society; in the summers he stayed with his wife in Pupastvere. After the war ended the sculptor worked for some time as a restorer at the State Art Museum. The post-war years were the most productive in the artist's oeuvre; his main workplace was a studio on Lauristini Street in Tallinn.

artists.b: H. E. Hartmann õppis kunsti Tartus A.M.Hageni juures, Düsseldorfi kunstiakadeemias ja Münchenis. 1841–44 töötas ta Lätis Bērzaines kooliõpetajana, aastast 1845 Tartus joonistusõpetajana ja linnakassa raamatupidajana. 1845 sai Peterburi kunstiakadeemialt vabakunstniku nimetuse, aastast 1860 oli Õpetatud Eesti Seltsi kogude konservaator. Maalis portreid ja maastikke, eriti oluline on ta Estica- teemaline graafika. Hartmanni puulõiked eestlastest ilmusid väljaannetes: Talurahva Postimees, Tartu Postimees, Das Inland (saksa k), Pasaule (läti k) jm.
artists.ben: H. E. Hartmann studied art in Tartu under A. M. Hagen, at the Düsseldorf Academy of Arts and in Munich. In 1841–44 he worked in Latvia as a schoolteacher in Bērzaine, from 1845 in Tartu as a drawing teacher and city treasury accountant. In 1845 he received the title of free artist from the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts, and from 1860 he was conservator of the collections of the Learned Estonian Society. He painted portraits and landscapes, but especially significant is his Estica-themed graphic art. Hartmann's woodcuts of Estonians appeared in the publications: Talurahva Postimees, Tartu Postimees, Das Inland (in German), Pasaule (in Latvian), etc.

artists.b: Õppinud maalriametit, saabus G. F. Schlater 1828 Riiast Tartusse, kus asutas 1832. aastal litograafiatöökoja. Peale olulise tegevuse graafika alal tegutses oli ka maalikunstnik ning Tartu gümnaasiumi ja veterinaarinstituudi joonistusõpetaja. 1857 müüs oma litograafiapressi Louis Höflingerile ja hakkas fotograafiks.
artists.wdesc: Baltic German painter and graphic artist (1807-1888)
artists.ben: Having studied the painter's craft, G. F. Schlater arrived in Tartu from Riga in 1828, where in 1832 he founded a lithography workshop. In addition to his significant activity in the field of graphic art, he was also a painter and a drawing teacher at the Tartu gymnasium and the veterinary institute. In 1857 he sold his lithography press to Louis Höflinger and became a photographer.

artists.b: Woldemar Hau õppis oma isa ja Carl Ferdinand von Kügelgeni juures, lõpetas 1836 Peterburi kunstiakadeemia ja täiendas end pärast seda Saksamaal ning Itaalias. 1842 sai keiserlikuks õukonnakunstnikuks ja 1849 akadeemikuks. Oli Venemaa üks olulisemaid akvarellportreede meistreid.
artists.ben: Woldemar Hau studied with his father and with Carl Ferdinand von Kügelgen, graduated from the Petersburg Academy of Arts in 1836, and afterwards furthered his education in Germany and Italy. In 1842 he became an Imperial Court artist and in 1849 an academician. He was one of Russia's most important masters of watercolour portraits.

artists.b: Inga Heamägi (s. 1961 Viljandis) on lõpetanud Tallinna Kunstiülikooli graafika eriala. Ta on Eesti Vabagraafikute Ühenduse liige ning Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige. Isiknäitustega esinenud Eestis, Lätis, Soomes.
artists.ben: Inga Heamägi (b. 1961 in Viljandi) has graduated from Tallinna Kunstiülikool, majoring in graphic art. She is a member of the Eesti Vabagraafikute Ühendus and a member of the Eesti Kunstnike Liit. She has held solo exhibitions in Estonia, Latvia, Finland.

artists.b: Täiendas end  aastatel 1929–1930 Reimsis Institut Spécial de Peinture Décorative de Reimsis, mille lõpetas kuldmedaliga ja Pariisis École Nationale des Arts Décoratifsis, Académie Ransonis ja Conservatoire Nationale des Arts e Métiers's.
artists.ben: He/she furthered his/her studies in 1929–1930 in Reims at the Institut Spécial de Peinture Décorative de Reims, which he/she completed with a gold medal, and in Paris at the École Nationale des Arts Décoratifs, the Académie Ranson and the Conservatoire Nationale des Arts et Métiers.

artists.b: Mirjam Hinn (snd 1990) on lõpetanud Tartu Ülikooli maalikunsti õppetooli MA (2018) ja Tartu Kõrgema Kunstikooli (2014). Kunstiõpinguid alustas aastal 2010 Tartu Kunstikoolis. Tal on olnud mitmeid isikunäituseid, neist viimane “Hõljuvad perspektiivid”(2022) Itaalias, Montesarchios, varasemad peamiselt kodulinnas Tartus, näiteks “Tardunud helid” Tartu Kunstimajas (2018), “Kõrgepinge” Tartu Kunstimuuseumis (2019) ja “Tuhandesilmne saar” Tartu Kunstimajas (2021). Aktiivselt ühisäitustel osalemisega alustas 2011. aastal, esmalt Eestis, seejärel ka Soomes, Leedus, Itaalias ning Saksamaal. Dünaamilise ja abstraktse kujundikeelega maalikunstniku loomingus on saanud äratuntavaks värvipalett ning puhtad värvipinnad vastandumas pintslitõmbeis vonklevate pindadega. Kirkad ja kohati ebamaiselt tehislikud toonid, mis lausa helendavad, on saanud teoste kandvaks aktsendiks. Hinn on oma näitustel tihti ühendanud maalikunsti meediumi ka valguse installatsiooni ja helikunstiga, luues kogu näitusesaali ja erinevaid meeli hõlmavaid isikunäituseid. Tema varasema loomingu fookuses on olnud peamiselt heli ja valguse nähtused ja nende isiklik tõlgendus värvi ja kujundi keelde. Näitus “.
artists.ben: Mirjam Hinn (b. 1990) has completed an MA in painting at the University of Tartu (2018) and graduated from the Tartu Art College (2014). She began her art studies in 2010 at the Tartu Art School. She has held several solo exhibitions, the most recent of which, "Hõljuvad perspektiivid" (2022), was in Montesarchio, Italy; earlier ones were mainly in her home town of Tartu, for example "Tardunud helid" at the Tartu Art House (2018), "Kõrgepinge" at the Tartu Art Museum (2019) and "Tuhandesilmne saar" at the Tartu Art House (2021). She began actively participating in joint exhibitions in 2011, first in Estonia, then also in Finland, Lithuania, Italy and Germany. In the work of this painter, characterised by a dynamic and abstract visual language, a recognisable colour palette has emerged, along with clean fields of colour contrasted with surfaces winding with brushstrokes. Bright and at times unearthly artificial tones, which seem to glow, have become the defining accent of the works. Hinn has often, in her exhibitions, combined the medium of painting with light installation and sound art, creating solo exhibitions that encompass the whole exhibition hall and different senses. Her earlier work has focused mainly on the phenomena of sound and light and their personal translation into the language of colour and form. The exhibition "

artists.b: Õppis maalikunsti Viinis ja Roomas. Alates 1820 töötas Peterburis ja alates 1849 Tallinnas portretisti ja joonistusõpetajana. Loonud ka eestlaste portreid ning 8 vihku kivitrükiportreid Vene riigitegelastest, teadlastest ja kunstnikest ("Les contemporains", alates 1822, venekeelne väljaanne 1828) vararealismi e. biidermeierliku realismi vaimus (artiklite kogumik "Neli baltisaksa kunstnikku", Tallinn 1994, näituse kataloog "Vene valitsejad", Tallinn 2006)
artists.ben: Studied painting in Vienna and Rome. From 1820 worked in Petersburg and from 1849 in Tallinn as a portraitist and drawing teacher. Also created portraits of Estonians and 8 volumes of lithographic portraits of Russian statesmen, scholars and artists ("Les contemporains", from 1822, Russian-language edition 1828) in the spirit of early realism, i.e. Biedermeier realism (collection of articles "Four Baltic German Artists", Tallinn 1994, exhibition catalogue "Russian Rulers", Tallinn 2006)

grp: school:Saint Petersburg Stieglitz State Academy of Art and Design

artists.b: 1922 tuli Eestisse, kus töötas algul saeveskis lihttöölisena, hiljem joonestajana põllumajandusministeeriumis ja joonistajana tekstiilivabrikus. Illustreeris raamatuid ja kujundas teatridekoratsioone ning postkaarte. Osales kohalikes vene kirjandusühingutes.
artists.ben: In 1922 he came to Estonia, where he initially worked as an unskilled laborer at a sawmill, later as a draftsman at the Ministry of Agriculture and as a draughtsman at a textile factory. He illustrated books and designed theatre sets and postcards. He took part in local Russian literary societies.

artists.b: Sündinud 05.02.1851, Tartu; surnud 03.03.1912. Haridus: Sai maalikunsti alal Tartus algteadmisi K. von Kügelgenilt ja litograafia alal C. A. Shulzi töökojas. Jätkas õpinguid 1872–77 Düsseldorfi Kunstiakadeemias, sealhulgas 1874 E. von Gebhradti ja aastast 1875 E. Dückeri juures. Tegi õpimatku Vestfaali, Reini ülemjooksule ja Põhjamere saartele. Õppis lühikest aega Pariisis.
artists.ben: Born 05.02.1851, Tartu; died 03.03.1912. Education: Received basic knowledge in painting in Tartu from K. von Kügelgen and in lithography in C. A. Shulz's workshop. Continued studies 1872-77 at the Düsseldorf Academy of Art, including in 1874 with E. von Gebhardt and from 1875 with E. Dücker. Made study trips to Westphalia, the upper reaches of the Rhine and the North Sea islands. Studied briefly in Paris.

artists.wdesc: English painter, printmaker, pictorial satirist, social critic and editorial cartoonist (1697-1764)

artists.b: 1862-64  Birkenruh maakonnagümnaasiumi õpetaja (Cesise lähedal)1864. aastast  Kuressaare progümnaasiumi (1865 - gümnaasiumi) vanade keelte ja saksa kirjanduse ülemõpetaja. Aktiivse ühiskonnategelasena võttis õpetaja juhtivalt osa linnapargi rajamisest, hoiukassa loomisest, tuletõrjeühingu asutamisest.Suurimad on Holzmayeri teened muististeuurijana. Tema juhatusel korraldati arheoloogilisi väljakaevamisi Kaarma maalinnal, Pöide ordulinuses jne. Tänu tema tegevusele olid Saaremaa ja Muhumaa 19. sajandi teisel poolel arheoloogiliselt üheks paremini uuritud alaks Baltimail.Saaremaa Uurimise Seltsi (Verein zur Kunde Oesels) asutajaliige, seltsi viitsepresident ja muuseumi juhataja  1867-1890.
artists.ben: 1862-64 teacher at the Birkenruh county gymnasium (near Cesis). From 1864 senior teacher of ancient languages and German literature at the Kuressaare progymnasium (from 1865 - gymnasium). As an active public figure, the teacher took a leading part in the establishment of the town park, the founding of a savings bank, and the establishment of a fire brigade society. Holzmayer's greatest merits are as a researcher of antiquities. Under his direction archaeological excavations were carried out at the Kaarma hill fort, the Pöide Order castle, etc. Thanks to his activity, Saaremaa and Muhumaa were, in the second half of the 19th century, one of the archaeologically best-studied areas in the Baltic provinces. Founding member of the Society for the Study of Saaremaa (Verein zur Kunde Oesels), vice-president of the society and curator of the museum 1867-1890.

artists.b: Geboren im Gouvernement Orjol. Studierte Kriegswissenschaften an der Universität Dorpat und gleichzeitig das Zeichnen bei K. A. Senff. 1827 bewarb er sich um die Stelle des Zeichenlehrers an der Universität Åbo. Er schickte Probezeichnungen dorthin und wurde auch angenommen, trat jedoch die Stelle in Åbo nicht an. Lebte in Dorpat bis 1841. Von Zeit zu Zeit beschäftigte sich mit der Kunst, vor allem mit dem Porträt. Lebte nachmals in Moskau und Tbilisi.
artists.ben: Geboren im Gouvernement Orjol. Studierte Kriegswissenschaften an der Universität Dorpat und gleichzeitig das Zeichnen bei K. A. Senff. 1827 bewarb er sich um die Stelle des Zeichenlehrers an der Universität Åbo. Er schickte Probezeichnungen dorthin und wurde auch angenommen, trat jedoch die Stelle in Åbo nicht an. Lebte in Dorpat bis 1841. Von Zeit zu Zeit beschäftigte sich mit der Kunst, vor allem mit dem Porträt. Lebte nachmals in Moskau und Tbilisi.

artists.b: OLI Algul moelehejoonistaja ja humor. illustr. autor. lÕI Ka anat.-joonised Iinimese ja hobuse anatoomia atlasele. Viljeles hiljem litot, oforti ja puugravüüri, samuti akv. ja külmnõela eri töötlusmeetodeid. Ta on loonud palju tarbegraafikat, eriti ekslbr., aga ka portreid, akte, interjööre jm.
artists.ben: Was initially a fashion-magazine illustrator and author of humorous illustrations. Also created anatomical drawings for an atlas of human and horse anatomy. Later practised lithography, etching and woodcut, as well as various techniques of watercolour and drypoint. He has created much applied graphic art, especially ex libris, but also portraits, nudes, interiors, etc.

artists.b: 1857-1875 Tartus tegutsenud litograaf, fotograaf ja ärimees, pärit Saksamaalt. 1857 omandas endise G. F. Schlateri litograafiatöökoja Tartus. Andis välja Tartu vaategraafikat ja muid trükiseid, valmistas portreid ja grupipilte, rakendas palju fotolitograafiat. L. Höflingeri fotoateljee asus Tartus, Promenaadi tänaval (Sukoffsky majas).
artists.ben: A lithographer, photographer and businessman active in Tartu from 1857-1875, originally from Germany. In 1857 he acquired the former G. F. Schlater lithography workshop in Tartu. He published views of Tartu and other prints, produced portraits and group pictures, and made much use of photolithography. L. Höflinger's photography studio was located in Tartu, on Promenaadi Street (in the Sukoffsky house).

artists.wdesc: Flemish painter, engraver, poet and playwright (1584–1635)
Estonian graphic artist and photo artist (born 1952)

artists.ben:
Mihkel Ilus, view to exhibition "Up to a Point" with Árpád Forgó, curated by Gábor Pintér at Klaipėda Culture Communication Center (KKKC), 2024. Photo by: Gediminas Sass

Mihkel Ilus (1987) is visual artist, who works in the expanded field of painting. Often, he makes large installations to which a painterly approach is central. An important part of his oeuvre is made up of an intertwining critical approach to contemporary exhibition culture and performance art. Lately, he has been focusing on the effect of object-based art in the settings of the black box and white cube.

One of his first painting-critical exhibitions was “Robusto” (2013), in which he exhibited constructive architectonic objects, from which expressive canvas surfaces were robustiously clinging on. Seldom aesthetic methods and similar treatment of canvas was continued in the series “First Method” (2014), in which Ilus experimented with ornamental and other decorative intentions on stripped frames.

His master thesis’ project “Outlet Workspace” (2015) progressed from the surface of the canvas by exhibiting a voluminous installation made of fluorescent lamps. The found-situationist work, derived from the former factory’s conditions and material memory, followed the same compositional notions as tension, rhythm, figure, surface, contour, which are used for describing a painting, allowing to understand “painting” and “painterly” much more freely.

artists.b: Sergei Inkatov sündis 1971 Bakuus, õppis Bakuu Kunstide Koolis 1987-1989, Bakuu Azim Zade kunstikoolis 1989-1992, Venetsianovi nimelises kunstikoolis 1994. Elab Tallinnas. Tunnustused: 2006 Diploma of Excellence, Global Art Annual, London, Suurbritannia; 2010 „Cultural Propety” fondi laureaat, Venemaa; 2011 Tallinn-Euroopa pealinn, kunstikonkurssi laureaat; 2017 Mondial Academia liige, Prantsusmaa; 2017 Saadik Mondial Academiast Eestis; 2017 Kuldmedal „Prix international des Galeries” abstraktse maali kategoorias, Prantsusmaa; 2019 1. koht konkursil „Artweeks France” Miramas; 2019 Kuldmedal „Prix international des Galeries“ abstraktse maali kategoorias, Prantsusmaa. Alates 2020 Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Sergei Inkatov was born in 1971 in Baku, studied at the Baku Art School 1987–1989, at the Azim Zadeh Art School in Baku 1989–1992, and at the Venetsianov Art School in 1994. He lives in Tallinn. Recognitions: 2006 Diploma of Excellence, Global Art Annual, London, United Kingdom; 2010 laureate of the "Cultural Property" foundation, Russia; 2011 laureate of the Tallinn – European Capital of Culture art competition; 2017 member of the Mondial Academia, France; 2017 Mondial Academia Ambassador in Estonia; 2017 Gold Medal "Prix international des Galeries" in the category of abstract painting, France; 2019 1st place at the "Artweeks France" competition in Miramas; 2019 Gold Medal "Prix international des Galeries" in the category of abstract painting, France. Since 2020 member of the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.b: Eesti näitleja, lavastaja ja teatrijuht, õppis Tallinna linnakoolis, lõpetas 1916 eksternina Tallinna reaalkooli. Täiendas end 1908 Berliinis Emanuel Reicheri teatrikursustel, hiljem käis õppereisidel Peterburis, Pariisis ja Brüsselis. Oli 1899–1906 Tallinna ringkonnakohtus ja linnavalitsuses kantseleiametnik ning mängis Estonia asjaarmastajate näitetrupis ja 1906 ka Tallinna saksa teatris. Oli kutselise Estonia asutajaid (1906) ning lavastas ja mängis seal aastani 1914. Andis 1910 koos Theodor Altermanniga välja ajakirja Näitelava. Esines suvel 1913 Kieli Linnateatris ning 1914–15 Nižni Novgorodi, Kaasani, Samaara, Saratovi ja Moskva Nikitski teatris. Teenis 1915–20 sõjaväeametnikuna (kapten) Tallinnas, mängis ühtlasi Estonias ning oli 1918–21 Draamateatri komandant, näitleja ja lavastaja ja 1921–22 direktor. Töötas 1922–23, 1927–41 ja 1944–49 Estonias, asutas 1923 omanimelise Rahvateatri, juhtis seda aastani 1927. Mängis 1919–39 aeg‑ajalt ka Tallinna vene teatris, Endlas, Ugalas, Vanemuises, Narva Teatris ja Kuressaare Teatris. Mobiliseeriti reservohvitserina 1941 Punaarmeesse, kuulus 1942–44 Eesti NSV Riiklikesse Kunstiansamblitesse.
artists.ben: Estonian actor, director and theatre manager, studied at the Tallinn town school, graduated in 1916 as an external student from Tallinn Realschule. He furthered his education in 1908 at Emanuel Reicher's theatre courses in Berlin, later going on study trips to St Petersburg, Paris and Brussels. From 1899 to 1906 he was a clerical official at the Tallinn district court and city administration, and performed with the Estonia amateur theatre troupe, and in 1906 also at the Tallinn German Theatre. He was one of the founders of the professional Estonia theatre (1906) and directed and acted there until 1914. In 1910, together with Theodor Altermann, he published the journal Näitelava. He performed in the summer of 1913 at the Kiel City Theatre and in 1914–15 at the theatres of Nizhny Novgorod, Kazan, Samara, Saratov and the Nikitsky theatre in Moscow. From 1915–20 he served as a military official (captain) in Tallinn, while also performing at Estonia, and from 1918–21 was the commandant, actor and director of the Drama Theatre, and from 1921–22 its director. He worked at Estonia in 1922–23, 1927–41 and 1944–49, founded his eponymous People's Theatre in 1923, and led it until 1927. From 1919–39 he also occasionally performed at the Tallinn Russian Theatre, Endla, Ugala, Vanemuine, the Narva Theatre and the Kuressaare Theatre. He was mobilised as a reserve officer into the Red Army in 1941, and from 1942–44 belonged to the State Art Ensembles of the Estonian SSR.

artists.b: Töötanud vabakunstnikuna Tartus. Aastast 1950 KL-i liige. Loonud skulptuurportreid, viljelenud monumentaalkunsti, teinud pastellitehnikas lillemaale. Graafikas eelistanud värvilist monotüüpiat ja akvatintat. Näitused aastast 1951.
artists.ben: Worked as a freelance artist in Tartu. Member of the Estonian Artists' Union (EKL) from 1950. Created sculptural portraits, practised monumental art, made flower paintings in pastel technique. In graphic art, preferred colour monotype and aquatint. Exhibitions from 1951.

artists.b: Sündinud 31.01.1921, Tartu; surnud 18.09.2003.

Voldemar Vaga on oma “Eesti kunstis” (1940) väitnud, et kuigi Jansen on neid kunstnikke, kes “väsimatult töötavad enda kunstilise isiksuse ja võimete igakülgse väljakujundamise kallal”, ning kuigi tema “areng on kogu aeg käinud tõusuteed”, on ta “oma küpsemad ning huvitavaimad tööd loonud” just 1930ndate II poolel – eriti headeks peab Vaga kunstilise vormi tiheduse ja veenvuse poolest tema värskeid ja rõõmsailmelisi maastikke.
artists.ben: Voldemar Vaga has stated in his "Eesti kunst" (1940) that although Jansen is among those artists who "tirelessly work on the comprehensive development of their artistic personality and abilities," and although his "development has continually been on an upward path," he "created his most mature and interesting works" precisely in the second half of the 1930s – Vaga considers especially good, in terms of the density and persuasiveness of artistic form, his fresh and cheerful-looking landscapes.

artists.b: Ashot Jegikjan (s. 1955 Armeenias Jerevanis). Alates 1985 on Jegikjan vabakutseline kunstnik Eestis ning esineb regulaarselt isiku- ja grupinäitustega. Ta on illustreerinud ja kirjutanud raamatuid (“Kirjad Hamletile”-1994; “Kirjad Viinist”–1999) ning jutte ajakirjadele Vikerkaar, Sirp, Tallinn jm. 1997. aastast on Ashot Jegikjan Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Ashot Jegikjan (b. 1955 in Yerevan, Armenia). Since 1985 Jegikjan has been a freelance artist in Estonia and regularly takes part in solo and group exhibitions. He has illustrated and written books ("Kirjad Hamletile" [Letters to Hamlet] - 1994; "Kirjad Viinist" [Letters from Vienna] - 1999) and stories for the magazines Vikerkaar, Sirp, Tallinn, etc. Since 1997 Ashot Jegikjan has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.b: Andrei Jegorov elas 1887–1921 Peterburis. Kaotanud lapseeas kuulmise, õppis ta 1887–1896 Peterburi kurttummade koolis. 1898 astus Peterburi Kunstide Edendamise Seltsi joonistamiskooli. 1901–1909 õppis vabakuulajana Peterburi Kunstide Akadeemias Ilja Repini Täiendas end Münchenis Dmitri Kardovski ateljees. Seejärel asus tööle vabakunstnikuna. Oli 1919–1920 tsaariarmees Semjon Budjonnõi 1. ratsaarmee kunstnik. Opteerunud Eestisse, tegutses Tallinnas vabakunstnikuna. II maailmasõja ajal evakueerus NSV Liidu tagalasse.
grp: school:Higher Art School at the Imperial Academy of Arts
artists.ben: Andrei Jegorov lived in St. Petersburg from 1887 to 1921. Having lost his hearing in childhood, he studied from 1887 to 1896 at the St. Petersburg school for the deaf and mute. In 1898 he entered the drawing school of the St. Petersburg Society for the Encouragement of the Arts. From 1901 to 1909 he studied as an auditor at the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts under Ilya Repin. He furthered his training in Munich at Dmitri Kardovski's studio. He then began working as a freelance artist. In 1919–1920 he was an artist with Semyon Budyonny's 1st Cavalry Army in the tsarist army. Having opted for Estonian citizenship, he worked as a freelance artist in Tallinn. During the Second World War he was evacuated to the rear of the USSR.

artists.b: Tegutses tarbegraafiku, ajalehtede illustraatori ja karikaturistina, ka maalijana. Oli 1924–1932 reklaamikunstnik Tallinnas, 1941 "Soviet Estonia" karikaturist. II maailmasõja ajal viibis nõukogude tagalas Jaroslavlis ja osales Eesti Nõukogude Kunstnike Liidu asutamises, oli selle esimees 1962–1967. Töötas 1943–1946 ajalehe "Rahva Hääl" toimetuses ja 1945–1946 ajakirja "Pikker"  toimetuses. 1946–1950 oli Tallinna Riikliku Tarbekunsti Instituudi õppejõud, 1950–1962.

Vadim Jerohhin on sündinud 1962. aastal Kundas. Õppinud 2000- 2015. aastatel kunstiõpetust stuudios „Stupeni“ õpetaja Vladislav Kuznetsovi juures. Alates 2009 Eesti vene kunstnike ühenduse liige. Alates 2010 Narva kunstnike ühenduse „Vestervalli“ liige, alates 2017 juhatuse liige. Lisaks kahe kunstnike ühenduse „Kunsti Sadam“ ja „Symbol 4“ juhatuse liige. Kunsti Sadam on korraldanud 8 rahvusvahelist kunstilaagrit, 16 personaalnäitust ja ligi 200 grupinäitust nii Eestis kui välisriikides (Venemaa, Hiina, Italia, Prantsusmaa, Serbia, Slovakkia, USA)
artists.ben: Vadim Jerohhin was born in 1962 in Kunda. He studied art from 2000 to 2015 in the "Stupeni" studio under teacher Vladislav Kuznetsov. Since 2009 a member of the Association of Russian Artists in Estonia. Since 2010 a member of the Narva artists' association "Vestervalli", since 2017 a member of its board. He is also a board member of two artists' associations, "Kunsti Sadam" and "Symbol 4". Kunsti Sadam has organised 8 international art camps, 16 solo exhibitions and nearly 200 group exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad (Russia, China, Italy, France, Serbia, Slovakia, USA)

artists.b: Alates 1728 elas Narvas. 1730 abiellus Anna Margaretha Laudreriga/Lauterer/Lauter/Lauder. 1733 osales Narva Jaani kirikus enamike maalide uuendamisel (restaureerimine ?). Võeti Narva kodanikuks 1734.a.
artists.ben: From 1728 lived in Narva. In 1730 married Anna Margaretha Laudrer/Lauterer/Lauter/Lauder. In 1733 participated in the renewal of most of the paintings in Narva Jaani Church (restoration?). Was accepted as a citizen of Narva in 1734.

artists.b: 1933 kunstiühingu Pallas liige. Reisis 1934 ja 1935 NSVL-s, 1936-1937 täiendas end Vabrikantide Ühisuse stipendiaadina Berliinis, Pariisis ja Amsterdamis.
artists.ben: In 1933, member of the art association Pallas. Travelled in the USSR in 1934 and 1935, in 1936-1937 furthered his education as a scholarship holder of the Manufacturers' Association in Berlin, Paris and Amsterdam.

artists.b: Tiia Johannson oli meediakunstnik, õppejõud ja teadlane. Ta alustas akvarellisti ja maalijana. Teda on peetud üheks uusekspressionismi esindaja eesti 1980ndate aastate kunstis. 1990. aastast töötas ta peamiselt arvukate meediakunsti projektide kallal, mis käsitlesid videot, multimeediat ja infoühiskonna tehnoloogiaid.
artists.ben: Tiia Johannson was a media artist, lecturer and researcher. She began as a watercolourist and painter. She has been considered one of the representatives of neo-expressionism in Estonian art of the 1980s. From 1990 she worked mainly on numerous media art projects dealing with video, multimedia and information society technologies.

artists.b: Alustas Varssavis kaupmehena. Vasegraveerimist õppis hiljem Londonis, kujundas oma punktmaneeritehnika. Naasnud Varssavisse, graveeris portreid Poola aadlike ja kuningas Stanislaw August Poniatowski tellimusel. Sõitis 1793 Viini end täiendama, töötas Viinis, hiljem Münchenis, Leipzigis jm. Graveeris palju vanade meistrite ja kaasaegsete kunstnike maalide järgi.
artists.ben: He began as a merchant in Warsaw. He later studied copper engraving in London, developing his own stipple-engraving technique. Having returned to Warsaw, he engraved portraits of Polish noblemen and, commissioned by King Stanisław August Poniatowski. In 1793 he travelled to Vienna to further his training, worked in Vienna, later in Munich, Leipzig and elsewhere. He engraved many works after paintings by old masters and contemporary artists.

artists.b: Andrus Joonas (1970-2021) oli nii tegevuskunstnik, maalija kui ka installatsioonikunstnik. Eesti Kunstiakadeemia kolledži Academia Grataga on Joonas olnud seotud nii õpilase kui õppejõu rollis; õppejõuna on ta tegutsenud ka Academia Non Gratas.
artists.ben: Andrus Joonas (1970-2021) was a performance artist, painter and installation artist. Joonas has been connected with the Estonian Academy of Arts college Academia Grata both as a student and as a lecturer; as a lecturer he has also worked at Academia Non Grata.

artists.wdesc: Flemish painter, draftsman and designer of prints and tapestries (1593-1678)

artists.b: 1919 asutas Eesti esimese kutseliste fotograafide organisatsiooni "Päevapildikunsti Ettevõtjate Ühisus Eestis". Kuulus ka Eesti Kunstnikkude Liitu. Muuhulgas on pildistanud Draamateatri etendusi ja näitlejaid.
artists.ben: In 1919 he founded Estonia's first organisation of professional photographers, "Päevapildikunsti Ettevõtjate Ühisus Eestis". He also belonged to the Eesti Kunstnikkude Liit. Among other things, he has photographed performances and actors of the Draamateater.

artists.b: Loit Jõekalda (s. 1951) on lõpetanud Eesti Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi foto- ja graafika erialal (1986). Ta on Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige ja Eesti Vabagraafikute Ühenduse esimees, Eesti Muinastaideseltsi (1987), Eesti Saami Ühenduse (1988) ja Soome Muinastaideseltsi (1990) ning kunstnikeühenduse YDI (1998) liige. Jõekalda on esinenud kunstinäitustel aastast 1979, korraldanud isiknäitusi kodu- ja välismaal ning kureerinud arvukalt graafika- ja muinastaidealaseid näitusi ja sündmusi.
artists.ben: Loit Jõekalda (b. 1951) graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute in photography and print (1986). He is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and chairman of the Estonian Print Artists' Association, a member of the Estonian Ancient Art Society (1987), the Estonian Sami Association (1988), the Finnish Ancient Art Society (1990) and the artists' association YDI (1998). Jõekalda has participated in art exhibitions since 1979, has organised solo exhibitions at home and abroad, and has curated numerous exhibitions and events related to print and ancient art.

artists.b: Virge Jõekalda (1963) kasutab tehnikaid nagu kuivnõel ja ofort, mis seovad teda graafika traditsioonidega, kuid tähendusliku fragmendi eraldamine ja selle töötlemine kujundiks, jõuline joon ja värvilise pinna tundlik käsitlus näitavad ainult temale omast teekonda. Jõekalda on lõpetanud ERKI graafika eriala (1988) ning osalenud arvukatel näitustel Eestis ja välismaal. Tema teoseid leidub paljudes (era)kogudes ning ta on pälvinud mitmeid tunnustusi. Jõekalda on Eesti Vabagraafikute Ühenduse ja Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Virge Jõekalda (1963) uses techniques such as drypoint and etching, which connect her to the traditions of printmaking, but the isolation of a meaningful fragment and its processing into an image, a forceful line and a sensitive treatment of the coloured surface reveal a path uniquely her own. Jõekalda graduated from ERKI in printmaking (1988) and has participated in numerous exhibitions in Estonia and abroad. Her works can be found in many (private) collections and she has received several accolades. Jõekalda is a member of the Estonian Association of Free Graphic Artists and the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.b: Ernst Jõesaar õppis Tartu Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis Pallas skulptuuri ja maali, lõpetades kooli 1933. a. skulptorina. Sõjaeelne loomingulaad haakus 1930. aastatel Euroopas üldlevinud realistlike suunitlustega. Rootsi emigreerus ta 1944.a. juba väljakujunenud skulptorina. Tema loomingut vabas maailmas mõjutasid paratamatult 20. sajandi esimese poole euroopaliku modernismi kaanonid, teisalt võib tema loomingut pidada erakordselt iseseisvaks. Sõjajärgseil aastakümneil loodud teostest moodustavad suure grupi psühholoogilised portreed kaasaegsest pagulaskonnast. Arvukas figuuriplastika ja reljeefid tegelevad kujundlikult suurte, üldinimlikult mõistetavate teemadega; võib lugeda vihjeid nii antiikmütoloogiale kui ka piiblilegendidele. Ekspressiivne, Vahemere maade kultuuri elemente sisaldav, ent samas põhjamaiselt karge stilisatsioon kannab filosoofilist mõtet, eluraskusi ja kodumaa kaotust kogenud kunstniku resignatsiooni ning samas lootust inimliku loomingu igikestvusele.
artists.ben: Ernst Jõesaar studied sculpture and painting at the Tartu Higher Art School Pallas, graduating from the school in 1933 as a sculptor. His pre-war creative style was connected with the realistic tendencies prevalent in Europe in the 1930s. He emigrated to Sweden in 1944 already as an established sculptor. His work in the free world was inevitably influenced by the canons of European modernism of the first half of the 20th century, but on the other hand his work can be considered extraordinarily independent. Of the works created in the post-war decades, a large group consists of psychological portraits of the contemporary refugee community. Numerous figurative sculptures and reliefs deal figuratively with great, universally human themes; one can read allusions to both antique mythology and biblical legends. An expressive stylisation, containing elements of Mediterranean culture but at the same time northern in its austerity, carries a philosophical thought, the resignation of an artist who had experienced life's hardships and the loss of his homeland, and at the same time hope for the eternity of human creation.

Sandra Jõgeva (1976) is an installation and performance artist, writer, critic and documentary maker. Her work stands out with its rhetoric opposing hierarchies, exposing inequality and the uneven distribution of resources.

Between 2001 and 2006 Sandra Jõgeva collaborated with Margus Tamm in the artist duo Avangard, referring to the taboo of using the term in contemporary art with its name. Avangard’s work was characterised by irony and provocation. Next, Jõgeva worked in the artist group Pink Punk (2003–2006, various members) that highlighted social issues: for example the selling of a person's body, or the notion of prostitution in everyday relationships in the performance “Fair Deal” (2003), or marginalisation of “superfluous” people in society in “Happy holocaust” (2002). Pink Punk’s one of the more extreme examples of using an institutional art space was their performance “Wooligans” (2006), where the members of the group brought a herd of sheep to the cloakroom of Tallinn Art Hall.

In her solo practice Jõgeva also continues with the radical performances she is known for. Her performance “Südame külalisraamat” (Guestbook of the Heart, 2005) was based on the idea that the most important people (and events) leave a trace in a person's heart. During the piece, Jõgeva got a tattoo on the left side of her chest, depicting a blank list that could be signed in the future. The performance was a collaboration with Peter Anderson and took place at the Living Art Museum in Reykjavík.

Jõgeva has also experimented with the medium of sculpture. She has created large gelatine female figures (“Millest on tehtud väikesed tüdrukud” (What Are Little Girls Made Of), 2009) as well as silicone, latex and caramel objects. The exhibition “Seisused” (Ranks, 2008, together with Kaarel Sammet) presented fake bronze statues made of plastic, textile, wigs and spray paint. It presented a cross-section of Estonian society – a middle age teacher, a gangsta rapper, an old photographer, a business man, a young actress – while hinting at their social status.

artists.b: Kunstniku kineetilised objektid paistavad silma nõudliku inseneri­tehnilise lahendusega. 1973. aastast ehitas ta elektroonikapõhiseid valgus- ja häälekineetilisi objekte, ent vaid vähesed leidsid eksponeerimist nende valmimisajal. Objekt „Kaleidoskoop“ (EKM) on üks neist, mida näidati esimest korda juba 1976. aastal Tallinna Kunstihoones eksperimentaalarhitektuuri näitusel. Jõgeva kineetiliste objektidega sai avalikkus põhjalikumalt tutvuda alles 1993. aastal näitusel „Mobile 1“. Mitmed tema objektid (näiteks „Sinine“, EKM, 1973, taastatud 2004; „Oranž torn“, EKM, 1978, taastatud 1994/2004) põhinevad heli- ja valgusefektidel. Jõgeva kaks objekti on omandanud USA Rutgersi ülikooli Zimmerli muuseum.
artists.ben: The artist's kinetic objects stand out for their demanding engineering-technical solutions. Starting in 1973 he built electronics-based light- and sound-kinetic objects, but only a few were exhibited during the period of their creation. The object "Kaleidoskoop" ["Kaleidoscope"] (EKM) is one of these, first shown as early as 1976 at the Tallinn Art Hall at an exhibition of experimental architecture. The public was able to become thoroughly acquainted with Jõgeva's kinetic objects only in 1993, at the exhibition "Mobile 1". Several of his objects (for example "Sinine" ["Blue"], EKM, 1973, restored 2004; "Oranž torn" ["Orange Tower"], EKM, 1978, restored 1994/2004) are based on sound and light effects. Two of Jõgeva's objects have been acquired by the Zimmerli Art Museum at Rutgers University, USA.

artists.b: Tartu painter of restrained, tonal figure and landscape compositions.
artists.ben: Tartu painter of restrained, tonal figure and landscape compositions.

artists.b: Õppis Karkis ja Pöögli vallakoolides ning töötas mõnda aega talutöölisena. Õppis siis 1896. aastast Bandelier’i mööblitööstuses Tartus puunikerdust ja Tartu saksa käsitöökoolis joonistamist. Töötas Riias puunikerdaja Johansoni juures, Liepajas Ahi mööblitööstuses ja Odessas. 1900. aastast töötas Steinbergi mööblitööstuses Rakveres 1901-1904. aastani, mil asus alaliselt elama Pärnusse, kus töötas siseseisva puunikerdajana. Tema teostatud on Pärnu Issanda Muutmise kiriku altarikaunistused (1904), kirjutuslaua garnituurid Riigikohtule (1935). Korraldas 1935. aastal oma tööde näitused Pärnus ja Tartus, kus oli välja pandud muu hulgas „Eesti muistne elu 14 pildis“. Hiljem valmistas 27 pildilise töö Eesti elust 100 aastat tagasi ja olevikus. Näitusel välja pandud reljeef puulõiked omandas Eesti Rahva Muuseum. Olnud Pärnu Loomakaitse Seltsi asutaja ja juht. Teenete eest saanud Eesti Loomakaitse Liidu II järgu Rohelise Risti.
artists.ben: He studied at the Karksi and Pöögle parish schools and worked for a while as a farmhand. He then studied wood carving from 1896 at Bandelier's furniture factory in Tartu and drawing at the Tartu German Crafts School. He worked in Riga under the wood carver Johanson, in Liepāja at the Ahi furniture factory, and in Odessa. From 1900 he worked at the Steinberg furniture factory in Rakvere until 1901–1904, when he settled permanently in Pärnu, where he worked as an independent wood carver. His works include the altar decorations of Pärnu Transfiguration of the Lord Church (1904), and writing desk sets for the Supreme Court (1935). In 1935 he organised exhibitions of his works in Pärnu and Tartu, where, among other things, "Ancient Estonian Life in 14 Pictures" was on display. Later he made a 27-picture work about Estonian life 100 years ago and in the present. The wood-cut relief displayed at the exhibition was acquired by the Estonian National Museum. He was a founder and leader of the Pärnu Animal Protection Society. For his services he received the 2nd class Green Cross of the Estonian Animal Protection League.

artists.wdesc: Estonian glass artist, engraver and pedagogue (1925-2013)
Estonian painter, opera singer and film producer (1903-1987)

artists.b: Siiri Jüris on Tartus elav ja tegutsev kunstnik. Ta on lõpetanud Tartu Kunstikooli dekoraator-stilisti erialal (2012) ning omandanud nii bakalaureuse kui ka magistrikraadi Tartu Ülikooli maaliosakonnas (vastavalt 2015 ja 2017). Alates oma bakalaureusetööst on Jüris korduvalt pöördunud portreemaali juurde, tundes huvi indiviidi ja tema seisundite kujutamise võimaluste ja võimalikkuse vastu, seades sealjuures järjepidevalt kahtluse alla selle maaližanri konventsioone ja traditsioone. Jürise maale on mitmetes erakollektsioonides.
artists.ben: Siiri Jüris is an artist living and working in Tartu. She graduated from the Tartu Art School in the specialty of decorator-stylist (2012) and obtained both a bachelor's and a master's degree from the Painting Department of the University of Tartu (2015 and 2017 respectively). Since her bachelor's thesis, Jüris has repeatedly turned to portrait painting, being interested in the possibilities and possibility of depicting the individual and their states, while consistently questioning the conventions and traditions of this painting genre. Jüris's paintings are held in several private collections.

artists.b: Aime Jürjo (1928) on viljelnud lüürilist, materjalimõjule suunatud vabaskulptuuri ja portreeloomingut. Tema figuraalset loomingut iseloomustab vaoshoitud põhjamaine meeleolutunnetus, täpne modelleering ning panustamine kaunile, üldistatud siluetimõjule. Ta on eelistanud dolomiiti, marmorit ja puud, ent kasutanud dekoratiivloomingus ka keraamikat. Ta lõpetas 1953. aastal ENSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi skulptuuri erialal ning olnud pikaajalise staažiga kunstipedagoog.
artists.ben: Aime Jürjo (1928) has cultivated lyrical, material-influence-oriented free-standing sculpture and portraiture. Her figurative work is characterized by restrained northern mood sensibility, precise modelling, and an emphasis on beautiful, generalized silhouette effect. She has preferred dolomite, marble and wood, but has also used ceramics in her decorative work. She graduated in 1953 from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in the field of sculpture and has been an art educator with long-standing experience.

artists.wdesc: Estonian graphic designer, writer and playwright (1966-2018)

artists.b: Ivar Kaasik (s. 1965 Kuressaares) on Eesti maali- ja ehtekunstnik. Kaasik alustas õpinguid Eesti Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis arhitektuuri kateedris, kuid lõpetas ülikooli metallikunstnikuna. Alates 1992. aastast elab Kaasik Berliinis. Aastatel 1989–1990 õppis ta Halle Kunsti- ja Disainiülikoolis Saksamaal. Alates 2001. aastast on Kaasik Saksa Maalikunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Ivar Kaasik (b. 1965 in Kuressaare) is an Estonian painter and jewelry artist. Kaasik began his studies in the Department of Architecture at the Estonian State Art Institute, but graduated from the university as a metal artist. Since 1992, Kaasik has lived in Berlin. In 1989–1990, he studied at the Halle University of Art and Design in Germany. Since 2001, Kaasik has been a member of the German Association of Painters.

artists.b: Kunstnik on päästja, lohutaja. Kui keegi päästmist ei vaja, peab päästja kuidagi hakkama saama – lavastades endale ise olukorrad, kus teda vajatakse ja koondades enda ümber noori jüngreid, kes võiksid tema ideid edasi kanda. Need, kes vajavad päästmist, otsivad valede päästmisvõimaluste hulgast. Mõlemad on piinlikus  olukorras, kus üks peab lavastuse abil ennast teisele välja reklaamima. Slaidid ei paku tegelikult valmislahendusi, vaid vihjavad päästmisprotsessi algusele, selle võimalikkusele.
artists.ben: The artist is a saviour, a comforter. When no one needs saving, the saviour must somehow manage — staging situations for himself in which he is needed and gathering around him young disciples who might carry forward his ideas. Those who need saving search among false rescue possibilities. Both are in an awkward situation, where one must advertise himself to the other through a performance. The slides do not actually offer ready-made solutions, but hint at the beginning of the rescue process, its possibility.

Kai Kaljo is primarily known as a video artist, although her work also includes painting, photography, fresco, stained glass, and installation art. Kaljo's themes are inspired by her personal and everyday life extending into existential and social statements. Using black humour and irony, she often questions power relations in the art world, whether they are based on gender (male artists vs female artists), choice of artistic media (traditional art vs new media), geography (Estonia and Eastern Europe vs the international Western art world) or economic status (the precarity of freelance artists).

In the 1980s, Kaljo studied monumental painting, and in the 1990s she found herself in a new society, where state art commissions had suddenly disappeared and the art field of newly independent Estonia saw the emergence of new media. Her first notable moment of recognition came in 1994 with her site specific installation “Genesis and Disappearance of Life” at the 2nd Annual Exhibition of the Soros Center of Contemporary Arts, Estonia “Unexistent Art”.

Kaljo became known internationally in 1997 when she presented her first video “Loser” at the exhibition “Funny versus Bizarre” at the Contemporary Art Centre, Vilnius. The work was soon exhibited at other international shows as well. In the video, using laconic irony, Kaljo describes her lived reality as an Estonian woman artist – so far from the success stories heralded as part of the official cultural politics. She has addressed the precarious situation of artists in her later work, for example, in the photo installation “The more I work the poorer I am” (2006), depicting scenes from the artist's work days during which she makes a loss of € 246.

The art historian Mari Laaniste has described Kai Kaljo's work as “a sceptical meditation bordering on self-deprecation”. In the video “I am no Adamson-Eric” (2018) she plays with the idea of who is allowed to participate in the community of art (history). Kaljo tells the story of a conversation she had with her mother: when she was younger, she asked her mother, why she could not become an artist as multifaceted as the famous Estonian artist Adamson-Eric. Her mother snapped back at her: “But you are no Adamson-Eric!” In the video “Even the name is sometimes the same” (2017), also shown in Paris and Berlin at the Rencontres Internationales festival, Kaljo contemplates the randomness of human life, as she searches for figures who often remain in the background in historic photographs.

artists.b: 1956	Vastavalt Paul Amburi periodiseeringule, algas eksliibriseloomingu teine periood; alates 1957. aastast võttis osa kõigist suurematest ja enamikest temaatilistest Nõukogude Eesti eksliibrisenäitustest. Eksliibrisekunstnikuna muutus tuntuks ka väljaspool Nõukogude Liitu, tema eksliibrised omandati NSVLi, idabloki ja Lääne-Euroopa, Ameerika ja Austraalia erakollektsionääride kogudesse (mh tegi ta eksliibrise rahvusvahelise ekslibristide föderatsiooni presidendile Gianni Manterole) ning eksponeeriti rahvusvahelistel eksliibriste näitustel.
artists.ben: 1956	According to Paul Ambur's periodisation, the second period of ex-libris creation began; from 1957 he took part in all major and most thematic Soviet Estonian ex-libris exhibitions. As an ex-libris artist he also became known outside the Soviet Union; his ex-libris were acquired into private collections in the USSR, the Eastern Bloc, Western Europe, America and Australia (among others he made an ex-libris for Gianni Mantero, president of the International Federation of Ex-libris Societies) and were exhibited at international ex-libris exhibitions.

artists.b: Kallis alustas kunstiõpinguid 1907.aastal Ants Laikmaa ateljeekoolis, jõudes seal esialgu õppida vaid ühe semestri, ent jätkas Laikmaa juures 1913-1916, täiendades vahepeal end 1912-13 Eesti Kunstiseltsi Joonistuskursustel.
artists.ben: Kallis began his art studies in 1907 at Ants Laikmaa's studio school, initially managing to study there for only one semester, but continued with Laikmaa in 1913-1916, meanwhile furthering his education in 1912-13 at the Drawing Courses of the Estonian Art Society.

artists.b: Karin Kalman (1962) kasutab oma loomingus erinevaid savimasse – portselanist jämeda šamottsavini – ning põletab oma töid nii elektri- kui ka puupõletusahjus. Näitusetegevuse kõrval töötab ta EKA-s keraamika eriala õppejõuna ja tegutseb enda asutatud Stuudiokeraamika ateljees. Kalman on lõpetanud ERKI keraa- mika eriala (1986) ja osalenud arvukatel näitustel nii Eestis kui ka välismaal. Tema teoseid leidub mitmes (era)kogus. Kalman on Eesti Keraamikute Liidu ja Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Karin Kalman (1962) uses various types of clay in her work – from porcelain to coarse chamotte clay – and fires her works in both electric and wood-burning kilns. Alongside her exhibition activity she works as a lecturer in ceramics at the Estonian Academy of Arts and works in her own Studio Ceramics workshop. Kalman graduated from the ceramics department of ERKI (1986) and has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad. Her works can be found in several (private) collections. Kalman is a member of the Estonian Ceramists' Association and the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.b: Sõjajärgsetel aastatel oli tal raske kohaneda muutunud kunstiesteetiliste väärtushinnangutega. Hilda Orgusaare abiga leidis ta tagasihoidliku töökoha Tallinnas Nunne tänaval asunud arstiriistade kaupluses.
artists.ben: In the postwar years he found it difficult to adapt to the changed aesthetic values in art. With Hilda Orgusaar's help he found a modest job in Tallinn at a medical instruments shop on Nunne Street.

artists.b: Pärast katkestusi 1946 graafikuna. Võeti samal aastal ENSV Kunstnike Liidu liikmeks, kuid peagi heideti sealt välja. Elas Tartus tagasitõmbunult, kuid näitustel esinemata maalis palju. Tema loomingu iseloomustuseks: assamblaaž, kollaaž, akvarell, teadusväljaannete täppisjoonistused jm.
artists.ben: After interruptions, as a graphic artist in 1946. He was admitted to the ESSR Artists' Union that same year, but was soon expelled from it. He lived withdrawn in Tartu, but, without appearing at exhibitions, painted a great deal. His work is characterised by: assemblage, collage, watercolour, precise drawings for scientific publications, etc.

artists.b: Osad: Vanapagana eit (Kitzbergi Kaval-Ants ja Vanapagan, 1931), Lilly (Kálmáni Tsirkusprintsess, 1933), Taali (Raudsepa Roosad prillid, 1934); Niina (Lutsu ja Särevi Tagahoovis, 1936); Niida (Mälgu Õitsev meri, 1936) ja  Nataša (Raudsepa Lipud tormis, 1943)
artists.ben: Roles: The Devil's Old Woman (Kitzberg's Kaval-Ants ja Vanapagan, 1931), Lilly (Kálmán's Tsirkusprintsess, 1933), Taali (Raudsepp's Roosad prillid, 1934); Niina (Luts and Sarev's Tagahoovis, 1936); Niida (Mälk's Õitsev meri, 1936) and Nataša (Raudsepp's Lipud tormis, 1943)

artists.b: 1993-1997 õppis Tallinna Kunstiülikoolis maali. Isikunäitused 1996 Muu-ry galerii Helsingis; 1997 Mustpeade Maja Galerii, Tallinn; 1998 Tallinna Kunstisalong; 1999 koos Toomas Tõnissooga Corkis, Iirimaal; 1999 Tallinna Linnagalerii koos T. T.; 2001 Tartu Kunstimuuseumis koos T. T.; 2002 Rakvere galeriis koos T. T.; 2003 Hobusepea galerii koos T. T.; 2004 Maison de la Baie in Vains, Prantsusmaa koos T. T.; 2005 Vaal galerii koos T. T. ; 2006 Koguva kunstgalerii.
artists.ben: 1993-1997 studied painting at the Tallinn Art University. Solo exhibitions 1996 Muu-ry gallery in Helsinki; 1997 Mustpeade Maja Gallery, Tallinn; 1998 Tallinn Art Salon; 1999 together with Toomas Tõnissoo in Cork, Ireland; 1999 Tallinn City Gallery with T. T.; 2001 Tartu Art Museum with T. T.; 2002 Rakvere Gallery with T. T.; 2003 Hobusepea Gallery with T. T.; 2004 Maison de la Baie in Vains, France with T. T.; 2005 Vaal Gallery with T. T.; 2006 Koguva Art Gallery.

artists.b: Õppis Arumetsa algkoolis ja Tartu poeglaste reaalgümnaasiumis, gümnaasiumi lõpetas Viljandis. 1931–1935 õppis Tartu Ülikooli filosoofiateaduskonnas kunsti- ja kirjandusajalugu ning rahvaluulet. 1934 õppis Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis Pallas Ado Vabbe graafikaateljees. 1940-1941 õppis Konrad Mäe nim. Riigi Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis. 1943 lõpetas Kõrgemad Kujutava Kunsti Kursused graafika alal.
artists.ben: He studied at Arumetsa Primary School and at the Tartu Boys' Science Gymnasium, graduating from gymnasium in Viljandi. From 1931 to 1935 he studied art and literary history and folklore at the Faculty of Philosophy of the University of Tartu. In 1934 he studied at the Pallas Higher Art School in Ado Vabbe's graphic art studio. In 1940-1941 he studied at the Konrad Mägi State Higher Art School. In 1943 he graduated from the Higher Courses of Fine Art in graphic art.

artists.b: Sündis Vahi mõisas Tartumaal, õppis 1907-1909 Kristjan Raua stuudios Tartus, 1909 Münchenis Anton Ažbé kunstikoolis, 1910-1913 Pariisis École des Beaux Arts'is ja vabaakadeemiates, 1919 Pallases ja 1922-1923 Hamburgi kunsttööstuskoolis. Oli kunstiühingu Pallas asutajaliige. Mobiliseeriti Punaarmeesse, tema surmakuupäev 1943. aastal on teadmata.
artists.ben: Born at Vahi manor in Tartumaa, studied 1907–1909 in Kristjan Raud's studio in Tartu, in 1909 at Anton Ažbé's art school in Munich, 1910–1913 at the École des Beaux-Arts and free academies in Paris, in 1919 at Pallas and 1922–1923 at the Hamburg School of Applied Arts. Was a founding member of the art society Pallas. Was mobilized into the Red Army; his date of death in 1943 is unknown.

artists.b: Kes oma Tärkma värkstoas tegi pille kandlest kontrabassini. Ma ei tea, kas see on kena legend, või vastab tõele, et ta tegi omal ajal nii palju mandoliine, et kõigis Hiiumaa koolides olid mandoliiniansamblid.Seerias oli algselt 21 tööd erinevatest Hiiumaa küladest, mis on mulle olulised, inimesed ja linnud-loomad on kõik Hiiumaaga seotud.
artists.ben: Who in his Tärkma workshop made instruments from the kannel to the double bass. I don't know whether it's a nice legend, or whether it's true that at one time he made so many mandolins that every school on Hiiumaa had a mandolin ensemble. The series originally consisted of 21 works from different villages of Hiiumaa that are important to me, the people and the birds and animals are all connected to Hiiumaa.

artists.b: Haridus: 2006–2008 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia (MA, installatsioon ja skulptuur); 2003–2006 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia (BA, installatsioon ja skulptuur)
artists.ben:
Edith Karlson (1983) is a sculptor who is mostly working with large-scale installations. The figures in Karlson's work evoke the duality encoded within working as an artist and also being a member of society. Frequently creating animal forms and anthropomorphic figures, she approaches humans as animalistic beings whose impulses, wants, and desires are hidden beneath their morals.

(2016), consisting of 100 animal figures and rabbit droppings, Karlson moved from massive large-volume sculptures to demanding small forms and ceramics, looking closer at the laws of nature and the food chain.

(2012-2013) reflected on people’s (and the artist’s) personal doubts about the world around them. This series can be seen as the artist’s method for dealing with conflict in everyday life, and potential dramatic scenarios. For example,

(2013) presented a plaster cast army of child-size ghosts, which simultaneously referred to fears from childhood but also to the anxiety of adulthood, emerging after Karlson’s 30th birthday. The exhibition.

artists.b: Itaalias veedetud kaheksa aasta jooksul kujunes välja kunstniku isikupärane stiil. Avaldus Rubensi mitmekülgsus kunstnikuna: altarimaalid, portreed, mütoloogilise ja allegoorilise sisuga maalid ning usuteemalised kompositsioonid. Noore Rubensi tööd olid suurepärase tehnilise teostusega. Umbes aastaks 1620 oli tema maalimislaad välja kujunenud. Selle tunnuseks olid lopsakate eluküllaste vormidega figuurid, kirglikud liigutused ja säravad värvid. Talle on iseloomulik täidlaste alasti naiste kujutamine.
artists.ben: During the eight years spent in Italy, the artist developed his distinctive style. Rubens's versatility as an artist became apparent: altarpieces, portraits, paintings with mythological and allegorical content, and religious compositions. The young Rubens's works were of superb technical execution. By around 1620 his painting style had fully developed. Its characteristics were figures of lush, vigorous forms, passionate movements and brilliant colours. He is characterised by the depiction of plump nude women.

artists.b: Skulptor. Loonud monumentaalteoseid, portreid ja mütoloogiaainelisi figuurkompositsioone. Saavutanud ekspressiivsuse ja plastilise väljendusrikkuse erinevaid klassikalisi materjale (kipsi, pronksi, kivi, puud) omavahel ühendades või neid eraldi või koos valmismaterjalidega kasutades. Omane on iroonilise ja groteskse põimumine tõsisega. 1990. aastaist loonud installatsioone ja kontseptuaalseid projekte.
artists.ben: Sculptor. He has created monumental works, portraits and figural compositions on mythological subjects. He has achieved expressiveness and plastic richness of expression by combining various classical materials (plaster, bronze, stone, wood) with one another, or using them separately or together with ready-made materials. Characteristic of him is the interweaving of the ironic and the grotesque with the serious. Since the 1990s he has created installations and conceptual projects.

artists.b: Mari Kartau aka Siram (s. 1968) on lõpetanud Eesti Kunstiakadeemia kunstiteaduse eriala, õppinud mitteformaalses kunstiõppeasutuses Academia Non grata ning omab ka metsanduslikku haridust. Oma loomingus on ta tegelenud peamiselt performance’ ja maalikunstiga, vähem ka teinud installatsioone ja graafikat. On kureerinud arvukalt näitusi ja kirjutanud kunstikriitikat. Kunsti valdkonnas oli aktiivsem aastatel 1992 – 2015, kuid tegutseb ka praegu.
artists.wdesc: Estonian artist, art historian, art critic and curator (born 1968)
artists.ben: Mari Kartau aka Siram (b. 1968) has graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in art history, studied at the non-formal art education institution Academia Non Grata, and also holds a forestry education. In her work she has mainly engaged in performance and painting, and to a lesser extent has also made installations and graphic art. She has curated numerous exhibitions and written art criticism. She was more active in the field of art in 1992–2015, but is still active today.

artists.b: Artist of institutions and property; her own house is her museum.
artists.ben:
Flo Kasearu (1985) is an artist whose work brings together performative practices with video, painting, drawing, sculpture and installation, and explores themes like domestic violence, small businesses, unemployment, gender, identity, freedom, patriotism, nationalism and the oppositions of public and private space. In her art, Kasearu reacts to social and political processes with a fine sense of humour. She often uses biographical material as the basis for her works.

In one of her first performances, “Estonian Sculpture” (2005), Kasearu stood on a podium in a gallery, dressed in Estonian national dress, with a sign hanging from her neck “I am dead”, as a marker of her fears regarding her identity and the fate of her country. In the video “Mulgi Travels” (2007), a woman in Estonian national dress introduces Estonia in Berlin. The main character in the video acts like a self-appointed diplomat, with the duty of introducing her home country to the people she meets in the street. Acting like a sales agent, her actions evoke Estonia as a company operating according to the logic of the market. In the video “Estonian dream” (2011), Kasearu looks at the idea of patriotism and discusses being home sick, and being a hostage in your own home. The protagonist of the video is a great example of in-betweenness: she wants to be here and elsewhere, home and away from home.

In 2013 Flo Kasearu founded a house museum, a site specific and continuously developing thematic exposition of the artist’s work in her own home. The house museum is an artwork and a conceptual project, encompassing the Pebre Street house in its entirety, from basement to attic, and also her garden. For example, as part of the Gwangju Biennale, Kasearu invited a professional gardener to create a traditional Korean style garden in her backyard. “Korean garden” (2016) is the most extensive installation in the museum, and one of the few of its kind in Europe. Since Kasearu mostly works at home, her art addressed current everyday themes. For example, she has created several site-specific works in the museum, looking at issues of building ownership – “Nightmares of the house owner” and “Ars Longa Vita Brevis” (both 2013).

Kasearu’s work also features a playful approach to spatial studies. For example, she conducted guided tours in her home and house museum, designed to shift people’s perception of private and public spaces. A similar approach is evident in the work titled “Party next door” (2014) and the participatory performance “Members only” at the Performa Biennial (2017). Kasearu notably addressed.

artists.b: Sculptor of heavy, memorial-scale objects with a horror undertow.
artists.ben:
Jass Kaselaan (1981) is an artist, who combines sculpture, sound and other mediums in his work creating powerful spatial installations. His works contain an existential spirituality, bringing up questions about religion and science in relation to technological progress, but also about the relation between animals and humans. Kaselaan looks at life in its totality, not delimiting it to solely an earthly existence. Life, death, resurrection, transmigration of souls, faith, memory, family – are the pinpoints of his work, but not physically perceptible constraints.

One of the first exhibitions by Kaselaan, in which he dealt with the otherworldly, “Return You Children of Man” (2010), depicted a symbolic cemetery in which you could move between the crosses and listen to Chopin’s funeral march from the megaphones. The triptych at his personal exhibition “Transmigration of Souls” (2011) depicted the journey of souls to the otherworld. Although the composition has sacral connotations, the whole layout derives from technocratic positioning – the transmigration of souls is carried by mechanical noises and the otherworld shines as a giant projector lamp. The previous, so-called white period ends with the personal exhibition “Light is our Strength” (2011) – Kaselaan exhibits a mine-looking black-coloured perpetuum mobile. The “black period” is continued by the exhibition “Garden” (2012), in which the space, heated by intensive projector lamps are highlighting a cobbled wooden construction in the middle.

Several of Kaselaan’s personal exhibitions are characterised by an intensive spatial experience – the distance between the spectator and the work is reduced to a minimum. On several occasions, the artist has expanded the exhibition space through photographs on the walls: in the exhibition “Objects in The Field” (2013), Kaselaan exhibited photos of snowy fields, in “Garden” he showed images of the skeletons of prehistoric animals. The portraits of larger-than-life dolls made of concrete in the installation “The Square of Dolls” (2014), were framed by photos of panel houses.

Kaselaan has also collaborated with sculptor Edith Karlson. The work “Toys” (2017) exhibited at their joint exhibition “Hudnoi”, Kaselaan further developed his interest in toys, creating memorials for a childhood – for the ephemeral moment in space-time. Slightly crumpled and gnarly looking toys have obviously lost their has-been significance, but still they bring out the warm memories of childhood.

artists.b: Markus Kasemaa (sündinud 28. augustil 1972 Tallinnas) on eesti kunstnik, tuntud oma uuenduslike ja mitmekesiste kunstiprojektide poolest. Ta õppis aastatel 1990–1991 Tartu Kunstikooli skulptuuriosakonnas ning 1991–1995 Tartu Ülikooli maaliosakonnas.
artists.ben: Markus Kasemaa (born 28 August 1972 in Tallinn) is an Estonian artist known for his innovative and diverse art projects. He studied in 1990–1991 in the sculpture department of the Tartu Art School and in 1991–1995 in the painting department of the University of Tartu.

Erki Kasemets (1969) is an artist working with installation, painting, performance and theatre. His work includes trash art, polygon theatre performances, systematic documentation of personal life, focus on material, kinetic art, set and stage design, and activities in artist groups Vedelik and P.E.A.. Kasemets views his practice and method as bricolage, often creating art works from broken, useless or discarded everyday objects. Many of his works address themes like time and memory from a subjective standpoint.

Kasemets began exhibiting in early 1990s when studying scenography in the Estonian Academy of Arts. The Estonian public mainly knows him for his work in trash art. Among the first objects that found a place in Kasmets’ work and which he started collecting were one-litre milk cartons. The project “Life-file” presents empty painted milk cartons with dates or text that mark certain dates in the artist’s life. In that sense, Kasemets’ practice of trash art is cumulative, process-based and evolving in time – the collected objects are like units of data. As such, use of rubbish in his works is not a critique of capitalism through material but rather a means for analysing themes like time and memory. He also uses many other items as records: tin cans (the modular system “Kompurker”), cigarette packages (“Homepage”, 1997), CDs and DVDs (“Information”, 2006), buttons, etc.

Kasemets began daily and systematically documenting the flow of time in an attempt to organise the collected matter already in the 1980s. In his solo exhibition “Recycling of Time” (1996) Kasemets used the modular system “Kompurker” made of tin cans to construct images and installations. “Kompurker” allows the artist to create raster images, which can later be disassembled and assembled anew. Kasemets uses collecting and selecting as a means against forgetting, to physically record episodic memory. There is nevertheless a human perspective in Kasemets’ machine-like approach – sometimes the archives are left unfinished, for example in the case of the “Chronicle of Banalities” (1996–2002).

The concept of polygon theatre was established in 1996 as part of his Master’s thesis. The polygon theatre is a space of all possibilities aiming to broaden the idea of theatre. The word “polygon” is borrowed from military terminology and refers to a training area for testing out technologies or tactics. Kasemets’ concept of polygon theatre refers to unfinished thoughts and theatre that is always open to experimentation. Polygon theatre has performed in real military polygons, art galleries, public s.

Alice Kask (1976) is a painter whose work is often associated with new figurative painting. Kask's paintings are characterised by a sketch-like quality and taking the quotidian into a territory where it becomes detached from reality. At first glance, the paintings seem to solely centre on the figure and human body, however, a focus on space and environment is nevertheless always there – through shadows, black holes, images rising out of emptiness, and juxtaposition of planes and spaces. The power of her pieces relies in the inseparability of the work and the physical object, the image's contact with the underlying surface or detachment from it.

In the interaction between absolute generalisation and anatomical detail, Kask's approach to human becomes agonising, yet powerful, forging a monumentality that consists of an equal part of existential angst. Kask's world is schematic, the fine modelled figure is in contrast with the background that refuses to give any details on the scene, the image seemingly only existing in a vacuum of its own making. Her grey paper beings and male figures act as if guided by an unseen force.

Kask has always depicted her figures as anonymous basic forms, dressed in various garments carrying the spirit of the era. In 2005, the works exhibited at Hobusepea Gallery depicted suits, in the 2015 exhibition at Tallinn City Gallery, however, these were replaced by T-shirt, tracksuit and trainers. With the exhibition “Murdosa” (Fraction, 2011) alongside her interest in relations between objects, figures and space, the artist added another element, time, to her work – capturing the moment, the fraction of a second and presenting it on a static two-dimensional surface.

At the show “Alice, Neeme & Jass” (2018) in Kunsthalle Helsinki, the audience was greeted by Kask's large-scale painting “Kekkoneni käsi” (Kekkonen's Hand), a sketch of a human silhouette with the right hand waving hello. The hand as an archetypal tool for making a mark has occurred in Kask's work before, referencing ways of perceiving the human body and environment and the shifts between the two.

artists.b: Eve Kask (s 1958) on Eesti kunstnik, kes tegutseb põhiliselt järgmistes valdkondades: graafika, kunstnikuraamat ja foto. Tema töid on kirjeldatud alateadvuse, müütilisuse, sümbolismi, ekspressionismi, feminismi ja antropoloogilise dokumentalismi võtmes. Viimastel kümnenditel tegelenud põhiliselt fotoprojektidega – “Käsmu inimesed” 1999–2004. a., “Kärberi 37” 2004. a., “Bussiputkad” 2004–2008. a., “Mida inimesed tahavad” 2007–2010. a. Eesti Kunstnike Liidu ja Vabagraafikute Ühingu liige.
artists.ben: Eve Kask (b 1958) is an Estonian artist who works mainly in the following fields: print, artist's book and photography. Her works have been described in terms of the subconscious, mythicalness, symbolism, expressionism, feminism and anthropological documentalism. In recent decades she has worked mainly on photo projects – "Käsmu inimesed" ["People of Käsmu"] 1999–2004, "Kärberi 37" 2004, "Bussiputkad" ["Bus Shelters"] 2004–2008, "Mida inimesed tahavad" ["What People Want"] 2007–2010. Member of the Estonian Artists' Association and the Estonian Print Artists' Association.

artists.b: Jüri Kask (s. 1949 Kolga-Jaanis) on maalikunstnik, graafik ja skulptor. Näitustel osalenud alates 1970. aastast. Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige (1979), Eesti Maalikunstnike Liidu liige (1992). Loomingule on iseloomulik monumentaalsus ning vormi- ja värvikontrastid.
artists.ben: Jüri Kask (b. 1949 Kolga-Jaani) is a painter, graphic artist and sculptor. He has taken part in exhibitions since 1970. Member of the Estonian Artists' Association (1979), member of the Estonian Painters' Association (1992). His work is characterised by monumentality and contrasts of form and colour.

artists.b: Jüri Kass (1956) on Eesti kunstnik. Lõpetanud Eesti Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi tööstuskunsti (1979). Tegutsenud graafilise disaineri, maalija, graafiku, õppejõuna. Näitustel esineb alates 1974. aastast. On eksponeerinud kümmekond isikunäitust (plakatid, joonistused, maalid, graafika). Ühisnäitus „Vüüming“ Ülle Marksiga Kunstihoone galeriis (2016).
artists.ben: Jüri Kass (1956) is an Estonian artist. He graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute in industrial art (1979). He has worked as a graphic designer, painter, printmaker, and teacher. He has taken part in exhibitions since 1974. He has held about ten solo exhibitions (posters, drawings, paintings, prints). Joint exhibition "Vüüming" with Ülle Marks at the Kunstihoone gallery (2016).

artists.b: Avo Keerend (1920–2012) oli eesti graafik ja maalikunstnik, kelle loominguline teekond ulatus enam kui kuue aastakümne taha. Ta alustas kunstiõpinguid juba 1936. aastal, keskendudes esialgu graafikale, kuid täiendas hiljem ka oma maalimisoskust. Varasemas loomingus kasutas Keerend peamiselt sügavtrükitehnikaid, luues natuuritruusid natüürmorte, akte ja olustikustseene.
artists.ben: Avo Keerend (1920–2012) was an Estonian graphic artist and painter whose creative career spanned more than six decades. He began his art studies as early as 1936, initially focusing on graphic art, but later also developed his painting skills. In his earlier work, Keerend mainly used intaglio printing techniques, creating naturalistic still lifes, nudes, and genre scenes.

Raul Keller (1973) has focused his practice on experimental art; relating to location, improvisation and sound art since the 1990s. Keller’s work is largely based on process, acoustics of the space, and DIY-practices. He is one of the few artists in Estonia working in sound art consistently.

One of Keller's first radiophonic experiments was titled “Jammer” (2002). It was a radio program, broadcasted with a monophonic transmitter at a frequency of 105,8 MHz in Tallinn. The channel was open to everyone for three hours. The aim of the project was to create a low-frequency democratic environment to explore the creative and technological possibilities of radio broadcasting, without media or technological censorship. With the work “Radio – it’s really simple!” (2002) Keller promoted creating DIY radio receivers. This work borrows its title from the book “Radio? … it’s really Simple!” by the French radio enthusiast Eugen Aisberg, translated into Estonian in 1969.

In his installations, Keller often makes use of already existing soundscapes. For example, “Reflector” (2007) is 24-hour sound composition, for which he recorded sound bites in the surroundings of the installation over a two-week period. The installation reflects the particular sound environment in its location, and also complements and shifts it. “Torpedoes in” (2013) is a material-based spatial installation that uses sound as a “natural” tool – five torpedoes constructed by Keller, made to rumble by air flow. His earlier work “Torpedoes out” (2011) is based on the same material and powered by air. A more recent piece, “mem: interference” (2022) exhibited at Villa Elisabeth in Berlin, also focused on reflecting and shifting of the surrounding soundscape. The work consists of giant helium balloons with strings attached to speakers playing low frequency sound files, which makes the balloons act as oscillating systems. Touching the vibrating balloon strings changes the sound. Independently of the player, the installation develops the sound on its own.

Keller's first retrospective exhibition “KLANG!” (2012) in the Estonian Maritime Museum's Gunpowder Store gave an overview of his sound objects and installations created in the second half of the 2000s. In his most monumental exhibition to date titled “What You Hear is What You Get (Mostly)” (2014) in the Contemporary Art Museum of Estonia, running through the museums three floors, displayed a multi-part low frequency sound work, exploring the relationship between sound objects and architectural space, human perception and habits, offering abundant in-de.

artists.b: Raivo Kelomees (s. 1960) on kunstnik ja kunstiajaloolane. Ta on õppinud Tartu Ülikoolis psühholoogiat ning Eesti Kunstiakadeemias kunstiajalugu ja disaini. Ta on Eesti Kunstiakadeemia vabade kunstide teaduskonna vanemteadur ja rakenduskõrgkooli Pallas professor. Kelomees on raamatute “Sürrealism” (Kirjastus Kunst, 1993) ja artiklikogumike “Ekraan kui membraan” (Tartu Kõrgema Kunstikooli toimetised, 2007) ja “Sotsiaalsed mängud kunstiruumis” (EKA, 2013) autor. Tema doktoritöö on “Postmateriaalsus kunstis. Indeterministlikud kunstipraktikad ja mittemateriaalne kunst” (Dissertationes Academiae Artium Estoniae 3, 2009). Koos briti teadlase Chris Halesiga toimetas ta artiklite kogumikku “Constructing Narrative in Interactive Documentaries” (Cambridge Scholars Publishing, 2014). Koostöös Varvara Guljajeva ja Oliver Laasiga toimetas ta artiklikogumiku “The Meaning of Creativity in Age of AI” (EKA Press, 2022). Näitustel esineb Kelomees 1980. aastast. Ta on eelistanud elektroonilist ja digikunsti, kuid ka maal on kuulunud tema meediumite hulka. Viimati esines ta näitusel “Sürrealism 100. Praha, Tartu ja teised lood…” (Kuraatorid: Anna Pravdová (Praha Rahvusgalerii), Joanna Hoff.
artists.ben: Raivo Kelomees (b. 1960) is an artist and art historian. He has studied psychology at the University of Tartu and art history and design at the Estonian Academy of Arts. He is a senior researcher at the Faculty of Fine Arts of the Estonian Academy of Arts and a professor at the Pallas University of Applied Sciences. Kelomees is the author of the book "Sürrealism" (Kirjastus Kunst, 1993) and the article collections "Ekraan kui membraan" (Proceedings of the Tartu Art College, 2007) and "Sotsiaalsed mängud kunstiruumis" (EKA, 2013). His doctoral thesis is "Postmateriaalsus kunstis. Indeterministlikud kunstipraktikad ja mittemateriaalne kunst" (Dissertationes Academiae Artium Estoniae 3, 2009). Together with the British scholar Chris Hales he edited the collection of articles "Constructing Narrative in Interactive Documentaries" (Cambridge Scholars Publishing, 2014). In collaboration with Varvara Guljajeva and Oliver Laas, he edited the collection of articles "The Meaning of Creativity in Age of AI" (EKA Press, 2022). Kelomees has been exhibiting since 1980.
