He has preferred electronic and digital art, but painting has also been among his media. Most recently he took part in the exhibition "Sürrealism 100. Praha, Tartu ja teised lood…" (Curators: Anna Pravdová (National Gallery Prague), Joanna Hoff.

artists.b: Rein Kelpman (s. 1960 Tartus) on vabakutseline kunstnik, maalikunstnikuna iseõppinu. Kelpman on näitustel osalenud alates 1981. a, Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige alates 1986 a. Töötanud külalisõppejõuna Tartu Ülikoolis.
artists.ben: Rein Kelpman (b. 1960 in Tartu) is a freelance artist, self-taught as a painter. Kelpman has participated in exhibitions since 1981, a member of the Estonian Artists' Association (Eesti Kunstnike Liit) since 1986. Has worked as a visiting lecturer at the University of Tartu.

artists.b:
Ilmar Kimm sündis Petrogradis. Õppis aastatel 1927–1935 Leningradis eesti koolis, aastatel 1936–1939 Ülevenemaalise Kunstiakadeemia kunstikeskkoolis. Aastatel 1939–1941 õppis ta Ülevenemaalises Kunstiakadeemias. Sügisel 1941 mobiliseeriti Punaarmeesse. Sai Velikije Luki all lahingus raskesti haavata ja demobiliseeriti. Jätkas aastal 1944 kunstiõpinguid, lõpetas 1948. aastal Ilja Repini nimelise kunstiinstituudi Leningradis.

Ta töötas aastatel 1948–1951 Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis maaliõppejõuna. Aastatel 1952–1988 ERKIs õppejõuna: oli aastast 1954 dotsent, aastast 1965 professor. Aastatel 1963–1983 oli ta maalikateedri juhataja, aastatel 1983–1988 oli ta konsultantprofessor. Aastast 1951 oli ta Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben:
Ilmar Kimm was born in Petrograd. He studied from 1927–1935 at the Estonian school in Leningrad, and from 1936–1939 at the secondary art school of the All-Russian Academy of Arts. From 1939–1941 he studied at the All-Russian Academy of Arts. In the autumn of 1941 he was mobilised into the Red Army. He was severely wounded in battle near Velikiye Luki and was demobilised. In 1944 he resumed his art studies, graduating in 1948 from the Ilya Repin Institute of Art in Leningrad.

From 1948–1951 he worked as a teacher of painting at the Tartu State Art Institute. From 1952–1988 he was a teacher at ERKI: from 1954 he was docent, from 1965 professor. From 1963–1983 he was head of the painting department, and from 1983–1988 he was consultant professor. From 1951 he was a member of the Artists' Union.

artists.b: Töötas joonistusõpetajana ja maaliõppejõuna ning Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis monumentaalmaali kateedri juhatajana (1947–1949). Alates 1949. aastast tegutses vabakutselise kunstnikuna.
artists.ben: Worked as a drawing teacher and painting instructor, and as head of the department of monumental painting at the Tartu State Art Institute (1947–1949). From 1949 worked as a freelance artist.

artists.b: Sai kunstihariduse 1903-1908 Peterburis Stieglitzi kunsttööstuskoolis ofordi alal. Töötas õpetajana Piiral, Rakveres ja Tallinnas. Valiti 1909 Eesti Kunstiseltsi juhatusse. 1914-1918 oli seltsi asutatud Tallinna Kunsttööstuskooli joonistus-, graafika- ja stiiliõpetaja. 1921-1932 Haapsalus Läänemaa Õpetajate Seminari õppejõud.
grp: school:Saint Petersburg Stieglitz State Academy of Art and Design
artists.ben: He received an art education in 1903-1908 in St. Petersburg at the Stieglitz School of Technical Drawing, in the field of etching. He worked as a teacher in Piiral, Rakvere and Tallinn. In 1909 he was elected to the board of the Estonian Art Society. From 1914 to 1918 he was a teacher of drawing, graphic art and style at the Tallinn School of Applied Arts, founded by the society. From 1921 to 1932 he was a lecturer at the Läänemaa Teachers' Seminary in Haapsalu.

artists.b: Kalju Kivi (snd 1951) õppinud Tartu Kunstikoolis puidu kunstilist töötlemist, Eesti Riiklikus Kunstiinstiduudis moekunsti.Lõpetanud 1980 õpingud asunud tööle “Tallinfilmi”. Lavastanud 12 animafilmi, olnud aastatel 1995 – 2012 Nukuteatri peakunstnik, olnud 12ne mängufilmi kunstnik. Eest Kinoliidu ja Eesti Lavastuskunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Kalju Kivi (b. 1951) studied artistic wood processing at the Tartu Art School, fashion design at the Estonian State Art Institute. Having completed his studies in 1980, he started working at "Tallinnfilm". He has directed 12 animated films, was the chief artist of the Puppet Theatre in 1995–2012, has been the artist of 12 feature films. Member of the Estonian Film Union and the Estonian Union of Production Designers.

artists.b: Sündinud 11.11.1975, Tartu. Haridus: 2002–2004Tartu Ülikool, filosoofiateaduskond; 1996–1998Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, skulptuur; 1992–1996Tartu Kunstikool, skulptuur; 1992–1993Grigori Lotmani Kunstistuudio.
artists.ben:
Kiwa (1975) can be viewed as a reluctant machine, disrupting leitmotifs and quotes. Bringing together principles of anarchy and pop, the artist uses various media from sculpture to painting, performance to video and sound to text.

Since 1997 Kiwa has been working with “media graffiti”, which entails having his name or image frequently presented in the media. This is inspired by the saying that it does not matter who you are, but how others see you. “Media graffiti” could be understood as marketing – just like with marketing in advertising, media hacking amplifies the aspects of least importance.

Kiwa demonstrated his opposition to joining the EU in the video work “Graffiti Patrol” (1998, Art Museum of Estonia). The video shows the anti-EU artist lurking near the House of the Representation of the European Commission saying: “

,” in broken, even ridiculous-sounding English. Graffiti as the barometer of society makes visible what has been suppressed and presents alternative truths that have no place in the official discourse. Kiwa claims graffiti to be a peaceful act of violence.

artists.b: Sündis Venemaal, 1942 asus perekond Eestisse, Rakverre. Õppis 1952-1957 Tartu kunstikoolis ja 1957-1963 ERKI-s (EKA) graafikat, oli 1966-1994 TPÜ (TLÜ) õppejõud. Pälvis Grand Prix Tallinna III graafikatriennalil.
artists.ben: Born in Russia, in 1942 the family moved to Estonia, to Rakvere. Studied at the Tartu Art School in 1952-1957 and graphic art at ERKI (EKA) in 1957-1963, was a lecturer at TPÜ (TLÜ) in 1966-1994. Received the Grand Prix at the III Tallinn Graphic Art Triennial.

grp: school:State Academy of Fine Arts Stuttgart

artists.b: Aleksander Koemets sündis Moskvas vabrikutöölise perekonnas, Esimese Maailmasõja algul pöördus isa koos pojaga tagasi sünnimaale Eestisse, kus A. Koemets omandas Võrus ja Pärnus alghariduse. Pärast õhtugümnaasiumi lõpetamist Tartus 1931 õppis alates 1936 Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis, lõpetas 1941 J. Koorti nimelise Riigi Rakenduskusti kooli. Täiendas end Prantsusmaal ja Belgias. Mobiliseeriti Punaarmeesse, oli Teises maailmasõjas rindevõitleja, sai haavata. Jätkas kunstiõpinguid ja lõpetas 1948 kunstiinstituudi (EKA) raamatugraafikuna. Oli kirjastuse Ilukirjandus ja Kunst kunstiline toimetaja, 1957-1970 kirjastuse Kunst peakunstnik.
artists.ben: Aleksander Koemets was born in Moscow into a factory worker's family; at the beginning of the First World War his father returned with his son to his native land, Estonia, where A. Koemets received his elementary education in Võru and Pärnu. After finishing evening secondary school in Tartu in 1931, he studied from 1936 at the State School of Applied Arts, graduating in 1941 from the J. Koort State School of Applied Art. He furthered his education in France and Belgium. He was mobilised into the Red Army, was a front-line combatant in the Second World War, and was wounded. He continued his art studies and graduated in 1948 from the Art Institute (EKA) as a book graphic artist. He was an art editor at the publishing house Ilukirjandus ja Kunst, and from 1957 to 1970 chief artist of the publishing house Kunst.

artists.b: Ellen Kolk (1942) kuulub naiskunstnike ringi, kes muutsid 1970. aastate algul Eesti kunstinäituste üldpilti. Nagu mitme tema kaasaegse noore naisskulptori puhul 1970. aastate alguses, võib ka Ellen Kolgi tulekut kunstinäitustele seostada estetismi taasväärtustamisega skulptuuris. Just tema tõi pronksi skulptuurimaterjalina taas näitusesaalidesse ning seda tunduvalt enne ARS Monumentaali regulaarsete pronksivalude algust. 1970. aastal valminud „Veenus” on üks esimesi täisfiguure uusestetistlikus laadis. Kolki on huvitanud nii antiikmütoloogiast lähtuvad motiivid kui ka klassitsistlikult õilistatud kujundlikkus ja allegoorilised teemavalikud. Mitme figuurikompositsiooni juures esinevad atribuutidena looduselemendid. Tundlikult modelleeritud ning meisterliku pinnatöötlusega skulptuurid haakusid 1970. aastate algusaja uue põlvkonna esteetikaga. Teosed on figuraalsed, paistavad silma täpse modelleeringu, selge klassikalise vormikõne ja meisterliku pinnatöötlusega. Suurem hulk töid on teostatud pronksis, ent ta on loonud ka marmoris ja dolomiidis. Kammerliku olemusega figuurid ja portreed on leidnud aastatega tee avalikku ruumi (nt Põhja-Eesti Regionaalhaigla esine basseiniga haljasala Mustamäel, Kuressaare haigla, Maardu mõis, Palmse mõis, Komandandi aed Tallinnas Toompeal, SEB Pank Tallinnas, Vene saatkond Luxembourgis). Kolk lõpetas 1962. aastal Tartu Kunstikooli ning 1967. aastal ENSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi skulptuuri erialal. Ta on pälvinud Kristjan Raua preemia (1981).
artists.ben: Ellen Kolk (1942) belongs to the circle of women artists who changed the overall picture of Estonian art exhibitions at the beginning of the 1970s. As with several of her contemporary young women sculptors in the early 1970s, Ellen Kolk's arrival at art exhibitions can also be linked to the revaluation of aestheticism in sculpture. It was she who brought bronze back into exhibition halls as a sculptural material, considerably before the beginning of the regular bronze casting of ARS Monumentaal. The "Venus" completed in 1970 is one of the first full figures in the new aestheticist manner. Kolk has been interested both in motifs derived from ancient mythology and in classicistically ennobled imagery and allegorical choice of themes. Elements of nature appear as attributes in several figural compositions. Sensitively modelled sculptures with masterly surface treatment connected with the aesthetics of the new generation of the early 1970s. The works are figural, distinguished by precise modelling, clear classical formal language and masterly surface treatment. Most of the works are executed in bronze, but she has also created works in marble and dolomite. Chamber-like figures and portraits have over the years found their way into public space (e.g. the green area with a pool in front of the North Estonia Medical Centre in Mustamäe, Kuressaare Hospital, Maardu Manor, Palmse Manor, the Commandant's Garden on Toompea in Tallinn, SEB Bank in Tallinn, the Russian Embassy in Luxembourg). Kolk graduated from Tartu Art School in 1962 and from the State Art Institute of the ESSR in the speciality of sculpture in 1967. She has been awarded the Kristjan Raud Prize (1981).

artists.b: Lõpetas 1937 Viljandi Maakonna Poeglaste Gümnaasiumi ja 1946 TÜ arstiteaduskonna. 1946–1951 TÜ üldkirurgia kateedri assistent, 1951–1952 hospitaalkirurgia kateedri assistent, 1952–1960 Jõhvi haigla kirurgia osakonna juhataja, 1960–1962 Viljandi Rajooni Keskhaigla kirurg, 1962–1968 kirurgia osakonna juhataja, 1968–1978 peaarsti asetäitja ravi alal, 1978–1994 haiglas ja polikliinikus kirurg.
artists.ben: Graduated in 1937 from Viljandi County Boys' Gymnasium and in 1946 from the University of Tartu Faculty of Medicine. 1946–1951 assistant at the Department of General Surgery of the University of Tartu, 1951–1952 assistant at the Department of Hospital Surgery, 1952–1960 head of the surgery department of Jõhvi Hospital, 1960–1962 surgeon at Viljandi District Central Hospital, 1962–1968 head of the surgery department, 1968–1978 deputy chief physician for treatment, 1978–1994 surgeon at the hospital and polyclinic.

artists.b: Noore naise või tüdruku poolprofiilis portree. Tüdruk istub küljetsi portreteerija suunas, seljas tumesinises toonis rõivad. Tumedad juuksed on üle pealae kokku seotud punase paelaga. Tüdruku selja taga seinal paistab riputatud maal.
artists.ben: A half-profile portrait of a young woman or girl. The girl sits sideways towards the portraitist, wearing clothing in a dark blue tone. Her dark hair is tied together over the crown of the head with a red ribbon. Behind the girl's back, on the wall, a hung painting is visible.

artists.b: Maali esiplaanil jõgi ja seal suplevad alasti naised. Kokku pildil 14 naist, nendest vees 6. Enamus naisi (7) istuvad, lamavad valgetel rättidel jõe paremal kaldal. Vasakul kaldal aluspesus naine riietub. All vasakul on ühel naisel käte vahel laps. Maali ülemine taust roheline, liivakarva äärega jõekallas. Paremal küljel puu, taamal erinevate suurustega põõsad. Näha on ka taevast, ühtlaselt sinine.
artists.ben: In the foreground of the painting a river with naked women bathing in it. In total there are 14 women in the picture, of which 6 are in the water. Most of the women (7) sit or lie on white towels on the right bank of the river. On the left bank a woman in underwear is getting dressed. At the bottom left one of the women has a child in her arms. The upper background of the painting is green, with a sandy-coloured edge of the riverbank. On the right side a tree, in the distance bushes of various sizes. The sky is also visible, uniformly blue.

Kristi Kongi (1985) is an Estonian painter and installation artist whose work focuses on colour, light, and space, often in paintings which take the form of installations created for specific settings. In her most recent projects Kongi used colour and light as a way to collect and preserve memories, by creating immersive, colourful spatial installations. These works relate to the space where they’re located as well as exploring the memories of the spaces the artist has visited.

Kristi Kongi emerged in the art scene during the 2010s. Her works are characterised by bright colours and the use of personal narratives that have become increasingly abstract. The personal subjects of a young girl’s life, such as love, loneliness, partying and popular culture characterised her first exhibitions – ‘transformer’ (2010, Draakon gallery) and ‘HEAVEN’ (in collaboration alongside Marta Stratskas, 2010 at Vaal gallery).

Her visual language became more abstract during the exhibition Androgynous Mind Machines (a collaborative exhibition alongside Raoul Kurvitz, 2013 at Kunstihoone gallery) and with the installation ‘There is Silence Between the Trees’ at the group exhibition ‘Merike Estna and I’m a Painting’ (2014, Kumu art museum). It was at this moment when she moved from canvas to immersive spatial installations. In the autumn of 2017 Kristi Kongi held a personal exhibition at Vaal gallery, titled ‘Aberration. Exercises with light and shadow’ where she used small-scale photographs taken on her research trip to Mexico City as a base for the paintings. An artist book accompanied the exhibition. In her newer works, Kongi has become even more tied to space and landscapes – using performative elements to explore the topics.

Kristi Kongi studied painting at Tartu Art College (BA, 2004-2008) and graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts painting department (MA, 2008-2011). She’s been awarded with Young Artist Prize (2011), Sadolin Art Prize (2013) and was nominated for the Köler Prize in 2016. Kongi was awarded with the Konrad Mägi Prize in 2017. She is an associate professor at Estonian Academy of Arts painting department. Kristi Kongi is among the recipients of the national artists' salary between 2022-2024. She was awarded with Estonian Cultural Endowment’s annual award (2020).

artists.b: Väljapaistev eesti kujur, monumentalist, maalija ning keraamik. Jaan Koort õppis Tartus Hugo Treffneri gümnaasiumis ja saksa käsitööliste seltsi joonistuskursustel, 1902-05 Peterburis Stieglitzi kunstikoolis. Elas 1905-15 Pariisis, õppides skulptuuri ja maali. Töötas 1915-16 ja 1920 Moskvas. 1919 juhatas Lõuna-Eesti kunstikaitsetoimkonda. 1921-22 oli Tallinna kunsttööstuskooli skulptuuritöökoja juhataja. 1927 viibis Austraalias. 1934-35 töötas Venemaal Gželi keraamikatehase kunstnikuna.
grp: school:Saint Petersburg Stieglitz State Academy of Art and Design
artists.ben: A prominent Estonian sculptor, monumentalist, painter and ceramicist. Jaan Koort studied at Hugo Treffner's Gymnasium in Tartu and at the drawing courses of the German craftsmen's society, and in 1902-05 at Stieglitz's Art School in Peterburi. He lived in Paris in 1905-15, studying sculpture and painting. He worked in Moscow in 1915-16 and 1920. In 1919 he headed the South Estonian Art Protection Committee. In 1921-22 he was the head of the sculpture workshop of the Tallinn School of Applied Art. In 1927 he stayed in Australia. In 1934-35 he worked in Russia as an artist at the Gzhel ceramics factory.

artists.b: Artist of investigations and reconstructions, working in photography, video and installation.
artists.ben:
Karel Koplimets (1986) is a photographer, video and installation artist, working with notions like urban space, fear, paranoia, prejudice and criminality. In his latest projects, Koplimets explores travelling and migration caused by economic and geopolitical realities, expressed in phenomena like shopping tourism and commuting. One of the most notable traits of Koplimets' work is the psychological aspect – his large scale installations influence the viewers' sense of space.

Together with artists Sigrid Viir and Taaniel Raudsepp, Koplimets initiated the art project OÜ Visible Solutions (2010–ongoing), investigating the relationship between art and economy. Their works analyse various aspects of the creative economy, for example, the situation where artists are also entrepreneurs, making art into merchandise.

In several of his projects, Koplimets has blended the everyday with fiction, creating works where the fragile line between reality and imagination is ambivalent or blurred. His “Suburbs of Fear” (2012) explores fears related to urban environment. The artist was interested in residential areas and how people consider some of those areas to have a poor reputation. “Case No 12. Kalamaja” (2016), exhibited at Draakoni Gallery, focused on gentrification and paranormal phenomena occurring around the artist's neighbourhood. Koplimets shifts the viewer's sense of space by creating a tense and frightening atmosphere in his photos. The video installation in the gallery's basement centred on an appearing and disappearing human figure and the resulting anxiety in the viewer.

In projects “Case No 11. TALSINKI” (2016/1017) and “Case No 13. Waiting for the Ship of Empties” (2017) Koplimets was looking at migration between Estonia and Finland. The first to be observed were cruise ship passengers, both tourists and workers, who often commute to their job on the other side of the Baltic Sea. Among the cruise tourists there is a considerable amount of people visiting Estonia to buy cheap alcohol. So the economic relations between Finland and Estonia should be viewed from two sides: tourists contribute to the Estonian economy, and Estonians working in Finland enliven the economy there. The artist's interest in shopping tourism and commuters was also evident in “Case No 13. Waiting for the Ship of Empties”. In Helsinki, Koplimets built a raft from the empties of various alcoholic drinks with Estonian tax stamps, and used it to sail to Estonia. After successfully landing in Tallinn the raft of empties together with a video installation about the journey was exhibited in.

artists.b: Raivo Korstnik (1932-1992) on sündinud Ida-Virumaal Maidlas. Kunstihariduse omandas ERKI-s (1951–1957). Pärast ERKI lõpetamist algas 1960ndatel Korstniku loomingu tuntuim ja hinnatuim ajajärk. Sellesse aega mahub ka Korstniku ülesastumine 1966. aasta noortenäitusel, mida loetakse Eesti kunstiajaloo üheks olulisimaks uuele kunstile keskendunud väljapanekuks. Teadolevalt toimus kunstniku elu jooksul vaid üks isiknäitus. Olgugi, et tegemist oli tuntud ja tunnustatud kunstnikuga, eelistas ta aktiivsele näitustegevusele õppejõuna töötamist. Kuni oma surmani töötaski Korstnik Eesti NSV Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis (ERKIs) ning Tallinna Pedagoogilises Instituudis, jäädes paralleelselt seotuks tele- ja kinomaailmaga. Kui varem tõsteti Korstniku loomingust põhiliselt esile 1960ndate realistlikke, enamasti mereteemalisi maale, “karmi” stiili esindavaid tööstusmaastikke ning kubistlike sugemetega linnavaateid, siis nüüd pakuvad enim kõneainet kunstniku sürrealistlikud teosed. Sürrealistlike elemente võib leida kunstniku varastel maastikumaalidel, aktimaalidel ja krokiidel. Kunstnik maalis oma eluajal sageli ka maastikke ja Tallinna vaateid.
artists.ben: Raivo Korstnik (1932-1992) was born in Maidla, Ida-Virumaa. He received his art education at ERKI (1951–1957). After graduating from ERKI, the 1960s marked the beginning of Korstnik's best-known and most highly regarded period of creative work. This period also includes Korstnik's appearance at the 1966 youth exhibition, which is considered one of the most important displays in Estonian art history focused on new art. As far as is known, only one solo exhibition took place during the artist's lifetime. Although he was a well-known and recognized artist, he preferred working as a lecturer over active exhibition activity. Until his death Korstnik worked at the Estonian SSR State Art Institute (ERKI) and at the Tallinn Pedagogical Institute, while remaining connected in parallel to the world of television and film. Whereas earlier attention was mainly drawn to Korstnik's realistic works from the 1960s, mostly sea-themed paintings, industrial landscapes representing the "harsh style", and cityscapes with cubist touches, now it is the artist's surrealist works that attract the most attention. Surrealist elements can be found in the artist's early landscape paintings, nude paintings and sketches. During his lifetime the artist also frequently painted landscapes and views of Tallinn.

artists.b: Baltisaksa päritolu maalikunstnik (lahingumaalija). Sündis August von Kotzebue 3. abielust noorima pojana. Teenis Vene sõjaväes, õppis Peterburi kunstiakadeemias 1837-45 (A. Sauerweidi j), viibis Nikolai I pensionärina 1847-48 Pariisis. Alates 1850 elas Münchenis, 1851-53 reisis Šveitsis, Itaalias, Belgias. 1857 sai Peterburi kunstiakadeemia professoriks, oli ka keiserlik õuemaalija, Müncheni kunstiakadeemia auliige.
artists.ben: Painter of Baltic German origin (battle painter). Born as the youngest son of August von Kotzebue's 3rd marriage. Served in the Russian army, studied at the St Petersburg Academy of Arts 1837-45 (under A. Sauerweid), stayed in Paris 1847-48 as a pensioner of Nicholas I. From 1850 lived in Munich, 1851-53 travelled in Switzerland, Italy, Belgium. In 1857 became professor at the St Petersburg Academy of Arts, was also imperial court painter, honorary member of the Munich Academy of Arts.

artists.b: Pärnu Nikolai kiriku sisevaade pealöövile lääne suunas. Avaneb kesklöövi lõunapoolsest külglöövist lahutav madalate arkaadkaartega sein pilastrite ja ülal asuvate akendega. Pealöövi lõpul orelirõdu oreliga ja kiriku läänesissepääs selle all. Paremal kantsel baldahhiiniga. Kirikus suletud ustega pinkide read. Vasakult lõunalöövi akendest langeb valgust, üldiselt kirik hämar. Kahelt poolt raamivad vaadet triumfikaare küljed.;.
artists.ben: Interior view of Pärnu St. Nicholas' Church towards the main nave, facing west. Opens onto the wall with low arcade arches separating the central nave from the southern side nave, with pilasters and windows above. At the end of the main nave the organ gallery with the organ, and the church's western entrance below it. On the right, a pulpit with a canopy. In the church, rows of pews with closed doors. Light falls from the windows of the south nave on the left, the church is generally dim. The sides of the triumphal arch frame the view from both sides.;.

artists.b:
Sündis Peterburis rootslasest isa ja venelannast ema pojana. 1916–1917 õppis Peterburi Karl Mai Gümnaasiumis. Tuli 1921 Eestisse, lõpetas Narva Vene Gümnaasiumi. Õppis joonistamist Tallinnas K. Zeidleri ja E. Verberi juures. 1926-1928 õppis Riigi kunsttööstuskoolis graafikat ja 1928-1930 Tartus Pallases maali (N. Triigi ja A. Vabbe ateljeedes). Täiendas end Pariisis ja töötas Eestis maalikunstnikuna.

Külastas korduvalt Petseri kloostrit ja võttis 19-aastasena vastu õigeusu. Pärast II maailmasõda elas Pariisis, astus mungaseisusesse ja pühendus ikoonimaalimisele. Suri Püha Vaimu skiitas Mesnil-Saint-Denis lähedal Prantsusmaal.
artists.ben:
Born in St. Petersburg as the son of a Swedish father and a Russian mother. In 1916–1917 studied at the Karl May Gymnasium in St. Petersburg. Came to Estonia in 1921, graduated from the Narva Russian Gymnasium. Studied drawing in Tallinn under K. Zeidler and E. Verber. In 1926–1928 studied graphic art at the State School of Applied Art, and in 1928–1930 studied painting at Pallas in Tartu (in the studios of N. Triik and A. Vabbe). Continued his training in Paris and worked in Estonia as a painter.

He repeatedly visited the Pechory Monastery and at the age of 19 converted to Orthodoxy. After World War II he lived in Paris, entered monastic life and devoted himself to icon painting. He died at the Skete of the Holy Spirit near Mesnil-Saint-Denis in France.

artists.b: Kunstnik, karikaturist. Õppis Ranna vallakoolis, Tallinna Nikolai I gümnaasiumis, A. Laikmaa ateljeekoolis ja Peterburis Kunstide Edendamise Seltsi koolis. Krusteni  karikatuure ja šarže ilmus väljaannetes Sädemed, Kratt, Meie Mats, Kilk jt.
artists.ben: Artist, caricaturist. Studied at Ranna rural school, at the Nikolai I Gymnasium in Tallinn, at A. Laikmaa's studio school and in St. Petersburg at the school of the Society for the Advancement of the Arts. Krusten's caricatures and cartoons appeared in the publications Sädemed, Kratt, Meie Mats, Kilk and others.

artists.b: Liisa Kruusmägi on sündinud Tallinnas 1988 aastal. Ta õppis Eesti Kunstiakadeemia bakalaureuse astmes maali ja lõpetas joonistamise magistrantuuri 2013 aastal. Kruusmägi on täiendanud ennast Rhode Island Schools of Design, ja osalenud residentuuri programmides Vancouveris James Black gallerys, AIRY’s ja Yosugas Jaapanis ja Kitokia Grafika risotrüki stuudios Leedus. Isikunäituseid on toimunud Portugalis, Rootsis, Kanadas, Jaapanis, USA’s, Leedus, Lätis, Saksamaal ja Eestis. Ta on osalenud grupinäitustel nimetatutele lisaks veel osalenud Londonis, Berliinis, Slovaikkias, Itaalias, Soomes ja Venemaal. Liisa Kruusmägi on vabakutseline kunstnik, kes kasutab peamiselt maali ja joonistamise meediumit ja töötab illustraatorina. Ta on kunstnike liidu liige aastast 2013.
artists.ben: Liisa Kruusmägi was born in Tallinn in 1988. She studied painting at the bachelor's level at the Estonian Academy of Arts and completed her master's degree in drawing in 2013. Kruusmägi has furthered her studies at the Rhode Island School of Design, and has taken part in residency programmes in Vancouver at James Black Gallery, at AIRY, and at Yosuga in Japan, as well as at the Kitokia Grafika risograph printing studio in Lithuania. She has held solo exhibitions in Portugal, Sweden, Canada, Japan, the USA, Lithuania, Latvia, Germany and Estonia. In addition to those mentioned, she has also taken part in group exhibitions in London, Berlin, Slovakia, Italy, Finland and Russia. Liisa Kruusmägi is a freelance artist who mainly works with the media of painting and drawing and works as an illustrator. She has been a member of the Artists' Union since 2013.

artists.b: Photographer and film artist working on architecture, material and light.
artists.ben:
Paul Kuimet (1984) explores a world in his work that can only be experienced through a camera lens. He creates photo installations and films, which he shoots on 16 mm film. His practice centres on modernist forms and materials such as steel and glass, examining their relationship to the development of capitalism since the mid-19th century.

One of Kuimet’s earliest photo series – “In Vicinity” (2010) – presents a personal and collective experience of the 21st-century Estonian landscape. The series also captures new residential districts, where middle-class dreams meet relentless emptiness. In the exhibition “Viewfinders” (2011) at Tallinn Art Hall, Kuimet continued to explore questions surrounding the urban environment and the formation of its identity, placing the viewer at the heart of contradictions between objects, landscapes, and place names. As a documenter of the urban environment, he has also contributed to the book “Notes on Space: Estonian Monumental Painting 1879–2012”, which records local art history. The photographs published in the book combine a cool style, arithmetic clarity, and conceptual romanticism.

Kuimet’s films “2060”, “Exposure”, and “Golden Home”, produced between 2014 and 2017, express an interest in modernist forms. “Golden Home” originated from photographs depicting a terraced house named Kuldne Kodu (Estonian for Golden Home), built in the 1970s by the Pärnu KEK construction company (architect Toomas Rein). The film was inspired by the architectural similarity – but ideological contrast – between this building and a nearby apartment block built in the 2000s. Both films are defined by their dialogue with space, use of continuous repetition, and a meditative rhythm.

The exhibition “Late Afternoon”, held at the Tallinn City Gallery in 2016, examined reflections in architecture and interiors, the shifting qualities of light, and the subtleties of modernist experience of space. The works explored the viewer’s relationship with both real and photographed environments, as well as with movement and stillness. A highlight of the exhibition was “Perspective Study”, which featured reflections of the Atomium building, constructed in Brussels in 1958. The piece also connected to Kuimet’s ongoing interest in modernist utopias and their everyday manifestations. His films and photographs captured office spaces emptied at the end of the workday, where anonymous furniture, piles of documents, and a solitary potted plant on a windowsill combined to evoke a world that is at once ordinary and aestheticised.

artists.b: Viive Kuks alustas kunstiõpinguid 1966 Tallinna Kergetööstustehnikumis kangaste kunstilise kujundamise erialal, mille lõpetas 1970. Samal aastal alustas Kuks õpinguid Tallinna Kunstiülikoolis (EKA) graafika erialal. Ta põhiliseks õpetajaks oli Evald Okas. 1976 sai ta vabagraafiku diplomi ja asus elama Võrru, tegustedes vabakutselise kunstnikuna. Viive Kuks on Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige 1984. aastast, näitustel esineb alates 1977. aastast.
artists.ben: Viive Kuks began her art studies in 1966 at the Tallinn Light Industry Technical School in the field of artistic textile design, which she completed in 1970. That same year Kuks began studies at the Tallinn Art University (EKA) in the field of graphic art. Her main teacher was Evald Okas. In 1976 she received a diploma in printmaking and moved to live in Võru, working as a freelance artist. Viive Kuks has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1984, and has participated in exhibitions since 1977.

artists.b: Ilme Kuld (1938) on arvukate lüüriliste naisfiguuride autor. Tema teosed on pälvinud suurt publikumenu. On kasutanud materjalina nii puud, plastmassi kui ka marmorit. Viimaste kümnendite jooksul on ta osalenud Euroopa skulptuurisümpoosionidel ning märkimisväärne osa tema figuraalsetest skulptuuridest on jäänudki välismaale, eriti Prantsusmaale. Ilme Kuld on ühtviisi meisterlik nii puuskulptuuris kui ka marmoris. Osa tema teostest on valatud ka pronksi.
artists.ben: Ilme Kuld (1938) is the author of numerous lyrical female figures. Her works have won great public favour. She has used wood, plastic as well as marble as materials. Over the last few decades she has participated in European sculpture symposia, and a considerable part of her figural sculptures have remained abroad, especially in France. Ilme Kuld is equally masterful in wood sculpture and in marble. Some of her works have also been cast in bronze.

artists.b: Riho Kuld (1936) on enamikule tallinlastest tuttav oma valge „Raadiotuviga” (1975) raadiomaja seinal. Ta astus Eesti kunstiavalikkuse ette modernismilaines 1960. aastate keskel ja oli üks Eesti skulptuuri uuendajaid. Riho Kulla barokselt mänglevas liikumises skulptuurid on mõjusad oma rikkalike struktuuride ja täpse kompositsiooniga. Tema loominguga on Eesti skulptuuris esindatud põhjamaades küllaltki erandlik keerukas liikumine ja tajutav dünaamiline jõud. Riho Kulla monumentaalloomingust on oma modernistlikus uuenduslikkuses eriti silmapaistev Kuressaare fašismiohvrite monument (1965) ja Tehumardi obelisk (1967; mõlemad on loodud koos Matti Varikuga). Ta on pälvinud Kristjan Raua preemia (1973).
artists.ben: Riho Kuld (1936) is familiar to most residents of Tallinn from his white "Raadiotuvi" ["Radio Dove"] (1975) on the wall of the radio building. He appeared before the Estonian art public in the wave of modernism in the mid-1960s and was one of the renewers of Estonian sculpture. Riho Kuld's sculptures, with their baroquely playful movement, are effective through their rich structures and precise composition. His work brings to Estonian sculpture a complex movement and a perceptible dynamic force that is fairly exceptional among the Nordic countries. Among Riho Kuld's monumental works, particularly outstanding in its modernist innovativeness are the Kuressaare monument to the victims of fascism (1965) and the Tehumardi obelisk (1967; both created together with Matti Varik). He has received the Kristjan Raud Prize (1973).

artists.b: Kulkoff on loonud vene juugendliku sümbolismi laadis maastikumaale, maalinud ka seltskonnategelaste ja kunstnike portreesid ning teatraalseid usuteemalisi maale. Kunstihariduse omandas Kulkoff Moskvas Maali-, Raid- ja Ehituskunstikoolis (ning pälvis I järgu kunstniku nimetuse).
artists.ben: Kulkoff created landscape paintings in the style of Russian Art Nouveau symbolism, and also painted portraits of society figures and artists as well as theatrical religious-themed paintings. Kulkoff received his art education in Moscow at the School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture (and was awarded the title of First-Class Artist).

artists.b: Küll täiendas ta end  K. S. Malevitši juures. Ta huvitus kubismist ja katsetas värvi ja maalitehnikatega. Ta püüdis luua oma, „vene kubismi“, kasutades vaikeludel tüüpilisis vene esemeid nagu samovar, balalaika ja vildid.
artists.ben: He also furthered his studies with K. S. Malevich. He was interested in Cubism and experimented with colour and painting techniques. He attempted to create his own "Russian Cubism", using typical Russian objects such as the samovar, balalaika and felt boots in still lifes.

artists.b: Tartu Lastekunstikooli galerii, mis 2013.aastast kannab nime Jakobi galerii, sai 2015. novembris 20. aastaseks. Galerii ajaloo jooksul on seal toimunud silmapaistvaid ja märgilisi näitusi, legendaarsed Tegevuskunstiööd ja performance`id.
artists.ben:
With Humour, the Absurd and Seriousness I Emerged. Bop and Bop! – Interview With Kaarel Kurismaa.Kaarel Kurismaa (1939) is one of the founders of Estonian sound and kinetic art. In his artworks Kurismaa brings together movement, light, sound and form, both in monumental and smaller objects.

His original approach and artistic expression were recognised early in his career – he was involved in two pioneering avant-garde group exhibitions in Estonia, “SOUP ’69” and “Harku ’75”. Kurismaa's early art machines reused examples of Soviet industrial design by factories such as Salvo, Estoplast and Norma. One of his best known works, the three giant megaphone sculpture titled “Dripping Sounds” (1975, Art Museum of Estonia) is inspired by the round forms of industrial design of the 1960s and images of mass culture, which can be seen as a reference to pop culture. Kurismaa uses seemingly simple imagery, constructing streamlined pulsating and sound-emitting kinetic devices from found objects. His bright-coloured works often feature mythological creatures, like “Leprechaun” (1974), “Dwarf Altar” (1973) and “Amor Column” (1973).

Since it was not easy to participate in official art exhibitions in the Soviet Union, Kurismaa looked for an alternative creative outlet and joined the prog-rock group Mess, performing in 1975 and 1976 at the assembly hall of the Tallinn Polytechnic Institute.

After the 1970s wave of avant-garde receded, Kurismaa worked as a film director at studios Eesti Joonisfilm and Nukufilm, painted, and created notable public sculptures. Of the latter, “Kinetic Object” for restaurant Gloria (1987), the stained glass series “Rhythm of Light” for Paide Cultural Centre and “Tallinn Tram Object” (1993) have survived to this day. However, many of his well-known works have perished, among them “Kinetic Object” (1980, with Härmo Härm and Rait Prääts, dismantled 2002) at the Tallinn Post Office, “Object” (1981, removed 2000) for the electrical company Põhja Kõrgepingevõrgud, “Column of Light” (1986) near the entrance of Tabasalu Secondary School.

artists.b: Sündinud 19.04.1956. Haridus: 1979 lõpetas Eesti Kunstiakadeemia (ERKI) sisearhitektina; 1994 kaitses kunstimagistri kraadi Eesti Kunstiakadeemia juures.
artists.ben: Born 19.04.1956. Education: in 1979 graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts (ERKI) as an interior architect; in 1994 defended a master's degree in art at the Estonian Academy of Arts.

artists.b: Raoul Kurvitz õppis ERKI-s (praegune Eesti Kunstiakadeemia) arhitektuuri, lõpetas 1984. aastal. Koos  Urmas Muruga moodustasid nad 1986. aastal grupeeringu Rühm T, peagi liitus nendega ka arhitekt Peeter Pere ning veel mitmeid loomeinimesi.
artists.ben: Raoul Kurvitz studied architecture at ERKI (present-day Estonian Academy of Arts), graduating in 1984. Together with Urmas Muru they formed the group Rühm T in 1986, soon joined by architect Peeter Pere as well as several other creative people.

artists.b: Aime Kuulbusch-Mölder (1942) astus Eesti kunstiellu 1970. aastate algul. Tema loominguga seonduvalt võib rääkida estetismi taasväärtustamisest skulptuuris. Väljapeetud vormi ning meisterliku pinnatöötlusega figuurid ja portreed haakusid 1970. aastate alguse uue põlvkonna esteetikaga. Tema 1970. aastail loodud portreid noortest Eesti kunstnikest ja intellektuaalidest – nende seas näiteks Juhan Viiding, Malle Leis, Tiit Pääsuke jt – võib vaadelda kui koondportreed kogu tollasest nõukogulikule režiimile vastanduvast loomingulise intelligentsi põlvkonnast. 1970.–1980. aastail loodud portreeskulptuurid ning portreeliselt lahendatud kultuuri- ja haridustegelaste mälestussambad järgivad 1970. aastatel väljakujunenud esteetilisi kaanoneid. Ta on eelistanud materjalina pronksi, ent loonud ka dekoratiivseid šamottfiguure ning kasutanud plastmassi ja alumiiniumi. 1980. aastail kujunes temast üks viljakamaid monumentaalkunstnikke. Aime Kuulbusch lõpetas 1969. aastal ENSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi. Ta on pälvinud Kristjan Raua kunstipreemia (1983) ning nimetatud ENSV teeneliseks kunstnikuks (1984).
artists.ben: Aime Kuulbusch-Mölder (1942) entered Estonian art life at the beginning of the 1970s. In connection with her work, one can speak of a revaluation of aestheticism in sculpture. Her figures and portraits, with their restrained form and masterful surface treatment, connected with the aesthetics of the new generation of the early 1970s. Her portraits created in the 1970s of young Estonian artists and intellectuals – among them, for example, Juhan Viiding, Malle Leis, Tiit Pääsuke and others – can be viewed as a collective portrait of the entire generation of creative intelligentsia of the time that stood in opposition to the Soviet regime. The portrait sculptures created in the 1970s–1980s, as well as memorial monuments to cultural and educational figures rendered in a portrait-like manner, follow the aesthetic canons established in the 1970s. As a material she has preferred bronze, but has also created decorative chamotte figures and used plastic and aluminium. In the 1980s she became one of the most prolific monumental artists. Aime Kuulbusch graduated from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1969. She has been awarded the Kristjan Raud Art Prize (1983) and named Honoured Artist of the Estonian SSR (1984).

artists.b: Sündis Tuhalaane vallas Viljandimaal, siirdus pärast keskkooli lõpetamist Peterburi, kus astus Stieglitzi kunstikooli, mille lõpetas 1902 esimese eestlasena dekoratsiooni- ja klaasimaali alal. Kunstikooli nõukogu poolt valiti ta kooli klaasmaali osakonna juhatajaks, misjärele käis erialalisi teadmisi täiendamas Pariisis ja Müncheni Kuninglikus Klaasimaali Instituudis. Hiljem käis samal otstarbel Darmstatdis ning maalis Vene keisrikoja kabineti ülesandel suurem klaasimaali Peeter Pauli kindluse mausoleumi tarbeks. Maalis klaasimaal-altaripildi ka Vladimiri katedraali. 1905 oli keiser Nikolai II poolt Darmstadti ehitatud vene kiriku sisedekoratsiooni-maali juhiks. Reisis korduvalt Saksamaa, Prantsusmaa, Itaalia kunstikoolides ja muuseumides ning Türgis, Kreekas, Egiptuses, Palestiinas ja Süürias. Oli 13 aastat joonistusõpetaja Peterhofi gümnaasiumis ja St Katharina koolis Peterburis. 1917 lõpetas diplomiga Keiserliku Arheloogiainstituudi. 1918-1929 oli õpetaja Leningradi I reaalkoolis ning määrati Eesti Töörahva Ülikooli professoriks. 1920 naasis Eestisse ning asus tööle Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis, Tallinna Tehnikumis ning Konservatooriumis. 1925-1928 oli Eesti Kunstimuuseumi direktor, 1926. aastast Eesti Kunstnike Liidu esimees, 1935 aastast Eesti Akadeemilise Kutseõiguslike Kunstnike Koondise esimees. Läks erru 1940. aastal.
grp: school:Saint Petersburg Stieglitz State Academy of Art and Design
artists.ben: He was born in Tuhalaane Parish, Viljandimaa, and after finishing secondary school moved to St Petersburg, where he entered the Stieglitz School of Art, which he graduated from in 1902, becoming the first Estonian to complete studies in decorative and glass painting. He was elected by the school's council as head of the glass painting department, after which he went to further his professional knowledge in Paris and at the Royal Institute of Glass Painting in Munich. Later he went to Darmstadt for the same purpose, and painted, on commission from the Russian imperial court's chancery, a large glass painting for the mausoleum of the Peter and Paul Fortress. He also painted a glass-painting altarpiece for Vladimir Cathedral. In 1905 he was head of the interior decorative painting of the Russian church built in Darmstadt by Emperor Nicholas II. He travelled repeatedly to art schools and museums in Germany, France and Italy, as well as to Turkey, Greece, Egypt, Palestine and Syria. He was a drawing teacher for 13 years at the Peterhof gymnasium and at St Catherine's School in St Petersburg. In 1917 he graduated with a diploma from the Imperial Archaeological Institute. From 1918 to 1929 he was a teacher at Leningrad's 1st Realschule and was appointed professor at the Estonian Workers' University. In 1920 he returned to Estonia and began working at the State School of Applied Art, the Tallinn Technical School and the Conservatory. From 1925 to 1928 he was director of the Estonian Art Museum, from 1926 chairman of the Estonian Artists' Union, and from 1935 chairman of the Estonian Academic Association of Professional Artists. He retired in 1940.

artists.b: Tartu painter who worked toward abstraction outside official exhibition life.
artists.ben: Tartu painter who worked toward abstraction outside official exhibition life.

artists.b: Endel Kõks õppis Tartu Ülikoolis filosoofiat ja psühholoogiat. Kunstiõpinguid alustas 1934. aastal Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis Pallas, mille lõpetas 1940. aastal Ado Vabbe õpilasena. 1944. aastal põgenes ta Saksamaale, kus oli üks esimese sõjapõgenike kunstinäituse organiseerijaid 1945. Oli Geislingeni põgenikelaagris moodustatud Eesti Kujutavate Kunstnike Keskuse esimene esimees. 1950. aastal siirdus Kõks Rootsi ja asus elama Örebrosse.

1848 astus Peterburi Kunstide Akadeemia õhtukursustele ning 1851 sai täieõiguslikuks õpilaseks, mille lõpetas ajaloomaali alal (lõputöö "Herakles toob Kerberose põrguväravast". Peale õpinguid täiendas end välismaal.
artists.ben: In 1848 enrolled in the evening courses of the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts and in 1851 became a full-fledged student, which he completed in the field of history painting (diploma work "Hercules Brings Cerberus from the Gates of Hell"). After his studies he continued his education abroad.

artists.b: MuIS dates this Gerhard von Kügelgen 1806–1883 — a later member of the Baltic-German Kügelgen family of painters, not the Romantic portraitist (1772–1820) of the same name.
artists.ben: MuIS dates this Gerhard von Kügelgen 1806–1883 — a later member of the Baltic-German Kügelgen family of painters, not the Romantic portraitist (1772–1820) of the same name.

artists.b: Hermann von Kügelgen (1828-1897) oli Carl ja Emilie von Kügelgeni noorim laps. Ta sündis Eestis, õppis Tallinna Toomkoolis ja sai insenerihariduse Dresdenis. Pärast esimese abikaasa Emma surma abiellus ta Tartu kunstniku August Matthias Hageni tütre Johannaga. Kügelgen oli Tartu reaalkooli ja Saksa Käsitööliste Seltsi kunstikursuste õpetaja. Ta suri 1897. aastal Tartus.
artists.ben: Hermann von Kügelgen (1828-1897) was the youngest child of Carl and Emilie von Kügelgen. He was born in Estonia, studied at the Tallinn Cathedral School, and received an engineering education in Dresden. After the death of his first wife Emma, he married Johanna, daughter of the Tartu artist August Matthias Hagen. Kügelgen was a teacher at the Tartu Realschule and at the art courses of the German Craftsmen's Society. He died in 1897 in Tartu.

Neeme Külm (1974) is a sculpture and installation artist working with site-specific and minimalist spatial installations. In his works created for a public space, Külm often creates spatial shifts and plays with emotions, making the viewer physically participate in the piece, raising questions about social and political issues.

Külm has been exhibiting since the 1990s, his most notable works were created in the early 2000s. In 2001 Külm took part in an exhibition of artistic interventions in the public space of Tallinn, titled “On the Ruins of Capitalism” (curated by Anders Härm), where he created a traffic jam by blocking a gate between two streets in the Old Town with a pile of logs. This installation-intervention focused on the volume and mass of a specific structure and material, its central components being a large mass and gravity. In Külm's work, his focus on gravity has been seen as a repeating element, as a reference to his background as a sculptor. At the same time, a crucial element of his practice is a dialogue with the public space.

In the mid-2000s Külm created video works, addressing existentialism through the physical properties of gravity. In these works, the artist takes the role of protagonist, often using the image of hanging, falling, floating, or bearing heavy weights, to focus on the existential angst and awareness of mortality (e.g. “Hangs”, 2004; “Sleep”, 2004; “Untitled”, 2004; “Fountain”, 2005–2006). The 2005 video “Beslan“ shows that Külm can also use heaviness as a metaphor to address political conflicts – in the video the artist carries around the lid of a coffin in front of the Russian Embassy in Tallinn to commemorate those who died in the Beslan hostage crisis. Nevertheless, a political tone is not the goal for the artist, rather, it is the contextual frame of the moment, in which the work was created.

In Külm's work, the theme of political conflicts peaked with the 2008 project “Gas Pipe” at the Venice Architecture Biennale (together with Maarja Kask and Ralf Lõoke, curated by Ingrid Ruudi). “Gas Pipe” consisted of a 60 metre bright yellow steel pipe, set up in the Giardini between the Russian and the German pavilion, commenting on the Baltic Sea Nord Stream gas pipe debate, causing controversy at the time. “Gas Pipe” was the strongest international project in Estonian architecture in the 2000s, highlighting the spatial and architectural qualities of politics. The work was a conceptual installation project that, among other things, asked questions about the relationship between infrastructure and architecture, making.

artists.b: Painter of flat, affectionate portraits of public figures and buildings.
artists.ben: Painter of flat, affectionate portraits of public figures and buildings.

artists.b: Mati Kütt (s. 1947 Tallinnas) on maalikunstnik ning animatsioonfilmide režissöör. 2001–2002 töötas ta Ameerikas, Colorado osariigi pealinnas Denveris Rocky Mountaini Kunsti- ja Disainikolledžis eksperimentaalanimatsiooni õppejõuna. Kütt on Eesti Kinoliidu (1985), Eesti Kunstnike Liidu (1999) ja Eesti Maalikunstnike Liidu liige (1999).
artists.ben: Mati Kütt (b. 1947 in Tallinn) is a painter and animated film director. In 2001–2002 he worked in America, in Denver, the capital of the state of Colorado, as a lecturer in experimental animation at the Rocky Mountain College of Art and Design. Kütt is a member of the Estonian Filmmakers' Union (1985), the Estonian Artists' Association (1999) and the Estonian Painters' Association (1999).

artists.b: Tarrvi Laamann (s. 1973) on kunstnik, DJ ja tuntumaid reggae-kultuuri eestvedajaid Eestis. Laamann on lõpetanud Eesti Kunstiakadeemia magistriõppe graafika erialal (2000) ning kuulub alates 1994. a. Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liikmeskonda. Alates 1998. aastast on Laamann korraldanud reggae-kultuuri tutvustavaid ürituste sarja Bashment.
artists.ben: Tarrvi Laamann (b. 1973) is an artist, DJ and one of the best-known promoters of reggae culture in Estonia. Laamann graduated with a master's degree in graphic art from the Estonian Academy of Arts (2000) and has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1994. Since 1998 Laamann has organised the Bashment series of events introducing reggae culture.

artists.b: Tõnis Laanemaa (sündinud 1937) on õppinud Tartu kunstikoolis maalimist ning Eesti Riiklikus Instituudis graafikat. 1960. aastate Eesti kunsti uuendusliku rühmituse ANK’64 esialgne juht ja hiljem liige. Näitustel esinemist alustas Tõnis maalidega, tuntust kogus eelkõige vabagraafika ja plakatitega, kuid läbi ajastu on ta eksponeerinud nii akte, portreid kui abstraktseid kompositsioone. 1970. aastast alates on Laanemaa osalenud mitmetel näitustel Baltikumis, Poolas, Ungaris, Tšehhis, Saksamaal, Venemaal, Hollandis. Tõnis Laanemaa kuulub kunstnike põlvkonda, kellele korralik natuurist joonistamine on endastmõistetav. Ta on tuntust kogunud ka aktijoonistajana ning on hinnatud joonistusõpetajana. .
artists.ben: Tõnis Laanemaa (born 1937) studied painting at the Tartu Art School and graphic art at the Estonian State Institute. Initial leader and later member of ANK'64, the innovative Estonian art group of the 1960s. Tõnis began exhibiting with paintings, but gained recognition primarily for his free graphic art and posters, although throughout his career he has also exhibited nudes, portraits and abstract compositions. Since 1970 Laanemaa has taken part in numerous exhibitions in the Baltic states, Poland, Hungary, Czechia, Germany, Russia, and the Netherlands. Tõnis Laanemaa belongs to the generation of artists for whom proper drawing from nature is self-evident. He has also gained recognition as a figure drawer and is a highly regarded drawing teacher.

artists.b: 1924 liitus Eesti Kunstnikkude Rühmaga ja sai selle vaimseks juhiks, 1928 toimetas EKR programmilist almanahhi Uue Kunsti Raamat, 1926–1927 Eesti Kunsti aastaraamatut ja 1928–1929 noorsooajakirja Taie. Esines EKKKY ja RaKÜ näitustel. Avaldas kunstikriitikat ajalehtedes ja ajakirjades Olion, Looming ning Kunst ja Kirjandus. Töötas õpetajana Tallinna koolides 1945. aastani (J. Westholmi gümn. jm), seejärel oli vabakutseline kunstnik.
artists.ben: In 1924 he joined the Estonian Artists' Group and became its spiritual leader, in 1928 he edited the EKR's programmatic almanac Uue Kunsti Raamat (The Book of New Art), in 1926-1927 the Estonian Art yearbook, and in 1928-1929 the youth magazine Taie. He participated in the exhibitions of EKKKY and RaKÜ. He published art criticism in the newspapers and magazines Olion, Looming, and Kunst ja Kirjandus. He worked as a teacher in Tallinn schools until 1945 (J. Westholm Gymnasium, among others), after which he was a freelance artist.

artists.b: Tema varasem vabalooming keskendub peamiselt laste ja noorukite portreedele ning aktifiguuridele. 1930. aastate lõpul ja sõja-aastail valminud kompositsioonid mõjuvad oma hapra ekspressiivse figuurikäsitusega väga õrnade ja poeetilistena. Lydia Laasi nõukogude perioodi figuraalsed teosed omandasid 1960. aastaile iseloomuliku lihtsa askeetliku vormikultuuri. Alates 1945. aastast töötas ta vabakunstnikuna Tallinnas, olles Eesti esimestest naisskulptoritest ainus, kes kohandus sõjajärgseil aastakümneil nõukoguliku kunstieluga.
artists.ben: Her earlier free creative work focuses mainly on portraits of children and adolescents and on nude figures. Compositions made in the late 1930s and during the war years have a very delicate and poetic effect due to their fragile, expressive treatment of the figure. Lydia Laas's figurative works of the Soviet period acquired the simple, ascetic culture of form characteristic of the 1960s. From 1945 she worked as a freelance artist in Tallinn, being the only one of Estonia's first women sculptors who adapted to Soviet art life in the postwar decades.

artists.b: Sündis Tallinnas ukrainlasest vasksepa pojana, õppis 1922-27 Tartus"Pallases" maalikunsti. 1929, 1936-37 ja 1939 oli Pariisis õppereisidel. 1939 abiellus Anita Obst'iga (Oeste).1927-37 oli Võrus vabakunstnik, 1937-41 "Pallases" graafika õppejõud. 1937 sai Pariisi maailmanäitusel audiplomi, 1939 ja 1940 Eesti Raamatufondi auhinna. Liitus 1940 Tartus kunstielu reorganiseerijatega. Arreteeriti 26.05.1943 sakslaste poolt. Osaliselt vanglas valmis mapp "Põlevkivitööstus", mille signatuuri juures on trellid. Hukati arvatavasti 23.07.1944 Tallinna lähedal.
artists.ben: He was born in Tallinn as the son of a Ukrainian coppersmith, studied painting at "Pallas" in Tartu in 1922–27. In 1929, 1936–37 and 1939 he was on study trips to Paris. In 1939 he married Anita Obst (Oeste). In 1927–37 he was a free artist in Võru, in 1937–41 a teacher of graphic art at "Pallas". In 1937 he received an honourable diploma at the Paris World Exhibition, and in 1939 and 1940 the Estonian Book Fund prize. In 1940 he joined the reorganisers of art life in Tartu. He was arrested by the Germans on 26.05.1943. The portfolio "Põlevkivitööstus" ["Oil Shale Industry"], the signature of which includes bars, was partly completed in prison. He was presumably executed on 23.07.1944 near Tallinn.

artists.b: Käis aastatel 18931898 Cornelia Niclaseni nelja-, hiljem viieklassilises saksa tütarlaste erakoolis. Pärast õpingute lõpetamist töötas ta raamatukaupluses müüjana. Hakkas 13-aastaselt luuletama saksa keeles.Aastal 1902 abiellus ta eesti raamatupidaja Carl Eduard Friedrich Hackeriga ning noorpaar kolis Kutinosse Moskva äärelinna. Neil oli 2 last. 1904. aastal armus Marie eesti maalikunstnikku Ants Laikmaasse. Laikmaa veenis Mariet, et ta oma luuletused tõlgiks eesti keelde, et hiljem need avaldada kohalikus ajalehes.Aastal 1906 pöördus Under tagasi Tallinna. 1913. aastal kohtus ta Artur Adsoniga, kes hakkas tema kirjatoimetajaks. Adson kogus Marie luulematerjali kokku, et avaldada esimene luulekogu.Aastal 1924 lahutas Marie Carl Hackerist ning abiellus Adsoniga.Marie Under kuulus isiklikku tundeluulet viljelevasse rühmitusse "Siuru" ja saavutas luuletajamaine esikkoguga "Sonetid", mis ilmus 1917. aastal.Under on eesti suurimaid lüürikuid. Tema sisendav ja tundeid täis looming kujutab elujanuselt armastust ja loodust. Hilisem, mõtisklevam luule juurdleb elu valguse- ja varjupoole üle. 1944. aastal põgenes Under Rootsi. Seal kirjutatud värssides võib tunda koduigatsust.Underi luulet on tõlgitud paljudesse keeltesse.(Wikipedia)
artists.ben: From 1893 to 1898 she attended Cornelia Niclasen's four-, later five-grade German girls' private school. After finishing her studies she worked as a salesperson in a bookshop. She began writing poetry in German at the age of 13. In 1902 she married the Estonian bookkeeper Carl Eduard Friedrich Hacker, and the young couple moved to Kutino, a suburb of Moscow. They had 2 children. In 1904 Marie fell in love with the Estonian painter Ants Laikmaa. Laikmaa persuaded Marie to translate her poems into Estonian so that they could later be published in a local newspaper. In 1906 Under returned to Tallinn. In 1913 she met Artur Adson, who became her literary editor. Adson gathered together Marie's poetic material in order to publish her first collection of poetry. In 1924 Marie divorced Carl Hacker and married Adson. Marie Under belonged to the group "Siuru", which cultivated personal, emotional poetry, and achieved fame as a poet with her debut collection "Sonetid" ["Sonnets"], published in 1917. Under is one of the greatest Estonian lyric poets. Her evocative and emotion-filled work portrays love and nature with a thirst for life. Her later, more contemplative poetry ponders the light and shadow sides of life. In 1944 Under fled to Sweden. In the verses she wrote there one can sense a longing for home. Under's poetry has been translated into many languages.

Marco Laimre (1968; Marko Laimre before 2004) is an artist whose work includes photography, installation, sculpture, painting, performance sound art, intervention, curation and text. Laimre’s work is not stylistically coherent, nor does he have a signature style; his artistic output is concept not media based. In his art, Laimre looks at common everyday phenomena, approaching them from the perspective of the humanities.

Marco Laimre studied painting in the early 1990s at the Estonian Academy of Art and entered the art scene as an anarchist, an uncompromising and critical artist. His early work has been categorised as part of the aggressive self-assertion practices of the generation that began its artistic path in the 1990s, expressed in the post-socialist context as institutional critique and New Left rhetoric in art. For example, in 1994 Laimre opened a marble memorial plaque at the lobby of the Estonian Academy of Arts stating: “The department of cave painting was founded here on 23.X.1994”. Many of his early works focus on the local political and cultural context and analyse the self-mythologisation and the discourse of freedom in the newly independent republic (“Shared territories”, 1995; “§ 45”, 1998, etc.). For example, his “Red arrow” (1996) is an interactive installation made of a quern-stone and speakers. When the quern-stone is turned in the direction the arrow indicates, a distorted version of the Estonian national anthem starts playing at the speed of which the stone is turned. The work was created for the Annual Exhibition of the Soros Center for Contemporary Arts, Estonia titled “Estonia as a sign” as an ironic comment on national self-mythologising.

Laimre’s early work clearly presents pieces that centre on “me” (“Me and art”, 1994; “Me and the constitution”, 1996; “Me and optimism”, 1996; “Me and theatre”, 1996, etc.) that defined the artist’s relationship to the world and explored structures of power and the symbolic order. His work often blends autobiographical and social elements in a polemical way, which results in the praise of individuality (“My world maps I–III”, 1997–2001) or presenting a common phenomenon as something personal (“Manifest Labjekti kohta”, 2000). The work “Sugarfree” (1996) is based on the artist’s personal experience in a psychiatric clinic and draws attention to isolation as a mechanism of institutional violence. Performances “Bonj-njonj-nonj-non-now” (1999) and “L’ile mysterieuse” (2000) refer to artists’ fate and role in society in a bodily and masochist manner, pointing to the continuous need to disregard no.

artists.b: 1975. a. 1. augustist elas ja töötas ta Hiiumaal. Esialgseks töökohaks oli Hiiumaa Tarbijate Kooperatiiv, kus ta oli reklaamikunstnikuks.  Kärdla kultuurikeskuses töötas Ott alates aastast 1994,  töötades selle aja jooksul nii kunstiringi juhendajana, kunstnikuna kui ka kuraatorina.
artists.ben: From 1 August 1975 he lived and worked in Hiiumaa. His first place of work was the Hiiumaa Consumers' Cooperative, where he was an advertising artist. Ott worked at the Kärdla Culture Centre from 1994, working during this time as an art circle instructor, as an artist, and as a curator.

artists.n: The Elfriede Jelinek School of English Language

artists.b: Õppis ERKI-s (EKA) 1966-1971 arhitektuuri, töötas 1971-1974 Tallinna Restaureerimisvalitsuses arhitektina. Aastast 1990 on ERKI õppejõud, alatest 1995 professor. 1992-1998 oli õppejõud Helsingi kunstikoolis "Maa", 1993-1996 kooli juhtkonna liige, 1994. aastal oli Helsingi Tehnoloogiainstituudi külalisprofessor, 1997, 2002, 2005 külalisprofessor Eesti Muusikaakadeemias. 2001-2002 oli ta Tartu Ülikooli vabade kunstide professor.
artists.ben:
Leonhard Lapin (1947-2022) was one of Estonia’s most noteworthy avant-garde artists. He started out at the end of the 1960s with radical artistic innovation, and was the leading figure in introducing Pop Art, Suprematism, Neo-Avantgarde and performance in Estonia. Additionally, he also propagated innovative ideas in architecture, studied and introduced the ideas of Zen-Buddhism, and has written fiction and poetry, as well as art and architecture theory.

During his architecture studies at the Estonian State Art Institute, Lapin exhibited alongside his fellow-students Ando Keskküla, Andres Tolts, Ülevi Eljand, Rein Mets and Gunnar Meyer at the show “SOUP '69” that gave birth to Pop Art in Estonia. At the exhibition Lapin exhibited Pop-inspired coloured drawings, based on magnified fragments of old kitsch postcards (“Kiss of a Bunny”). A year later he created gouache drawings, among them “Lydia Koidula”, inspired by the portraits of pop icons from the USA.

Lapin's Pop Art period also includes the first Estonian original comic “Benno Bladrikorn – joie de vivre, views, and a useless death in the Pelegria Café ” (1970). An equally notable work is Lapin's artistic contribution to Rain Raamat's Pop-Psychedelic cartoon “Colour-Bird” (1974) that clearly shows his interest in Constructivism, De Stijl and Neo-Plasticism.

Lapin was greatly influenced by Russian avant-garde, especially Kazimir Malevich's theory of Suprematism. His works blend the avant-garde's concept of void and Eastern philosophy, well-known in Estonia in the 1960s and 1970s, which Lapin termed “objective art”. One of its expressions was geometrical art, which Lapin exhibited for the first time at the 1977 exhibition in the assembly hall of Estonian Artists' Association. At the time Lapin considered geometric art to be the artistic representation of the new, technical, and urbanised era.

artists.b: Heldur Laretei õppis Paul Luhtheina ja Evald Okase käe all Eesti NSV Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis graafikaosakonnas, mille lõpetas koos Peeter Ulase, Herald Eelma, Silvia Liibergi ja Olav Maraniga 1959. aastal. Laretei diplomitööks oli puugravüüride sari Shakespeare'i "Hamletile". 1960.–1970. aastatel viljeles vabagraafikat.
artists.ben: Heldur Laretei studied under Paul Luhtein and Evald Okas in the graphic art department of the Estonian SSR State Art Institute, which he graduated from together with Peeter Ulas, Herald Eelma, Silvia Liiberg and Olav Maran in 1959. Laretei's diploma work was a series of woodcuts for Shakespeare's "Hamlet". In the 1960s–1970s he practised free graphic art.

artists.b: Laurentsiust (Lauri Sillak; s. 1969 Kohtla-Järves) on oma loomingus nimetatud fetišistlikuks esteediks: ta läheneb oma objektile äärmise pühendumusega. Laurentsiuse teosed ühendavad akadeemilise maali popkunstiga. Hinnates ühelt poolt klassikalist vaikelu madalmaade 17. sajandi maalikoolkonna võtmes, on tema loomingut on tihti seostatud ka kitši ja camp’iga. Kasutades oskuslikuks kitši leksikat, on Laurentsiuse teosed samal ajal ühtlasi kitši paroodiaks, võimendades rõõmuga kitši elemente maksimumini.
artists.ben: Laurentsius (Lauri Sillak; b. 1969 in Kohtla-Järve) has been called a fetishistic aesthete in his work: he approaches his subject with extreme dedication. Laurentsius's works combine academic painting with pop art. While valuing, on the one hand, the classical still life in the manner of the 17th-century Low Countries school of painting, his oeuvre has also often been associated with kitsch and camp. By skilfully employing the lexicon of kitsch, Laurentsius's works are at the same time a parody of kitsch, joyfully amplifying the elements of kitsch to the maximum.

artists.b: Sündinud 30.07.1947. Eesti näitleja ja pedagoog. Isa meier, ema piimanduslaborant. Lõpetas 1965 Rakvere 1. Keskkooli, õppis 1965–68 Tallinna Polütehnilises Instituudis, lõpetas 1972 Tallinna Riikliku Konservatooriumi lavakunstikateedri. Töötanud 1972–75 ja 1978–95 Draamateatris näitlejana, olnud 1975–80 Tallinna Pedagoogilise Instituudi ja 1988–2004 Eesti Humanitaarinstituudi teatriala õppejõud, aastast 1995 Vanalinna Hariduskolleegiumi ja aastast 1997 samas ka Teatrikooli õpetaja (lavakõne jm). Kirjutanud koos Juhan Viidinguga näidendi „Olevused” (1980), koostanud ja lavastanud rühmatööna „Lavakavu” (I 1982, II 1984) ja kava „Kallis õhtu” (I 1992, II 2014). Laulnud (koos J. Viidingu ja Lembit Ulfsakiga) ansamblis Amor Trio, esinenud Viru varietees, mänginud telelavastustes („Mõmmi ja aabits”, 1973–77 ja 1998–99) ja filmis („Aeg maha!”, 1975, Eesti Telefilm), osalenud kontserdisarjas "Tornikell minu külas" (1979).
artists.ben: Born 30.07.1947. Estonian actor and pedagogue. Father a dairyman, mother a dairy laboratory assistant. Graduated from Rakvere 1st Secondary School in 1965, studied at Tallinn Polytechnic Institute in 1965–68, and graduated from the acting department of the Tallinn State Conservatory in 1972. Worked as an actor at the Drama Theatre in 1972–75 and 1978–95, was a lecturer in theatre studies at the Tallinn Pedagogical Institute in 1975–80 and at the Estonian Institute of Humanities in 1988–2004; from 1995 a teacher at the Old Town Educational Collegium and from 1997 also at its Theatre School (stage speech etc.). Wrote the play "Olevused" (1980) together with Juhan Viiding, compiled and directed as a group work "Lavakavu" (I 1982, II 1984) and the programme "Kallis õhtu" (I 1992, II 2014). Sang (together with J. Viiding and Lembit Ulfsak) in the ensemble Amor Trio, performed at the Viru Variety, played in TV productions ("Mõmmi ja aabits", 1973–77 and 1998–99) and in film ("Aeg maha!", 1975, Eesti Telefilm), took part in the concert series "Tornikell minu külas" (1979).

artists.b: Paremal esiplaanil kolm suletuttidega kiivrites sõdurit ründamas raudrüüs habemega meest, kelle habemest üks sõjamees on kinni haaranud. Teine sõdur on klammerdunud mehe juustesse ja ta hoiab käes lühikest mõõka, kolmas torkab habemikku odaga. Rünnatava jalge ees maas lamab juba üks elutu vanamees. Taamal marsivad sõdurid lippude ja odadega. Vasakul ees kolm sõdurit relvadega.
artists.ben: In the right foreground three soldiers in plumed helmets attack a bearded man in armour, whose beard one of the warriors has seized. A second soldier has clutched the man's hair and holds a short sword in his hand, a third stabs the bearded man with a spear. In front of the feet of the man under attack lies already one lifeless old man. In the distance soldiers march with flags and spears. On the left in front three soldiers with weapons.

artists.b: Sündinud 09.07.1940, Viljandi; surnud 09.08.2017.
artists.ben: Born 09.07.1940, Viljandi; died 09.08.2017.

artists.b: 1944.aastal siirdus Silvia Leitu elama Saksamaale. 1953. aastast elas ta Rootsis vabakutselise kunstnikuna, esines aktiivselt näitustel ning tegi raamatuillustratsioone. . Rootsis oli Silvia Leitu tuntud eelkõige virtuoosliku akvarellistina. Tema akvarellides Eesti rahvariietest on tunda kostüümikunstniku lähenemist.
artists.ben: In 1944 Silvia Leitu moved to live in Germany. From 1953 she lived in Sweden as a freelance artist, exhibiting actively and making book illustrations. In Sweden Silvia Leitu was known primarily as a virtuoso watercolourist. Her watercolours of Estonian folk costumes show the approach of a costume designer.

artists.b: Ceramic and performance artist of hybrid, half-animal bodies.
artists.ben:
Kris Lemsalu (1985) is sculptor and installation artist often experimenting with ceramics. Her art combines porcelain with fur, wool textile, silicone, found objects, sounds and other materials. Lemsalu’s work is characterised by her attention to colour and surface effects, an interest in archetypal and symbolic motifs, and an ironic and reflexive relationship to the media she uses, as well as staged scenes and the absurd. Her work often touches upon timeless and profoundly human themes such as birth, transformation and death, pain and grief, passion and love, and a celebration of life. Lemsalu’s installations sometimes act as a stage for her performances; the sculptural artworks become props or part of her costumes.

Lemsalu’s “things” – this is what the artist calls her installations – are imbued with a wayward sense of humour, ironically looking at things we have come to consider necessary, beautiful and desirable. She draws her inspiration simultaneously from pop culture, religious cults, death rituals, parties, friendships, and intimate relationships. Her poetic titles open an affective and Dionysian perspective that cannot be put into words. The curator Tamara Luuk has said that with her background in ceramics and the lifestyle of a nomad, Kris Lemsalu fills the gap in Estonian art history, which lacks artists with “primitive energy”, who create authentic and wild imagery.

In addition to installations, Lemsalu also creates musical performances. Both in her performances as well as in many of her installations, birth and death are a natural part of life, laughter and sadness help to cope with loss (e.g. “Going Going” with Kyp Malone at the Performa Biennial in New York, 2017; “In Heaven Everything is Fine” at KOKO London, 2017; “The Birth of Venus”, 2010). Lemsalu blends art and life in the everyday, as well as in her work and her public presence. She often wears theatrical costumes and make-up, and uses her artworks as a stage or props.

The circle of life and the celebration of life are recurring motifs in Lemsalu's works and exhibitions. In 2018, Lemsalu’s exhibition “4LIFE” (at Goldsmiths Centre for Contemporary Art in London) presented installations depicting human life from birth to death. In 2019 Lemsalu represented Estonia at the 58th Venice Biennale with the project “Birth V – Hi and Bye”. At the heart of the exhibition stood a three-level and four-sided fountain/totem sculpture depicting ceramic vaginas with arms and legs, symbolising the three stages of life: birth, transformation and death. The show highlighted the matriarchal power in t.

artists.b: Esko Lepp sündis sepa pojana. Õppis 1935–1940 Tallinnas Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis graafikat ja tarbegraafikat (juhendaja G. Reindorff). Oli ERM-i teenistuses. Täiendas end 1940–1941 Tartus Konrad Mäe nimelises Riigi Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis. 1941 astus hävituspataljoni. II maailmasõja ajal töötas Venemaal kolhoosis ja tehases, 1942 astus Punaarmeesse, 1943 kutsuti Jaroslavli eesti kunstnike kollektiivi, oli ka rindejoonistaja. 1943-1948 õppis Moskvas Surikovi-nim. kunstiinstituudis graafikat, mille lõpetas P. Pavlinovi õpilasena puugravüüri erialal. 1948–1951 oli Lepp Tallinna Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi (EKA) õppejõud, seejärel vabakunstnik. Loonud sõja- ja tööstusteemalisi teoseid, puugravüürile sarju, illustratsioone, akvarelle, eksliibriseid.
artists.ben: Esko Lepp was born the son of a blacksmith. He studied graphic art and applied graphics at the State School of Applied Art in Tallinn from 1935-1940 (supervisor G. Reindorff). He was in the service of the Estonian National Museum (ERM). He furthered his education from 1940-1941 at the Konrad Mägi State Higher Art School in Tartu. In 1941 he joined a destruction battalion. During the Second World War he worked in a kolkhoz and a factory in Russia, joined the Red Army in 1942, was called up in 1943 to the Yaroslavl collective of Estonian artists, and also worked as a front-line draughtsman. From 1943-1948 he studied graphic art at the Surikov Art Institute in Moscow, graduating as a student of P. Pavlinov in the field of woodcut. From 1948-1951 Lepp was a lecturer at the Tallinn State Art Institute (ERKI), after which he became a freelance artist. He created works on war and industrial themes, series of woodcuts, illustrations, watercolours, and ex libris.

artists.b: 1930. aastate maastikumaalidest on säilinud vaid üksikud näited, hulk töid hävis sõjasündmuste keerises.  1944. aasta septembris, napilt enne pagemist Saksamaale, viis Erich Leps suurema osa oma töödest sõja eest varju tollal Elevandi tänaval asunud muuseumisse, mis aga pommitamise käigus kannatada sai.  Sõjaeelseid töid leidib mitmete eraisikute, kollektsionääride ja kunstimuuseumide kogudes. Ainus töö, mis kunstnikul õnnestus põgenedes kaasa võtta, oli „Ema portree“, mis signeeringu ja dateeringuta on ilmselt kunstniku üks esimesi säilinud teoseid. Tumedal taustal portree järgib Rembrandtile omast n-ö. „keldriluugivalguse“ tehnikat, kus valgus on suunatud ühtlase vihuna maalitavale objektile.
artists.ben: Only a few examples of the landscape paintings of the 1930s have survived; a number of works were destroyed in the turmoil of the war. In September 1944, shortly before fleeing to Germany, Erich Leps took the majority of his works for safekeeping from the war to the museum then located on Elevandi Street, which was however damaged during bombing. Pre-war works can be found in the collections of various private individuals, collectors and art museums. The only work the artist managed to take with him while fleeing was "Ema portree" ["Portrait of Mother"], which, being unsigned and undated, is apparently one of the artist's earliest surviving works. The portrait against a dark background follows the technique characteristic of Rembrandt, the so-called "cellar-door lighting", where the light is directed in an even beam onto the object being painted.

artists.wdesc: Born 1819, in Toul (Meurthe-et-Moselle); died 1894, in Paris. French, Engraver. (1819–1894)

artists.b: Liivia Leškin (1956) on tegelenud pikalt moe- ja tekstii- likunstiga, viimasel kümnendil aga üha enam ka maali- kunstiga. Tema abstraktset maaliloomingut iseloomusta- vad enesekindlad žestid ning julgus intuitsioonile truuks jääda. Leškin on lõpetanud ERKI moedisaini eriala ning töötanud sealsamas pikalt ka moeeriala õppejõu ja pro- fessorina; osalenud aktiivselt kunstielus ja näitustel nii Eestis kui ka rahvusvaheliselt. Ta on Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Liivia Leškin (1956) has long been engaged in fashion and textile art, but in the last decade increasingly also in painting. Her abstract painting work is characterised by confident gestures and the courage to remain true to intuition. Leškin has graduated from ERKI in fashion design and worked there for a long time also as a lecturer and professor of the fashion department; she has actively participated in art life and exhibitions both in Estonia and internationally. She is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.b: Sündinud 17.08.1928, Tallinn; surnud 06.05.2025. Haridus: 1948-1954 Tartu Riiklik Kunstiinstituut (1951-1955 ERKI Tartu osakond)
