artists.b: Anna Mari Liivrand (snd 1993 Keilas) on Tallinnas elav ja töötav kunstnik. Ta omandas Eesti Kunstiakadeemias kaasaegse kunsti magistrikraadi (2022) ja installatsiooni ja skulptuuri bakalaureusekraadi (2016), täiendanud end Islandi Kunstiakadeemias (2015). Võitis Kaasaegse Kunsti Eesti Keskuse ja Kaamos Groupi asutatud kunstistipendiumi (2025), on Köler Prize 2025 nominent, pälvinud Eesti Kultuurkapitali aastapreemia (2021), Eduard Wiiralti preemia (2020) ja noore skulptori preemia (2014).
artists.ben:
Anna Mari Liivrand (1993) is a sculptor and installation artist, who also works with drawing. She is a sensitive creator interested in the conventional use of everyday materials and related unconscious judgements. Using a poetic language, Liivrand explores evanescence and melancholy in today's society. She has also looked at the fragility of art, and methods of preservation. In recent years, Liivrand has focused on everyday rituals.

In the 2017, Liivrand presented her solo exhibition “Unshatterable” at Hobusepea gallery. The title of the exhibition highlights the fact that laminated glass does not shatter when it breaks. The works at the show touched upon questions of preservation and conservation. The hanging talismans, created using fish oil capsules, brought to mind ways in which the human organism is held together, the glass wall and the abstract objects in it pointed to the existence of desires and ideas.

Liivrand addressed similar themes in her 2019 solo show “Beds and Ripples” at Draakon gallery, inspired by unusual ephemeral materials, questions of conservation, and everyday rituals. Liivrand used different colours, textures, and liquids, with a variety of textures to draw attention to the various properties of elements: in beds with a particular form, these can be decorative elements, when flowing freely, the same elements can be seen as kinetic sculptures. Installations, hanging talismans, and silk drawings created an ephemeral and melancholic atmosphere. The liquids used in these landscapes demonstrated Liivrand's continuous interest in unusual and unstable materials, like marzipan (“untitled”, 2014); fish oil capsules; textile, incl. silk and wool; rose essence (“Landscape for Rose Tears”, 2018); cat hair (“Monument Valley (May Contain Artefacts)”, 2018).

The solo exhibition “Monument Valley (May Contain Artefacts)” at the Showcase Gallery of the Estonian Academy of Arts once again displayed Liivrand's sensitive approach. Contextualising her work in the Contemporary Art Museum of Estonia and its surrounding area as a significant space in local history of architecture, Liivrand used stained glass and curious objects to create a temporary passage to a space where space can be experienced on a shifted scale.

artists.b: 1944. aastal põgenes Rootsi, kus töötas Kuninglikus Draamateatris dekoraatori abilisena ning Göteborgi Linnateatris dekoraatorina, hiljem rakenduskunsti aladel. 1956. aastal siirdus USA-sse ("Eesti kunst paguluses" 2010)
artists.ben: In 1944 he fled to Sweden, where he worked as an assistant decorator at the Royal Dramatic Theatre and as a decorator at the Gothenburg City Theatre, later in fields of applied art. In 1956 he moved to the USA ("Estonian Art in Exile" 2010)

artists.b: Sündinud Tuulas, surnud arvatavasti enne 1930.a. Õppis Riias kunsti, alustades G. v. Lischewitzi juures. 1878 - 1883 Weimari Kujutava Kunsti koolis animalist A. Brendeli juures ja prof. M. Thedy juures. Pärast lühiajalist Düsseldorfi perioodi asus elama Weimarisse.
artists.ben: Born in Tuula, died presumably before 1930. Studied art in Riga, beginning with G. v. Lischewitz. 1878-1883 at the Weimar School of Fine Art under the animal painter A. Brendel and Prof. M. Thedy. After a brief Düsseldorf period he settled in Weimar.

artists.b: Loik on eesti kunstnik, kes viljeles figuurikompositsiooni, akti-, interjööri- ja vaatemaali ning natüürmorti, samuti on tema loomingus tähtsal kohal portreemaal. Alustas jutustava käsitluslaadiga, kuid muutus hiljem üldistavamaks ja jõulisemaks, lisas oma loomingusse intensiivsed värvid. Kunstihariduse omandas Loik N. Rothi erastuudios ning Pallase kunstikoolis Ado Vabbe õpilasena. Aastatel 1950 – 1976 tegutses ta ERKI-s õppejõuna.
artists.ben: Loik is an Estonian artist who cultivated figure composition, nude, interior and view painting, as well as still life; portrait painting also occupies an important place in his oeuvre. He began with a narrative manner of treatment, but later became more generalising and forceful, adding intense colours to his work. Loik received his art education at N. Roth's private studio and at the Pallas art school as a student of Ado Vabbe. From 1950 to 1976 he worked as a teacher at ERKI.

artists.b: Õppis Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis aastatel 1924–1930. Täiendas end aastatel 1931–1932 Leipzigi riikliku graafika ja raamatukunsti akadeemia meistriklassis. Seejärel õpetas ta pikalt Riigi Tööstuskoolis. Pääses 1944. aastal õppejõutööle ENSV Riiklikus Tarbekunsti Instituudis, kus sai graafikakateedri juhatajaks (dots 1946, prof 1952) ja ta jäi sellesse ametisse 1982.
artists.ben: Studied at the State School of Applied Arts in the years 1924-1930. Furthered his studies in the years 1931-1932 in the master class of the Leipzig State Academy for Graphic Arts and Book Design. He then taught for a long time at the State Industrial School. In 1944 he obtained a teaching position at the Estonian SSR State Institute of Applied Arts, where he became head of the graphic art department (docent 1946, professor 1952) and remained in this position until 1982.

artists.b: Eve Luik (1949) on tegelenud maali ja graafikaga alates 1965 a. töötades tollal reklaamikunstnikuna. Aastast 1992 kuulub Eve Luik Eesti Kunstnike Liitu. Samast aastast on ta õpetaja Tartu Lastekunstikoolis. Eve Luige teoseid on eksponeeritud näitustel nii Eestis, Soomes, Itaalias, Prantsusmaal, Šveitsis, Hiinas, Jaapanis kui ka reprodutseeritud postkaartidel, plakatitel, ajakirjades ja illustratsioonidena raamatutes. Tema maagilise tiheduse ja meditatiivse süvenemisega looming on leidnud tee paljudesse erakogudesse. Eve on ennast teostanud ka sisekujundajana ning moelooja ja jumestajana Tartu ilusalongides. Pikka aega on kunstnik praktiseerinud ka ida võitluskunste imiteerivat Chi‐Jog‐Katat ja andnud oma oskusi edasi treenerina Tartu Ülikooli Spordihoones.
artists.ben: Eve Luik (1949) has worked in painting and printmaking since 1965, working at the time as an advertising artist. Since 1992 Eve Luik has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association. Since the same year she has been a teacher at the Tartu Children's Art School. Eve Luik's works have been exhibited at exhibitions in Estonia, Finland, Italy, France, Switzerland, China, Japan, as well as reproduced on postcards, posters, in magazines and as illustrations in books. Her work, with its magical density and meditative depth, has found its way into many private collections. Eve has also fulfilled herself as an interior designer, as well as a fashion designer and make-up artist in Tartu beauty salons. For a long time the artist has also practised Chi-Jog-Kata, which imitates Eastern martial arts, and has passed on her skills as a trainer at the Tartu University Sports Hall.

artists.b: Õppis Tallinna Peetri reaalkoolis, 1925-1928 (vaheaegadega) Tartu ülikooli füüsika-matemaatikateaduskonnas ja 1928-1936 Tartus kunstikoolis "Pallas". Mobiliseeriti 1941 Punaarmeesse, viibis NSVL tagalas Jaroslavlis ja Moskvas. 1946-1951 oli Tallinna Riikliku Tarbekunsti Instituudi õppejõud, 1947-1950 ENSV Kunstnike Liidu esimees. 1952-1967 töötas Viljandis eri ametikohtadel (lastekodu direktor jm)
artists.ben: He studied at the Tallinn Peetri Secondary School, in 1925-1928 (with interruptions) at the Faculty of Physics and Mathematics of the University of Tartu, and in 1928-1936 at the "Pallas" art school in Tartu. He was mobilised into the Red Army in 1941, and stayed in the rear of the USSR in Yaroslavl and Moscow. In 1946-1951 he was a lecturer at the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art, and in 1947-1950 chairman of the Artists' Union of the ESSR. In 1952-1967 he worked in Viljandi in various positions (director of a children's home, etc.)

artists.b: Lõpetas Pallase kunstikooli 1929, töötas Võru Ühisgümnaasiumis joonistusõpetajana, 1937. aastal asus Tartusse ning töötas õpetajana õhtugümnaasiumis. Esines KÜ Pallase ning KKSKV näitustel, kuulus Eesti Kunstnikkude Rühma.
artists.ben: Graduated from the Pallas Art School in 1929, worked as a drawing teacher at the Võru Joint Gymnasium, in 1937 moved to Tartu and worked as a teacher at the evening gymnasium. Exhibited at exhibitions of the Pallas Art Society and KKSKV, belonged to the Estonian Artists' Group.

artists.b: H. Lukk õppis 1912-1915 kunsti arvatavasti Helsingis, Soome kunstiühingu koolis. Viljeles juugendlikku ja neoimpressionistlikku kunsti (A. Finchi mõju). Voldemar Vaga nimetas H. Lukki ainsaks puhtaks neoimpressionistiks Eesti kunstis. Esines Eesti kunsti ülevaatenäitusel 1919, äratas tähelepanu.
grp: school:Academy of Fine Arts of Helsinki
artists.ben: H. Lukk studied art probably in 1912-1915 in Helsinki, at the school of the Finnish Art Society. He practised Art Nouveau and Neo-Impressionist art (influence of A. Finch). Voldemar Vaga called H. Lukk the only pure Neo-Impressionist in Estonian art. He participated in the survey exhibition of Estonian art in 1919, attracting attention.

artists.b: Arst, õppis Berliinis Albert Reimanni kunstikoolis 1922, TÜ kasvandik (meditsiin 1923-1929), kunstikool "Pallas" kursused (skulptuur), eraarst Tallinnas 1930-ndad, evakueerus Tatarstani 1941, arst Punaarmees a-st 1943, Tallinna II Ühendatud Haigla teraapia osakonna ordinaator a-st 1945, juhataja, peaarsti asetäitja polikliinilisel alal, "Estonia" teatri arst, õppejõud Tallinnas kunstiinstituudis.
artists.ben: Physician, studied in Berlin at Albert Reimann's art school in 1922, graduate of the University of Tartu (medicine 1923-1929), courses (sculpture) at the "Pallas" art school, private physician in Tallinn in the 1930s, evacuated to Tatarstan in 1941, physician in the Red Army from 1943, resident of the therapy department of Tallinn 2nd United Hospital from 1945, head, deputy chief physician for polyclinic matters, physician of the "Estonia" theatre, lecturer at the art institute in Tallinn.

artists.b: Edward von Lõngust pole tema enda sõnul füüsiliselt olemas. On vaid ideed. Ta on ühiselt jagatud teoreetiline kontseptsioon, multiidentiteedi ajastu peegeldus informatsiooniväljas, mis on genereerunud kollektiivteadvuse võngetest. Ta eostus infoühiskonna viljakates tingimustes paljude erinevate mõtete kokkulangemise tõttu, ning sündis ridade vahelt 21. sajandi kaasnähtusena. Ta on kogus mõtteid suures infoväljas, kes levib teadvusest teadvusesse nagu arvutiväline arvutiviirus.
artists.wdesc: Estonian street artist with undisclosed real name
artists.ben: According to his own words, Edward von Lõngus does not physically exist. There is only an idea. He is a jointly shared theoretical concept, a reflection of the era of multi-identity in the information field, generated from the vibrations of the collective consciousness. He was conceived in the fertile conditions of the information society through the coincidence of many different thoughts, and was born between the lines as a side effect of the 21st century. He is a collection of thoughts in a vast information field, spreading from consciousness to consciousness like a non-computer computer virus.

“Urmas Lüüs is an Estonian artist working in the fields of jewellery, sculpture, installation, writing, music and theatre.” That’s the short explanation on the artist’s website. Embroidery, video and photography can be added to the list of permanent media with which he is familiar. Lüüs’s diverse artistic practice is based on a material mystery physically embedded in everyday objects, often beginning with an obsessive process of accumulation. For example, his last solo exhibition at the Tütar Gallery in 2023 was based on over 7,000 photographs taken in cemeteries. The exhibition

As an artist on the theoretical horizon of neo-materialism, Lüüs inverts the most important principle of conceptualism, which states that “thought should be more intense than the force of its embodiment”

. The credo of Lüüs is reflected in the belief that the artistic text is kept in operation by the energy of the personal poetic manipulation of the material. At the most general level, this implies a conscious opposition to the dominant patterns of behaviour of both the industrial production society and the service-based information society. The medium/genre dialogues that characterise Lüüs derive from the arsenal of practical craftsmanship of the applied artist. The system is based on the eloquence of a seemingly useless decorative gesture.

As an artist, Lüüs has an uncanny enduring relationship with the aesthetic of saturated poverty. In his case, it ranges from the imagery of religious kitsch in Catholic cemeteries to dusty souvenir horns on the walls of hunting lodges; and from tasteless nature images made from amber shards to Richelieu embroidery. His relationship with these object worlds, picked up from the peripheries of our aesthetic focus, is anything but nostalgic-sentimental camp. It is characterised by the retroactive excitement of the lived-through, collected and piled-up material into grotesque images and witty stories.

artists.b: Tõnu Maarand (1940) lõi 1960. aastate lõpul ja 1970. aastail nii üldistatud vormiga figuurikompositsioone kui ka Eesti kultuuritegelaste karakteerseid portreid. Materjalidena kasutas ta nii pronksi kui ka puud ja kohrutatud vaske. Hilisemas loomingus haarab portreelooming üha suurema osa skulptori teostest. Maarand kavandas 1980.–1990. aastail mälestusmärke ja monumente, samuti hauamonumente ja dekoratiivseid seinapannoosid. Loominguliselt aktiivne on ta olnud ka 21. sajandi alguskümnendil. Ta lõpetas 1965. aastal ENSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi skulptorina ning on olnud kauaaegne skulptuuriõppejõud.
artists.ben: Tõnu Maarand (1940) created, in the late 1960s and in the 1970s, both figure compositions with generalized form and characteristic portraits of Estonian cultural figures. As materials he used bronze as well as wood and hammered copper. In his later work, portraiture takes up an ever greater share of the sculptor's output. In the 1980s–1990s Maarand designed memorials and monuments, as well as gravestone monuments and decorative wall panels. He has also been creatively active in the first decade of the 21st century. He graduated in 1965 from the ESSR State Art Institute as a sculptor and has long been a teacher of sculpture.

Angela Maasalu (1990) is a painter whose work focuses on personal and intimate themes. She is interested in contradictory human experiences, simultaneously recognising happiness and sadness, the drama and comedy of life. She often uses autobiographic elements to tell stories, combining them with symbolic and poetic imagery in order to expand her personal experience to a more widely understood level. Her work is metaphorical, fairytale-like and relies on narrative beyond the image.

Maasalu begun working with personal and everyday topics during her Master's studies and after graduating she has often explored the daily life of her generation. She focuses on themes like socialising, relationships, personal space and home. In 2016 Maasalu presented her solo exhibition “Home” at The Back Room project space in London and in 2017 followed it up with “Kodu II” (Home II) at Vaal Gallery. During the performative exhibition project Maasalu continued examining the various meanings of home, building a house in the gallery space and relating that to the institutional white cube. Highlighting oppositions like a home that's secure and a home that's made dangerous by close relationships, public and private space, and goals and real opportunities, Maasalu contemplated ways to make oneself heard in the context of contemporary art. She addressed the notion of security and the meaning of home also with her solo exhibition “Clytemnestra never loved you” (2016) at the DA Gallery in Greece. At the group show “Metaphors for a home” (2018) at Tartu Art Museum Maasalu looked at themes like homelessness, community and constantly being on the road.

In 2019 Maasalu presented the show “Throbwerk” (with Kate Lyddon, curated by Tamara Luuk), focusing on the meanings and functions of female bodies. Maasalu introduced expressive and emotional paintings and drawings that made visible the relationship between physical and emotional pain, love and hate, humiliation and shame, and desires and suffering. She broke the art historical codes of depicting women and violently brought to light how the (market) value of the female body as an object of consumption decreases in time.

At the end of 2019 Maasalu opened her solo exhibition at Hobusepea gallery titled “Cave for forgotten dreams”, centred on the image of the cave as storage for memories and dreams. This exhibition confirmed the artist's interest in text and demonstrated its influence on her work. In parallel to paintings Maasalu presented fairytale-like texts and allegories.

artists.b: Herman Aunapuu sündis 12. märtsil 1915 Kokandis, Turkestanis Kesk-Aasias, kus tema isa oli jaamaülem. Pere kolis Tartusse 1921. aastal. 1933. aastal astus Aunapuu Kõrgemasse Kunstikooli «Pallas», kus ta sai esmaklassilise hariduse Jaan Vahtra, Voldemar Melliku ja Villem Ormissoni käe all. Tema peamine juhendaja oli aga Ado Vabbe, kelle juures ta jätkas ka 1944. aasta sügisel Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis. 1945. aasta märtsis Aunapuu arreteeriti ja mõisteti erinõupidamise otsusega 8. septembrist kaheksaks aastaks paranduslike tööde laagrisse kodumaa reetmise eest. Vangilaagreis Komi ANSV-s ja Arhangelski oblastis viibis ta 1953. aastani.Esimest korda esines Herman Aunapuu 1940. aastal Kunstiühingu «Pallas» korraldatud näitusel, kus eksponeeriti annetusi ja deposiite – alates Konrad Mäest ja lõpetades Elmar Kitsega —, mis pidid saama alusvaraks loodavale Tartu Kunstimuuseumile. Aunapuu oli siis alles õpilane, keda aga kõrvutati juba Endel Kõksi ja Elmar Kitsega. Pärast vangilaagreid esines Aunapuu näitustel harva, õigupoolest suruti ta neilt kõrvale. Teda ei võetud kunagi Kunstnike Liitu. 1971. aastast saadik elas kunstnik tagasitõmbunult Tartu lähedal Peedul. Herman Aunapuu suri 29. detsembril 1998 Tartus ja on maetud Raadi Maarja kalmistule.
artists.ben: Herman Aunapuu was born on 12 March 1915 in Kokand, Turkestan, Central Asia, where his father was a stationmaster. The family moved to Tartu in 1921. In 1933 Aunapuu entered the Pallas Higher Art School, where he received a first-class education under Jaan Vahtra, Voldemar Mellik and Villem Ormisson. His main supervisor, however, was Ado Vabbe, under whom he also continued his studies at the Tartu State Art Institute from autumn 1944. In March 1945 Aunapuu was arrested and, by decision of a special tribunal, sentenced from 8 September to eight years in a corrective labour camp for betraying the homeland. He remained in labour camps in the Komi ASSR and Arkhangelsk Oblast until 1953. Herman Aunapuu first exhibited in 1940 at an exhibition organised by the Pallas Art Society, where donations and deposits were displayed — ranging from Konrad Mägi to Elmar Kits — which were meant to become the founding stock of the Tartu Art Museum then being established. Aunapuu was at that time still a student, yet he was already being compared to Endel Kõks and Elmar Kits. After the labour camps Aunapuu rarely exhibited; in fact he was pushed aside from exhibitions. He was never admitted to the Artists' Union. From 1971 onward the artist lived in seclusion near Tartu, in Peedu. Herman Aunapuu died on 29 December 1998 in Tartu and is buried at Raadi Maarja Cemetery.

artists.b: Arne Maasik (s. 1971 Tallinnas) tegutseb arhitekti ja kunstnikuna 1995. aastast, mil lõpetas Eesti Kunstiakadeemia arhitektuuribakalaureusena. 1997. aastal lõpetas samas arhitektuuriosakonna magistratuuri.
artists.ben: Arne Maasik (b. 1971 in Tallinn) has worked as an architect and artist since 1995, when he graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts with a bachelor's degree in architecture. In 1997 he completed his master's studies in the same department of architecture.

artists.b:
Sündis Rakveres , leeris käis 1930.a. Tema isa Karl Johannes Madiberg Jakobi poeg sündis 1875.a. Aasperes ja suri Injus 1950.a

Tema ema Liina sündis Injus 1872.a. ja suri Rakveres 1951.a. Nende esimesed lapsed sündisid Varudis -Injus 1903.a. , siis Moel -Robert, kes siirdus 1935.a. Tallinnasse, Harald sündis Rakveres 1909.a. tema poeg Arvo sündis 1935.a. ,.
artists.ben:
Born in Rakvere, confirmed in 1930. His father Karl Johannes Madiberg, son of Jakob, was born in 1875 in Aaspere and died in Injus in 1950.

His mother Liina was born in Injus in 1872 and died in Rakvere in 1951. Their first children were born in Varudi-Injus in 1903, then in Moe -Robert, who moved to Tallinn in 1935, Harald was born in Rakvere in 1909, his son Arvo was born in 1935,.

artists.b: Põhiosa tema loomingust moodustavad realistlikud, valgusküllased, vabalt maalitud linna- ja küla vaated, peamiseks elatusallikaks oli aga ootuspäraselt portree, mis arvestades kodanlastest tellijate maitset oli palju magusam ja idealiseerivam.
artists.ben: The main part of his work consists of realistic, light-filled, freely painted views of the city and countryside, but his principal source of income was, as expected, portraiture, which, taking into account the taste of bourgeois patrons, was much sweeter and more idealising.

artists.b: Aastatel 1955–1973 (vaheaegadega) oli ta õppejõud Tartu Kunstikoolis, 1988–1992 Tallinna Kunstiülikooli Tartu osakonnas ning 1992–1993 Tartu Ülikooli maaliosakonnas.
artists.ben: From 1955 to 1973 (with interruptions) he was a lecturer at the Tartu Art School, from 1988 to 1992 at the Tartu Department of Tallinn Art University, and from 1992 to 1993 at the Painting Department of the University of Tartu.

artists.b: Eva Juliane Magdalena (Magda) Zoege von Manteuffel sündis teistel andmetel 1852 ja suri 1938. Tema surma kuupäev ei ole selge. Ema poolt von Maydell. Ta õppis 1891/92 maali Onorato Carlandi juures Roomas ja Carl von Winkleri ateljees Tallinnas. Võttis osa rändnäitustest Eestis 1927 ja 1929/30, esines ka Riias, Peterburis, Moskvas akvarellidega. Bibl.: Kuno Hagen, Lexikon deutschbaltischen bildender Künstler 20. Jahrhundert, 1983, lk152.
artists.ben: Eva Juliane Magdalena (Magda) Zoege von Manteuffel was born, according to other sources, in 1852 and died in 1938. The date of her death is not clear. On her mother's side, von Maydell. She studied painting in 1891/92 under Onorato Carlandi in Rome and in Carl von Winkler's studio in Tallinn. She took part in touring exhibitions in Estonia in 1927 and 1929/30, and also exhibited watercolours in Riga, Petersburg and Moscow. Bibl.: Kuno Hagen, Lexikon deutschbaltischen bildender Künstler 20. Jahrhundert, 1983, p. 152.

artists.b: Elfriide Maran (1905–1997) alustas kunstiõpinguid aastatel 1916–1918 Pihkvas kunsttööstuskoolis keraamika erialal, õppis 1920. aastate algul Tartus Konrad Mäe ateljees maali ning töötas aastaid naisterõivaste rätsepana. Seejärel alustas ta 1945. aastal Tallinna Riiklikus Tarbekunsti Instituudis skulptuuriõpinguid, lõpetades ENSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi 1951. aastal. 1950. aastate lõpul vahetus tema loomingus natuuri järgiv piiratud realismikäsitus vabama, üldistatud vormimõju vastu. On teostanud töid peamiselt keraamilistes tehnikates, harvem kasutanud marmorit. Loomingus on valdav portreežanr ja dekoratiivne figuuriplastika.
artists.ben: Elfriide Maran (1905–1997) began her art studies in 1916–1918 at the School of Applied Arts in Pskov, in the ceramics speciality, studied painting in the early 1920s in Tartu in Konrad Mägi's studio, and worked for years as a seamstress of women's clothing. She then began sculpture studies in 1945 at the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art, graduating from the ESSR State Art Institute in 1951. In the late 1950s, her work's limited realism following nature was replaced by a freer, more generalised formal effect. She has made works mainly in ceramic techniques, more rarely using marble. The portrait genre and decorative figural sculpture predominate in her work.

artists.b: Õppis ERKI-s 1953-1959 graafikat. Oli 1950.-1960. aastatel avangardist. Alates 1968. aastast pöördus religioosse maali suunda ja maalis maastikke ning vaikelusid. Loonud ka kollaaže.
artists.ben: Studied printmaking at ERKI in 1953-1959. Was an avant-gardist in the 1950s-1960s. From 1968 turned toward religious painting and painted landscapes and still lifes. Has also created collages.

artists.b:
Skulptor Georgi Markelov (19.05. 1929 – 15.01. 2014) sündis Narvas ehitusettevõtja pojana ning õppis 1937-1943 Narva 6. algkoolis. Sõjaaegsetes õhurünnakutes hävis ka Georgi Markelovi isakodu. Tema isa küüditati nõukogude okupatsiooni alguses Siberisse.

Pärast sõjajärgseid õpinguid Väike-Maarja keskkoolis astus ta 1950. aastal Eesti Riiklikku Kunstiinstituuti, mille lõpetas 1956. aastal skulptuuri erialal. Samast aastast on Markelov tegutsenud vabakunstnikuna Tallinnas , 1959. aastal võeti ta Kunstnike Liidu liikmeks ning 1979. aastal anti tollase valitsuse poolt teenelise kunstniku aunimetus.

Georgi Markelov on viljelnud realistlikus laadis portreeskulptuuri ent tema loodud on ka 14 puuskulptuurist koosnev sari „Ei iialgi enam sõda”, millest mitmed näidised asuvad Eesti Kunstimuuseumi skulptuurikogus. 1970.-1980. aastail voolis ta tammepuidust üleelusuuruses formaadis V.I. Lenini portreid, mis enamasti omandati ametiasutustele. Pöördelistel aegadel sattusid ka neist portreenäidistest mõned muuseumide hoidlaisse. Vanem kunstnike- ning kunstihuviliste seltskond meenutab ilmselt just neid meisterlikult voolitud päid omaaegsete Tallinna Kunstihoone ülevaatenäituste ekspositsioonis. 1975. aastal sai kunstnik Kristjan Raua preemia just ühe sellise portree eest. Meisterliku nikerdajana armastas ta luua ka lüürilisemaid väikeskulptuure, lilli ja linde ning puust maske. 2010. aasta suvel üllatas Markelov nii kolleege kui kunstipublikut isiknäitusega Raja tänava Monumentaalkunsti maja galeriis. Ta esines kogu galeriiruumi täitva installatsiooniga „Lilled emale”, kus maad katsid enam kui 6000 virtuoosselt lõigatud erinevat lilleõit mahagonist, tammest, saarest, pärnapuust etc. See oli nagu omalaadne kokkuvõte ühe skulptori ja ka ühe erinevaid aegu üleelanud inimese tegevusest ja seisukohavõtust oma kohast tänases päevas.
artists.ben:
The sculptor Georgi Markelov (19.05.1929 – 15.01.2014) was born in Narva as the son of a construction entrepreneur and studied at Narva Primary School No. 6 from 1937 to 1943. Georgi Markelov's paternal home was also destroyed in wartime air raids. His father was deported to Siberia at the beginning of the Soviet occupation.

After post-war studies at Väike-Maarja Secondary School, he entered the Estonian State Art Institute in 1950, graduating in 1956 in the field of sculpture. From that same year Markelov worked as a freelance artist in Tallinn; in 1959 he was accepted as a member of the Artists' Union, and in 1979 he was awarded the honorary title of Meritorious Artist by the government of the time.

Georgi Markelov cultivated portrait sculpture in a realistic style, but he also created a series of 14 wood sculptures titled "Ei iialgi enam sõda" ("Never Again War"), several examples of which are held in the sculpture collection of the Art Museum of Estonia. In the 1970s–1980s he carved over-life-size portraits of V. I. Lenin from oak, most of which were acquired by state institutions. In turbulent times, some of these portrait examples also ended up in museum storage. The older generation of artists and art enthusiasts probably remember precisely these masterfully carved heads from the exhibitions of the Tallinn Art Hall's survey shows of the time. In 1975 the artist received the Kristjan Raud Prize for one such portrait. As a masterful carver, he also loved to create more lyrical small sculptures, flowers and birds, and wooden masks. In the summer of 2010 Markelov surprised both colleagues and the art audience with a solo exhibition at the gallery of the Monumental Art House on Raja Street. He presented an installation filling the entire gallery space, "Lilled emale" ("Flowers for Mother"), where the floor was covered with more than 6000 virtuosically carved flower blossoms of various kinds, made of mahogany, oak, ash, linden, etc. It was, as it were, a unique summation of the activity and standpoint of a sculptor — and of a person who had lived through various eras — regarding his place in today's world.

artists.b: Õppis aastani 1933 Tartus Hugo Treffneri Gümnaasiumis (joonistusõpetaja Eduard Ole),  lõpetas 1934 Tallinna poeglaste reaalgümnaasiumi, õppis 1934–38 Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis dekoratiivmaali alal. Töötas aastast 1936 Tallinna Töölisteatris. Kujundas aastast 1937 Draamateatris nukulavastusi, töötas samas teatris (vaheajaga) aastani 1950 (1948–50 peakunstnikuna), 1946–48 oli ühtlasi Noorsooteatri lavakujundaja. Töötas 1950– 61 Eesti NSV Teatriühingu Tööstuskombinaadis, hiljem töötas tarbegraafikuna (1968– 86 eksperimentaalkombinaadis Bit). Kujundas raamatuid, näiteks Perrault' „Punamütsike” (1942), Kreutzwaldi „Puulane ja tohtlane” (1945), ilukirja valdajana tegi kaanekujundusi Eesti NSV Teatriühingu väljaandele „Eesti NSV Teatrid” (1957–60). Eesti Entsüklopeedia.
artists.ben: She studied until 1933 at the Hugo Treffner Gymnasium in Tartu (drawing teacher Eduard Ole), graduated in 1934 from the Tallinn Boys' Real Gymnasium, studied in 1934–38 decorative painting at the State School of Applied Art. From 1936 she worked at the Tallinn Workers' Theatre. From 1937 she designed puppet productions at the Drama Theatre, working at the same theatre (with a break) until 1950 (as chief artist 1948–50); in 1946–48 she was also the stage designer of the Youth Theatre. In 1950–61 she worked at the Industrial Combine of the Estonian SSR Theatre Union, later working as an applied graphic artist (1968–86 at the experimental combine Bit). She designed books, for example Perrault's "Little Red Riding Hood" (1942), Kreutzwald's "Puulane ja tohtlane" (1945); as a fiction-book designer she made cover designs for the Estonian SSR Theatre Union's publication "Eesti NSV Teatrid" (1957–60). Estonian Encyclopaedia.

artists.b: Sündis vana kalendri järgi 29. novembril 1795 Teenuse (Stenhusen) mõisas Läänemaal, õppis 1804-1810 Neuwiedis hernhuutlaste koolis ja 1811-1812 Tallinna Toomkoolis. Teenis 1812-1820 Vene sõjaväes, töötas 1820-1822 Tartu ülikooli arhiivis, õppis C. A. Senffi juhendamisel ülikooli joonistuskoolis. 1822 reisis Berliinis ja Dresdenis, kuni 1827 täiendas end Itaalias kunsti alal. 1824 kohtus kunstnik A. L. Richteriga ja 1825 rändas koos temaga peatudes Civitellas. 1827-1829 elas Teenuse mõisas, 1829 asus Tartusse, kus rajas 1835 puugravüüritöökoja. Alustas Liivimaa ajaloole pühendatud vasegravüüride (+ofort) sarja "Viiskümmend pilti...", millest 1839 ilmus 1. vihk ja 1842 2. vihk ning veel kaks lehte. Valmistas graafilisi õppevahendeid, maalis portreid ja altarimaale (1835 Saarde kirik, 1837 Ruhja kirik, 1845 Põlva kirik). Maydelli Tartu Jaani kiriku maalid on hävinud. Ta oli ka skulptor, hõbeda- ja puidutöö kujundaja. Alates 1829 tegutses Tallinna Oleviste kiriku restaureerimisel (valmis 1840). Suri vana kalendri järgi 6. septembril 1846 Tallinnas, maetud Kullamaa kirikuaeda.
artists.ben: Born according to the old calendar on 29 November 1795 at Teenuse (Stenhusen) manor in Läänemaa, studied 1804-1810 at the Herrnhuter school in Neuwied and 1811-1812 at the Tallinn Cathedral School. Served 1812-1820 in the Russian army, worked 1820-1822 in the archive of Tartu University, studied under the guidance of C. A. Senff at the university's drawing school. In 1822 travelled in Berlin and Dresden, until 1827 furthered his education in art in Italy. In 1824 met the artist A. L. Richter and in 1825 travelled together with him, staying in Civitella. Lived 1827-1829 at Teenuse manor, in 1829 settled in Tartu, where in 1835 he founded a wood-engraving workshop. Began a series of copper engravings (+etchings) devoted to the history of Livonia, "Viiskümmend pilti..." ("Fifty Pictures..."), of which the 1st issue appeared in 1839 and the 2nd issue in 1842, along with two further sheets. Produced graphic teaching aids, painted portraits and altarpieces (1835 Saarde church, 1837 Ruhja church, 1845 Põlva church). Maydell's paintings for Tartu St John's Church have been destroyed. He was also a sculptor, and a designer of silverwork and woodwork. From 1829 he worked on the restoration of Tallinn's St Olaf's Church (completed 1840). Died according to the old calendar on 6 September 1846 in Tallinn, buried in the Kullamaa churchyard.

artists.b: Sündinud 02.03.1941, Raikküla vallas Jalase külas Reino talus. Haridus: 1959–1964 õppis elekriinseneriks Tallinna Tehnikaülikoolis.
artists.ben:
Raul Meel (1941) is one of the most recognised Estonian avant-garde artists. He has been exhibiting since the beginning of the 1970s. Meel was one of the proponents of radical renewals in Estonian art that were not officially recognised during the Soviet period. Since his work erred from the approved directions in Estonian art, he was unable to accept many of the invitations from the West. He was accepted into the Estonian Artists Association only in 1987.

Meel is well-known as a pioneer of concrete poetry in Estonia, a printmaker, painter, sculptor, installation and fire performance artist, author of numerous artist books and a beekeeper – Meel is convinced that his experience with bees has pushed him forwards in his artistic practice. Thematically, Meel has continuously focused on the relationship between nature, technology, poetry and art, his art is an amalgam of visual art and literature, language, text, word, syllables and music, sound, voice, and phonemes. On the one hand, Meel's work is characterised by aesthetic minimalism. On the other, Meel operates mainly as an artist of conceptual large-scale processes – this is how his extensive series are born, for example, the serigraphy series titled “Under the Sky” (Taeva all, 1973, 1992) is comprised of 3000 pages (63 × 65 cm each), which Meel has composed field ensembles (Raul Meel's original term) of varying volume but of no more than 60 images.

Deviating from the norm at the Soviet time, Meel did not begin his path as an artist at the State Art Institute of the Estonian SSR but considers himself an autodidact. Meel's artistic practice was considerably influenced by his studies at the Tallinn Polytechnic Institute (currently Tallinn University of Technology) and after discovering his calling, he was involved with the Tõnis Vint circle that played an important role in the Estonian avant-garde. Later, he had a close relationship with alternative artists in Moscow and a long-time friendship with Ilya Kabakov. Meel's first images he created using a typewriter that are usually regarded as concrete poetry were made in 1967 during his military service in the Soviet army above the Arctic circle in Severomorsk. “Considering the Soviet context with its dire lack of international information, it is more than likely that Meel arrived at his system of concrete poetry independently, without knowing anything about the pivotal art movements in the West,” writes art historian Sirje Helme in “History of Estonian Art, Vol. 6”.

Out of Meel's typewriter drawings grew a system, functioning still today, used to generate.

artists.b: Lõpetas 1915 hõbemedaliga Tallinna Tütarlaste kroonugümnaasiumi, seejärel õppis 1915–1916 Peterburis J. Bagajeva arhitektuurikursustel ning 1916–1918 Petrogradi Naiste Polütehnilises Instituudis arhitektuuri. Töötas 1918–1919 arhitekti abina Tallinna linnavalitsuses. 1919 esines esmakordselt Tartus kunstiühingu Pallas kunstinäitusel ning täiendas end Nikolai Triigi juures maali alal. 1920–1921 töötas Tartu Õpetajate Seminaris joonistusõpetajana. Viibis 1922-1923 korduvalt Saksamaal sanatooriumides. Esines 1925. aastast näitustel Eestis, ka Helsingis, Riias, Berliinis, Amsterdamis jm. Oli alates 1925 Eesti Kujutavate Kunstnikkude Keskühingu liige, 1931–1935 Eesti Kunstnikkude Rühma liige, 1936 Rakenduskunstnike Ühingu liige ja alates 1946 ENSV Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: In 1915 she graduated with a silver medal from the Tallinn Girls' Crown Gymnasium, then studied in 1915–1916 at J. Bagayev's architecture courses in Petersburg and in 1916–1918 architecture at the Petrograd Women's Polytechnic Institute. In 1918–1919 she worked as an assistant architect at the Tallinn City Government. In 1919 she first appeared at an art exhibition of the Pallas art society in Tartu and furthered her training in painting under Nikolai Triik. In 1920–1921 she worked as a drawing teacher at the Tartu Teachers' Seminary. In 1922–1923 she stayed repeatedly in sanatoriums in Germany. From 1925 she took part in exhibitions in Estonia, as well as in Helsinki, Riga, Berlin, Amsterdam and elsewhere. From 1925 she was a member of the Central Union of Estonian Fine Artists, in 1931–1935 a member of the Estonian Artists' Group, in 1936 a member of the Applied Artists' Union, and from 1946 a member of the ESSR Artists' Union.

artists.b: Ametis Aleksander III sõjasadamas. Sündis viis last. Perekond asus 1912 elama Tallinna, 1917-1918 elati Petrogradis. Natalie Mei elas alates 1930 kuni surmani Tallinn-Nõmmel eramus (koos ema ja õe Lydiaga). 1962 oli tal isikunäitus Tallinna kunstimuuseumis.

Margus Meinart  (s. 1969 Tartus) asus pärast Eesti Humanitaarinstituudi lõpetamist 1993. aastal õppima Tartu Kunstkooli mööbli kujundamist ja restaureerimist ning lõpetas selle eriala 1998. aastal. 1994-1995 aastal õppis maalimist Norras ning 1991-1996 aastal Tartus Konrad Mäe ateljees. Margus Meinart on saanud “Pallase” stipendiumi 1998. aastal, samuti Aino Järvesoo stipendiumi. Kunstiühingu “Pallas” liige on ta 1994. aastast, lisaks kuulub Meinart ka Tartu Kunstnike Liitu ja Tartu Restauraatorite Klubisse.
artists.ben: Margus Meinart (b. 1969 in Tartu), after graduating from the Estonian Institute of Humanities in 1993, began studying furniture design and restoration at the Tartu Art School, graduating in this field in 1998. In 1994–1995 he studied painting in Norway, and in 1991–1996 in Tartu in Konrad Mägi's studio. Margus Meinart received the "Pallas" scholarship in 1998, as well as the Aino Järvesoo scholarship. He has been a member of the "Pallas" Art Society since 1994, and Meinart also belongs to the Tartu Artists' Union and the Tartu Restorers' Club.

artists.b: Viimased elukohad: Karksi ja Karksi-Nuia (Karksi pastoraadi hoone), hiljem Viljandi. Tutvus 1946-47 aastal Elmar Kitse (1913-1972) ja Evald Okasega (1915 – 2011), kes käisid tihti Roberti juures Karksis suvitamas (mõjutus kunstiga tegelemiseks).Maalijana oli R. Meister peamiselt iseõppija. Tema lemmikžanrid on maastiku- ja lillemaal. Tütre, Mari Meister mälestuste järgi maalis isa kogu oma elu aja jooksul. Oli ka kirglik kalamees.
artists.ben: Last places of residence: Karksi and Karksi-Nuia (the building of the Karksi parsonage), later Viljandi. In 1946-47 he became acquainted with Elmar Kits (1913-1972) and Evald Okas (1915-2011), who often came to visit Robert in Karksi for the summer (an influence on his taking up art). As a painter R. Meister was mainly self-taught. His favourite genres are landscape and flower painting. According to the recollections of his daughter, Mari Meister, her father painted throughout his entire life. He was also a passionate fisherman.

artists.b:
Ülle Meister sündis 27. VIII 1948 Lüganusel, suri 6. I 2021 Tallinnas. 1967-1973 õppis ERKIs (EKA) graafikat, lõpetas raamatugraafikuna. Diplomitööks oli aabits, mis oli koolides kasutusel palju aastaid. Seejärel töötas ta kirjastuses Valgus.

Ülle Meister on kujundanud heliplaadiümbriseid ja postkaarte, loonud eksliibriseid, tegelenud vabagraafika ja akvarelliga.
artists.ben:
Ülle Meister was born 27. VIII 1948 in Lüganuse, died 6. I 2021 in Tallinn. 1967-1973 studied graphic art at ERKI (EKA), graduated as a book graphic artist. Her diploma work was a primer that was used in schools for many years. She then worked at the publishing house Valgus.

Ülle Meister has designed record sleeves and postcards, created ex libris, and worked in free graphic art and watercolour.

artists.b: Kujur ja pedagoogõppis ka Peterburis Stieglitzi kunstööstuskoolis,a. 1918 vabakunstnik,siis asus Tartusse olles mitmes koolis õpetaja,käis välismaal,a.1920 "Pallas" liige;1924 esimees; hiljem Tallinnas mitmetes koolides.
grp: school:Saint Petersburg Stieglitz State Academy of Art and Design

artists.b:
Andreas von Löwis of Menar sündis 4. jaanuaril 1778 (vana kalendri järgi 1877. aasta lõpus) Läänemaal Kirbla kihelkonnas Vanamõisas erukindrali pojana. 1794–97 oli ta Peterburis sõjaväeteenistuses, teenides vahtmeistrina ratsaväes. 1801. aastal siirdus õppima Jena ja 1803 Heidelbergi ülikooli, 1806–1808 õppis Schwetzingeni metsainstituudis.

1811. aastal valiti von Löwis of Menar Riias asuva Liivimaa Üldkasuliku ja Ökonoomilise Sotsieteedi sekretäriks. Ta korraldas selle tegevust ja oli sotsieteedi väljaannete toimetaja. Järgnevalt asus Tartusse ja õppis tõenäoliselt C. A. Senffi juures kunsti.

1816–39 võttis osa Friedrich Georg Wilhelm Struve juhendusel tehtud Liivimaa trigonomeetrilisest mõõdistamisest ja kaartide koostamisest.

Olulisim teos on ta enda illustreeritud ülevaade Liivimaa rüütlilossidest: Denkmäler aus der Vorzeit Liv- und Estlands I-II (1821, 1827). Suri Kaipeni (Keipene) mõisas Lätimaal/Liivimaal.
artists.ben:
Andreas von Löwis of Menar was born on 4 January 1778 (at the end of 1877 according to the old calendar) at Vanamõisa in Kirbla Parish, Läänemaa, the son of a retired general. In 1794–97 he was in military service in St. Petersburg, serving as a warrant officer in the cavalry. In 1801 he went to study at Jena and in 1803 at the University of Heidelberg, and in 1806–1808 studied at the Schwetzingen Forestry Institute.

In 1811 von Löwis of Menar was elected secretary of the Livonian Public Benefit and Economic Society based in Riga. He organised its activities and was the editor of the society's publications. He subsequently moved to Tartu and probably studied art under C. A. Senff.

In 1816–39 he took part in the trigonometric survey of Livonia and the compiling of maps carried out under the direction of Friedrich Georg Wilhelm Struve.

His most important work is his own illustrated survey of the knightly castles of Livonia: Denkmäler aus der Vorzeit Liv- und Estlands I-II (1821, 1827). He died at Kaipen (Keipene) manor in Latvia/Livonia.

artists.b: Herkki Erich Merila (s. 1964 Tallinnas) on DeStudio liikmena Eesti nüüdisaegse fotokunsti isa. Ja klassikule kohaselt köidab teda kõigist võimalikest motiividest igavikuilisim: naisekeha.
artists.ben: Herkki Erich Merila (b. 1964 in Tallinn) is, as a member of DeStudio, the father of Estonian contemporary photographic art. And, as befits a classic, he is drawn to the most eternal of all possible motifs: the female body.

artists.b: Portree on tehtud Rakvere Galerii 17. portreenäitusele "Meie, virulased!"  22.02.2024 - 03.2024. Autori sõnul sai ta inspiratsiooni ETV saatesarjast "Ainulaadne aastakäik", kus tutvustati 1953. aastal sündinud inimesi, kel on Eesti ühiskondlikus elus olnud väga oluline roll. Raivo Riim on aastaid olnud Virumaal aktiivne kultuuritegelane ja õpetaja.
artists.ben: The portrait was made for the 17th Portrait Exhibition of Rakvere Gallery "Meie, virulased!" 22.02.2024 - 03.2024. According to the author, he was inspired by the ETV programme series "Ainulaadne aastakäik", which presented people born in 1953 who have played a very significant role in Estonian public life. Raivo Riim has for years been an active cultural figure and teacher in Virumaa.

artists.b: Aarne Mesikäpp on lõpetanud Tartu Kunstikooli teatridekoratsiooni erialal ja ERKI graafika erialal. Alates 1967. aastast töötab Eesti Kunstiakadeemias õppejõu ja meistrina. On osalenud mitmetel ühisnäitustel ja korraldanud ka isiknäituseid.
artists.ben: Aarne Mesikäpp graduated from Tartu Art School in the field of theatre decoration and from ERKI in the field of graphic art. Since 1967 he has worked at the Estonian Academy of Arts as a lecturer and master craftsman. He has participated in numerous joint exhibitions and has also organised solo exhibitions.

artists.b: Alustas kunstiõpinguid A. Kaigorodovi juures. 1925-1929 õppis "Pallases" skulptuuri. 1929-30 täiendas ennast maali ja tarbekunsti alal Pariisis Conservatoire National des Arts et Métriers'is. Skulptor, maalikunstnik, tarbegraafik. Läks 1944 Saksamaale, a-st 1947 elas Inglismaal, a-st 1952 Kanadas Torontos. Oli 1940 EKKKÜ liige ja 1961-85 EKKT liige. Maetud Tartusse.
artists.ben: Began art studies under A. Kaigorodov. 1925-1929 studied sculpture at "Pallas". 1929-30 furthered his studies in painting and applied art in Paris at the Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers. Sculptor, painter, applied graphic artist. Went to Germany in 1944, from 1947 lived in England, from 1952 in Toronto, Canada. Was a member of EKKKÜ in 1940 and a member of EKKT from 1961-85. Buried in Tartu.

grp: school:Aalto University School of Arts, Design and Architecture

artists.b: Astus kunstiellu 1970. aastate algul, kui kõiki kunstivaldkondi puudutanud uus esteetika hakkas iseloomustama ka arenevat skulptuuri. Loomingu algusaastaid mõjutanud hüperrealism ja popkunst ühinesid varakult välja kujunenud groteskse inimesekujutusega. Autor ehitab siiani kompositsiooni üles humoorikate lavastustena. Eesti kunstiavalikkust hämmastasid 1970. aastail Mikofi üleelusuurused portreed. Enamasti on ta portreteerinud ühiskonnahierarhia tippu jõudnud suurmehi; tema äratuntavad ja klassikaliselt selgejoonelised portreelahendused sisaldavad alati ka midagi iroonilist. Loonud on ta ka üldtuntud avalikke skulptuure. Ta on panustanud perfektsele vormimängule ning üllatavate materjalide koosmõjule. Praegusel ajal on tema arsenalis vahe huumor, rõhutatult ajutised materjalid ja alatine valmisolek eksperimenteerida.
artists.ben: He entered the art world in the early 1970s, when a new aesthetic that touched all fields of art began to characterise the developing field of sculpture as well. The hyperrealism and pop art that influenced his early years of creative work merged early on with a grotesque depiction of the human figure that had already taken shape. To this day the author builds his compositions as humorous stagings. In the 1970s Mikoff's over-life-size portraits astonished the Estonian art public. He has mostly portrayed great men who reached the top of the social hierarchy; his recognisable and classically clear-lined portrait solutions always also contain something ironic. He has also created well-known public sculptures. He has contributed to a perfect play of form and the interaction of surprising materials. At present his arsenal includes dry humour, deliberately temporary materials and a constant readiness to experiment.

artists.b: Mildeberg tegutses 1925. aastast fotograafi ja rakenduskunstnikuna. Ta evakueeriti 1941. aastal Nõukogude Liidu tagalasse Baškiiriasse, kus töötas Birski rajoonis põllutöölisena. 1942–1945 oli Punaarmee Eesti Laskurkorpuses rindekunstnik ja fotograaf. 1945 sai Kunstnike Liidu liikmeks. Mildeberg töötas Tallinna naastes 1945. aastal Rahva Hääle fotokorrespondendina, oli aastatel 1945–1946 oli Mildeberg ajakirja Pikker tehniline toimetaja, hiljem vabakunstnik. Eelistas graafikatehnikaid, tegi šarže ja karikatuure, illustreeris raamatuid.
artists.ben: Mildeberg worked as a photographer and applied artist from 1925. In 1941 he was evacuated to the rear of the Soviet Union, to Bashkiria, where he worked as a farm labourer in the Birsk district. In 1942-1945 he was a front-line artist and photographer in the Estonian Rifle Corps of the Red Army. In 1945 he became a member of the Artists' Union. After returning to Tallinn, Mildeberg worked in 1945 as a photo correspondent for Rahva Hääle, in 1945-1946 Mildeberg was the technical editor of the magazine Pikker, later a freelance artist. He preferred graphic techniques, made caricatures and cartoons, and illustrated books.

artists.b: Photographer and video artist on labour, desire and the display window.
artists.ben:
Marge Monko (1976) is an artist combining mainly photography, video and installation in her work. Her influences include feminist, psychoanalytical and visual culture theory. She focuses on themes like cultural representations of women, women's work in a post-socialist context as well as desire for consumption and love in modern capitalist societies.

Monko first started exploring representations of women in Vienna as a Master’s student in photography, inspired by the visual archives of psychoanalysts and the work of surrealists. Her series of photographs “Studies of Bourgeoisie” (2006) bridged the gap between 19th century “hysterical femininity” and its contemporary equivalent. Monko staged scenes evoking hysteria and its treatment, exhibiting them side by side with photographs of places associated with psychoanalytical studies and Sigmund Freud. She suggested that hysteria was caused by taboos of the bourgeois society and traced how historic understanding of psychological conditions has contributed to the development of a representation of women as the weaker and emotional sex as well as that of the “mystical and compulsive woman”.

After her Master’s studies, Monko focused her attention on female workers (“Nora’s Sisters”, 2009), giving a voice to her contemporaries, women whose life was destabilised by the 2009 economic crisis and unemployment (“Forum”, 2009). This marked Monko’s turn towards the local post-socialist context, characterised by the tension between the Soviet legacy and values of the newly independent Estonia (“Shaken Not Stirred”, 2010). In her works of this period Monko was looking at issues like gender, nationality and language, highlighting that in post-socialist Estonia it is Russian-speaking women who are the most vulnerable. Monko’s projects from the end of the 2000s can be described both from the perspective of the social and documentalist turn as well as the feminist paradigm – she combines the roles of an archivist, director and documentalist, building solidarity with women from other nationalities and social groups.

In 2013, Monko presented the exhibition “How to Wear Red” at Tartu Art Museum (curated by Rael Artel) and at mumok in Vienna, which confirmed the artist’s continuous interest in the past and its manifestations in the present. The title of the show hints at the communist history and asks how to approach this legacy today. Monko tied the post-socialist context and the changing labour policies to grass roots activism and feminist themes. The work “Free Love” (2013) juxtaposed a newspaper article from 1905 of the sam.

Eleonore de Montesquiou (1979) is an Estonian-French artist, whose films focus on the relationship between people's life stories and their official history, as well as on personal and national identity. Her works take a documentative approach, expressed through film, drawing and text. Montesquiou is a socially sensitive artist, using empiric research methods like interview, observation and archival materials.

One of Montesquiou's first exhibitions, “My home is my castle” (Tallinn Art Hall Gallery, 2002) focused on telling stories about home. The artist interviewed people of various ages living in Tallinn, asking them to talk about the history and current usage of their language in their mother tongue, and later presented these stories in a video, and in a booklet.

The project “Atom cities” (2005), consisting of a two-volume book and films, documents the “invisible” part of Estonia: the forgotten Sillamäe and Paldiski, cities that had a strategic economic and military significance during the Soviet period. Montesquiou has documented how holidays that originated from the Soviet era are celebrated in the 21st century – compared to the more common method of using objects and archival photographs, hers is a remarkably refreshing approach. She shows the cities, which during the Cold War enjoyed many privileges, in a new light; offering her audience a look into the fears of the inhabitants of these former closed cities and taboos in Estonian society. Montesquiou also highlights the political aspect of nationality in this context without favouring one or the other ideology. One such example would be two videos recorded on September 1st, one in an Estonian school, the other in a Russian school: one shows a quiet and restrained environment, and the other an emotional, open and visually colourful atmosphere.

The border city Narva has a special place in Montesquiou's work – it has featured in several of her video works. For example, in “Fabrika” (2009, Art Museum of Estonia) shows Kreenholm as a phenomenon – in its totality and inevitable decline. In collaboration with students from the Estonian Academy of Arts, a three language newspaper the Narva Gazette (2018), was published to give an overview of the historic development of the city and provide observations and illustrations about Narva as it is today in the form of a diary: its streets and people, paragraphs of interviews that were previously published in Montesquiou's book “Na Grane / Narva – Ivangorod” (2009). Life in the border city is also discussed in the video work “Travellers” (2007) that tells the st.

artists.b: Viljeles tonaalset puugravüüri, joonistust ja maali. Sai tuntuks J. Kapi mälestussammast ning J. Köleri sarka kujutava puugravüüriga. Tema puugravüüritehnikas naljapilte ja ilustisi ilmus 1899-1908. aastatel Viljandi ajalehes „Rahvaleht“, ajalehe „Kodumaa“ lisas „Ulak“ (tiitliilustis) ja „Postimehe“ lisas. Samuti J. Ploompuu kirjastatud pühadealbumeis, ka vene pildikirjas „Нива“. Maalis Suure-Jaani ning selle ümbruse kultuuriinimeste ja seltsitegelaste portreid. Kavandas Suure-Jaani Tuletõrjujate Seltsi lipu ja pritsimaja lavaeesriide. Reprodutseerivast graafikast on tuntuim ja tehniliselt õnnestunuim I. Repini maalitud L. Tolstoi portree puugravüür.
grp: school:Saint Petersburg Stieglitz State Academy of Art and Design
artists.ben: He practised tonal woodcut, drawing and painting. He became known for the monument to J. Kapp and the woodcut depicting J. Köler's sarcophagus. His woodcut-technique caricatures and decorations appeared in the years 1899-1908 in the Viljandi newspaper "Rahvaleht", in the supplement "Ulak" of the newspaper "Kodumaa" (title decoration) and in the supplement of "Postimees". Also in the holiday albums published by J. Ploompuu, and in the Russian picture magazine "Нива". He painted portraits of cultural figures and society activists of Suure-Jaani and its surroundings. He designed the flag of the Suure-Jaani Fire Brigade Society and the stage curtain of the fire station. Of his reproductive graphic works, the most well-known and technically most successful is the woodcut of I. Repin's painted portrait of L. Tolstoy.

artists.b: 1944 põgenes Rootsi. Oli 1945–1948 Kesk-Rootsi E.E.L.K. piirkonna õpetaja. Rootsi kiriku teenistuses oli aastatel 1948–1981; 1973–1983 teenis E.E.L.K. Gotlandi  ja Norrköpingi kogudust. Rootsi praostkonna praost aastatel 1981–1983 ja Eesti Evangeeliumi Luteriusu Kiriku Konsistooriumi assessor 1982-83.
grp: school:Saint Petersburg Stieglitz State Academy of Art and Design
artists.ben: In 1944 he fled to Sweden. He was the pastor of the Central Sweden E.E.L.K. district in 1945–1948. He was in the service of the Church of Sweden in 1948–1981; in 1973–1983 he served the E.E.L.K. congregation of Gotland and Norrköping. He was provost of the Sweden deanery in 1981–1983 and assessor of the Consistory of the Estonian Evangelical Lutheran Church in 1982–83.

artists.b: 1980 lõpetas Tartu Kunstikooli. 1991 lõpetas Tallinna Kunstiülikooli maalijana. Õppejõud Tallinna Kunstikoolis. 1987. a esines noortenäitusel, 1989 vabariiklikul näitusel. 1992 KL liige. Isiknäitused 1989 G-galeriis, 1991 galerii Viro, Helsingi; 1992 Tokko&Arrak; 1993 Espoos; 1994 KH galerii; 1997 Sammas galerii; 1998 teater "Estonia"; 2002 Narva Hermani kindlus; 2004 Vaal galerii.
artists.ben: In 1980 he graduated from the Tartu Art School. In 1991 he graduated from the Tallinn Art University as a painter. Lecturer at the Tallinn Art School. In 1987 he took part in a youth exhibition, in 1989 in a national exhibition. In 1992 became a member of the Artists' Union. Solo exhibitions: 1989 at G-Gallery, 1991 at Galerie Viro, Helsinki; 1992 Tokko&Arrak; 1993 in Espoo; 1994 KH Gallery; 1997 Sammas Gallery; 1998 "Estonia" theatre; 2002 Narva Hermann Castle; 2004 Vaal Gallery.

artists.b: Rauno Thomas Moss (s- 1977 Tallinnas) on eesti maalikunstnik ja graafiline disainer, kes saavutas laialdase tuntuse must-valges koloriidis ning autoerootiliste maalidega. Kantuna huvist 19. sajandi meditsiini vastu, lahkab Moss sügavuti oma lapsepõlvemälestuste ning kogemuste puutepunkte, tehes seda elavas ning kergelt unenäolises sürrealistlikus võõrandumises. Tulemus on häiriv ning meeldejääv.
artists.ben: Rauno Thomas Moss (b. 1977 in Tallinn) is an Estonian painter and graphic designer who achieved widespread renown for his black-and-white colouring and autoerotic paintings. Carried by an interest in 19th-century medicine, Moss delves deeply into the touchpoints of his childhood memories and experiences, doing so in a vivid and slightly dreamlike surrealist estrangement. The result is disturbing and memorable.

artists.b: Looming skulptorina: Peeter Mudist (1942–2013) on suurimaid Eesti 20. sajandi maalikunstnikke, kelle maalikompositsioonid tuginevad realismile, kuid esitavad samas ka nägemuslikke kujutlusi. Ta lõpetas ENSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi 1967. aastal maalijana ning asus samal aastal ka skulptuure looma. Esimeste maalitud kipsist portreede ja figuuride asemele astusid 1970. aastate lõpus stiliseeritud vormiga graniitskulptuurid. Neis on autor ajuti töödelnud naturaalset kivi vaid minimaalselt. Ta on loonud ka tugevalt üldistatud portreeloomingut ning suureformaadilisi graniidist figuure. Peeter Mudistit on autasustatud Kristjan Raua preemiaga (1989), Konrad Mäe medaliga (1991) ning Valgetähe III klassi teenetemärgiga (2001).
artists.ben: Work as a sculptor: Peeter Mudist (1942–2013) is one of the greatest Estonian painters of the 20th century, whose painterly compositions are based on realism while also presenting visionary imagery. He graduated from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1967 as a painter and began creating sculptures that same year. His first painted plaster portraits and figures were succeeded in the late 1970s by granite sculptures of stylised form. In these, the author has at times worked the natural stone only minimally. He has also created strongly generalised portrait works and large-format granite figures. Peeter Mudist has been awarded the Kristjan Raud Prize (1989), the Konrad Mägi Medal (1991), and the Order of the White Star, III Class (2001).

artists.b: Täisportree - Püstformaadis istuva noore naisterahva portree, külgvaates, näoga vaataja poole. Valge põhjaga sinisekirjus kleidis blond daam. Esiplaanil parem käsi toetab tooli istme nurka, taamal vasak käsi süles. Kompositsioon: portreteeritav istub suunaga pildi paremale poole, põlved ja jalad jäävad pildiraamist välja. 2/3 maali foonist punakas roosa, alumine osa soe roheline toon. Tool punakas pruun. Maalitud laseerivalt dekoratiivses lakoonilises stiilis.
artists.ben: Full portrait - Portrait of a young woman sitting in upright format, in profile view, face turned toward the viewer. A blonde lady in a blue-patterned dress on a white ground. In the foreground the right hand rests on the corner of the chair seat, further back the left hand in the lap. Composition: the sitter sits facing the right side of the picture, the knees and legs extending beyond the picture frame. 2/3 of the painting's background is reddish pink, the lower part a warm green tone. The chair is reddish brown. Painted in a glazing, decorative, laconic style.

artists.b: (Ants Murakini vend) Karl Murakin oli maalimist õppinud A. Laikmaa juures. Ta kuulus harrastuskunstnikuna Viljandi kultuurimaja kunstiringi esimesse, vanemasse põlvkonda. Tema maalilooming paistab silma professionaalsusele küündiva meisterlikkusega. Kunstnik valdas suurepäraselt impressionistlikku värvikäsitlust ja realistlikku vormi.
artists.ben: (Ants Murakin's brother) Karl Murakin had studied painting under A. Laikmaa. As an amateur artist he belonged to the first, older generation of the Viljandi cultural centre's art circle. His painterly oeuvre stands out for a mastery approaching professional level. The artist had an excellent command of impressionistic colour treatment and realistic form.

artists.b: Photographer on nationality, belonging and the politics of the portrait.
artists.ben:
Tanja Murasvkaja (1978) works with photo, video, and installation, focusing mainly on questions of identity in Estonian society, influenced by historic processes and global developments.

Muravskaja is well known for her series of portraits, one of the earliest of which, “Positions” (2007), juxtaposes young Estonian artists with young Estonian Neo-Nazis – the first group wearing nothing but the Estonian flag covering their bodies, the second standing to attention next to the national flag. The series of portraits, “They, who sang together” (2008), and the exhibition of the same title, depicts politicians and key figures of the Singing Revolution and the Popular Front of Estonia. The close-ups show, on the one hand, how people have aged, but also raises the question of what has become of the new republic of Estonia that had its beginnings in the Singing Revolution of the 1980s. Muravskaja continues with a closely related theme in “Lucky Losers” (2009), presenting video portraits of real, imaginary, and potential local Russian leaders on a black background.

The portrait series “Estonian race” (2010) shows young men, although without a hint to their names or social background. With this the artist speculates on the identity of “a typical Estonian” and asks if a “race” of such kind actually exists. She continues exploring nationality and race in the series “Our Own” (2017), that depicts NATO soldiers sent to serve in Estonia. The series focused on national security, the impact of political conflicts on the sense of self, and the creation of contemporary identities in the changing geopolitical reality.

In the two-channel video work “Three sisters” (2015), Muravskaja interviewed her cousins who live in two different information spaces after the political and military conflict flared up in Ukraine. The video shows ideological differences between close relatives, and its permeation in the private sphere, fuelling conflict. “Three sisters” centres on a question of ethics: how to refrain from offending your family, making enemies of your sisters, insulting viewers' convictions, how to stay true to oneself and stand your ground.

Maarit Murka (1981) is a painter working in printmaking, installation and video. Her work is characterised by use of narrative, film-like seriality, and extreme technical detail.

Murka is considered one of the most skilled photorealist painters who, having mastered this painting technique – and manipulating it, for example, in her series “0.34” (2009) –, has moved on to other means of expression, like spatial installations, use of different media and life situations. For example, during a research trip to the Helmand province in Afghanistan, she documented the daily life of Estonian soldiers and contemporary tactical war strategies, resulting in an ephemeral spray painting, a series of photographs and paintings (2013–2014). Her interest in military themes is also evident in series such as “Short Art Film” (2009) and “Targets” (2011), where Murka depicts a game of positions and wordless communication. In the exhibition “Contact” (2014) Murka interpreted political contacts that are expressed in militaristic form. Exhibiting black and white flags of NATO member states, she was referring to the organisation's principles based on rules and clearly stated activities, where differences between members have been levelled out. Dripping cans of various coloured paint hung from the ceiling hint that a perfect system could never exist.

Murka's work often conveys a film-like seriality, best visible in her 16-piece series of paintings, exhibited together with video and installation at the show “Hairpower” (2010). The paintings depict a still from the 1928 French film “The passion of Joan of Arc”, where the heroine's hair is cut prior to her execution. This scene shows the humiliation of a person, but Murka adds other symbolic meanings to the hair, making it simultaneously repulsive and attractive.

For the show “Objects in Mirror Are Closer than They Appear” (2013) Murka painted an anonymous and taped-up object from every side, and with the positioning of the paintings, created an illusion reminiscent of a display case. The relation between reality and painting was also in focus in “Sisus” (2015), where Murka was working in deconstructing painting. In her eyes already the surface of a painting is a site of numerous compromises, enough to enhance its nuances. The process of painting becoming a painting is dependent on quotidian and earthly conditions, often by chance: what is the material, how many times the surface has been coated, etc. The series of multi-surfaced paintings “Minus” (In me) takes the viewer right inside the work, as the surface is reflective and the.
grp: school:Academy of Fine Arts of Helsinki

artists.b: 1979-84 Tallinna Kunstiülikool arhitektuur. 1986 Rühm T; 1988 Eesti Arhitektide Liit; 1990 Maalikunstnike Liit. 1991 Mosabäcka galerri, Helsingi; 1999 Sebra galerii; 2001 Pirkko-Lias Topelius, Helsingi.
artists.ben: 1979-84 Tallinn Art University, architecture. 1986 Rühm T; 1988 Estonian Union of Architects; 1990 Estonian Painters' Association. 1991 Mosabäcka gallery, Helsinki; 1999 Sebra gallery; 2001 Pirkko-Lias Topelius, Helsinki.

artists.b: Tartu raehärra ja maalikunstnik. Lõpetas 1876 Tartus gümnaasiumi, õppis kodulinnas Woldemar Friedrich Krügeri ja Julie Wilhelmine Hagen-Schwarzi juures õli- ja akvarellmaali. Jätkas kunstiõpinguid Viinis William Ungeri juures ning Berliinis Gustav Richteri juures. Aastatel 1880–1897 pidas Tartus pruulikoda. Sai 1881 Tartu kodanikuks ning oli kuni 1897. aastani linnavolinik. 1888–1889 oli Tartu raehärra. 1898–1920 töötas pangaametnikuna Pihkvas, Łódźis, Šiauliais ja Riias.  Maalinud õli ja akvarelltehnikas maastikke. Esinenud näitustel Tartus, Riias, Peterburis ja Moskvas. - Vikipeedia.
artists.ben: Tartu town councillor and painter. Graduated from the gymnasium in Tartu in 1876, studied oil and watercolour painting in his home town under Woldemar Friedrich Krüger and Julie Wilhelmine Hagen-Schwarz. Continued his art studies in Vienna under William Unger and in Berlin under Gustav Richter. Ran a brewery in Tartu from 1880 to 1897. Became a citizen of Tartu in 1881 and was a town councillor until 1897. Was a Tartu town councillor in 1888–1889. Worked as a bank official in Pskov, Łódź, Šiauliai and Riga from 1898 to 1920. Painted landscapes in oil and watercolour technique. Exhibited in Tartu, Riga, St. Petersburg and Moscow. - Wikipedia.

artists.b: Sündis Tallinnas, õppis 7. keskkoolis ja 1962-1969 ERKI-s graafikat. Oli ANK 64 rühmituse asutajaliige. Töötas ajakirja "Noorus" toimetuses 1961-1962. Avaldas artikleid, kirjutas aforisme ja luuletusi.
artists.ben: Born in Tallinn, studied at the 7th Secondary School and in 1962-1969 graphic art at ERKI. Was a founding member of the ANK 64 group. Worked in the editorial office of the magazine "Noorus" in 1961-1962. Published articles, wrote aphorisms and poems.

artists.b: 1947–1951 õppis maali Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis Alfred Kongo käe all ning lõpetas õpingud Tallinnas 1953. aastal Eesti NSV Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis.
Sündinud 13.12.1965. Haridus: 1993–1995 Magistratuur Eesti Kunstiakadeemias; 1994 Rootsi Kuninglik Kunstiülikool, graafikatehnikad; 1988–1993 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, graafika.
artists.ben:
Marko Mäetamm (1965) is an artist whose work is based on personal stories, used to create existentially absurd and critical caricatures. Mäetamm has represented Estonia in the Venice Biennale twice: in 2003 (under the pseudonym John Smith, together with Kaido Ole) and in 2007. His work is characterised by an interdisciplinary, series-oriented and narrative approach, where figurative image and text carry an equal weight.

In the 1990s Mäetamm's work was influenced by the Pop Art of the 1960s, the so-called yellow submarine aesthetics – at the time he created colourful and abundant compositions. That period was followed by black-and-white schematic pictograms: in the series “The Chemistry of Being” (2000) the artist explored themes like birth, death and religion and in the exhibition „Loser’s Paradise“ (2007) Mäetamm focused on family and everyday life.

A distinct chapter in Mäetamm's work is the joint project with Kaido Ole under the pseudonym John Smith (2001–2006). In 2003 they represented Estonia at the Venice Biennale with the project “Marko und Kaido”. The artists created a set of paintings and installations, blending fiction with autobiographical details of childhood and life in Eastern Europe. John Smith's work offered a self-critical view on Estonia and Eastern Europe.

In 2007 Mäetamm exhibited at the Venice Biennale in the Estonian pavilion a project titled “Loser's Paradise”, a great example of his period of contemplation on the role of being a father and husband. How to create art, have a job, be there for your family and afford a bank loan and how to do all of this in harmony so that everyone would be happy? The drawings, paintings and comics that at first glance seem carefree and fun, tell stories about everyday life and existential problems, covering up fears, traumas and violent fantasies. The confessional stories have been exaggerated to absurd – to desperate situation that can only be solved through suicide, cannibalism or passive-aggressive silence.

artists.b: Rein Mägar (1944) on vabakutseline akvarellmaalile pühendunud kunstnik. Ta lõpetas Leipzigi Graafika ja Raamatukunsti Kõrgkooli (1971) ja on töötanud kirjastustes (ER, Valgus, Bit) kunstilise toimetajana. Näitustel osalemist alustas plakatistina 1972 aastal, Kunstnike Liidu liige (1977), Eesti Kujundusgraafikute Liidu (1995) ja Eesti Akvarellistide Ühenduse liige alates 1998 aastast. Sellest peale on akvarelliloominguga esinenud kõikidel EAÜ näitustel ja alates 2012 ka Euroopa Akvarelliühenduste Konföderatsiooni (ECWS) poolt korraldatud akvarellifestivalidel. Omanäitusi on toimunud Vabaduse (2009, 2014), Draakoni (2020) ja Viinistu tünnigaleriides (2022), samuti paljudes kultuuriasutustes üle Eesti. Rein Mägar on kureerinud näitusi Würthi kunstigaleriis 2005-2017 ja EAÜ näitusi Pärnu UKM-is ning Võru Linnagaleriis, neist viimasel kolmel aastal ühiseid näitusi koos Soome akvarellistidega. Ettevalmistamisel on Eesti ja Soome akvarellistide ühisnäitus Kadrioru Galeriis 2023 aasta jaanuaris. Rein Mägar on koostanud ja avaldanud kolm akvarelliteemalist trükist: „Teekond akvarellidega“ (2014), „Eesti Akvarell 2018“ ja Eesti-Soome ühisnäituse kataloogi „Mets/Metsä“ (2022).
artists.ben: Rein Mägar (1944) is a freelance artist dedicated to watercolour painting. He graduated from the Leipzig Academy of Graphic Arts and Book Design (1971) and has worked as an art editor at publishing houses (ER, Valgus, Bit). He began participating in exhibitions as a poster artist in 1972, became a member of the Artists' Union (1977), a member of the Estonian Union of Design Graphic Artists (1995) and a member of the Estonian Watercolourists' Union from 1998. Since then he has presented his watercolour work at all EAÜ exhibitions and, from 2012, also at the watercolour festivals organized by the European Confederation of Watercolour Societies (ECWS). Solo exhibitions have been held at the Vabaduse (2009, 2014), Draakoni (2020) and Viinistu barrel galleries (2022), as well as in many cultural institutions across Estonia. Rein Mägar has curated exhibitions at the Würth art gallery from 2005-2017 and EAÜ exhibitions at the Pärnu UKM and the Võru City Gallery, the latter three years' exhibitions being joint exhibitions with Finnish watercolourists. A joint exhibition of Estonian and Finnish watercolourists is being prepared at Kadrioru Galerii for January 2023. Rein Mägar has compiled and published three publications on the subject of watercolour: "Teekond akvarellidega" (2014), "Eesti Akvarell 2018" and the catalogue of the Estonian-Finnish joint exhibition "Mets/Metsä" (2022).

artists.b: Õppis 1888–1889 Uderna ministeeriumikoolis, seejärel Tartus Pelbergi algkoolis ja 1891. aastal linnakoolis. Sai kunstialased algteadmised 1899–1902 Tartu Saksa Käsitööliste Seltsi joonistuskursustel. Jätkas kunstiõpinguid 1903–1905 vabakuulajana Peterburis parun Alexander Stieglitzi kunsttööstuskoolis, keskendus Amandus Adamsoni õpilasena puunikerdusele ja modelleerimisele.
artists.ben: Studied 1888-1889 at the Uderna ministry school, then in Tartu at Pelberg's primary school and in 1891 at the town school. Received basic artistic knowledge 1899-1902 at the drawing courses of the Tartu German Craftsmen's Society. Continued art studies 1903-1905 as an auditor in St. Petersburg at Baron Alexander Stieglitz's School of Technical Drawing, focusing, as a student of Amandus Adamson, on wood carving and modelling.

artists.b: Männi loobus 1960. aastail naturalistlikult detailirikkast laadist, eksperimenteerides uudsete materjalidega ning taotledes senisest erinevat plastilist vabadusastet. Ta oli üks esimesi raudkonstruktsioonide ja keevitatud raudskulptuuride loojaid. Huvitudes kaasaegsetest väljendusvõimalustest skulptuuris, lõi ta 1967. aastal Eesti esimese mobiili. Rütmilise ülesehitusega tinglikult lahendatud figuuridega resoneerib ta 1960. aastate teiste poole maalikunsti vallanud nn karmi stiiliga. Uute materjalide väljendusvõimalusi testivad 1970. aastail loodud plastmassist, babiidist ja tinast teosed.
artists.ben: In the 1960s Männi abandoned the naturalistically detail-rich style, experimenting with novel materials and striving for a degree of plastic freedom different from before. He was one of the first creators of iron constructions and welded iron sculptures. Interested in contemporary means of expression in sculpture, he created Estonia's first mobile in 1967. With figures rhythmically constructed and conventionally rendered, his work resonates with the so-called hard-edge style that dominated painting in the latter half of the 1960s. Works created in the 1970s from plastic, babbitt metal and tin test the expressive possibilities of new materials.

artists.b: Õppis 1914–1916 Peterburi ülikooli ajaloo-keeleteaduskonnas ja 1924–1928 Tartu ülikooli õigusteaduskonnas. 1916–1917 oli I maailmasõjas, 1917–1918 sõjavangis Austrias, 1918–1919 teenis Arhangelskis Briti Põhjakorpuse staabis. 1919–1921 Eesti Vabariigi sõjaväeline esindaja, 1921–1923 chargé d’affaires Leedus. 1923–1927 Välisministeeriumi poliitilise osakonna juhataja, 1924–1925 chargé d’affaires Pariisis ja Brüsselis ning 1926 Moskva saatkonna nõunik. 1927–1931 välisministri abi. 1931–1934 saadik Itaalias ja Šveitsis ning alaline esindaja Rahvasteliidu juures, 1934–1971 saadik Inglismaal.
artists.ben: Studied 1914–1916 at the Faculty of History and Linguistics of the University of St. Petersburg and 1924–1928 at the Faculty of Law of the University of Tartu. Took part in the First World War in 1916–1917, was a prisoner of war in Austria in 1917–1918, and served in 1918–1919 at the staff of the British North Russia Corps in Arkhangelsk. 1919–1921 military representative of the Republic of Estonia, 1921–1923 chargé d'affaires in Lithuania. 1923–1927 head of the political department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 1924–1925 chargé d'affaires in Paris and Brussels, and in 1926 counsellor at the Moscow legation. 1927–1931 assistant to the Minister of Foreign Affairs. 1931–1934 envoy to Italy and Switzerland and permanent representative to the League of Nations, 1934–1971 envoy to England.

artists.b: Ants Mölder (1939–2009) tegutses modernistliku skulptorina aktiivselt 1970. ja 1980. aastatel. Talle omane mänguline suhe poolabstraktsete vormidega viis katsetama erinevate materjalidega, millest alumiinium ja epoksüvaik ilmestasid Eesti skulptuuris just 1970. aastaid. Ants Mölder on loonud dekoratiivseid vorme ja figuure ka puust ja marmorist. Erilist tähelepanu on pälvinud tema mahagonskulptuurid. Väikeseformaadilised mitmesugustes tehnikates loodud joonistused avavad vaatajale skulptori mõtteskeemid ajast, mis eelnes ühe või teise skulptuuri valmimisele. Olulise osa Ants Mölderi loomingust moodustavad mälestusmedalid, auhinnad ja väikevormid. Eesti avalikus ruumis on 1970. aastail tema loodud Teise maailmasõja monumendid.
artists.ben: Ants Mölder (1939–2009) was active as a modernist sculptor mainly in the 1970s and 1980s. His characteristic playful approach to semi-abstract forms led him to experiment with various materials, of which aluminium and epoxy resin were especially characteristic of Estonian sculpture in the 1970s. Ants Mölder has also created decorative forms and figures from wood and marble. His mahogany sculptures have received special attention. Small-format drawings made in various techniques reveal to the viewer the sculptor's schemes of thought from the time preceding the completion of one or another sculpture. Memorial medals, awards and small forms make up a significant part of Ants Mölder's oeuvre. Second World War monuments created by him in the 1970s can be found in Estonia's public space.

artists.b: Tema looming on jagunenud mitmesse erinevasse ajastusse. 1950. aastail valminud skulptuurid kuuluvad tollase realistliku laadi paremikku (Ühistööks abikaasa Signe Mölderiga jääb tänaseks teisaldatud V.I. Lenini monument Jõhvis (koos Enn Roosiga). Arseni Möldri väljapaistvamaks monumentaalteoseks jääb N. Pirogovi klassitsistlikus orderis teostatud monument Tartus (1952, koos Juhan Raudsepaga), F.R. Kreutzwaldi mälestusmärgi pronksreljeef „Assamalla lahing” 1957, mitmed väärismaterjalides teostatud mälestustahvlid jpm. Tema vabaskulptuuride paremik („Vormija” (1950, pronks 1964), „Teatejooksjad” (pronks, 1956), ).
artists.ben: His oeuvre is divided into several different periods. The sculptures made in the 1950s belong to the finest examples of the realistic style of the time (a joint work with his wife Signe Mölder is the now-relocated monument to V.I. Lenin in Jõhvi (together with Enn Roos)). Arseni Mölder's most outstanding monumental work remains the monument to N. Pirogov in Tartu, executed in a classicist order (1952, together with Juhan Raudsepp), the bronze relief "The Battle of Assamalla" of the F.R. Kreutzwald monument (1957), and several memorial plaques executed in precious materials, among other works. His finest free-standing sculptures ("The Moulder" (1950, bronze 1964), "Relay Runners" (bronze, 1956)).

artists.b: Photographer of thresholds, empty rooms and the edge of the visible.
