artists.ben:
Krista Mölder (1972) is an artist whose work focuses on space and the experience of the viewer. Her photos and videos are full of potential – contours of perspectives and outlines of possibilities. She is primarily interested in what remains outside or beside the image.

Mölder has studied geography and has applied that experience to directly mapping various phenomena, observations, and ideas, while presenting them in a visually structured manner. The aim of one of her first series “Landmarks” (2007) was to explore the possibilities of poetic language of space and photography. This is not unlike the photo series “Inter-Space” (2016), depicting landscapes in a non-three-dimensional way, balancing between painting and photography. These images, photographed from a bird's-eye view seem to map the impossible, while casting doubt on the veracity of photography.

In 2010 Mölder was chosen to participate in the project “European Eyes on Japan. Japan Today, vol. 13”, organised by the EU–Japan Fest. As part of the project Mölder stayed at a residency in Akita, which later led to an exhibition. Japanese architecture, for example the buildings of the architect Seiichi Shirai in the forests of the Akita region made an impact on Mölder's sense of space. Stemming from that, her imagery displays man-made and natural forms that are reduced to almost two-dimensional fields of colour in the wider whole of her work. In her wide-frame snapshots, an abundance of details are revealed to the keen eye, however, these are photographed in a way that does not leave an impression of exaggeration.

Mölder takes photos on a medium format camera and mostly does not manipulate her work digitally. With great sensitivity Mölder finds photographic and aesthetic still lifes in parks and gardens as well as in the city and in living and working spaces. Windows, doors and other liminal spaces are a recurring motif in Mölder's work. Mostly, these spaces are viewed from the inside out, so that the viewer is “here”, in the space with the artist.

artists.b: Eesti Kunstimuuseumi skulptuurikogus on mõningad tema sõjajärgsete aastate realistlikud olustikuskulptuurid, portreed ja keraamilist pisiplastikat. Tema mitmetest aiaskulptuuridest on tuntuim “Mõtted Pandiverest” Nõmmel Kristjan Raua majamuuseumi aias. Signe Mölder on loonud ka avalikke skulptuure ja monumentaalplastikat. Koos Arseni Möldri ja Enn Roosiga loodud Jõhvi V. I Lenini monument on tänaseks linnast teisaldatud. 1999. aastal paigaldati Tallinna Jüriöö parki tema loodud monument II maailmasõjas osalenud eesti sõjameestele.
artists.ben: The sculpture collection of the Art Museum of Estonia contains some of his realistic genre sculptures, portraits and small ceramic plastic works from the post-war years. Of his numerous garden sculptures the best known is "Thoughts from Pandivere" in the garden of the Kristjan Raud House Museum in Nõmme. Signe Mölder has also created public sculptures and monumental plastic works. The monument to V. I. Lenin in Jõhvi, created together with Arseni Mölder and Enn Roos, has by now been removed from the town. In 1999 a monument created by her to Estonian soldiers who took part in World War II was erected in Jüriöö Park in Tallinn.

artists.b: Pärit Rakverest, õppis "Pallases" 1927-1936 ning lõpetas selle N. Triigi õpilasena. Täendas end aasta hiljem Pariisis, Berliinis ja Dresdenis. Töötas 1940-1965 oma kodulinna Rakvere teatris lavakujundajana: kujundas umbes 150 lavastust. Ta oli hea professionaalse tasemega maalija, kes esines ka vabariiklikel näitustel.
artists.ben: From Rakvere, studied at "Pallas" 1927-1936 and graduated as a student of N. Triik. He furthered his education a year later in Paris, Berlin and Dresden. From 1940-1965 he worked as a stage designer at the theatre of his home town Rakvere: he designed about 150 productions. He was a painter of good professional level, who also exhibited at national exhibitions.

artists.b: Aastast 1877 tegutses Tartus joonistusõpetaja ja portreemaalijana, 1883–1908 juhatas Tartu Saksa Käsitööliste Seltsi joonistuskursusi. R. von zur Mühleni käe all on kunsti õppinud M. Pukits, K. Mägi, J. Koort, A. Tassa, eraõpilasena K. Raud. 1901 sai Peterburi KA-lt vabakunstniku nimetuse.
artists.ben: From 1877 he worked in Tartu as a drawing teacher and portrait painter, and from 1883 to 1908 directed the drawing courses of the Tartu German Craftsmen's Society. M. Pukits, K. Mägi, J. Koort, A. Tassa studied art under R. von zur Mühlen, and K. Raud as a private student. In 1901 he received the title of free artist from the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts.

artists.b: Õppis 1913–1916 Eesti Kunstiseltsis ja Ants Laikmaa ateljeekoolis. 1917–1918 asutas koos B. Tomasbergi, O. Kallise ja A. Krimsiga ühingu Vikerla. 1919 panustas kunstivara päästmisse ja kogus kokku Vabadussõjas langenud B. Tomasbergi pärandi. 1920 ilmus Tartus tema 10-leheline linoollõigete album Primeurs. 1921 siirdus Pariisi, kus elatus juhutöödest.
artists.ben: Studied in 1913–1916 at the Estonian Art Society and at Ants Laikmaa's studio school. In 1917–1918, together with B. Tomasberg, O. Kallis and A. Krims, founded the society Vikerla. In 1919 contributed to the rescue of art treasures and collected the legacy of B. Tomasberg, who had fallen in the War of Independence. In 1920 his 10-sheet album of linocuts Primeurs was published in Tartu. In 1921 he moved to Paris, where he made a living from odd jobs.

artists.b: Õppis Jenas, Göttingenis ja Erlangenis teoloogiat. 1790. aastal asus Dresdeni Kunstiakadeemiasse akadeemik Chr Klengeli juurde maali õppima. Pärast korduvat Itaalias viibimist asus ta elama Stuttgardi, kus temast sai kunstikooli õpetaja ja kuninglik õukonnakunstnik.
artists.ben: Studied theology in Jena, Göttingen and Erlangen. In 1790 he entered the Dresden Academy of Art to study painting under academician Chr. Klengel. After repeated stays in Italy he settled in Stuttgart, where he became a teacher at the art school and royal court painter.

artists.b: On sündinud Tartus (1972). Lõpetanud TÜ õpetajakoolituse (2001), TÜ filosoofiateaduskonna maalikunsti eriala (1999), Tartu Kunstikooli (1992). Tartu Kõrgema Kunstikooli maalimise õppejõud alates 2001-2009. Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige alates 2005. Tartu Kunstnike Liidu liige alates 2000. Näitustel esinenud alates 1997.
artists.ben: Born in Tartu (1972). Graduated from the University of Tartu teacher training programme (2001), the painting specialty of the Faculty of Philosophy of the University of Tartu (1999), the Tartu Art School (1992). Lecturer in painting at the Tartu Art College from 2001-2009. Member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 2005. Member of the Tartu Artists' Association since 2000. Has exhibited since 1997.

artists.b: Karl-Kristjan Nagel (s. 1977) on lõpetanud Eesti Kunstiakadeemia maali erialal (1999). Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige alates 2011. a.
artists.ben: Karl-Kristjan Nagel (b. 1977) graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in painting (1999). Member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 2011.

artists.b: Sündinud 10.08.1970, Võru.
artists.ben: Born 10.08.1970, Võru.

artists.b: Üldhariduse sai ta Tartu Poeglaste Gümnaasiumis. 1937. aastal asus kunstikooli Pallas, kus õppis Villem Ormissoni maaliklassis. Olnud vahepeal aasta sõjaväes, jätkas 1940. aastal õpinguid Aleksander Vardi ateljees. 1941-1942 oli rindel ja jätkas õpinguid 1943. aastal kuni Pallase kunstikooli sulgemiseni.
artists.ben: He received his general education at the Tartu Boys' Gymnasium. In 1937 he entered the Pallas art school, where he studied in Villem Ormisson's painting class. Having spent a year in the army in between, he continued his studies in 1940 in Aleksander Vardi's studio. In 1941–1942 he was at the front, and continued his studies in 1943 until the closure of the Pallas art school.

artists.b: Naima Neidre (1943) on pikka aega kõrgel tasemel tegutsenud graafik, illust- raator ja akvarellist, kelle ülimalt tundliku visuaalse käekirjaga teosed põimivad lugusid loodusest, merest ja inimestest. Neidre on lõpetanud ERKI graafika eriala (1971) ja osalenud arvukatel näitustel nii Eestis kui ka rahvusvaheliselt. Tema teoseid leidub paljudes (era)kogudes ning ta on pälvinud mitmeid tunnustusi, sh Kristjan Raua preemia (2004). Neidre on Eesti Vabagraafikute Ühenduse liige ja Eesti Kunstnike liidu auliige.
artists.ben: Naima Neidre (1943) is a graphic artist, illustrator and watercolourist who has long worked at a high level, whose works, marked by an extremely sensitive visual style, weave together stories of nature, the sea and people. Neidre graduated from ERKI in graphic art (1971) and has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and internationally. Her works can be found in many (private) collections, and she has received several honours, including the Kristjan Raud Prize (2004). Neidre is a member of the Estonian Association of Free Graphic Artists and an honorary member of the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.b: Kaljuvee on töötanud Rakvere MEKi juhatajana 1980–1986, Rakvere rajooni Täitevkomitee esimehena 1987–1990, Lääne-Viru maavanemana 1990–1992, Kunda Nordic Tsemendi juhatuse liikmena 1992–1994 ja nõukogu esimehena 1994–1999, Eesti Hoiupanga Ida regiooni direktorina ja peadirektori asetäitjana 1994–1998 ning Eesti Põlevkivi juhatuse liikmena 1999–2006 ja juhatuse esimehena 2006–2007.
artists.ben: Kaljuvee worked as the director of the Rakvere MEK from 1980–1986, as chairman of the Rakvere district Executive Committee from 1987–1990, as governor of Lääne-Viru county from 1990–1992, as a board member of Kunda Nordic Tsement from 1992–1994 and as chairman of the supervisory board from 1994–1999, as director of the Eastern region and deputy director general of Eesti Hoiupank from 1994–1998, and as a board member of Eesti Põlevkivi from 1999–2006 and as chairman of the board from 2006–2007.

artists.b: Lõpetas 1926 Viljandi Eesti Haridusseltsi Tütarlaste Gümnaasiumi 1928. aasta algul astus ta Kõrgemasse Kunstikooli Pallas, kus õppis maali esialgu Nikolai Triigi, siis Ado Vabbe ateljees. Kooli lõpetas ta 1936. aastal koos Johannes Võerahansu, Richard Sagritsa, Karl Pärsimäe ja Ellinor Aikiga.
artists.ben: Graduated in 1926 from the Viljandi Estonian Education Society Girls' Gymnasium. At the beginning of 1928 he entered the Higher Art School Pallas, where he studied painting initially in Nikolai Triik's studio, then in Ado Vabbe's studio. He graduated from the school in 1936 together with Johannes Võerahansu, Richard Sagrits, Karl Pärsimägi and Ellinor Aikas.

artists.b: Arreteeriti 26. aprillil 1941, Kirovi oblasti NKVD sõjatribunal määras talle 25. juulil 1941 § 58-13 alusel mahalaskmise koos kogu vara konfiskeerimisega. Teadaolevalt lasti maha 1. septembril 1941 kell 18.15.
artists.ben: He was arrested on 26 April 1941; on 25 July 1941 the NKVD military tribunal of Kirov Oblast sentenced him to death by shooting under § 58-13, together with confiscation of all property. He is known to have been shot on 1 September 1941 at 18.15.

artists.b: MM-pronks ja 1924. aasta olümpialane Noormägi  one esimese Eestist olümpiale jõudnud puudega sportlane. Nimelt oli ta kurttumm (Eesti Spordileht: "Kurttumm, ei kuule ega kõnele, sellevast aga tubli tõstja!"), kes jõudis spordi juurde tänu Georg Lurichile. Lurich külastas nimelt Vändra kurttummade kooli just sel ajal, kui Noormägi seal õppis.
artists.ben: World championship bronze medallist and 1924 Olympian Noormägi was the first athlete with a disability from Estonia to reach the Olympics. Namely he was deaf-mute (Eesti Spordileht: "Deaf-mute, he neither hears nor speaks, but nevertheless a fine weightlifter!"), who came to sport thanks to Georg Lurich. Lurich indeed visited the Vändra school for the deaf-mute precisely at the time when Noormägi was studying there.

Kristina Norman (1979) is an artist whose interdisciplinary work includes video installations, sculptural objects, and interventions in the city space, as well as documentaries and performance. Norman's artistic practice is context-focused and she works with themes that relate to ideologies, controversial political processes and the sore points of history, looking for ways to approach polarising subject matter beyond mutually exclusive narratives.

A notable part of Norman's work addresses the collective memory and identity through monuments. One of her most well-known projects “After-war” represented Estonia at the 53rd Venice Biennale in 2009 (curated by Marco Laimre). The work was based on the story of the Bronze Soldier, a monument to the Soviet army that the Estonian government had removed from Tallinn city centre in 2007, which was then replaced by a golden replica of the statue by Norman. Through this intervention the artist was looking for ways to use the golden monument to draw attention to the various groups living in Estonia who do not share the same historic memory. “After-war” was based on Norman's several previous projects addressing the Bronze Soldier, such as the film “Monolith” (2007), and the installation “Community” (2007) that consists of souvenir size figurines of the Bronze Soldier, painted in the colours of various pop culture characters.

This was followed by the film “A monument to please everyone” (2011) looking at the process of putting up the monument to commemorate the Estonian War of Independence. The film focused on the reorganising of the landscape of Estonian collective memory and correlating it to the nation-focused narrative immediately after the Bronze Soldier was moved. This was also a project for the people in power to establish their political will  that came to divide the mostly Estonian-speaking public regarding the monument's name and meaning (a monument to freedom or a statue to victory) as well as its aesthetic qualities. Following the young patriotic authors of the monument and the politicians who directed them, the film shows the behind-the-scenes of the process.

Her following works “0.8 square metres” (2012) and “Common Ground” (2013) also address perpetuating or erasing collective memory, tied together into a trilogy by an artistic exploration of spatial aspects of remembering and relying on historic parallels. In 2014 Norman took part in the 10th Manifesta Biennial in St. Petersburg (curated by Kasper König and Joanna Warzsa) with the public sculpture project “Souvenir” (2014) and a video installation “Ir.

artists.b: Post-internet artist working with image ecology, biotech and the digital creature.
artists.ben:
Katja Novitskova (1984) deals in her work with the depiction of evolutional development, using internet as the source of visual data. In the early 2010s, she was among the first artists, who took post-internet for subject matter and designed its aesthetics. Novitskova’s

situates in the crossing of visual culture and science fiction, inducing discomfort and enstrangement by blending futuristic fantasy with everyday reality. In general, Novitskova works in installative method, using photo-sculptures as her main medium.

” is a pioneering handbook, which offers solutions for coping with the situation in which internet has become a pre-condition and therefore the senses of a human-being are flooded with signs. In 2017, Katja Novitskova represented Estonia in 57th Venice Biennial with the exhibition “

”, which focused on the digital culture of contemporary times, looking back at it from a science-fictional position, when the world as we know it today, didn’t exist. That brought up questions of recognizing the hi-tech reality – who dares to say that the actual life is fantastic film and future is now?

artists.b: Sündinud 06.12.1964. Haridus: 1985–1992 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, graafika, magistrikraad.
artists.ben: Born 06.12.1964. Education: 1985–1992 Estonian Academy of Arts, graphic art, master's degree.

artists.b: Lõpetanud Tartu Ülikoolis ajaloo (1984) ja maali (1995 B.A. cum laude; 2017 M.A.) erilalad, läbinud samas filosoofia teadusmagistrantuuri. Õpetanud erinevates koolisüsteemides, sh olnud pikka aega Tartu Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis nii teoreetilistes (kaasaja kunsti loengud) kui praktilistes (maalikursused, loovjoonistamine jm) ainetes külalisõppejõud; Tartu Ülikoolis lugenud Lääne kaasaegse kunsti loengukursust magistrantidele. Teostanud monumentaalmaalinguid koolidesse, kureerinud ja kujundanud ca 10 teemanäitust, kirjutanud kunstist ligi 300 pikemat või lühemat vähem või rohkem interpreteerivat artiklit ja esseid, koostanud Lola Liivati loomingu kataloogi (2008) jt trükiseid, teinud kaaskunstnikega biograafilise aktsendiga tervik-intervjuusid ajakirjale Kunst.ee. LOOMING: Alates 1994 üle 30 isiknäituse, peamiselt Eestis, struktuurilt kontseptuaalsed tervikekspositsioonid koos vähema või rohkema kohaspetsiifilise ja ruumiinstallatiivse aktsendiga. Käsitleb läbi isikliku kogemuse universaalset ja eksistentsiaalset. Loomingus ühendab spontaansuse ja analüüsi. Elukestev protsess on eksperimendid maalikunsti väljendusvahenditega, inspireeritult moderni praktikaist ja kaasaja materjalidest.T.
artists.ben: Graduated from the University of Tartu with specialities in history (1984) and painting (1995 B.A. cum laude; 2017 M.A.), and completed a master's programme in philosophy there as well. Has taught in various school systems, including for a long time as a visiting lecturer at the Tartu Art College in both theoretical (lectures on contemporary art) and practical (painting courses, creative drawing, etc.) subjects; at the University of Tartu has given a lecture course on Western contemporary art to master's students. Has executed monumental paintings for schools, curated and designed approximately 10 thematic exhibitions, written nearly 300 longer or shorter, more or less interpretive articles and essays on art, compiled a catalogue of Lola Liivat's work (2008) and other publications, and made comprehensive biographically accented interviews with fellow artists for the magazine Kunst.ee. WORK: Since 1994, over 30 solo exhibitions, mainly in Estonia, structurally conceptual comprehensive expositions with a greater or lesser site-specific and spatial-installative accent. Addresses the universal and the existential through personal experience. Combines spontaneity and analysis in her work. A lifelong process is experimentation with the expressive means of painting, inspired by modernist practices and contemporary materials.T.

artists.b: 1936–1939 1936–1938 töötas ta Tartu Ülikooli didaktilis-metoodiline seminar, 1937–1940 kunstikooli Pallas joonistamise metoodika õpetaja, 1940 Konrad Mäe nimelise Riigi Kõrgema Kunstikooli direktori kohusetäitja, 1941 direktor, 1942–1943 Kõrgemate Kujutava Kunsti Kursuste õppejõud, 1943-1944 Pallase õppejõud.
artists.ben: 1936–1939 1936–1938 he worked at the didactic-methodological seminar of the University of Tartu, 1937–1940 teacher of drawing methodology at the art school Pallas, 1940 acting director of the Konrad Mägi State Higher Art School, 1941 director, 1942–1943 lecturer at the Higher Courses of Fine Art, 1943–1944 lecturer at Pallas.

artists.b: Esialgse kunstihariduse sai oma venna portselanimaalija Anton Oechsi käe all Regensburgis. 1795. aastast õppis Nürnbergis portselanimaalija K. Trosti juures ja siis Erfurtis portselanimaalija Bollermanni ning Dresdenis professor Klengeli juures. 1804. aastal kolis Jelgavasse. Õppis Tartu ülikooli joonistuskoolis Karl August Senffi juures. 1824. aastast töötas joonistusõpetajana Jelgava gümnaasiumis.
artists.ben: He received his initial art education under his brother, the porcelain painter Anton Oechs, in Regensburg. From 1795 he studied in Nuremberg under the porcelain painter K. Trost, and then in Erfurt under the porcelain painter Bollermann, and in Dresden under professor Klengel. In 1804 he moved to Jelgava. He studied at the drawing school of Tartu University under Karl August Senff. From 1824 he worked as a drawing teacher at the Jelgava gymnasium.

artists.b: Sündinud 14.02.1955.
artists.ben:
Jüri Ojaver (1955) is mainly known as a sculptor and installation artist, however he also works with video and performance. Ojaver's research-based explorations look into material heritage from the past, often characterised by the absurd and existential dimension of randomness. His works that focus on memory and history are often site-specific.

Ojaver began his artistic career as a restorer, working with heritage protected objects in Tallinn Old Town. In the 1980s his sculptures were mostly figurative, using granite, marble and limestone. The changes in society in the 1990s made it possible to discuss events and subjects that were not publicly acknowledged during the Soviet period. Inspired by these developments Ojaver began creating site-specific installations, focusing on sites of memory and history.

The works “Niche. Image” (1993) and “Nonexistent Cemetery” (1994) that were exhibited at the annual exhibitions of the Soros Center for Contemporary Arts, Estonia, where they won Grand Prix, act as frames for something that, although physically absent, exists in the memory of people. The absence of matter while a mental image is present, is a universal issue, explorations of which positioned Ojaver as one of the most notable artists in Estonia after the country regained its independence.

Ojaver's international success is marked by his participation in the 1995 1st Gwangju Biennale in South-Korea with the work “Father. Son” (1995) In 1999 Ojaver represented Estonia at the Venice Biennale together with Peeter Pere and Ando Keskküla. Jüri Ojaver's work “Keystone” was a two-part waterproof plywood sculpture, exhibited in front of and in the garden of Palazzo Querini. The sculpture was based on the motif of spread legs, placed as a bridge over the canal in front of the palazzo. In the back garden of the palazzo viewers saw an upside down version of the sculpture, legs stretching towards the sky. Ojaver's bridge changed the spatial logic of the building, connecting the water gates of both shores and thus making the kitchen door into its main entrance.

artists.b: Ameerika kunstikriitik, poeet, romaanikirjanik, teadlane. Kunstiajaloo õppejõud Rice Ülikoolis USA-s, Kunstikriitika osakonna looja ja arendaja New Yorgi Kunstikoolis (School of Visual Arts in New York).
artists.ben:
Terje Ojaver (1955) is a sculptor, whose work includes abstract and figurative monumental painting, site-specific installations, performative paraphrases, classical sculpture, and video. She has also created notable monumental sculptures for public space.

In the 1990s Terje Ojaver mostly focused on site and material specific installations, characterised by a conceptual approach to nature. During the 3rd Annual Exhibition of Soros Center for Contemporary Arts, Estonia titled “Biotopia”, she exhibited the work “Bio-Top” (1994) on the columns in front of the entrance of the Tallinn Art Hall building, measuring the level of air pollution. At the open-air art centre Le vent des forêts Lahaymeix’ in Lorraine, France, Ojaver built massive protective planters around living trees (1998). At the Tallinn Botanic Garden the artist covered the ground with a ruffling carpet of natural grass, highlighting the unity of man and nature. In Kuressaare she released blocks of ice taken from the Kuressaare Castle pond in winter and preserved in a freezer, back into the pond in spring (2001), demonstrating the eternal cycles of nature. With the show “Dance of the deceived” (Petetute tants, 2009) Ojaver begun her series of replicas of large rocks, continuing it at the Sculpture Quadrennial Riga on the square of St Peter’s Church (2016), followed by a display of the rocks as floating pieces in Swan Pond in Kadriorg Park (2016), and later in Århus, Denmark (2019).

Ojaver's work ties together canons of classical sculpture and controversial technical or narrative solutions, blending high and low art. Her figure-based work (mostly using her own image) make up a significant part of her practice, telling stories of women's real and illusory positions, but also of herself as a wife, mother, daughter, her freedoms and obligations, strengths and resignations. Among these works we find “Blind” (Pime, 2011), “Awkward egg body” (Piinlik munakeha, 2015), “Self-portrait as burning fish” (Autoportree põleva kalana, 2014), “Self-portrait as a camel” (Autoportree kaamelina, 2012), “Self-Portrait as a tortoise” (Autoportree kilpkonnana, 2018). In creating these creatures as self-portraits Ojaver uses materials that during the past 50 years have been associated primarily with women artists: everyday objects, soft fabrics, etc. In her solo show “Stripclub” (Striptiisiklubi, 2015, Vabaduse Gallery) Ojaver exhibited “Madonna”, a work depicting a figure dressed in tarp, a bitter-looking woman, who will never be free of her burden. In contrast, she exhibited a series of bronze figurines focusing on d.

artists.b: Sündis tisleri perekonnas, omandas üldhariduse Nõmme Linna 1. algkoolis ja Tallinna Linna Poeglaste Reaalgümnaasiumis. Kunsti õppis 1931-1937 Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis (dekoratiivmaal), 1938-1941 Riigi Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis (maal). Mobiliseeriti 1941 Punaarmeesse tööpataljoni, 1944 kuulus Jaroslavli eesti kunstnike kollektiivi. Pärast II maailmasõda õppis Moskva Kunstiakadeemias. Alates 1944 oli ERKI (TKÜ, EKA) õppejõud, 1993 emeriitprofessor. E. Okas reisis teoseid luues 1958 Hollandis, Belgias ja Luksemburgis, 1961 Itaalias, 1962 Prantsusmaal, 1963 Jaapanis.
artists.ben: Was born into a joiner's family, obtained general education at Nõmme City 1st Primary School and Tallinn City Boys' Secondary School. He studied art from 1931-1937 at the State School of Applied Art (decorative painting), and from 1938-1941 at the State Higher Art School (painting). In 1941 he was mobilised into a labour battalion of the Red Army, and in 1944 belonged to the Yaroslavl collective of Estonian artists. After World War II he studied at the Moscow Academy of Arts. From 1944 he was a teacher at ERKI (TKÜ, EKA), and in 1993 became professor emeritus. In creating his works E. Okas travelled in 1958 to the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg, in 1961 to Italy, in 1962 to France, in 1963 to Japan.

artists.b: Õppis TPI-s (TTÜ, TalTech) 1968-1970 ehitust ning 1970-st ERKI-s (EKA) arhitektuuri. On loonud performance`e, installatsioone, graafikasarju, kitsasfilme jm. Graafikas kasutab sageli fotot ja filmikaadreid.
artists.ben: Studied construction at TPI (TTÜ, TalTech) 1968-1970 and from 1970 architecture at ERKI (EKA). Has created performances, installations, print series, short films etc. In graphic art he often uses photographs and film frames.

artists.b: Eduard Ole sündis 1898 Valgamaal Karula kihelkonnas Kaagjärve vallas Saibasoo talus. Ta õppis pastor Wühneri neljaklassilises kirikukoolis ja Valga linnakoolis. Kunstihariduse sai 1914-1918 Venemaal Penza erakunstikoolis (Peterburi Kunstide Akadeemia filiaal), mille lõpetas joonistusõpetaja kutsega. Pärast Eestisse naasmist töötas alates 1919 õpetajana Rakvere Reaalgümnaasiumis ja Õpetajate Seminaris, aastast 1922 Tartu tütarlastegümnaasiumis ning kommerts- ja kaubanduskoolis ja 1924–1936 Hugo Treffneri Gümnaasiumis; aastast 1936 Tallinna Prantsuse Lütseumis. 1923 oli E. Ole avangardistliku Eesti Kunstnikkude Ryhma asutajaliige, 1927. aastast kuulus Eesti Kujutavate Kunstnikkude Keskühingusse, hiljem oli ühingu aseesimees. E. Ole väisas korduvalt Pariisi, esmakordselt 1927. aastal. 1937. aastal reisis koos Juhan Raudsepaga Inglismaal, Belgias, Prantsusmaal, Itaalias ning Kesk-Euroopas. 1943 põgenes kunstnik Eestist Soome, alates 1944 elas Rootsis Lääne-Stockholmis Vällingbys ja töötas Põhjamaade Muuseumis. 1946. aastal võttis Ole koos Eduard Wiiraltiga ette reisi Lapimaale.
grp: school:Higher Art School at the Imperial Academy of Arts
artists.ben: Eduard Ole was born in 1898 in Valga County, Karula Parish, Kaagjärve Municipality, at the Saibasoo farm. He studied at pastor Wühner's four-grade church school and at Valga town school. He received his art education in 1914–1918 in Russia at the Penza private art school (a branch of the Saint Petersburg Academy of Arts), from which he graduated with the qualification of drawing teacher. After returning to Estonia, he worked from 1919 as a teacher at Rakvere Secondary School and the Teachers' Seminary, from 1922 at the Tartu Girls' Gymnasium and the Commercial and Trade School, and from 1924–1936 at Hugo Treffner Gymnasium; from 1936 at the Tallinn French Lyceum. In 1923, E. Ole was a founding member of the avant-garde Estonian Artists' Group; from 1927 he belonged to the Estonian Central Society of Visual Artists, later serving as the society's vice-chairman. E. Ole visited Paris repeatedly, for the first time in 1927. In 1937 he travelled together with Juhan Raudsepp to England, Belgium, France, Italy and Central Europe. In 1943 the artist fled Estonia for Finland; from 1944 he lived in Sweden, in Vällingby, West Stockholm, and worked at the Nordic Museum. In 1946, Ole, together with Eduard Wiiralt, undertook a trip to Lapland.

artists.b: Sündinud 25.02.1963. Haridus: Tallinna Kunstiülikool, lõpetanud 1992.
artists.ben:
Kaido Ole (1963) is one of the most well known contemporary Estonian painters, active in art since 1989, and a long time teacher at the Estonian Academy of Arts. Ole often models for his own paintings but also creates peculiar characters, recurring in various series and compositions. Ole's work is characterised by humour and self-irony and a critical sense of the absurd, stemming from his identity as an Estonian, an Eastern European, artist, and citizen.

Kaido Ole's solo exhibition “Basic” (2001) has been said to be one of the most notable Estonian solo shows of all times by the art historian Anders Härm. The leitmotif of the show was an anonymous subject, a basic human figure bubblehead, used to denote different hierarchies of power.

Also part of Ole's work is the project John Smith, a pseudonym he worked under together with Marko Mäetamm between 2001 and 2006. In 2003 they represented Estonia at the 50th Venice Biennale with “Marko und Kaido”, a work blending autobiography and fantasy. In this compilation of paintings and installations the authors tell the story of a German gene researcher who came to the Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic in the 1960s. Through the eyes of this character the artists present a self-ironic view on the dreams and aspirations of a small country in Eastern Europe.

In his solo exhibition “Handsome Hero and Plenty of Still Lifes” (2012) in the Great Hall of Kumu Art Museum, Ole exhibited paintings with the recurring motif of a wheel balancing on abstract combinations of material, forms and surfaces, which can be interpreted as a witty comment on balance in the contemporary world. In the show “Freaks” (2014) Ole developed his trademark anonymous stick figures into all kinds of Dadaist characters, turning his previously carefully constructed mythologies upside down.

artists.b: Helgi-Maret Olvet oli 1955–1964 Moskvas ja Tallinnas kujunduskunstnik, 1974–1975 Eesti Televisiooni peakunstnik ja 1976–1977 Eesti NSV Kohaliku Tööstuse Ministeeriumi peakunstnik, 1979–1986 ERKI joonistuskateedri vanemõpetaja, seejärel oli ta vabakunstnik. Tegeles eksliibrisekunsti ja vabagraafikaga.

Kirjanik; Õppis Penuja vallas Niitsaadu vallakoolis, hiljem täiendas end iseõppijana, 1871–77 ja 1891–92 elas Pöögle-Maie külakoolis, kus vend Jaan oli õpetaja. Töötas 1872 Pöögles vallakirjutaja abilisena, aastast 1873 Pornusel ja mujal kohtukirjutajana, hiljem Karksis, Pollis ja mitmes teises Mulgimaa vallas vallakirjutajana. Pidi 1893 vene keele oskamatuse tõttu kirjutajaametist lahkuma, töötas lühikest aega Viljandi Põllumeeste Seltsi ökonoomina, aastast 1894 Daugavpilsi lähedal Kalkune mõisas piiritusevabriku raamatupidajana, aastast 1898 Riias Phoenixi vagunivabrikus osakonnajuhatajana, 1901–04 Tartus Postimehe ärijuhina ja 1904–20 Liivimaa Hüpoteegi Seltsi pangaametnikuna.
artists.ben: Writer; Studied at Niitsaadu village school in Penuja parish, later continued as an autodidact, in 1871–77 and 1891–92 lived at Pöögle-Maie village school, where his brother Jaan was the teacher. Worked in 1872 in Pöögle as an assistant parish clerk, from 1873 in Pornuse and elsewhere as a court clerk, later in Karksi, Polli and several other Mulgimaa parishes as parish clerk. In 1893, due to lack of knowledge of Russian, had to leave the clerk's post, worked briefly as the economist of the Viljandi Farmers' Society, from 1894 as bookkeeper at the spirits factory of Kalkuse manor near Daugavpils, from 1898 in Riga as head of department at the Phoenix wagon factory, 1901–04 in Tartu as business manager of Postimees, and 1904–20 as a bank official of the Livonian Mortgage Society.

artists.b: Enno Ootsing (s. 1940) on Eesti kunstielus osalenud 1964. aastast alates vabagraafiku, raamatukunstniku ja akvarellistina, kuuludes Eesti kunsti uuendusliikumises olulist kohta omanud rühmitusse ANK ’64.
artists.ben: Enno Ootsing (b. 1940) has taken part in Estonian art life since 1964 as a printmaker, book artist and watercolourist, belonging to the group ANK '64, which held an important place in the innovative movement of Estonian art.

artists.b: Segatehnikas töö kujutab kunstniku lapsepõlvekodu aknaraami Pärnus Mihkli tn 18. Aplikatsioon, pastell, pliiats, foto. Paremas ülaruudus peegeldub majakatus tuulelipuga ja kontuurina joonistatud hobune vankriga, all paremas nurgast koduaknast sissevaatava kunstniku peegeldus aknaklaasil.;.
artists.ben: The mixed-media work depicts the window frame of the artist's childhood home at Mihkli tn 18 in Pärnu. Appliqué, pastel, pencil, photo. In the upper right pane a house roof with a weathervane is reflected, along with a horse and cart drawn in outline; in the lower right corner the artist's reflection looking in from the home window is seen on the windowpane.;.

artists.b: V. OrmissonLoonud peamiselt maastikke ja natüürmorte. Varaseis teostes on märgata impressionismi ja Konrad Mäe loomingu mõju. Pärast Saksamaal käimist sugenes maalidesse ekspressionistlikke jooni, koloriit tumenes ja valdavaks sai rohekassinine toon. 1920. aastate II poolel muutus maastikukäsitlus õhu- ja valguseküllasemaks.
artists.ben: V. Ormisson mainly created landscapes and still lifes. In his early works the influence of impressionism and the work of Konrad Mägi can be noticed. After a visit to Germany, expressionistic traits appeared in his paintings, the colouring darkened and greenish-blue tones became predominant. In the second half of the 1920s, his treatment of landscape became more filled with air and light.

artists.b: Jaan Paavle oli eesti kirjanik ja kunstnik. Paavle andis välja kuus luulekogu, neist esimene oli 1972. aastal ilmunud "Vabaarmastus". 35-aastasena astus ta Tallinna kunstiinstituuti keraamikat õppima. 1990ndatel huvitus Paavle performance-kunstist. Ta õpetas Tallinna kunstikoolis lastele performance'it ning töötas Tarbekunsti- ja Disainimuuseumis valvurina. Jaan Paavle lõi keraamikat, maalis, kirjutas luuletusi, näidendeid, filmi- ja teatrikriitikat, tegi ise mõned filmid ning mängis mitme filmi massistseenides.
artists.ben: Jaan Paavle was an Estonian writer and artist. Paavle published six poetry collections, the first of which, "Vabaarmastus", appeared in 1972. At the age of 35 he entered the Tallinn Art Institute to study ceramics. In the 1990s Paavle became interested in performance art. He taught performance to children at the Tallinn Art School and worked as a guard at the Estonian Museum of Applied Art and Design. Jaan Paavle created ceramics, painted, wrote poems, plays, film and theatre criticism, made a few films himself and appeared in mass scenes of several films.

artists.b: Juhan Paberit (1917) on loonud 1960.–1970. aastatel rahutu dünaamikaga ning emotsionaalselt mõjuvaid mälestusmärke ja hauatähiseid. Tema valdavalt reljeefidena lahendatud mälestusmärgid on äratuntavad kauni maalilise pinnatöötluse järgi. Paberit on üks esiletõusvamaid reljeefi-skulptoreid Eestis. Ta oli valdavalt Tartu-keskne kunstnik, nii on Paberiti hauaskulptuurid suures osas Tartu kalmistutel; Teises maailmasõjas langenute mälestusmärgid asuvad Lõuna-Eestis (Elvas, Õisus, Kanepis), aga ka Paides. Portreeloomingus kasutas meelsasti keraamikat – olulise osa tema loomingust moodustavadki portreed – kunstniku suhe modelli on enamasti soe ja lüüriline. Paberit oli Teises maailmasõjas mobiliseeritud punaarmeesse, alustas skulptuuriõpinguid 1946. aastal Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis ning lõpetas ENSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi 1952. aastal skulptorina.
artists.ben: Juhan Paberit (1917) created restless, dynamic and emotionally powerful monuments and gravestones during the 1960s–1970s. His monuments, mostly executed as reliefs, are recognisable by their beautiful painterly surface treatment. Paberit is one of the most outstanding relief sculptors in Estonia. He was predominantly a Tartu-centred artist, and thus Paberit's gravestone sculptures are largely found in Tartu's cemeteries; the monuments to those fallen in the Second World War are located in South Estonia (in Elva, Õisu, Kanepi), but also in Paide. In his portrait work he gladly used ceramics – portraits indeed form a significant part of his oeuvre – the artist's relationship to the model is usually warm and lyrical. Paberit was mobilised into the Red Army during the Second World War, began his sculpture studies in 1946 at the Tartu State Art Institute, and graduated as a sculptor from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1952.

artists.b: Kunstileksikonides tema nime ei mainita, küll on seal andmeid Olga kohta. Kahjuks ei ole teada, kus Maria kunsti õppis. Võimalik, et neil oli õega ühine kodune kunstiõpetaja ning hiljem võis ta saada juhendust oma õelt Olgalt. Palmse mõisaga on Maria v.d. Pahleni seos üsna kaudne. Ta pärines küll Pahlenite suguvõsa  Palmse harust, kuid mitte otse Palmse mõisast. Tema isa Diedrich oli Voore (Forell) mõisa omanik, kelle isa, kunstniku vanaisa, Peter v.d. Pahlen (1777-1828) oli samuti Voore mõisnik. Alles Peter v. d. Pahleni isa, Arend Dietrich v. d. Pahlen (1738-1778) oli sündinud Palmses Palmse mõisa omaniku lapsena. Kuid noorema pojana ta sünnimõisa ei pärinud ning temast sai Koila (Koil) mõisa omanik Virumaal".
artists.ben: Art lexicons do not mention her name, though there is information there about Olga. Unfortunately it is not known where Maria studied art. It is possible that they shared a home art teacher with their sister, and later she may have received guidance from her sister Olga. Maria v.d. Pahlen's connection to Palmse Manor is rather indirect. She did indeed descend from the Palmse branch of the Pahlen family, but not directly from Palmse Manor. Her father Diedrich was the owner of Voore (Forell) Manor, whose father, the artist's grandfather, Peter v.d. Pahlen (1777–1828), was likewise the owner of Voore Manor. Only Peter v.d. Pahlen's father, Arend Dietrich v.d. Pahlen (1738–1778), was born in Palmse as a child of the owner of Palmse Manor. However, being a younger son he did not inherit his birth manor, and instead became the owner of Koila (Koil) Manor in Virumaa".

artists.b: Põgenenud Soome kaudu Rootsi, lõpetas 1947. aastal Sigtuna Eesti Gümnaasiumi ja 1951. aastal Stockholmi Kõrgema Rakenduskunstikooli. Graafika erialal täiendas 1954-1955 Oslos Norra Rahvusliku Kunstiakadeemia graafikaklassis Chrix Dahli juures.
artists.ben: Fled through Finland to Sweden, graduated in 1947 from the Sigtuna Estonian Gymnasium and in 1951 from the Stockholm Higher School of Applied Arts. In the field of graphic art, from 1954-1955 he continued his studies in Oslo in the graphic art class of the Norwegian National Academy of Art under Chrix Dahl.

artists.b: Tiiu Pallo-Vaik (1941) on maalinud peamiselt lüürilisi, maheda koloriidiga portreid.
artists.ben: Tiiu Pallo-Vaik (1941) has painted mainly lyrical portraits with a mild colouring.

artists.b: Hille Palm õppis aastatel 1957–1962 Tartu Kujutava Kunsti Koolis ja seejärel Eesti Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis, mille lõpetas 1972. aastal. Tema looming keskendub naisekeha ja tunnete ekspressiivsele kujutamisele. Palm on osalenud rahvusvahelistel näitustel ja saanud mitmeid tunnustusi, sealhulgas Kristjan Raua nimelise preemia 1985. aastal.
artists.ben: Hille Palm studied from 1957 to 1962 at the Tartu Art School and afterwards at the Estonian State Art Institute, which she graduated from in 1972. Her work focuses on the expressive depiction of the female body and emotions. Palm has participated in international exhibitions and received several awards, including the Kristjan Raud Prize in 1985.

artists.b: Sündinud 14.04.1937, Tallinn; surnud 27.04.2002. Haridus: 1957-1963 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, keraamika, graafika, lõpetas graafik-plakatistina.

Lembit Palm (1944) viljeles 1970. aastatel peamiselt dekoratiivskulptuuri, huvitudes nii loomingu sümboolsest väärtusest kui ka vormi väljendusrikkusest. Tema figuratsioonid ning algvormidele taandatud dekoratiivskulptuurid on lahendatud nii pronksis kui ka tinas ja kivis. Samuti on ta loonud elava modelleeringuga karakteerseid portreeskulptuure. Ta on laiendanud oma loomingulisi võimalusi valdkondadesse nagu rahvusvahelised jää- ja lumeskulptuuri sümpoosionid ja võistlused ning võtnud osa linnaskulptuuri sümpoosionidest, kus lühiajalise tööprotsessi tulemusega paigutatakse linnaruumi peamiselt dolomiidist või puust taiesed.
artists.ben: Lembit Palm (1944) mainly cultivated decorative sculpture in the 1970s, interested both in the symbolic value of the work and in the expressiveness of form. His figurations and decorative sculptures reduced to primary forms have been rendered in bronze as well as in tin and stone. He has also created character portrait sculptures with lively modelling. He has extended his creative possibilities into fields such as international ice and snow sculpture symposiums and competitions, and has taken part in urban sculpture symposiums, where works, mostly of dolomite or wood, resulting from a short working process are placed in urban space.

artists.b: Priit Pangsepp (s. 1966 in Kohtla-Järvel) on üks Kursi koolkonna rajajaid. Pangsepp lõpetas Tartu Kunstikooli 1985. a. ning alustas näitustel osalemist aasta varem, 1984. Ta on Eesti Kunstnike Liidu ja Tartu Kunsntike Liidu liige alates 1992. a.
artists.ben: Priit Pangsepp (b. 1966 in Kohtla-Järve) is one of the founders of the Kursi school. Pangsepp graduated from the Tartu Art School in 1985 and began participating in exhibitions a year earlier, in 1984. He has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and the Tartu Artists' Association since 1992.

artists.b: Anne Parmasto (s. 1952) on lõpetanud Eesti NSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi 1981. a. maalikunstnikuna (teatridekoraatori lisaeriala). Alates 1999. on Parmasto maalikunsti dotsent Tartu Ülikooli kultuuriteaduste ja kunstide instituudis. Parmasto on esinenud alates 1984. aastast 35 isiknäitusega Eestis, Saksamaal ja USA-s ning osalenud enam kui 300. grupi- ja ülevaatusnäitusel Eestis, Austrias, Belgias, Luksemburgis, Leedus, Itaalias, Rootsis, Saksamaal (sh ART COLOGNE), Soomes, Türgis, USA-s, Valgevenes, Venemaal.
artists.ben: Anne Parmasto (b. 1952) graduated from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1981 as a painter (with a supplementary specialty in theatre decoration). Since 1999 Parmasto has been an associate professor of painting at the Institute of Cultural Sciences and Arts of the University of Tartu. Since 1984 Parmasto has held 35 solo exhibitions in Estonia, Germany and the USA and has participated in more than 300 group and overview exhibitions in Estonia, Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg, Lithuania, Italy, Sweden, Germany (incl. ART COLOGNE), Finland, Turkey, the USA, Belarus, Russia.

artists.b: Illimar Paul (s. 1945) alustas graafikaõpinguid Eesti Kunstiakadeemias (ERKI) 1964. aastal. Jätkas õpinguid Leipzigi Kõrgemas Graafika- ja Raamatukunsti Koolis, mille lõpetas diplomiga 1971. aastal. Osalenud enam kui 300 ühisnäitusel nii kodu- kui ka välismaal, isikunäitusi on toimunud 68. “Illimar Pauli 1970ndate hüperrealistlikus laadis serigraafiatehnikas linnavaated ei kuulu mitte ainult meie graafika klassikasse, vaid olid omal ajal ühed novaatorlikumad graafikateosed, seda nii tehnika kui ka kujutamisviisi poolest. Paul on oma loomingus kasutanud mitmeid tehnikaid – siiditrüki kõrval teisi graafikatehnikaid (linoollõige), aga ka akvarelli, värvilist pliiatsijoonistust, neid kokku miksinud, tulnud kahemõõtmelisest esitusviisist ruumi, teinud kolmemõõtmelisi kollaaže jne., kuid armastus detaili vastu on säilinud siiani. Enamgi veel: detail on talle alati tähendanud midagi väga isiklikku ja emotsionaalset.” Reet Varblane, 2015.
artists.ben: Illimar Paul (b. 1945) began his graphic art studies at the Estonian Academy of Arts (ERKI) in 1964. He continued his studies at the Leipzig Higher School of Graphic Arts and Book Design, from which he graduated with a diploma in 1971. He has taken part in more than 300 joint exhibitions both at home and abroad, and has had 68 solo exhibitions. "Illimar Paul's townscapes made in the hyperrealistic style of the 1970s in the serigraphy technique belong not only to the classics of our graphic art, but were at the time among the most innovative works of graphic art, both in terms of technique and manner of depiction. In his work Paul has used several techniques – besides silkscreen printing, other graphic techniques (linocut), but also watercolour, coloured pencil drawing, mixing them together, moving from a two-dimensional mode of presentation into space, making three-dimensional collages, etc., but his love of detail has survived to this day. Moreover, detail has always meant something very personal and emotional to him." Reet Varblane, 2015.

artists.b: Aleksander PEEK (1915, Kunda – 1982, Tallinn) oli eesti teatri- ja maalikunstnik ning graafik, kes omandas lavakujunduse-alase hariduse Siberis Omski kunstikoolis. On olnud Estonia kunstnik, hiljem vabakunstnik. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
artists.ben: Aleksander PEEK (1915, Kunda – 1982, Tallinn) was an Estonian theatre and painting artist and graphic artist, who obtained his education in stage design in Siberia at the Omsk Art School. He has been an artist at Estonia, later a freelance artist. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.

artists.b: Õpinguid jätkas aastatel 1928–1932 Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis Pallases, 1942–1944 Kõrgematel Kujutava Kunsti Kursustel ja aastast 1945 Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis, mille lõpetas 1948. aastal ning oli samas 1947–1949 ka õppejõud.
artists.ben: Studies were continued in 1928–1932 at the Pallas Higher Art School, in 1942–1944 at the Higher Courses of Fine Art and from 1945 at the Tartu State Art Institute, which he/she graduated from in 1948, and was also a lecturer there in 1947–1949.

artists.b: Voldemar PEIL (1907, Narva – 1999) oli eesti teatrikunstnik, kes muuhulgas on viljelenud ka realistlikku tahvelmaali (lille- ja maastikupildid ning portreed). Lavakunstnikuna kujundanud umbes kolmsada lavastust. Tema laad on peamiselt olustikuline. Maalitud dekoratsioonide kõrval on Peil tulemuslikult kasutanud ka projektsiooni ja valgustust. Kunstihariduse omandas maalierialal Pallase kunstikoolis Jaan Vahtra, Voldemar Melliku, Villem Ormissoni ja Ado Vabbe käe all, lõpetas kunstikooli joonistusõpetaja kutsega. Stsenograafia alal täiendas end Moskva ja Leningradi teatrites. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
artists.ben: Voldemar PEIL (1907, Narva – 1999) was an Estonian theatre artist who, among other things, also practised realistic easel painting (flower and landscape pictures as well as portraits). As a stage designer he designed about three hundred productions. His style is mainly of a genre character. Alongside painted scenery, Peil also made effective use of projection and lighting. He received his art education in the painting speciality at the Pallas Art School under Jaan Vahtra, Voldemar Mellik, Villem Ormisson and Ado Vabbe, graduating from the art school with the qualification of drawing teacher. In scenography he furthered his education at theatres in Moscow and Leningrad. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.

grp: school:State Academy of Fine Arts Stuttgart

artists.b: Tegutses 19. sajandil Tallinnas maalijana, joonistusõpetajana, kunstikaupmehena ja litograafiate kirjastajana. Tuntuim teos litograafiate sari "Album von Reval" (max 29 erinevat lehte). Litograafiad trükiti F. Schwabe poolt Berliinis.
artists.ben: Active in the 19th century in Tallinn as a painter, drawing teacher, art dealer and publisher of lithographs. His best-known work is the series of lithographs "Album von Reval" (max 29 different sheets). The lithographs were printed by F. Schwabe in Berlin.

artists.b: Per William Petersen (s. 1955 Taanis) on kunstnik ja disainer, kes elab ja töötab alates 2006. a. Tartus. Ta on eksperimenteerinud mitmete meediumite ja tehnikatega, sh maal, 3D-maal, skulptuur, film, foto, jne. Petersen tegeleb teemadega, mis on seotud meid ümbritsevate inimestega – sootsiumiga. Teda huvitavad inimeste elamise viisid, unistused, ellujäämistaktikad. Kõige rohkem aga huvitab teda kõik, mis seostub vabadusega, õiguse ja võimalusega midagi vabalt teha, kuna vabadust võib pidada elu ning inimkonna arengu tähtsaimaks aluseks. Per Petersen on Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Per William Petersen (b. 1955 in Denmark) is an artist and designer who has lived and worked in Tartu since 2006. He has experimented with numerous media and techniques, incl. painting, 3D-painting, sculpture, film, photography, etc. Petersen deals with themes related to the people around us – society. He is interested in people's ways of living, dreams, survival tactics. But what interests him most is everything connected with freedom, the right and opportunity to do something freely, since freedom can be considered the most important foundation of life and the development of humankind. Per Petersen is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.b: Sündis Rakvere maakonnaarsti pojana, oli Udriku mõisaomaniku krahv Rehbinderi kasupoeg. Õppis Tallinna toomkoolis ja 1812-1814 Tartu ülikoolis arstiteadust. 1814 asus õppereisile Berliini, edasi 1815-1816 Viini, elas 1817-1820 Itaalias, Saksamaal, Šveitsis, Inglismaal ja Prantsusmaal. 1821-1823 elas mitmel pool Eestis ja Lätis, 1823-1830 oli Peterburis Smolnõi instituudi kunstiõpetaja. 1827 reisis Soomes. 1839 sai Peterburi kunstiakadeemia akadeemiku kandidaadiks. Alates 1842 elas püsivalt Peterburis.
artists.ben: He was born as the son of a district doctor in Rakvere, and was the stepson of Count Rehbinder, the owner of Udriku manor. He studied at the Tallinn Cathedral School and, from 1812 to 1814, medicine at the University of Tartu. In 1814 he went on a study trip to Berlin, then in 1815-1816 to Vienna, and lived in 1817-1820 in Italy, Germany, Switzerland, England and France. In 1821-1823 he lived in various places in Estonia and Latvia, and in 1823-1830 he was an art teacher at the Smolny Institute in St. Petersburg. In 1827 he travelled in Finland. In 1839 he became a candidate for academician at the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. From 1842 he lived permanently in St. Petersburg.

artists.b: Priit Piirmets on sündinud 15.03.1948. Hageri vallas. Rakvere tuli 1956.a. Õppis Rakvere I 8-kl. koolis. Lõpetas Rakveres Kaugõppe KK. Rakvere I 8.kl.koolis õpetas joonistamist õpetaja  Gustavson. Keskkooli ajal käis kultuurimaja kunstiringis, kus juhendas Ella Rajani. 1973. aastast oli ise kunstiringi juhendaja. Oli Kunstnike Liidu Noortekoondise liige. Oma õpetajaks ja eeskujuks peab Luulik Kokamägi`t. 1974. aastal asus elama Tallinna.
artists.ben: Priit Piirmets was born on 15.03.1948 in Hageri Parish. He came to Rakvere in 1956. He studied at Rakvere 1st 8-year School. He graduated from the Rakvere Correspondence Secondary School. At Rakvere 1st 8-year School, drawing was taught by teacher Gustavson. During his secondary school years he attended the art circle at the House of Culture, led by Ella Rajand. From 1973 he was himself the leader of an art circle. He was a member of the Artists' Union Youth Group. He considers Luulik Kokamägi to be his teacher and role model. In 1974 he moved to live in Tallinn.

artists.b: Akvarellist, loonud ka plakateid, lavakujundusi. Sündis Sevastoopolis, elas Jugoslaavias, aastast 1922 Eestis. Kunsti õppis A. Kaigorodovi stuudios ja 1938-41 Riigi kunsttööstuskoolis. 1941 mobiliseeriti punaarmesse, 1942-44 viibis Jaroslavlis. 1968-88 juhendas üleliidulist akvarellistide gruppi.
artists.wdesc: Estonian artist of Baltic German origin (1912-1989)

artists.b:
Sündis Venemaal Smolenskis, 1914 tuli pere Eestisse. Elas Laeval. Õppis 1938-40 Tartus Pallase kunstikoolis, jätkas õpinguid kuni arreteerimiseni 1945 kevadel (õppejõud Aleksander Vardi jt). 1944 üritas koos Valve Janovi ja Kaja Kärneriga Läände põgeneda. Oli kuni 1954 Venemaal Arhangelski oblasti vangilaagris. Alates 1958 elas Tallinnas, kus ka suri. Maalikunstnik, akvarellist. 1937-39 oli Tartu Töölisteatris dekoraator. 1960. aastatel jõudis, nagu ka Lembit Saarts, loodusmotiividega lähedale abstraktsele maalikunstile.

Bibl.: Eesti kunsti ajalugu 2, 1970, lk 89; Sirje Helme, Jaak Kangilaski, Lühike Eesti kunsti ajalugu. Tln: 1999, lk 128, 144, 196 (ill 98). Vt ka: Enn Lillemets "Enne valguse vaheaega", näitus Tartu Linnamuuseumis 2010.
artists.ben:
He was born in Smolensk, Russia; the family moved to Estonia in 1914. He lived on Laeva. He studied at the Pallas Art School in Tartu from 1938-40, continuing his studies until his arrest in spring 1945 (teachers included Aleksander Vardi and others). In 1944 he attempted to flee to the West together with Valve Janov and Kaja Kärner. He was held until 1954 in a prison camp in Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia. From 1958 he lived in Tallinn, where he also died. Painter, watercolourist. From 1937-39 he was a stage designer at the Tartu Workers' Theatre. In the 1960s, like Lembit Saarts, he approached abstract painting through nature motifs.

Bibl.: Eesti kunsti ajalugu 2, 1970, p. 89; Sirje Helme, Jaak Kangilaski, Lühike Eesti kunsti ajalugu. Tln: 1999, pp. 128, 144, 196 (ill. 98). See also: Enn Lillemets "Enne valguse vaheaega", exhibition at the Tartu City Museum, 2010.

artists.b: Eesti vabariigi 1- ja 2- krooniste rahatähtede autor. Lõpetas 1962 Tartu Kunstikooli, 1970 Eesti Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi. Töötas Eesti Riiklikus Kirjastuses, Kunstitoodete Kombinaadis ARS, Kunstifondis. Alates 1978 vabakutseline kunstnik. Sündis Võrus.
artists.ben: Author of the 1- and 2-kroon banknotes of the Republic of Estonia. Graduated from Tartu Art School in 1962, and from the Estonian State Art Institute in 1970. Worked at the Estonian State Publishing House, the ARS Art Production Combine, and the Art Fund. A freelance artist since 1978. Born in Võru.

artists.b: 1989 Eesti NSV Ministrite Nõukogu poolt väljakuulutatud rahakavandite konkursil ja sai U. Ploomipuu kolmanda auhinna ja tema kujundusega trükiti Eesti 1- ja 2-krooniste sedelid. Viimaseid emiteeriti 1992, 2006, 2007 ja need olid käibel kuni eurole üleminekuni 2011.
artists.ben: 1989 at the competition for banknote designs announced by the Council of Ministers of the Estonian SSR, and U. Ploomipuu received third prize and his design was used to print the Estonian 1- and 2-kroon notes. The latter were issued in 1992, 2006, 2007 and were in circulation until the transition to the euro in 2011.

artists.b: Õppis aastatel 1856-1858 Tartu ülikoolis matemaatikat ja keemiat, tegeledes samaaegselt ka skulptuuriga. Õppis Weimari kunstikoolis ning professor Caueri juures Karlsruhes. Käte halvatuse tõttu oli sunnitud skulptuurist loobuma ning valis erialaks maalikunsti.
artists.ben: Studied mathematics and chemistry at the University of Tartu from 1856 to 1858, simultaneously also engaging in sculpture. Studied at the Weimar art school and under Professor Cauer in Karlsruhe. Due to paralysis of the hands he was forced to give up sculpture and chose painting as his profession.

21. juunil 1940 oli ta juunipöörde juht Tartus. Ta oli juulis 1940 ajalehe Kommunist vastutav toimetaja ning 8. juulist kuni augustini 1940 sõjaväe poliitiline peajuht. Viimane ametikoht asutati president Konstantin Pätsi otsusega 5. juulist 1940. Paul Keerdo oli esimene ja viimane isik sellel ametikohal.
artists.ben: On 21 June 1940 he was the leader of the June coup in Tartu. In July 1940 he was the responsible editor of the newspaper Kommunist, and from 8 July to August 1940 he was the chief political leader of the army. This last post was established by decision of President Konstantin Päts of 5 July 1940. Paul Keerdo was the first and last person to hold this post.

artists.b: Rait Prääts (1952) alustas loometeed suurte vitraažide loomisega avalikku ruumi, muu hulgas Niguliste kiri- kusse ja Rahvusraamatukokku. Klaasis töötas ta välja oma autoritehnika, mis võimaldas n-ö kolmemõõtme- liselt maalida. Liikudes skulptuuri suunas, kasutab ta modelleerimiseks tsemendisegusid, millele lisab maali- tud klaasdetaile, saavutades omamoodi sünteesi maali ja skulptuuri vahel. Prääts on lõpetanud Eesti Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi klaasikunsti eriala (1975), osalenud paljudel näitustel nii Eestis kui ka rahvusvaheliselt ning pälvinud ka mitmeid tunnustusi, sh Kristjan Raua pree- mia (2013). Tema (tellimus)tööd on jõudnud mitmele poole maailma ja paljudesse kogudesse. Prääts on Eesti Klaasikunstnike Ühenduse liige ja Eesti Kunstnike Liidu auliige.
artists.ben: Rait Prääts (1952) began his artistic career by creating large stained-glass windows for public spaces, including for St. Nicholas' Church and the National Library. In glass he developed his own authorial technique, which allowed him to paint, so to speak, three-dimensionally. Moving in the direction of sculpture, he uses cement mixtures for modelling, to which he adds painted glass details, achieving a kind of synthesis between painting and sculpture. Prääts graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute in the speciality of glass art (1975), has taken part in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and internationally, and has also received a number of accolades, including the Kristjan Raud Prize (2013). His (commissioned) works have reached many places around the world and many collections. Prääts is a member of the Estonian Glass Artists' Union and an honorary member of the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.wdesc: French born engraver, known for his 1765 frontispiece of the "Encyclopédie ou Dictionnaire raisonné des sciences, des arts et des métiers"

artists.b: Urmas Puhkan (1967) lõpetas 1992. aastal Eesti Kunstiakadeemia keraamika erialal. Juba õpingute ajal osales näitustel ning on 1988. aastast tegutseva kunstirühmituse Neoeksprepost asutaja. Ta on loonud skulpturaalset keraamikat, kureerinud keraamikanäitusi nii Eestis, kui ka välismaal, olnud üks ARS Keraamikakeskuse algatajaid.
artists.ben: Urmas Puhkan (1967) graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in ceramics in 1992. Already during his studies he participated in exhibitions and is a founder of the art group Neoeksprepost, active since 1988. He has created sculptural ceramics, curated ceramics exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad, and was one of the initiators of the ARS Ceramics Centre.

artists.b: On sündinud 3. oktoobril 1962. aastal Tartus. Ema Laine Pukk (sünd 1935-2023) oli üle 30. aasta Tartu Lastekunstikooli õpetaja. Isa, Aleksander Suuman (1927-2003) oli maalikunstnik ja luuletaja. Tartu Lastekunstikoolile järgnes Eesti Riiklik Kunstiinstituut (Eesti Kunstiakadeemia)1980-1986, kus õppis graafika erialal. Aapo on Ameerika Portreekunsti Ühingu (PSOA) liige aastast 1999 ja Signature Member aastast 2017. Rahvusvahelistelt portree konkurssidelt on Aapo Pukk toonud koju kümneid auhindu. Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige aastast 2011. Aapo Pukk töötab Eesti Kunstiakadeemias lepingulise õppejõuna aastast 2012. Aapo tegeleb põhjalikult kunsti õpetamisega ja metoodikate väljatöötamisega omanimelises kunstikoolis. Viimase 15 aasta jooksul on Aapo andnud üle 200 kursuse. Ta ise ütleb, et armastab lillede ja maastiku maalimist sama palju kui portreteerimist.
artists.ben: He was born on 3 October 1962 in Tartu. His mother Laine Pukk (b. 1935-2023) was a teacher at the Tartu Children's Art School for over 30 years. His father, Aleksander Suuman (1927-2003), was a painter and poet. The Tartu Children's Art School was followed by the Estonian State Art Institute (Estonian Academy of Arts) 1980-1986, where he studied in the graphic art speciality. Aapo has been a member of the Portrait Society of America (PSOA) since 1999 and a Signature Member since 2017. Aapo Pukk has brought home dozens of awards from international portrait competitions. A member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 2011. Aapo Pukk has worked as a contracted lecturer at the Estonian Academy of Arts since 2012. Aapo is deeply engaged in teaching art and developing methodologies at his eponymous art school. Over the past 15 years Aapo has taught more than 200 courses. He himself says that he loves painting flowers and landscapes just as much as portraiture.

artists.b: August Pulst oli seotud Eesti Kunstimuuseumi, Eesti Teatri- ja Muusikamuuseumi, Tori Muuseumi, Eesti Vabaõhumuuseumi asutamise ja juhatamisega. 1915. aastal asutasid A. Pulst, Ants Laikmaa, Kristjan Raud, Mihkel Aitsam ja Peeter Parikas Eesti Rahva Muuseumi Tallinna osakonna, mis muudeti 1919 Tallinna Eesti Muuseumiks ning millest on välja kasvanud praegune SA Eesti Kunstimuuseum.
artists.ben: August Pulst was involved in the founding and management of the Estonian Museum of Art, the Estonian Theatre and Music Museum, the Tori Museum, and the Estonian Open Air Museum. In 1915 A. Pulst, Ants Laikmaa, Kristjan Raud, Mihkel Aitsam, and Peeter Parikas founded the Tallinn branch of the Estonian National Museum, which in 1919 was converted into the Tallinn Estonian Museum, from which the present-day SA Eesti Kunstimuuseum [Art Museum of Estonia Foundation] has grown.

artists.b: Kaisa Puustak (sündinud 1945 Tallinnas) on tunnustatud Eesti kunstnik, kelle looming keskendub vabagraafikale. Ta lõpetas 1969. aastal Eesti Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi graafika eriala (MA). Alates 1973. aastast on Puustak aktiivselt osalenud näitustel, ta on nii Eesti Kunstnike Liidu kui Eesti Vabagraafikute Ühenduse auliige.
artists.ben: Kaisa Puustak (born 1945 in Tallinn) is a recognised Estonian artist whose work focuses on free graphic art. She graduated in 1969 from the Estonian State Art Institute in the field of graphic art (MA). Since 1973, Puustak has actively participated in exhibitions, she is an honorary member of both the Estonian Artists' Association and the Estonian Print Society.

artists.b: 1919. aastal astus ta 17-aastasena vastavatud Kunstiühingu Pallas kunstikooli. Ta õppis esialgu Konrad Mäe, seejärel Nikolai Triigi ja hiljem Ado Vabbe käe all. 1923. aasta kevad-suvel tegi ta Anton Starkopfi juhtimisel õppereisi Saksamaale.
artists.ben: In 1919, at the age of 17, he enrolled in the newly founded art school of the Art Society Pallas. He studied initially under Konrad Mägi, then under Nikolai Triik, and later under Ado Vabbe. In the spring-summer of 1923, he made a study trip to Germany under the guidance of Anton Starkopf.
