artists.b: Artist-archivist of queer histories suppressed in Soviet Estonia.
artists.ben:
Jaanus Samma (1982) is an artist working in several contemporary art mediums, ranging from printmaking and installation to textiles. Over the years, he has extensively researched themes of gender and nationality while focusing on the construction of the idea of nationality and highlighting relevant decisions and choices in the process.

Rising to prominence in the Estonian art scene during the 2000s, Samma’s work employed an ambivalent camp play with male eroticism and gay symbolism; such as fountains, cannons and dolphins. He began to explore Estonian history in the project

(2007/2011), Samma gave a voice to gay men who shared their experiences from a time when homosexual relations were criminalised. They talk about fear, norms, finding partners in Soviet Estonia, and the impact of sexual repression on their lives.

(2015), Samma told the story, in the form of a fictional opera, of a kolkhoz chairman in the 1960s who was sentenced to prison for homosexual activity. He lost his job and his family as a result, but later found acceptance in gay circles. The artist traced the Chairman’s tragic fate through a spatial installation, videos, photographs, archive material, and found objects. The chairman was murdered in 1990, shortly before homosexuality was decriminalised. With this exhibition, Samma represented Estonia at the 56th Venice Biennale and attracted international attention.

artists.b: Sampu valis oma instituudi lõputööks plakatikujunduse ning jäigi plakatikunstnikuks enam kui paariks aastakümneks. Kuuekümnendail kujundas ta ka mitmeid raamatuid ning postkaarte, enamasti Eesti Riikliku Kirjastuse (1948–1962), hiljem kirjastuste Eesti Raamat, Kunst ning Perioodika tellimustööna. Sampu kujundusgraafiline looming valmis põhitöö kõrval Tallinna Pedagoogilises Insti­tuudis, kus ta töötas kunstiõppejõuna aastail 1960–1980.
artists.ben: Sampu chose poster design as his institute graduation work and remained a poster artist for more than two decades. In the sixties he also designed several books and postcards, mostly as commissioned work for the Estonian State Publishing House (1948–1962), and later for the publishing houses Eesti Raamat, Kunst and Perioodika. Sampu's design graphic work was created alongside his main job at the Tallinn Pedagogical Institute, where he worked as an art lecturer from 1960 to 1980.

artists.b: 1915-1916 töötas Rakveres Arguse fotoäris päevapiltniku retušeerijana, 1917 teenis Petrogradis tsaariarmees. 1918-1920 töötas Eesti kaitseväkke mobiliseerituna Tartu sõjavangilaagris. 1922 oli kunstiühingu Pallas ja aastast 1925 EKKKÜ liige. 1923-1925 töötas Pallases kipsivaluõpetajana,.

Sündis käsitöölise perre. Töötas kuni 1940. aastani Tartus erinevates trükikodades. Viljeles nii vaba-, raamatu- ja tarbegraafikat, eksliibrist ning plakatikunsti. Osales näitustel alates 1929. aastast. Suurest missioonitundest jagas ta paljudega oma teadmisi graafikast.
artists.ben: Was born into a craftsman's family. Worked until 1940 in various print shops in Tartu. Cultivated free graphic art, book and applied graphic art, ex libris and poster art. Participated in exhibitions from 1929. Out of a strong sense of mission, he shared his knowledge of graphic art with many.

artists.b: 1951. aastal lõpetas Tallinna 22. keskkooli, järgnes sõjaväeteenistus. 1955 astus Eesti Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi maaliosakonda, mille lõpetas 1961. aastal. 1961–1964 Tallinna 18. keskkooli joonistamisõpetaja, seejärel vabakutseline kunstnik.
artists.ben: In 1951 graduated from Tallinn Secondary School No. 22, followed by military service. In 1955 entered the painting department of the Estonian State Art Institute, which he graduated in 1961. 1961-1964 drawing teacher at Tallinn Secondary School No. 18, thereafter freelance artist.

artists.b: 1971-87 Porkuni Eriinternaatkool; 1988-92 Tartu Kunstikool maal; 1994-98 EKA maal. Isikunäitused 1997 Kastellaanimaja galerii; 2001 Raatuse galerii; 2002 Deco galerii; 2002 Pärnu Jazz kohvik; 2003 Artline galerii Tallinn; 2005 Kunstihoone galerii.
artists.ben: 1971-87 Porkuni Special Boarding School; 1988-92 Tartu Art School, painting; 1994-98 EKA, painting. Solo exhibitions: 1997 Kastellaanimaja Gallery; 2001 Raatuse Gallery; 2002 Deco Gallery; 2002 Pärnu Jazz Café; 2003 Artline Gallery Tallinn; 2005 Kunstihoone Gallery.

artists.b: Sündis Tallinnas kaupmehe pojana, õppis Tartus A. M. Hageni juures ja 1834-1839 Dresdeni kunstiakadeemias, tegutses Riias, Tallinnas ja Peterburis. Kandideeris 1838 edutult Tartu ülikooli joonistuskooli juhataja kohale. 1845 sai Peterburi kunstiakadeemiast vabakunstniku nimetuse. 1850-1871 oli Tallinna Toomkooli kunstiõpetaja, 1853-54 pidas Tallinnas fotoateljeed. 1871 siirdus Dresdenisse. 1850. aastail tegi sarja rannarootslasi kujutavaid akvarelle, mis litografeeriti ja avaldati 1854-1856 C. F. W. Russwurmi teadusraamatus (Eibofolke...). Maalinud ka maastiku-, olustikumaale ja linnavaateid.
artists.ben: Born in Tallinn as the son of a merchant, he studied in Tartu under A. M. Hagen and, from 1834 to 1839, at the Dresden Academy of Art, and worked in Riga, Tallinn and St. Petersburg. In 1838 he unsuccessfully applied for the position of head of the drawing school at the University of Tartu. In 1845 he received the title of free artist from the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. From 1850 to 1871 he was an art teacher at the Tallinn Cathedral School, and in 1853–54 ran a photography studio in Tallinn. In 1871 he moved to Dresden. In the 1850s he made a series of watercolours depicting Coastal Swedes, which were lithographed and published in 1854–1856 in C. F. W. Russwurm's scholarly book (Eibofolke...). He also painted landscapes, genre paintings and townscapes.

artists.wdesc: Austrian copperplate engraver, graphic designer and draughtsperson (1733-1811)

artists.b: Tema esimesed kunstiõpetajad olid G. W. Langewitz ja G. Büttner Riias, kelle käe all õppis litograafiat. 1843. aastal astus Peterburi Kunstide Akadeemiasse ning aastatel 1845-1846 õppis Dresdeni kunstiakadeemias. Läks 1851. aastal edasi õppima Antwerpenisse. 1856 sai akadeemiku tiitli. 1858. aastast töötas Jelgava gümnaasiumis ja reaalkoolis joonistusõpetajana.
artists.ben: His first art teachers were G. W. Langewitz and G. Büttner in Riga, under whom he studied lithography. In 1843 he entered the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts, and in 1845-1846 he studied at the Dresden Academy of Arts. In 1851 he went on to study in Antwerp. In 1856 he received the title of academician. From 1858 he worked as a drawing teacher at the Jelgava gymnasium and the realschule.

artists.b: Asus Tartusse 1850. aastatel, alustas L. Höflingeri joonistajana, avas 1858 oma litograafiatöökoja. 1859-1861 juhatas ka raamatutrükikoda. Pärast raskusi avas 1866 taas Tartus Rüütli ja Küütri t nurgal Schrammi majas litograafiatöökoja ning fotoateljee, hiljem viis selle üle Vana ja Aia t nurgale, lõpuks kolis Riiga. Vt Sven Lepa. Esimesed paiksed fotograafid Tartus, Tartu Linnamuuseumi aastaraamat 2015, lk 108-109.
artists.ben: He settled in Tartu in the 1850s, starting out as a draughtsman for L. Höflinger, opened his own lithography workshop in 1858. From 1859-1861 he also managed a book printing house. After difficulties, he reopened a lithography workshop and photographic studio in Tartu in 1866, at the corner of Rüütli and Küütri Streets in the Schramm building, later moved it to the corner of Vana and Aia Streets, and finally moved to Riga. See Sven Lepa. Esimesed paiksed fotograafid Tartus, Tartu Linnamuuseumi aastaraamat 2015, pp. 108-109.

artists.b: W. Schwank õppis kunsti Peterburis ja Dresdenis prof. Kribeli juures. Tegutses alates 1885 Düsseldorfis ja Altenburgis, hiljem Lätis. Kunstnikuna maalis peamiselt portreid ja vaikelusid, töötas ka kunstiõpetajana.
artists.ben: W. Schwank studied art in St. Petersburg and Dresden under prof. Kribel. He was active from 1885 in Düsseldorf and Altenburg, later in Latvia. As an artist he painted mainly portraits and still lifes, and also worked as an art teacher.

artists.b: Gravöörina mitte eriti oluline, kuid graveeris viimase Goethe portree tema eluajal. (See valmis alles pärast kirjaniku surma.) See portree ja teraslõigete tsükkel M. Lutheri elust on tema olulisemad teosed.
artists.ben: Not particularly significant as an engraver, but he engraved the last portrait of Goethe during the writer's lifetime. (It was only completed after the writer's death.) This portrait and the cycle of steel engravings of M. Luther's life are his most important works.

artists.b: Klaasikunstniku jaoks on Hiiumaal ja Hütil seetõttu eriline koht. See ajendas minu soovi klaasikunsti Hiiumaal edasi tutvustada, jutustada klaasi põnevat saamis- ja kujunemislugu ning olen oma stuudio töös pühendanud erilise koha Hiiumaaga seotud esemetele."
artists.ben: For a glass artist, Hiiumaa and Hüti therefore hold a special place. This prompted my wish to further introduce the art of glass in Hiiumaa, to tell the exciting story of glass's origin and development, and in my studio's work I have devoted a special place to objects connected with Hiiumaa."

artists.b: Valev Sein (1964) loob teoseid miniatuuridest monumentaalseteni. Ta katsetab ja mängib materjalidega – lisades tavapärastele maalivahenditele klaasi, puitu, tekstiili, peeglitükke jne, loob ta sürrealismiga haakuvaid assamblaaže. Kunstnik on teostanud vitraaže tellimustöödena nii eramutesse kui ka kirikutesse. Sein on lõpetanud ERKI maali- ja monumentaalkunsti eriala (1990), osalenud arvu- katel näitustel nii Eestis kui ka rahvusvaheliselt ning olnud ka Hiiumaal pikalt tegutsenud Nelja Nurga galerii üks eestvedajatest. Ta on Eesti Maalikunstnike Liidu ja Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Valev Sein (1964) creates works ranging from miniatures to monumental pieces. He experiments and plays with materials – by adding glass, wood, textile, pieces of mirror etc. to conventional painting media, he creates assemblages that connect with surrealism. The artist has executed stained-glass windows as commissioned works both for private homes and for churches. Sein graduated from ERKI in the field of painting and monumental art (1990), has taken part in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and internationally, and was also one of the driving forces behind the Nelja Nurga gallery, which operated for a long time on Hiiumaa. He is a member of the Estonian Painters' Association and the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.b: Sündinud 04.04.1969, Tallinn. Haridus: 1989–1995 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, stsenograafia.
artists.ben: Born 04.04.1969, Tallinn. Education: 1989–1995 Estonian Academy of Arts, scenography.

artists.b: Wittgenstein, Ludwig Adolf Peter (1769-1843), krahv, aastast 1834 vürst zu Sayn-Wittgenstein-Ludwigsburg, saksa päritolu Vene kindralfeldmarssal (1826), lühikest aega (1813 ja 1828-29) Vene armee ülemjuhataja.
artists.ben: Wittgenstein, Ludwig Adolf Peter (1769-1843), count, from 1834 Fürst zu Sayn-Wittgenstein-Ludwigsburg, a German-born Russian Field Marshal (1826), briefly (1813 and 1828-29) commander-in-chief of the Russian army.

artists.b:
Sündis Tartu ülikooli joonistusõpetaja Karl August Senffi vanima pojana, õppis 1823-27 Tartu ülikoolis. Temast pidi saama Tartu ülikooli arhitektuuriprofessor. 12. XII 1827 sai K. J. Senff hõbemedali filosoofilistele küsimustele vastamise eest; üliõpilasena koostas maastikumaalijaile-iseõppijaile perspektiiviõpiku (ilmunud 1825). 1827 sai Tartu ülikoolis filosoofia kandidaadi kraadi (auhinnatud töö "Systematische Darstellung der Hauptsätze der Geometrie im Raume" trükiti ülikooli kulul). 1829 sai keiserliku, Venemaa Rahvahariduse ministeeriumi summadest reisistipendiumi 3 aastaks ja sõitis Jenasse, kus sai filosoofiadoktori kraadi, seejärel läks Prahasse ja Viini, kus õppis arhitektuuri. 1831 viibis Münchenis. Tegi 10 akvatintatehnikas illustratsiooni oma teosele "Praha Püha Vituse katedraal" (see ilmus Berliinis 1831). Koos oma onu Karl Adolf Senffiga reisis 1831 Itaaliasse, kus elas Roomas, külastas Napolit ja Pompeij'd. Tagasiteel haigestus närvipalavikku ja viidi teadvusetult Milanosse, kus suri.

Tema teoseid leidub EKM-s 72 (neist 3 kaheldava autorlusega) ja Tartu Ülikooli raamatukogus. Bibl: G. H. Vogel, artikli käsikiri, 2011.
artists.ben:
He was born as the eldest son of Karl August Senff, drawing teacher at the University of Tartu, and studied at the University of Tartu in 1823-27. He was supposed to become professor of architecture at the University of Tartu. On 12. XII 1827 K. J. Senff received a silver medal for answering philosophical questions; as a student he compiled a textbook on perspective for self-taught landscape painters (published 1825). In 1827 he received the degree of candidate of philosophy at the University of Tartu (his award-winning work "Systematische Darstellung der Hauptsätze der Geometrie im Raume" was printed at the university's expense). In 1829 he received a travel stipend for 3 years from the funds of the imperial Russian Ministry of National Education and travelled to Jena, where he received a doctorate in philosophy, then went to Prague and Vienna, where he studied architecture. In 1831 he stayed in Munich. He made 10 aquatint illustrations for his work "Praha Püha Vituse katedraal" (this was published in Berlin in 1831). Together with his uncle Karl Adolf Senff he travelled to Italy in 1831, where he lived in Rome, visited Naples and Pompeii. On the way back he fell ill with nervous fever and was brought unconscious to Milan, where he died.

His works are found in the EKM, 72 in number (3 of them of doubtful authorship), and in the Tartu University library. Bibl: G. H. Vogel, manuscript of article, 2011.

artists.b: Ahti Seppet on (s. 1953.a. Tartus) on peamiselt tuntud skulptorina ja skulpturaalsete installatsioonide meistrina, kuid viljelenud ka maali ja graafikat. Seppet lõpetas 1973.a. Tartu Kunstikooli puidu kunstilise kujunduse erialal. Ta on näitustel osalenud alates 1978. aastast (maalijana). Aastast 1990. on Seppet Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Ahti Seppet (b. 1953 in Tartu) is mainly known as a sculptor and a master of sculptural installations, but has also practised painting and printmaking. Seppet graduated in 1973 from the Tartu Art School in the specialty of artistic wood design. He has participated in exhibitions since 1978 (as a painter). Since 1990 Seppet has been a member of the Artists' Association.

artists.b: Kunstnik sündis Peterburis. Tuli pärast 1917.a. revolutsiooni Hiiumaale, kus töötas Kärdla Kalevivabriku direktori autojuhina, tema isa Nikolai (1873-1933) oli Hiiumaal arst. Umbes 1939.a. läks elama Saaremaale. Arreteeriti 1945 Kuressaares, tribunali otsus 19.06.1945 paragrahv 58-1a, 15+5 aastat.
artists.ben: The artist was born in St. Petersburg. He came to Hiiumaa after the 1917 revolution, where he worked as the driver for the director of the Kärdla Cloth Factory; his father Nikolai (1873-1933) was a doctor on Hiiumaa. Around 1939 he moved to live on Saaremaa. He was arrested in 1945 in Kuressaare, the tribunal's decision of 19.06.1945 under paragraph 58-1a, 15+5 years.

artists.b: Valentin Serov sündis helilooja Aleksandr Serovi peres. 1878–1879 õppis maalikunsti Ilja Repini juhendamisel, 1880–1885 õppis Peterburi Kunstide Akadeemias. 1897–1909 töötas pedagoogina Moskva Maali-, Raid- ja Ehituskunstikoolis. Oli üks peredvižnikutest (aastast 1894, rühmituse.
artists.ben: Valentin Serov was born into the family of the composer Aleksandr Serov. In 1878–1879 he studied painting under the guidance of Ilya Repin, in 1880–1885 he studied at the Imperial Academy of Arts in St. Petersburg. In 1897–1909 he worked as a teacher at the Moscow School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture. He was one of the Peredvizhniki (from 1894, a member of the group.

Liina Siib (1963) works mainly in photography, video and installation. The most prominent and recurring themes in Siib's work include social spaces, marginalised groups and overlooked experiences. Siib has said that she aims not to document but to deconstruct the everyday life of her contemporaries, guided by a feminine approach and experiences from her childhood. In her work Siib looks into how history gets written and the role of memory in shaping various groups in society, often using interviews, observation or archival materials as her method of working.

The first half of the 1990s in Siib's practice was characterised by experiments with means of printmaking, collage and found objects, however, in the second half of the decade she mainly focused on photography. In the 1990s Siib's photography often highlighted socially sensitive themes. One of her most notable works from that period is “Desidentifikatsioon” (Disidentification, 1996), exhibited at the show “Estonia as a Sign” in 1996. The work consists of a double-sided photo board with the detail of Saint Victor's decapitated head from an altarpiece in St Nicholas church in Tallinn painted by Hermen Rode in 1481 on one side and a police photo from 1996 of a human head found near Pirita River on the other. This work drew attention to the different readings of a similar scenario and used the comparison to provoke the viewer to examine how they read visual images – why is it that in one case we look at an act of violence from a religious and art historical perspective, but in the other in horror and disgust.

Siib often focuses on social groups that have fallen behind in the new neoliberal and West-oriented system. For example, in the photo installation “Külalislahkus” (Hospitality, 1997) we see a house inhabited by homeless people and objects found there and “Hooaja palitu” (Coat of the Season) brings attention to people living in poor conditions. In the five-part video series “Kompromiss välistatud” (Compromise Excluded, 2003) Siib asks what compromises are made by people who say compromises are out of question. She is also visualising the monophonic history-writing in 20th century Estonia. To exemplify that the artist asked Russian-speaking and seemingly not very well-off people to repeat in a choir in the Baltic Station: “I am dead!”, thus creating a narrative of “yesterday's heroes”. The installation “Huldufólk / Varjatud rahvas” (Huldufólk / Hidden People, 2020) focuses on the activity at the back of a 24/7 shop in Reykjavík. Her photo series, evoking capitalist realism, and video shows the activ.

artists.b: Sündinud 20.11.1938, Alma-Ata. Haridus: 1958–1965Eesti NSV Riiklik Kunstiinstituut, maal; 1953–1958Tartu Kujutava Kunsti Kool.
artists.ben: Born 20.11.1938, Alma-Ata. Education: 1958–1965 Estonian SSR State Art Institute, painting; 1953–1958 Tartu Art School.

artists.b: Alates 1932 elas Tallinnas ja tegutses alates 1936 mööblitööstuse ja tarbekunsti alal. Oli alates 1935 EKKKÜ ja 1934 Ra Kü liige. Tema vabakunstide-alane looming jäi napiks, enam tuntud on ta mööblidisaineri ja ruumikujundajana. Propageeris funktsionalismi ja rakendas art décod.
artists.ben: From 1932 he lived in Tallinn and from 1936 worked in the field of furniture industry and applied art. He was a member of EKKKÜ from 1935 and of Ra Kü from 1934. His work in the fine arts remained scant; he is better known as a furniture designer and interior designer. He promoted functionalism and applied art deco.

artists.b: Avatud ukse ees välistrepil põlvitab heledas riietuses laia halli kübaraga noor daam. Teda aitab üles juurdeastunud isa - vanem mees lihtsas pruunis ülikonnas, punase vestiga. Taga seisab käsi kokku lööv ema, tanu peas ja prillid ninal. Paremal seisab isa kuuest kinni hoidev, tõsise näoga väike õde. Lapse peas on roosa paelaga kaunistatud lai õlgkübar ja tal on ees ruuduline põll.
artists.ben: In front of an open door, on the outdoor stairs, a young lady in light-coloured clothing and a wide grey hat kneels. She is being helped up by her father, who has stepped closer - an older man in a simple brown suit with a red waistcoat. Behind stands the mother, clapping her hands together, wearing a bonnet and glasses on her nose. On the right stands a small, serious-faced sister holding on to her father's coat. On the child's head is a wide straw hat decorated with a pink ribbon, and in front she wears a checked apron.

artists.b: Kujunes 1970. aastail Eesti modernistliku skulptuuri uuendajaks. Koos plastiliste mahtude ja ruumi koosmõjule rajatud vormiotsingutega ilmus tema loomingusse erandlik elegantsusetaotlus. Soans on suutnud poetiseerida pronksi skulptuuri väärismaterjalina ning tema pronksskulptuurid on loodud puhta siluetimõjuga. Ta avardas Eesti skulptuuri temaatikat ja kommunikatiivsust, tuues oma teostesse eksistentsiaalseid arutlusi inimese ja humanitaire’i võimalustest tehnoloogiapõhises võõranduvas maailmas. Soansi võib vaadelda intellektuaali ja õpetajana, keda on järginud nii tema õpilased kui ka kolleegid. Üldsus tunneb teda valdavalt monumentalistina. Ta on loonud enam kui 30 monumenti ja avalikku skulptuuri ning jäädvustanud rahvuslikke suurkujusid: näiteks A. H. Tammsaare (1978), Voldemar Panso (1980) ja Michel Sittowi (1982) monumendid Tallinnas, Kristjan Jaak Petersoni (1983) ja Jakob Hurda (1994) monumendid Tartus, August Gailiti monument Valgas (2009). Samuti on ta loonud abstraktseid suurvorme Eestis, Soomes, Hollandis ja Argentiinas. Soansi viimaste aastate loomingut kannab rõõmsameelne intellektuaalne mäng kujundite tähendusväljaga. Möödunud kümnendite pronksi on asendanud teras, puu ja muud vähem kestvad materjalid ning ready-made. Ruumiinstallatsioonides kohtab äratuntavaid püsikujundeid, arutlusi skulptuuri olemuse ning tema suhete üle aja ja ruumiga. Jaak Soans on Eesti Kunstiakadeemia emeriitprofessor. Ta on pälvinud ENSV teenelise kunstniku (1980) ja ENSV rahvakunstniku (1986) aunimetuse, Kristjan Raua kunstipreemia (1974 ja 1986), Riia skulptuurikvadriennaali peapree.
artists.ben: He became a renewer of Estonian modernist sculpture in the 1970s. Alongside formal searches based on the interaction of plastic volumes and space, an exceptional pursuit of elegance appeared in his work. Soans has managed to poeticise bronze as a sculptural material of value, and his bronze sculptures are created with a pure silhouette effect. He broadened the thematics and communicativeness of Estonian sculpture, bringing into his works existential reflections on the possibilities of man and the humanities in a technology-based, alienating world. Soans can be viewed as an intellectual and a teacher, followed both by his students and his colleagues. The public knows him predominantly as a monumentalist. He has created more than 30 monuments and public sculptures and immortalised great national figures: for example the monuments to A. H. Tammsaare (1978), Voldemar Panso (1980) and Michel Sittow (1982) in Tallinn, the monuments to Kristjan Jaak Peterson (1983) and Jakob Hurt (1994) in Tartu, the monument to August Gailit in Valga (2009). He has also created abstract large-scale forms in Estonia, Finland, the Netherlands and Argentina. Soans's work of recent years carries a cheerful intellectual play with the field of meaning of figures. Bronze of past decades has been replaced by steel, wood and other less durable materials, as well as ready-made objects. In his spatial installations one encounters recognisable recurring motifs, reflections on the nature of sculpture and its relations with time and space. Jaak Soans is professor emeritus of the Estonian Academy of Arts. He has been awarded the honorary title of Meritorious Artist of the ESSR (1980) and People's Artist of the ESSR (1986), the Kristjan Raud Art Prize (1974 and 1986), the grand prize of the Riga Sculpture Quadrennial.

artists.b: Graafik. Oli 1960ndail eesti graafika uuendajaid (võttis kasutusele elektrograalise sõeltrüki). Taotles oma loomingus dokumentaalsust. Viljeles kõrvuti vabagraafikaga uudsete kompositsioonivõtetega raamatugraafikat (P. Rummo "Proloog ja probleemid" 1961, H. Jürissoni "Puu silmapiiril" 1966). Aastast 1975 kujundas infograafiliste kaartide sarja , sh Eesti kultuuriloolist atlast (kirjanike sünnipaigad, ehitismälestised jms 1995).
artists.ben: Graphic artist. Was among the reformers of Estonian graphic art in the 1960s (introduced electrographic screen printing). Sought documentary quality in his work. Cultivated, alongside free graphic art, book graphics with novel compositional methods (P. Rummo's "Proloog ja probleemid" 1961, H. Jürissoni's "Puu silmapiiril" 1966). From 1975 designed a series of infographic maps, including a cultural-historical atlas of Estonia (writers' birthplaces, architectural monuments etc. 1995).

artists.b: Vabaloomingu kõrval tegeles väljaannete illustreerimisega, teinud kujundusi teatrile, oli kunstnikuks kahes populaarteaduslikus ja kahes multifilmis täiskasvanutele.
artists.ben: Alongside free creative work, he/she was engaged in illustrating publications, made designs for theatre, was the artist for two popular-science and two animated films for adults.

artists.b: Sündis Harzis, nn Saksi Šveitsis, pastori perekonnas, õppis 1848-52 Dresdeni ja 1852-56 Düsseldorfi kunstiakadeemias. 1855-56 elas Viiburis, seejärel Tallinnas. Oli 1872-77 Tallinna toomkooli joonistusõpetaja. Tegutses ka maalijana, joonistajana, kunstiarvustajana, luuletajana. Maetud Mõigu kalmistule.
artists.ben: Born in the Harz, the so-called Saxon Switzerland, into a pastor's family, studied 1848-52 at the Dresden and 1852-56 at the Düsseldorf Art Academy. Lived in Vyborg 1855-56, then in Tallinn. Was a drawing teacher at the Tallinn Cathedral School 1872-77. Also worked as a painter, draughtsman, art critic, poet. Buried at Mõigu Cemetery.

artists.b: 1816 reisis kolmandat korda Itaaliasse, oli Roomas "Instituto Archeologico Germanico" kaasasutaja, samuti 1824 "Römischen Hyperboraeer" rühma asutaja koos Põhja-Euroopa teadlastega, kes uurisid klassikalisi varemeid.
artists.ben: In 1816 he traveled to Italy for the third time, was co-founder of the "Instituto Archeologico Germanico" in Rome, and likewise in 1824 founder of the "Römischen Hyperboraeer" group together with Northern European scholars who studied classical ruins.

artists.b: Kujur ja pedagoog;kunstihariduse omandas 1911.12 Münchenis A.Azbe kunstikoolis;1912-13 Pariisis Academie Russe'is ja Academie de la Grande Chaumiere'is;1914 arreteeriti ja saadeti Lõuna -Saksamaale oli sõjavang;osales pärast Eestisse naasmist "Pallase" kunstikooli asutamises;ENSV rahvakunstnik 1964.
artists.ben: Sculptor and educator; received his art education in 1911-12 in Munich at A. Azbe's art school; 1912-13 in Paris at the Academie Russe and the Academie de la Grande Chaumiere; in 1914 he was arrested and sent to southern Germany, was a prisoner of war; after returning to Estonia took part in founding the "Pallas" art school; People's Artist of the ESSR 1964.

artists.b: Skulptor ja joonistaja, tuntud eelkõige terasgravüüri tehnikas Eesti-, Liivi- ja Kuramaa vaadete autorina. Sündis Kuldigas kaupmehe ja laenuraamatukogu omaniku pojana, töötas maamõõtja ning kartograafina. Pärast õpinguid Saksamaal tegutses alates 1849 kodumaal skulptorina, joonistades suviti looduses. 1857 alustas terasgravüüride sarja väljaandmisega, mis ilmus 10 vihuna, igas 3 lehte. Albumitena ilmusid gravüürid, mis trükiti Darmstadtis, koos tekstidega kolmes köites 1866-67. 1913 ilmus Tallinnas Stavenhageni teoste reproalbum (39 joonistust ja 4 skulptuuri, väljaandja Carl Meissner)
artists.ben: Sculptor and draughtsman, known primarily as the author of views of Estonia, Livonia and Courland in the steel engraving technique. Born in Kuldīga as the son of a merchant and owner of a lending library, he worked as a land surveyor and cartographer. After studying in Germany, he worked as a sculptor at home from 1849, drawing outdoors in nature during the summers. In 1857 he began publishing a series of steel engravings, which appeared in 10 fascicles, each containing 3 sheets. The engravings were published as albums, printed in Darmstadt, together with texts, in three volumes in 1866–67. In 1913 a reproduction album of Stavenhagen's works was published in Tallinn (39 drawings and 4 sculptures, publisher Carl Meissner).

artists.b: 1856-1871 ilmus Saaremaa rahvariiete album erilehtedena Die Trachten d. XII Kirchspiele d. Oeselschen Kreises; sisaldas 14 lehte kivitrükke. Ümbertöötatult ilmus see Album oeselscher Bauerntrachten (20 lehte), 1914.a. Riias järeltrükk (13 lehte).
artists.ben: 1856–1871 an album of Saaremaa folk costumes was published as separate sheets, Die Trachten d. XII Kirchspiele d. Oeselschen Kreises; it contained 14 sheets of lithographs. In a reworked form it was published as Album oeselscher Bauerntrachten (20 sheets); in 1914 a reprint (13 sheets) was published in Riga.

artists.b: Marta Stratskas (s.1986) on Berliinis elav eesti kunstnik. Ta on lõpetanud Eesti Kunstiakadeemia maalikunsti magistrantuuri. Marta julgetes ja tekstureeritud maalides on ühendatud vanad baroki ja gooti elemendid, vastandudes kaasaegsetele popmotiividele, põimides omavahel sakraalseid, ekstreemseid inimtingimusi ja piirolukordi. Tema töödes sulanduvad teema ja teostus. Uurimus värvi, valguse ja kunstniku kohaloleku/kavatsuse vahel hetkes. Marta Stratskas on Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige aastast 2014 ja osalenud näitusetel alates 2009.aastast.
artists.wdesc: Estonian artist residing in Berlin, Germany (born 1986)
artists.ben: Marta Stratskas (b.1986) is an Estonian artist living in Berlin. She graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts with a master's degree in painting. Marta's bold and textured paintings combine old Baroque and Gothic elements, contrasting them with contemporary pop motifs, interweaving sacred, extreme human conditions and borderline situations. In her works theme and execution merge. A study of colour, light, and the presence/intention of the artist in the moment. Marta Stratskas has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 2014 and has participated in exhibitions since 2009.

artists.b: Oma pika elu jooksul jõudis ta tegutseda kirjaniku ja kirjastaja, ajakirjaniku, sportlase ja spordiorganisaatori, harrastusteatri näitleja ja eestvedaja, kunstniku-raamatu illustraatori, amatöörarheoloogina, elu lõpupoole ka paranähtuste uurija ja rahvaravitsejana. Ta oli tegev seltsi- ja karskusliikumises.
artists.ben: In the course of his long life he managed to work as a writer and publisher, journalist, athlete and sports organizer, amateur theatre actor and leader, illustrator of art books, amateur archaeologist, and towards the end of his life also as a researcher of paranormal phenomena and a folk healer. He was active in the temperance and society movement.

artists.b: Jakub Kolas (ka Jakub Kołas, valgevene keeles Якуб Колас; kodanikunimega Kanstancin Michajłavič Mickievič (Канстанцiн Міхайлавіч Міцкевіч); 22. oktoober (vkj 3. november) 1882 Stoŭbcy – 13. august 1956 Minsk) oli Valgevene kirjanik, üks valgevene kirjanduse rajajaid ning klassikuid.
artists.ben: Jakub Kolas (also Jakub Kołas, in Belarusian Якуб Колас; civil name Kanstancin Michajłavič Mickievič (Канстанцiн Міхайлавіч Міцкевіч); 22 October (o.s. 3 November) 1882 Stoŭbcy - 13 August 1956 Minsk) was a Belarusian writer, one of the founders and classics of Belarusian literature.

artists.b: Töötas aastail 1938–1944 Tartus vabakunstnikuna, kuuludes koos Amanda Jasmiini, Lydia Laasi, Salme Riigi ja Leontine Lind-Karuga Pallases kunstihariduse omandanud esimesse eesti naisskulptorite põlvkonda. Põgenes 1944 Saksamaale ja sealt 1950. aastal koos pojaga Itaaliasse Sanremosse.
artists.ben: Worked from 1938–1944 in Tartu as a freelance artist, belonging, together with Amanda Jasmiin, Lydia Laas, Salme Riig and Leontine Lind-Karu, to the first generation of Estonian women sculptors who acquired their art education at Pallas. Fled to Germany in 1944 and from there in 1950, together with her son, to Sanremo in Italy.

artists.b: 1942. a. asus õppima Tartusse Kõrgematele Kujutava Kunsti Kursustele. Õpetajateka A. Vabbe, A. Vardi, E. Kits, J. Võerahansu. Täiendas ennast KKKK-s. 1949. a. töötas Pärnu Linakombinaadis kunstnikuna. 1974-83. töötas Pärnu EPT-s kunstnikuna. Näitustel hakkas esinema 1947. aastast. 1991. sai Pärnu Linnavalitsuse poolt kujutava kunsti aastapreemia. Viljelenud õlimaali ja akvarelli. Hilised abstraktsed tööd nn akvamise tehnikas.
artists.ben: In 1942 he began studying at the Higher Courses of Fine Art in Tartu. His teachers were A. Vabbe, A. Vardi, E. Kits, J. Võerahansu. Furthered his studies at the KKKK. In 1949 he worked as an artist at the Pärnu Linakombinaat. From 1974-83 he worked as an artist at the Pärnu EPT. Began exhibiting in 1947. In 1991 received the Pärnu City Government's annual prize for fine art. Cultivated oil painting and watercolour. Late abstract works in the so-called akvamis technique.

artists.b:
Joann Sõstra sündis 1913. aastal Peipsi järve ääres Lisje külas paljulapselises peres. Ta käis neli klassi külakoolis, juba 15. aastasena töötas Joann Lauassaare turbarabas, hiljem tegi metsatöid.

1932. aastal läks Joann Sõstra Pärnumaale Kanakülla metsatöödele, kus sattus Leppoja tallu kostiliseks. Sealt leidis Joann Sõstra endale uue kodu ja lisaks kolmele kasulapsele, sündisid perenaise Olgaga veel 4 last.

Seoses talumaade riigistamisega, suundus Joann Sõstra 1949. aastal Viljandisse Metsakombinaati raietööliseks. 1967. aastal läks ta tööle Kilingi-Nõmmele Näidismetsamajandisse, kus tegeles erinevate metsatöödega.

Pärast infarkti 1977. aastal, mil tervis enam rasket füüsilist tööd teha ei lubanud, pühendus ta üha enam puuskulptuuride valmistamisele. Lisaks tema väga mitmekesisele puuskulptuuri loomingule, on Joann Sõstra teinud pajuvitstest mööbliesemeid, aiavärava, vaase, kummalise kujuga jalutuskeppe, puulusikaid ja -kulpe, punutud korve ja kandikuid. Tööde koguarvu on raske määrata, sest nende üle arvet peetud pole. Palju esemeid on tuttavatele ja sugulastele kingitud.

Joann Sõstrast on mitmel korral kirjutatud kui väga tublist töömehest, kuid mitte kunagi kui harrastuskunstnikust. Joann Sõstra suri 1992. aastal.
artists.ben:
Joann Sõstra was born in 1913 by Lake Peipsi in the village of Lisje, into a family with many children. He attended four grades of village school; already at the age of 15 Joann worked at the Lauassaare peat bog, later doing forest work.

In 1932 Joann Sõstra went to Kanaküla in Pärnumaa for forest work, where he ended up as a lodger at the Leppoja farm. There Joann Sõstra found himself a new home, and in addition to three foster children, 4 more children were born together with the mistress of the house, Olga.

In connection with the nationalisation of farmlands, Joann Sõstra moved to Viljandi in 1949 to work as a logger at the Forestry Combine. In 1967 he went to work at the Kilingi-Nõmme Demonstration Forestry Enterprise, where he was engaged in various forestry tasks.

After a heart attack in 1977, when his health no longer allowed heavy physical labour, he devoted himself increasingly to making wood sculptures. In addition to his very diverse body of wood sculpture, Joann Sõstra has made willow-wicker furniture pieces, a garden gate, vases, walking sticks of curious shapes, wooden spoons and ladles, woven baskets and trays. It is difficult to determine the total number of works, as no record of them has been kept. Many items have been given as gifts to acquaintances and relatives.

Joann Sõstra has on several occasions been written about as a very diligent working man, but never as an amateur artist. Joann Sõstra died in 1992.

artists.b: 1929–30 sai Kujutava Kunsti Sihtkapitali Valitsuse stipendiumi ja täiendas end Pariisis, kus töötas L'Academie de la grande Chaumière'is. Haridusministeeriumi ülesandel külastas ta prantsuse suurimat keskkooli Lycé Buffoni, kus tutvus keskkoolide õpetamismeetoditega joonistamise vallas. Esines maalidega Pariisis.
artists.ben: In 1929–30 he received a scholarship from the Board of the Cultural Endowment for Visual Art [Kujutava Kunsti Sihtkapital] and continued his education in Paris, where he worked at the Académie de la Grande Chaumière. On assignment from the Ministry of Education he visited the largest French secondary school, the Lycée Buffon, where he became acquainted with secondary-school teaching methods in the field of drawing. He exhibited paintings in Paris.

Taavi Talve (1970) is a Tallinn-based artist. His recent 16 mm analogue films are based on research stemming from a desire to connect events of the past to the present and with the artist himself. In his work, observations blend fact and fiction, and simultaneously take on a documentary and an imaginative approach.

Talve entered the Estonian art scene in 2005 as a member of the group Johnson & Johnson (with Indrek Köster). Together they made short films, videos, spatial installations, sculptures, objects, and site specific installations. Their work relies on neo-conceptual institutional and media critique, as well as a leftist resistance to market capitalism. One of the best known projects by J & J is the “Paldiski Project” (2006–2013), which involved a large part of the inhabitants of the city of Paldiski; discussing what kind of a sculpture should be created to commemorate Amandus Adamson, one of the best known sculptors in Estonia, in his home town. As Adamson was seen as a father figure for various communities of the city, the project aimed to set in motion a democratic process of decision-making in a city with a complicated history, as well as to propose a model of cooperation between the Estonian and Russian speaking communities. In 2013 a replica of Adamson's sculpture “Last Sigh of a Ship” (1899) was installed at the heart of Paldiski, however, only a month later, it was removed by the city authorities, and after a few years, due to a local initiative, it found a new home on the Pakri peninsula near Paldiski.

Talve's other collaborative projects and earlier work is characterised by a focus on the failure of articulation and self-expression, referencing, and a laconic visual language. His earlier works display elements of social criticism aimed at the political discourse of the newly independent Estonia, where market capitalism and nationalism intertwine. For example, Talve's first solo exhibition “Bookmarks” (2010, Hobusepea gallery) linked Margaret Thatcher's 1975 speech “Free Society”, Estonian song festivals, the neoliberal economic and social model, the economic crisis, political activism, and riots.

Talve's later works focus on archiving and connecting past and present events; here the artist acts as an agent conserving memories, presenting subjective interpretations and new imaginaries. In 2016 Talve exhibited at the show “Between Archive and Architecture. Neeme Külm, Krista Mölder, Taavi Talve” at the Kumu Art Museum (curated by Kati Ilves, 2016/2017), screening his film “Blind Spot” (2016). It tells the story of Epp Kotkas, who lived a.

artists.b: 1934. aastast hakkas Herman Talvik esinema Soome ja Eesti kunstinäitustel, II maailmasõja ajal töötas õpetajana (põhiliselt Tallinna Reaalkoolis), 1944 põgenes Rootsi, kus oli vabakutseline kunstnik. Väljapaistva eesti eksiilkunstniku isiknäitused Eestis toimusid 1971 ja 1981 Eesti Kunstimuuseumis Kadrioru lossis, 1991 Tartu Kunstimuuseumis, 2006-2007 Eesti Kunstimuuseumis Adamson-Ericu Muuseumis ja 2016 Hiiumaa muuseumis.
artists.ben: From 1934 Herman Talvik began exhibiting at art exhibitions in Finland and Estonia; during World War II he worked as a teacher (mainly at Tallinn Secondary School), in 1944 he fled to Sweden, where he was a freelance artist. Solo exhibitions of this outstanding Estonian émigré artist were held in Estonia in 1971 and 1981 at the Art Museum of Estonia in Kadriorg Palace, in 1991 at the Tartu Art Museum, in 2006-2007 at the Art Museum of Estonia's Adamson-Eric Museum, and in 2016 at the Hiiumaa Museum.

artists.wdesc: Estonian art critic, art historian and curator (born 1983)

artists.b: Laulja ja helilooja; Õppis Haapsalu kõrgemas algkoolis ja Petrogradi tehnikaülikoolis, laulmist eraviisil Armanda degli Abbati juures. Laulis 1918–44 Estonia ooperikooris, oli 1920–22 ühtlasi miniatuuriteatri Apollo näitleja ja muusikajuht, 1924–27 Paul Pinna Rahvateatri muusikajuht ja 1929–35 Tallinna Töölismuusika Ühingu koori- ja laulumängujuht. Asutas 1939 Estonia lauljatest meeskvarteti Heli 4. Põgenes 1944 Saksamaale, kuulus 1945–46 ühendusse "Eesti kunstnikud Lübeckis", hiljem ühendusse "Eesti kunstnikud Blombergis". Läks 1949 USA-sse, elas aastani1973 Chicagos, seejärel elu lõpuni Kanadas, laulis Toronto Eesti Meeskooris. Loonud ligi 50 laulu („Üksainus õis”, „Paula, sul on poisipea”, „Vanapoisi polka” jt). Isa kaupmees ja koduorelimeister.
artists.ben: Singer and composer; Studied at Haapsalu Higher Elementary School and the Petrograd Polytechnic Institute, and singing privately with Armanda degli Abbati. Sang in the Estonia opera choir from 1918-44, was also an actor and music director of the miniature theatre Apollo from 1920-22, music director of Paul Pinna's Rahvateater (People's Theatre) from 1924-27, and choir and singing-game leader of the Tallinn Workers' Music Society from 1929-35. Founded the male quartet Heli 4 from Estonia singers in 1939. Fled to Germany in 1944, belonged to the association "Estonian artists in Lübeck" from 1945-46, and later to the association "Estonian artists in Blomberg". Went to the USA in 1949, lived in Chicago until 1973, then in Canada for the rest of his life, singing in the Toronto Estonian Men's Choir. Composed nearly 50 songs ("Üksainus õis", "Paula, sul on poisipea", "Vanapoisi polka" and others). His father was a merchant and maker of home organs.

artists.b: Tiina Tammetalu (1961) eelistab määratleda end voolava identiteediga ja meediateülese, mittelahterdatava kunstnikuna, kes teostab end üheaegselt mitmel erineval loomealal: maalikunstis, graafilises disainis, illustratsioonis ning kureerib muu hulgas ka näitusi Eesti elavast maaliklassikast. Tammetalu on lõpetanud Eesti Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi maali eriala (1989) ning täiendanud end Eesti Kunstiakadeemia interdistsiplinaarsete kunstide magistriõppe (2003-2006). Ta on osalenud arvukatel näitustel nii Eestis kui mujal ning tema teosed kuuluvad mitmetesse kogudesse. Ta on Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Tiina Tammetalu (1961) prefers to define herself as an artist of fluid identity, transcending media and not to be pigeonholed, who realises herself simultaneously in several different creative fields: painting, graphic design, illustration, and, among other things, also curates exhibitions of living Estonian painting classics. Tammetalu graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute in painting (1989) and furthered her education in the interdisciplinary arts master's programme at the Estonian Academy of Arts (2003–2006). She has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and elsewhere, and her works belong to several collections. She is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.wdesc: Estonian sculptor, figure skating and roller skating coach and sportsperson (1950-2013)

artists.b: Sündinud 22.03.1947, Valga. Haridus: 1964–1973Tartu Kunstikool.
artists.ben: Born 22.03.1947, Valga. Education: 1964–1973 Tartu Art School.

artists.b: Erika Tammpere (s. 1942 Rakveres) on pikaajalise kogemusega tekstiilikunstnik, kelle looming ühendab sügava materjalitunnetuse, sotsiaalse tundlikkuse ja kaasaegse vormi. Ta lõpetas 1966. aastal Eesti NSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi kunstilise tekstiili erialal ning töötas pea kolmkümmend aastat tekstiilidisainerina mitmes Eesti ettevõttes, sealhulgas “Mistras”, kus oli ka peakunstnik.
artists.ben: Erika Tammpere (b. 1942 in Rakvere) is a textile artist with long experience, whose work combines a deep sense of material, social sensitivity and a contemporary form. She graduated in 1966 from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in the speciality of artistic textiles and worked for almost thirty years as a textile designer at several Estonian enterprises, including "Mistra", where she was also chief artist.

artists.b: Astus 1934. aastal vanemate soovil Tartu Ülikooli matemaatikat õppima. 1935. aastal alustas ta maaliõpinguid Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis Pallas Nikolai Triigi käe all. Ta põgenes 1944. aastal Saksamaale. Seal astus ta Müncheni Tehnikaülikooli, mille lõpetas arhitektina. Ta töötas seejärel samas õppeasutuses arhitektuuriprofessor Döllgasti assistendina. Siirdus hiljem Rootsi, kus töötas arhitektuuribüroos.
artists.ben: In 1934, at his parents' wish, he entered Tartu University to study mathematics. In 1935 he began painting studies at the Pallas Higher Art School under Nikolai Triik. He fled to Germany in 1944. There he entered the Technical University of Munich, which he graduated from as an architect. He then worked at the same institution as an assistant to the professor of architecture Döllgast. He later moved to Sweden, where he worked at an architecture bureau.

artists.b: Kalevivabrik asutati 1829. aastal, toodanguks oli villane kangas - kalev. 1858. aastal töötas Kärdla kalevivabrikus juba 373 meest ja 430 naist. Vabriku töös esines küll lühiajalisi seisakuid ja kehvemaid aegu (1870. aastal põles vabrik maha, misjärel valmis 1873. aastal uus neljakorruseline hoone; ja sajandivahetusel seisti silmitsi majanduslike raskustega), kuid hoolimata sellest oli kuni Esimese maailmasõjani tegemist saare kõige olulisema tööstusettevõttega. 1879. aastal oli toodang 200 000 arssinat ligikaudu 800 000 rubla väärtuses. 1908. aastal ühendas Narva Manufaktuur hättasattunud Kärdla kalevivabriku endaga. Kärdla vabrik tootis siis aastas 100 000 meetrit kalevit (umbes kolm korda vähem kui 1879. aastal). 1941. aastal hävis vabrik tulekahjus.
artists.ben: The cloth factory (Kalevivabrik) was founded in 1829, its product being woollen cloth - kalev. In 1858, 373 men and 430 women already worked at the Kärdla cloth factory. Although the factory's operations experienced short-term stoppages and harder times (in 1870 the factory burned down, after which a new four-storey building was completed in 1873; and at the turn of the century it faced economic difficulties), it was nevertheless the island's most important industrial enterprise until the First World War. In 1879 output was 200,000 arshins worth approximately 800,000 roubles. In 1908 the Narva Manufaktuur merged with the struggling Kärdla cloth factory. The Kärdla factory then produced 100,000 metres of cloth per year (about three times less than in 1879). In 1941 the factory was destroyed by fire.

artists.b: Marje Taska on sündinud 1955. Aastal Tallinnas, lõpetanud Tallinna Muusikakeskkooli klaveri erialal ning õppinud germanistikat Tartu ülikoolis. Oma kunstiõpinguid alustas ta Tõnis Vindi juures, olles tema esimeseks õpilaseks. Edasised kunsti- ja keeleõpingud kuuluvad juba Rootsi eluperioodi. Pärast kolimist Stockholmi 1982. aastal on ta elanud nii Lapimaal kui Lõuna-Rootsis. Tänaseks kodulinnaks on taas Stockholm, kus ta paralleelselt Tallinnaga elab ja töötab vabakutselise kunstniku- ja kuraatorina.
artists.ben: Marje Taska was born in 1955 in Tallinn, graduated from the Tallinn Music High School in piano, and studied German philology at the University of Tartu. She began her art studies with Tõnis Vint, being his first student. Her further art and language studies belong already to her period of life in Sweden. After moving to Stockholm in 1982, she has lived both in Lapland and in southern Sweden. Today her home city is once again Stockholm, where, in parallel with Tallinn, she lives and works as a freelance artist and curator.

artists.b: Sündis Tartus. Õppis 1897-1898 Tartu saksa käsitööliste seltsi joonistuskursustel. 1904 Peterburis parun A. Stieglitzi kunsttööstuskoolis, 1905-1906 Ants Laikmaa stuudios Tallinnas ja 1906 Peterburis J. Goldblatti kunstikursustel. 1906 asus Helsingisse, 1907 Pariisi, kus jätkas kunstiõpinguid.
artists.ben: Born in Tartu. Studied in 1897-1898 at the drawing courses of the Tartu German Craftsmen's Society. In 1904 at Baron A. Stieglitz's School of Applied Art in Petersburg, in 1905-1906 at Ants Laikmaa's studio in Tallinn and in 1906 at J. Goldblatt's art courses in Petersburg. In 1906 he moved to Helsinki, in 1907 to Paris, where he continued his art studies.

artists.b: Kristjan TEDER (1901, Kuigatsi vald, Tartumaa – 1960, Tartu) oli eesti maalikunstnik ja aednik, kes viljeles peamiselt lillemaali, vähemal määral ka maastiku-, portree- ja olustikumaali. Tema varajane looming on uusasjalik, iseloomulikud on selgelt piiritletud vormid ja tuhmjas pruunikas koloriit. 1930. aastatel muutus tema maalimisviis impressionistlikult varjundirikkaks, koloriit heledaks ja teoseti värvierksaks, kujutuslaadis ilmneb kohati naivistlikku rohmakust. Pärast II maailmasõda valminud lillemaalides keskendas Teder tähelepanu ruumilisuse esiletoomisele ning valguse ja varjuga modelleerimisele. Barokselt lopsakate lillemaalide kõrval valmis tagasihoidlikumas värgigammas maastikke ja linnavaateid. 1950. aastate teisel poolel maalis Teder peamiselt värvierksaid lillepilte ja maastikke. Kunstihariduse omandas Teder Pallase kunstikoolis esmalt Konrad Mägi ja siis Ado Vabbe käe all ning Pariisis Vassili Šuhhajevi eraakadeemias. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
artists.ben: Kristjan TEDER (1901, Kuigatsi Parish, Tartumaa – 1960, Tartu) was an Estonian painter and gardener who mainly cultivated flower painting, and to a lesser extent also landscape, portrait and genre painting. His early work is New Objectivity in style, characterised by clearly delineated forms and a dull brownish colour scheme. In the 1930s his manner of painting became impressionistically rich in nuance, the colouring bright and, in some works, vivid, with the mode of depiction occasionally showing a naivistic roughness. In the flower paintings created after World War II, Teder focused his attention on bringing out spatiality and modelling with light and shadow. Alongside baroquely lush flower paintings, he also produced landscapes and townscapes in a more restrained colour range. In the second half of the 1950s Teder mainly painted vividly coloured flower pictures and landscapes. Teder acquired his art education at the Pallas Art School, first under Konrad Mägi and then under Ado Vabbe, and in Paris at Vassili Šuhhajev's private academy. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.

artists.b: Ülo TEDER (1923, Võru – 2008) oli eesti maalikunstnik, kes on viljelenud akvarell-, pastell-, õli- ja temperamaali. Loonud hoogsas laadis maastiku- ja linnavaateid, figuraalkompositsioone ja natüürmorte. Kujundanud muuhulgas ka filmiplakateid. Kunstihariduse omandas Teder Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis ja ERKI-s.
artists.ben: Ülo TEDER (1923, Võru – 2008) was an Estonian painter who worked in watercolour, pastel, oil and tempera painting. He created landscapes and townscapes, figural compositions and still lifes in a vigorous style. Among other things he also designed film posters. Teder received his art education at the Tartu State Art Institute and at ERKI.

artists.b: Enn Tegova (s.1946 Tartus) loominguline tegevus on läbivalt seotud Tartuga, mille kunstiellu on ta andnud tugeva ning kestva panuse. Tema maale iseloomustab tugev metafüüsiline lähenemine, maagilise ning müütilise alge otsimine, mis mõjutatud muuhulgas kodupiirkonna ürgsest loodusest.
artists.ben: Enn Tegova's (b. 1946 in Tartu) creative activity has been consistently connected with Tartu, to whose art life he has made a strong and lasting contribution. His paintings are characterised by a strong metaphysical approach, a search for magical and mythical origins, influenced, among other things, by the primeval nature of his home region.

artists.b: Sündinud 21.08.1932, Tapa.

Astus Pallasesse 1939. aastal, tema graafikaõpetajateks olid Arkadio Laigo ja Ado Vabbe. 1946. aastal lõpetas Tartu Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi. Töötas 1947-1949 samas graafikaõppejõuna, seejärel oli vabakunstnik. Kunstnike Liidu liige alates 1946. aastast. Viljeles erinevaid sügavtrükitehnikaid. On enim tuntud kui linnapiltide ja maastikuvaadete meister.
artists.ben: Entered Pallas in 1939, his teachers of printmaking were Arkadio Laigo and Ado Vabbe. In 1946 he graduated from the Tartu State Art Institute. From 1947-1949 he worked there as a printmaking instructor, after which he was a freelance artist. Member of the Artists' Union from 1946. He practised various intaglio printing techniques. He is best known as a master of cityscapes and landscape views.

artists.b: Valiti 1939 Eesti Kirjanikkude Liidu esimeheks. 1940–1941 töötas ajalehe Kommunist toimetuses ning oli kirjastuse Ilukirjandus ja Kunst peatoimetaja, lisaks oli ta Eesti Nõukogude Kirjanike Liidu organiseerimistoimkonna esimees. Teise maailmasõja ajal korraldas ta NSV Liidu tagalas eesti kirjanduselu. 1944–1946 ja 1950–1954 oli Eesti Nõukogude Kirjanike Liidu esimees, 1950–1958 Eesti NSV Ülemnõukogu Presiidiumi esimees ja NSV Liidu Ülemnõukogu Presiidiumi esimehe asetäitja.
artists.ben: He was elected chairman of the Estonian Writers' Union in 1939. In 1940–1941 he worked in the editorial office of the newspaper Kommunist and was editor-in-chief of the publishing house Ilukirjandus ja Kunst; he was also chairman of the organizing committee of the Estonian Soviet Writers' Union. During the Second World War he organized Estonian literary life in the rear of the USSR. In 1944–1946 and 1950–1954 he was chairman of the Estonian Soviet Writers' Union, and in 1950–1958 chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Council of the Estonian SSR and deputy chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Council of the USSR.

artists.b: Osvald Timmas sündis 17.09.1913 Saaremaal Kärla vallas, Pai külas, suri 27.10. 2005 Torontos, Kanadas. Ta õppis Saaremaa ühisgümnaasiumi humanitaarharus ja Tallinnas Tondi sõjakoolis, mille lõpetas 1934. Seejärel õppis Eesti Tarbiajateühistute Keskühistu (ETK) Ühistegevusliidu koolis ja 1937–1944 Tartu ülikooli majandusteaduskonnas. Oli korp! Rotalia liige. Kunsti alal võttis eratunde 1939–1942 Nikolai Kummitsalt ja 1942–1944 Günther Reindorffilt. 1944 põgenes koos abikaasa Erikaga Rootsi, kus töötas elukindlustuse alal. 1947–1949 õppis Stockholmis illustreerimiskursustel. 1951 asus Kanadasse Torontosse, kus töötas samuti elukindlustuse alal. 1956 sai Kanada kodakondsuse. 1960. aastatel äratas Timmas tähelepanu akvarellidega, milles kujutas geoloogilisi maapinnakihte ja veealust maailma, samuti vaateid mikroskoobist. 1972 pühendus täielikult kunstile. 1961–1968 oli Timmas Colour and Form Society president ja 1971–1975 Ontario Society of Artists asepresident, Timmas oli samuti Eesti Kunstide Keskuse (Estonian Arts Centre) asutajaliige 1974 Ontarios. 1973 valiti O. Timmas Kanada Kuningliku Kunstiakadeemia liikmeks. 1977 sai Briti kuninganna teenetemärgi. 2005 anti O. Timmasele Eesti Vabariigi Valgetähe V klassi teenetemärk.Oma testamendis asutas ta Erika ja Osvalt Timmase mälestusfondi, eesmärgiga säilitada ja arendada eesti kultuuri ja kunsti. Sellest fondist on toetatud näiteks Kumu ehitamist, Tartu Kunstimuuseumi tegevust, eesti pagulaskunsti näitust 2010–2011 Tallinnas, Tartus jm. Isiknäitused Eestis toimusid: 1990 Adamson-Ericu muuseumis, 2003 Rahvusraamatukogus ja Saaremaa muuseumis.
artists.ben: Osvald Timmas was born 17.09.1913 in Saaremaa, Kärla parish, Pai village, died 27.10.2005 in Toronto, Canada. He studied in the humanities branch of Saaremaa Joint Gymnasium and at the Tondi Military School in Tallinn, which he graduated from in 1934. He then studied at the school of the Estonian Consumer Cooperatives' Central Union (ETK) Cooperative Union and in 1937–1944 at the Faculty of Economics of the University of Tartu. He was a member of the fraternity Rotalia. In art, he took private lessons in 1939–1942 from Nikolai Kummits and in 1942–1944 from Günther Reindorff. In 1944 he fled together with his wife Erika to Sweden, where he worked in the life insurance field. In 1947–1949 he studied on illustration courses in Stockholm. In 1951 he moved to Toronto, Canada, where he also worked in life insurance. In 1956 he received Canadian citizenship. In the 1960s Timmas attracted attention with watercolours depicting geological layers of the earth's surface and the underwater world, as well as views seen through a microscope. In 1972 he devoted himself entirely to art. In 1961–1968 Timmas was president of the Colour and Form Society and in 1971–1975 vice-president of the Ontario Society of Artists. Timmas was also a founding member of the Estonian Arts Centre in Ontario in 1974. In 1973 O. Timmas was elected a member of the Royal Canadian Academy of Arts. In 1977 he received a decoration from the British Queen. In 2005 O. Timmas was awarded the Order of the White Star, 5th Class, of the Republic of Estonia. In his will he established the Erika and Osvald Timmas Memorial Fund, with the aim of preserving and developing Estonian culture and art. This fund has, for example, supported the building of Kumu, the activities of the Tartu Art Museum, the exhibition of Estonian émigré art in 2010–2011 in Tallinn, Tartu and elsewhere. Solo exhibitions in Estonia took place: in 1990 at the Adamson-Eric Museum, in 2003 at the National Library and at the Saaremaa Museum.

artists.b: Esines kunstinäitustel alates 1930. aastate lõpust. Skulptorina ühines 1950. aastate lõpul üldistava vormikäsitlusega, pühendudes peamiselt portreeloomingule. Töötles eriti meisterlikult puud, kuid on loonud ka šamott-, terrakota- ja betoonskulptuure. Isikunäitused 1958, 1980 Tartu Kunstimuuseumis.

15. jaanuaril 1920 kuulutas sõjaministeerium välja konkursi Vabadussõja mälestusmedali kavandi väljatöötamiseks. Konkursi võitis ka skulptorina tuntud August Timus. Muide, järgmisel aastal sai August Timus Eesti riigivapi kavandivõistlusel teise koha, pakkudes vapi põhielemendiks stiililt sellist kotkast, millest hiljem kujunes Kaitseliidu embleem.

artists.ben: On 15 January 1920 the Ministry of War announced a competition for the design of the War of Independence commemorative medal. The competition was also won by August Timus, known as a sculptor. Incidentally, the following year August Timus took second place in the competition for the design of the Estonian state coat of arms, proposing as the main element of the coat of arms an eagle of the style from which the emblem of the Defence League later developed.

artists.b: Tjurina omandas tekstiilidisaini hariduse Moskva Tekstiiliakadeemias aastatel 1985–1990 ning töötas seejärel kangadisainerina Kreenholmi Manufaktuuris aastatel 1990–1993. Alates 1994. aastast on ta olnud Narva Kunstikooli õpetaja, panustades järjepidevalt noorte kunstnike arengusse. Täiendades oma haridusteed lõpetas taTallinna Ülikooli kunstiõpetaja eriala kaugõppeosakonna (2008–2013). Kunstielus on ta aktiivselt osalenud alates 1990. aastast, olles Narva kunstnike ühenduse „Vestervalli“ liige.
artists.ben: Tjurina obtained her education in textile design at the Moscow Textile Academy from 1985 to 1990, and subsequently worked as a fabric designer at the Kreenholm Manufaktuur from 1990 to 1993. Since 1994 she has been a teacher at the Narva Art School, consistently contributing to the development of young artists. Continuing her education, she completed the correspondence department of art teacher studies at Tallinn University (2008–2013). She has actively participated in artistic life since 1990, being a member of the Narva artists' association "Vestervalli".

artists.b:
6. augustil saadeti Aleksander Nevski katedraalist viimsele teekonnale skulptor Tamara Ditman. Ta maeti Aleksander Nevski kalmistule.

Tamara Ditman sündis Venemaal Habarovskis sõjaväelase perekonnas 9. VIII 1945. Tema lapsepõlv möödus Tallinnas. Pärast ERKI lõpetamist töötas ta kunstipedagoogina Tallinna 52. keskkoolis ning spordiühingus Kalev kunstnikuna, 1985. aastast oli vabakutseline.

Viimastel eluaastatel kannatas kunstnik raskete tervuseprobleemide tõttu, ta loobus tööst tegevkunstnikuna ja pühendus usuelule ortodoksi kirikus.
artists.ben:
On 6 August the sculptor Tamara Ditman was sent on her final journey from Alexander Nevsky Cathedral. She was buried at Alexander Nevsky Cemetery.

Tamara Ditman was born in Russia, in Habarovsk, into a military family on 9 August 1945. Her childhood was spent in Tallinn. After graduating from ERKI she worked as an art teacher at Tallinn Secondary School No. 52 and as an artist at the sports society Kalev, and from 1985 she was a freelance artist.

In her last years the artist suffered from serious health problems, she gave up work as a practising artist and devoted herself to religious life in the Orthodox church.

artists.b: Lembit Tolli (1927–2013) lõpetas 1953. aastal ENSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi ning alustas samal aastal kunstinäitustel esinemist. 1950. aastate looming järgib natuuri ning omaaegset soovituslikku temaatikat. Kümnendi lõpu modernistlik kujundlikkus haarab kaasa ka Lembit Tolli; ta laiendab materjalivalikut, huvitudes dolomiidist, puuskulptuuri võimalustest, keevitatud skulptuurist, epoksüvaigust ning kohrutatud metallist. Portree- ja figuuriloomingu kõrval on Tolli loonud meisterlikud reljeefid Martin Saksa ja Endel Taniloo F. R. Kreutzwaldi mälestusmärgile Kadriorus (1958) ja rahvuseepose motiividele tugineva poeetilise pronksreljeefi „Sõit maailma otsa” Jääretke obeliskile (1960) Tallinnas Maarjamäel.
artists.ben: Lembit Tolli (1927–2013) graduated from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1953 and began exhibiting his work the same year. His creative work of the 1950s follows nature and the recommended thematics of the time. The modernist imagery of the end of the decade also drew in Lembit Tolli; he expanded his choice of materials, taking an interest in dolomite, the possibilities of wood sculpture, welded sculpture, epoxy resin and embossed metal. Alongside portrait and figure work, Tolli created masterful reliefs for Martin Saks and Endel Taniloo's monument to F. R. Kreutzwald in Kadriorg (1958) and the poetic bronze relief "Sõit maailma otsa" ["Journey to the End of the World"], based on motifs from the national epic, for the Ice Voyage obelisk (1960) at Maarjamäe in Tallinn.

artists.b: Sündis Tallinnas, õppis 1947-49 Tallinna Tarbekunsti Instituudis keraamikat ja 1949-53 ERKI-s graafikat. On töötanud kunstiakadeemia õppejõuna, 1992. a. professor. 1965. a. ENSV teeneline kunstnik. Silmapaistvamaid, viljakamaid ja rahvusvaheliselt tuntumaid eesti graafikuid, peamiselt sügavtrüki alal. Loonud ka eksliibriseid ja illustratsioone pms eesti luuletustele.
artists.ben: Born in Tallinn, studied ceramics 1947-49 at the Tallinn Institute of Applied Art and graphics 1949-53 at ERKI. Has worked as a teacher at the art academy, professor since 1992. Honoured Artist of the ESSR in 1965. One of the most outstanding, prolific and internationally best-known Estonian graphic artists, mainly in the field of intaglio printing. Has also created ex libris and illustrations, mostly for Estonian poems.

artists.b: Astus Peterburi Kunstiakadeemiasse, kus tegi kiireid edusamme. Pälvis joonistusklassis oma andekusega suurt tähelepanu. Selleks, et õppida figuuride joonistamist, käis akadeemia antiigi-osakonnas harjutamas. Uuris seal väga põhjalikult kreeka antiik-kunsti.
artists.ben: He entered the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts, where he made rapid progress. In the drawing class his talent attracted great attention. In order to study figure drawing, he practised in the academy's antiquities department. There he studied Greek ancient art very thoroughly.

artists.b: Lõpetanud Eesti Kunstiakadeemia maali erialal, töötanud maali õppejõuna Tartu Ülikoolis, Eesti Kunstiakadeemias ja Sally Stuudios. Aastatel 2013-2019 oli ta Eesti Kunstnike Liidu president, seejärel kuni 2025 asepresident. Allsalu on Eesti Maalikunstnike Liidu juhatuse ning mitmete kunstiasutuste nõukogu liige. Tema teoseid leidub Eesti Kunstimuuseumi, Tartu Kunstimuuseumi, Eesti Panga, AkzoNobeli ja Eesti Rahvusraamatukogu kogudes, samuti erakogudes Eestis ja välismaal.
artists.ben:
Jaan Toomik (1961) is a painter, video installation and performance artist, whose work stems from a metaphysical, biocentric and shamanist outlook on the world. His work, mostly nature-poetic and autobiographical, focuses on eternal themes like life and death, religion and spirituality, that tie the human body to the cyclical processes in nature. In his imagery Toomik is a minimalist, often choosing simple tools to achieve meditative repetition and dynamics.

Toomik started out as a painter at the end of the 1980s. His early works include the large-scale Neo-Expressionist paintings “Menstruatsioon” (Menstruation, 1989) and “Tantsija” (Dancer,1990). Influenced by the political situation in newly-independent Estonia at the beginning of the 1990s, Toomik found site-specific performance and installation. During his transition into a post-conceptual artist, Toomik created boundary-probing work commenting on the attitudes and political situation of the time. One of the most symbolic among them is the installation “15. mai – 1. juuni 1992” (15 May – 1 June 1992), exhibited at the pavilion of Eesti Näitused at “Artmix”, the second exhibition by the art collective S&K. The work consisted of glass jars that contained the artist's excrement, collected between the above mentioned dates, and a description of his menu. By now, the afterlife of this work and the meanings surrounding it, have become a notable episode in recent Estonian art history. At the time when the piece was exhibited, the installation did not cause a scandal, however it became controversial in 1995 when the newspaper Eesti Ekspress wrote about it. “Shitting in a jar” became a metaphor for Toomik's artistic practice in the media, and Estonian contemporary art as a whole for everything that seemed even a little incomprehensible or disturbing. The work was recreated in 2012 for the exhibition “MÖH? FUI! ÖÄK! OSSA! VAU! The Classics of Estonian Contemporary Art”.

Finding a language in his installation and performance art, that was simultaneously minimal and impersonal in form but suggestive in content, Toomik was among the first artists in Estonia to document their performances in video. His natural-poetic videos were masterfully created, using simple means to convey a mental space, captivating to the audience. In 1994 Toomik created a video installation for the São Paulo Biennial, titled “Teekond São Paulosse” (Way to São Paulo), consisting of a mirror cube, floating on rivers in Tartu, Prague and São Paulo; cities located on the same geographical parallel. artists.b: Media artist working with data, surveillance and the machinery of e-Estonia.
artists.ben:
Timo Toots (1982) is an interdisciplinary artist, who creates interactive installations, which deal with social behavioural patterns, information fields and virtuality. His work problematizes the impact of technological advancements on society and the individual’s life quality.

One of the first works by Toots which exemplifies the relationship between a human being and technology was “Media Bubble” (2008). It created a media landscape around the spectator, in which titles from international and local media were projected. The more rapid one swirls on the plate, the more media foam will appear around the spectator and on the floor.

Interactive installation “Hall of Fame” (2009) maps the personal information field and calculates ones social position based on an ID-card. If “Hall of Fame” leaves a rather playful impression due to its ability to generate pseudo data, its advancement “Memopol-II” (2011-2013) is much more powerful, displaying information not only found from the internet, but also governmental databases. For evaluating one’s digital footprint, you’d have to insert your ID-card with PIN-code to the machine or scan your passport. One of the ideas of “Memopol”, is to show the same tools which are present in our everyday life, in a different aesthetic register. “Memopol-III” (2018) collects information in addition to the aforementioned databases also from smartphone and cloud services. The installation will be exhibited in KUMU at the exhibition “Archaeology of The Screen”.

The vulnerability of an individual trusting technological devices, is expressed in Toots’ exhibition “Z” (2014), in which the perception of reality and sense of danger for the exhibition guest was manipulated. By using infrared-sensitive screens, a completely different reality is exposed rather than looking with a naked eye. In the centre of the spatial installation was a (cyber) police car, which acquired different properties than when looking through the screen.

artists.b: Kunstnik sündis Tallinnas, 1944 lõpetas Kodasoo algkooli ja põgenes samal aastal Rootsi. 1947 lõpetas Norrköpingi kaubanduskooli. 1963-67 õppis Stockholmi ülikooli juures Kursverksamheteni graafikaateljees ning 1964-67 Stockholmi Kõrgema Rakenduskunstikooli õhtukursustel. 1968 sai Rootsi Eesti Kultuuri Koondise liikmeks. Ta loomingus on valdavad graafilised seeriad, ruumilised objektid, akrüülmaalid ja kollaažid.
artists.ben: The artist was born in Tallinn, in 1944 finished Kodasoo primary school and fled to Sweden the same year. In 1947 finished the Norrköping School of Commerce. 1963–67 studied at the graphic arts studio of Kursverksamheten at Stockholm University, and 1964–67 at the evening courses of the Stockholm Higher School of Applied Arts. In 1968 became a member of the Swedish-Estonian Cultural Association. His work is dominated by graphic series, spatial objects, acrylic paintings and collages.

(1967) is an Estonian queer feminist artist and activist, working since the 1990s and focusing mainly on feminist critique and questions of identity, using performance, video, installations and digital technologies.

Tralla studied painting in Estonian Academy of Arts and one of the most significant examples of her early work is the 1995 exhibition „Est. Fem“, where she participated both as curator and artist. This exhibition is considered to be the first feminist show in Estonia. At “Est.Fem” Tralla exhibited an installation entitled “This is how we gave birth to Estonian feminism” (1995) that brings together the most prominent themes in her work of the 1990s: the position of Eastern European women in transitional societies, expectations for women in newly independent Estonia and the lasting influence of the Soviet period that was perhaps greater than people were willing to admit.

In the end of the 1990s Tralla began increasingly working with digital technologies.From 2000 to 2003 she was a professor at the e-media centre at Estonian Academy of Arts. Tralla's work has been associated with cyber feminism, a movement that, according to Katrin Kivimaa, often uses “feminine” paraphernalia, themes and colour combinations to highlight and ridicule gender stereotypes and hierarchies. The interactive installation “Sing with me” (2000) revolves around the Estonian tradition of collective singing and national melodies. The computer animation depicts the artist in a swimsuit and swimming cap standing on the song festival grounds and singing “Kungla rahvas”. This work is an expression of Tralla's continuous interest in what it means to identify as an Estonian and a woman, although humour, irony and grotesque she often uses are clearly evident here too.

Since 1996 Tralla has lived in London, where her dedication to activism has increasingly deepened. Even though Tralla has consciously kept it separate from her artistic practice, taking political stances is nevertheless an integral part of her work. Already in the 1990s when Tralla was still living in Estonia, she saw media as a tool to convey her message as an artist, so she developed a media persona – a foul woman working outside the norms. Tralla has used expressions she has developed as an artist as tools in her activism and vice versa: she has taken her experiences as an activist and applied them to her artistic practice. In 2018 during the performance night of the 13th Baltic triennial “Bastard voices” Tralla used these experiences to create the background for her work, focusing on the question of the various.

artists.b: Trell sündis Jõhvi linnas ning maalimisega hakkas tegelema 1973. aastal. Aeg, mil Trell töötas koos Rein Kelpmanniga Tallinna II Toidukaubastu (asus Sepa ja Kopli tänava nurgal) reklaamikunstnikuna, oli tema kui maalija käekirja kujunemise aeg. Ta on olnud Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige 1986. aastast. Oluliseks impulsiks maalida oli inimese psühholoogiline seisund tolleaegses repressiivses Nõukogude ühiskonnas. Maalimine oli tingitud vajadusest välja elada pingeid iseendas selles situatsioonis. Sel ajal sündis palju figuraalseid maale, kus domineeris pühholoogiline sümbolism ja milles oli kihtide all ikka Trellile omane iroonia. On selge, et need teosed tolleaegses süsteemis jõudsid ülevaatenäitustele vaid läbi tõsise kadalipu, ning leidus maale, mis ei jõudnudki näitustele žürii ettevaatlikkuse tõttu. 1980ndate lõpu- ja 1990ndate algusaastatel kunstniku käekiri pisut muutus. Sellesse sugenes rohkem sümbolismi ja abstraktseid elemente. Tollest ajast on kodumaal vähe teoseid säilinud, sest enamik jõudis ja jäi Soome ning mujale välismaale. 1992. aastal Saaremaa perioodil muutusid teosed aina abstraktsemaks, teoste hulgas oli vaid paar portreed. 1990ndate lõpust järgnes pikk ekspressiiv.
artists.ben: Trell was born in the town of Jõhvi and began painting in 1973. The period when Trell worked together with Rein Kelpmann as an advertising artist at Tallinn Food Store No. 2 (located at the corner of Sepa and Kopli streets) was the time when his handwriting as a painter took shape. He has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1986. An important impulse to paint was the psychological state of a person in the repressive Soviet society of that time. Painting was driven by the need to work through the tensions within himself in that situation. Many figurative paintings were created at that time, dominated by psychological symbolism and, beneath the layers, always Trell's characteristic irony. It is clear that in the system of that time these works reached overview exhibitions only through a serious gauntlet, and there were paintings that never reached exhibitions at all due to the jury's caution. In the late 1980s and early 1990s the artist's handwriting changed somewhat. It acquired more symbolism and abstract elements. From that time few works have survived in the homeland, since most reached and remained in Finland and elsewhere abroad. In 1992, during the Saaremaa period, the works became increasingly abstract, and among them there were only a couple of portraits. From the late 1990s a long expressive.

artists.b: Sündinud 18.06.1982; surnud 30.05.2017. Haridus: 2012         Linköpingi Ülikool, Soouuringud, MA; 2010         Eesti Kunstiakdeemia, Fotograafia eriala, MA; 2007         Tartu Kõrgem Kunstikool, Fotograafia osakond, BA.
artists.ben:
Anna-Stina Treumund (1982–2017) was a lesbian artist, the first in Estonia to identify as such. Her background was in photography and gender studies, and a major part of her work is directly linked to queer-feminist activism and BDSM-culture.

The exhibition “You, Me and Everyone We Don't Know” (2010) included Treumund's first photo series which focused on lesbian identity and her contemporaries in the queer community in Estonia during the late 2000s. This series looked on the one hand, at the dreams of lesbian women, such as partnership, marriage, having children, sexual desires, familial intimacy, as well as the right of gender self-identification. On the other hand, the exhibition introduced terms like “drag” and “queer” to the Estonian feminist art community for the first time, and listed famous lesbians and lesbian feminists from Gertrude Stein to Lisa Duggan. The show was a turning point for the community of Estonian gender studies as well as for the art field – from that point on, queer theory and activism have been increasingly clearly highlighted. The work “Loser 2011” (2011), an homage to Kai Kaljo, took a strong critical stance against patriarchy, and ridiculed men whose masculinity was based on homophobia.

In the following years, Treumund continued seeking, creating and interpreting the lesbian and BDSM community in a historic context. In the series “Woman in the Corner of Mutsu's Drawings” (2010) Treumund re-staged Marju Mutsu's series of prints “One” and “Together”, in which the latter shows two women on a bed, yet in Treumund's interpretation she remained alone, waiting for the other. In 2012 the artist presented the series “Lilli, Reed, Frieda, Sabine, Eha, Malle, Alfred, Rein and Mari“. Treumund invited her close friends to embody women and transgender people from the 19th and 20th centuries, whose relationships we know nothing about or, conversely, whose intimate life has been published in newspapers extensively. With this series, Treumund created a visual image of a past yet to be discovered by historians. In 2013 Treumund closed a chapter in her research into lesbian identity and community with the exhibition “Well then, Jane, call to aid your fancy:– suppose you were no longer a girl well reared and disciplined, but a wild boy indulged from childhood upwards”. The artist looked at well-known children’s stories from a queer perspective, depicting them according to her own image and dreams.

In 2015 Treumund began a new creative chapter with the exhibition “Dread”, stemming from her interest in BDSM practices. One of the central photo.

artists.b: Maalikunstnik, graafik ja pedagoog. Loometee alguses joonistas Eesti satiiriväljaandeile poliitilise sisuga pilte, sh karikatuure (pseud Vaikne). Esimesena äratas tähelepanu figuur "Tulekandja" "Noor-Eesti" I albumi kaanel. Tegi juugendlikult stiliseeritud ornamendil ja sümbolkujundeil põhinevaid illustratsioone ja kujunduse G. Suitsu luulekogule "Tulemaa" (1913) ja "Noor-Eesti" V albumile (1915). Norras viibides keskendus maastikumaalile ("dekoratiivne Norra maastik" 1908). Varases maaliloomingus ilmneb sümbolismi mõju, eriti rahvusromantilistes muistendiainelistes ja kangelaslikke võitlussteene kujutavais kompositsioonides. Triik oli üks hinnatumaid portretiste, rõhutas vaimsust, sisemist väärikust ja dramatismi (K. Mägi 1908, Juhan Liiv 1909, M. Levin, I. Menning ja Viktoria Martna 1910). Hiljem muutus väljenduslaad esialgsega võrreldes ekspressiivsemaks (A. Laikmaa portree 1913). Ekspressionismile omast isiksuse lõhestatust ja traagikat väljendavad vabagraafilised joonistused "Märter" (1913) ja "Katastroof" (1917). I maailmasõja järgseid sündmusi kajastavad joonistused "Vabaduse sünd" (1919) ja "Ulguv koer" (1921). 1920. aastate teisest poolest pärineb hulk joonistatud isikupäraseid portreid (F.Tuglas 1928, H. Raudsepp 1932, G. Suits 1933), 1930. aastail viljeles taas rohkem maastikumaali, silmapaistvaimad on Paldiski lähedal Leetse-Lepikul valminud maastikud ja talvise Tartu vaated. Loonud ka tarbegraafikat ("Siuru" kirjastusmärk 1917) ning Vabadusristi kavandi (1920)
