artists.ben: Painter, printmaker and pedagogue. At the beginning of his creative path he drew pictures with political content, including caricatures (under the pseudonym Vaikne), for Estonian satirical publications. The figure "The Torch-Bearer" on the cover of the first "Noor-Eesti" album was the first to attract attention. He made illustrations and design based on Art Nouveau-stylised ornament and symbolic imagery for G. Suits's poetry collection "Tulemaa" (1913) and for the fifth "Noor-Eesti" album (1915). While staying in Norway he focused on landscape painting ("Decorative Norwegian Landscape", 1908). His early painterly work shows the influence of symbolism, especially in compositions with national-romantic legendary subjects and depicting heroic battle scenes. Triik was one of the most esteemed portraitists, emphasising spirituality, inner dignity and dramatism (K. Mägi 1908, Juhan Liiv 1909, M. Levin, I. Menning and Viktoria Martna 1910). Later his manner of expression became more expressive compared to the earlier one (portrait of A. Laikmaa, 1913). The free graphic drawings "Martyr" (1913) and "Catastrophe" (1917) express the split personality and tragedy characteristic of expressionism. The drawings "The Birth of Freedom" (1919) and "Howling Dog" (1921) reflect the events following World War I. From the second half of the 1920s comes a number of drawn, distinctive portraits (F. Tuglas 1928, H. Raudsepp 1932, G. Suits 1933); in the 1930s he again cultivated landscape painting more, the most outstanding being landscapes made near Paldiski at Leetse-Lepiku and winter views of Tartu. He also created applied graphics (the publisher's mark of "Siuru", 1917) and the design of the Cross of Liberty (1920)

artists.b: Õppis 1919-1926 Pallases, lõpetas 1926 maalijana Nikolai Triigi õpilasena. Juba 1923 sai joonistusõpetaja kutse. 1932-1935 õppis Pallases skulptuuri, tegeles akvarelliga. Pärast II ms asus 1949 Austraaliasse, kus abiellus Erik Kompusega.
artists.ben: Studied 1919–1926 at Pallas, graduated in 1926 as a painter, a student of Nikolai Triik. Already in 1923 received the qualification of drawing teacher. 1932–1935 studied sculpture at Pallas, worked with watercolour. After World War II moved to Australia in 1949, where she married Erik Kompus.

artists.ben: Actor, director and costume designer; ENL 1934; ETÜ 1946; 1926 Tallinn girls' gymnasium; studied painting under A. Laikmaa 1926–27, graduated from the Drama Studio theatre school in 1930; worked at the Drama Theatre 1930–52, at the Puppet Theatre 1952–1970, wrote puppet plays; ESSR Merited Artist 1964.

artists.b: Täiendas end Pariisis: l'Academie de la Grande Chaumiere, Atelier George Bramsen et Clot, Atelier Desjobert; samuti California ülikoolis Berkeleys. 1965-1973 oli Ontario kunstikolledži õppejõud, 1969 oli Toronto Open Studio Printmakersi asutajaliige. 1977 valiti R. Tulving Kanada Kuningliku Kunstiakadeemia liikmeks.
artists.ben: He furthered his education in Paris: at l'Academie de la Grande Chaumiere, Atelier George Bramsen et Clot, Atelier Desjobert; as well as at the University of California, Berkeley. From 1965-1973 he was a lecturer at the Ontario College of Art, in 1969 he was a founding member of the Toronto Open Studio Printmakers. In 1977 R. Tulving was elected a member of the Royal Canadian Academy of Arts.

artists.b: Alar Tuul (s 1982) on Eesti noorte autorite seas üks äratuntavama ja eripärasema käekirjaga kunstnikke. Tuule Karel Appel’it või Jean-Michel Basquiat’i meenutavad automatistlikult naiivsed pildipinnad on aastate jooksul liikunud üksikutelt detailidelt üha suuremate üldistusteni. Kriipsujukud ja rõngas-silmsed olendid on säilinud, kuid enam ei moodusta üksikud stseenid tervet kompositsiooni, vaid on osad suurematest panoraamidest. Emotsioon (värv) on asendanud kalkulatsiooni (joon), alateadvus selge ajendi ning nendest vaadetest võib välja lugeda tuhandeid lugusid ja konstrueerida üha uusi maailmu.
artists.ben: Alar Tuul (b. 1982) is one of the most recognisable and distinctive-styled artists among young Estonian authors. Tuul's automatistically naive picture surfaces, reminiscent of Karel Appel or Jean-Michel Basquiat, have over the years moved from isolated details towards ever greater generalisations. Stick figures and ring-eyed creatures have been preserved, but individual scenes no longer form a complete composition; instead they are parts of larger panoramas. Emotion (colour) has replaced calculation (line), the subconscious a clear motive, and from these views one can read out thousands of stories and construct ever new worlds.

artists.b: Loonud arvukalt puuskulptuure. Ta töötas välja omapärase puupõletustehnika ning kasutas seda peaaegu kõigi puidust tööde viimistlemisel. Teine lemmikmaterjal oli saaremaa dolomiit, millest valmisid aiaskulptuurid. Hilisemal eluperioodil katsetas paljusid erinevaid materjale -kips, tsement, epoksüüdvaik, alumiinium, pronks, alumiinium jne.
artists.ben: He created numerous wood sculptures. He developed a distinctive wood-burning technique and used it to finish almost all of his wooden works. Another favourite material was Saaremaa dolomite, from which he made garden sculptures. In his later life he experimented with many different materials — plaster, cement, epoxy resin, aluminium, bronze, aluminium, etc.

artists.b: ERKI-s teatridekoratsiooni-maali oli Uno Uibo prof. Voldemar Haasi Haasi ja Natalie Mei üliõpilane. Tema diplomitööks 1960. a. oli Anton Tšehhovi "Kirsiaed”. Pärnu Lydia Koidula nim. Draamateatris (Endla) töötades kujundas ta nt etendusi: M . Lassila "Tark neitsi”, Lope de Vega "Tantsuõpetaja”, Th . Wilder “Meie linnake”, K. Saja “Puutuvid ” jt.  1985. aastast vabakutselisena viljeles U. Uibo akvarell- ja pastellmaali (maastikud, linnavaated, lilled), osales teatrikunstnike ülevaatenäitustel ning esines isiknäitustega Pärnus, Tallinnas ja Vaasas. Viimastel aastatel oli kunstnik hinnatud pedagoog Pärnu Lastekunstikoolis.
artists.ben: At the ERKI, Uno Uibo studied theatre decoration painting as a student of Prof. Voldemar Haas and Natalie Mei. His diploma work in 1960 was Anton Chekhov's "The Cherry Orchard". While working at the Pärnu Lydia Koidula Drama Theatre (Endla), he designed, for example, the productions: M. Lassila's "The Wise Virgin", Lope de Vega's "The Dance Master", Th. Wilder's "Our Town", K. Saja's "Puutuvid" and others. From 1985, as a freelancer, U. Uibo practised watercolour and pastel painting (landscapes, cityscapes, flowers), participated in review exhibitions of theatre artists and held solo exhibitions in Pärnu, Tallinn and Vaasa. In recent years the artist was a valued teacher at the Pärnu Children's Art School.

artists.b: Kunstiõpinguid alustas 1942 Tallinna Kujutava ja Rakenduskunsti Koolis, jätkas 1943 Tartus “Pallases“, 1944-46 Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis, ning 1946-49 Tallinna Riiklikus Tarbekunsti Instituudis, lõpetas ERKI 1961.
artists.ben: Began art studies in 1942 at the Tallinn School of Applied Art, continued in 1943 in Tartu at "Pallas", 1944-46 at the Tartu State Art Institute, and 1946-49 at the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art, graduated from ERKI in 1961.

artists.b: Maria-Kristiina Ulas lõpetas Eesti Kunstiakadeemia 1991. aastal graafika erialal, astudes oma kunstnikest vanemate jälgedes – tema ema Concordia Klar (1938–2004) ja isa Peeter Ulas (1934–2008) on tuntud eesti graafikud.
artists.ben: Maria-Kristiina Ulas graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in 1991 in the field of graphic art, following in the footsteps of her artist parents – her mother Concordia Klar (1938–2004) and father Peeter Ulas (1934–2008) are well-known Estonian graphic artists.

artists.b: Sündinud Tallinnas 7. aprillil 1934, surnud samas 15. detsembril 2008. Õppinud ERKI-s 1952-59 keraamikat ning graafikat. Töötanud õppejõuna Tallinna Ülikoolis. Üks tunnustatumaid Eesti graafikuid.
artists.ben: Born in Tallinn on 7 April 1934, died there on 15 December 2008. Studied ceramics and graphic art at ERKI in 1952-59. Worked as a teacher at Tallinn University. One of the most recognised Estonian graphic artists.

artists.b: Adele Ulm-Augustas (1908–2000) lõpetas 1930. aastal Riigi Kunsttööstuskooli Tallinnas. Ta õppis aastatel 1942–1944 skulptuuri Tallinna Rakenduskunsti Koolis ning emigreerus 1944. aastal Eestist Rootsi, liikudes 1949. aastal edasi USAsse. 1952. aastal lõpetas ta Bostoni Kunstimuuseumi kunstikooli ning täiendas end 1952. aastal New Yorki asudes sealses disainikoolis. Tal õnnestus end paguluses tulemusrikkalt teostada, luues nii figuraalseid kompositsioone kui ka portreid, samuti voolava vormikeelega abstraktseid vorme Barbara Hepworthi (1903–1975) ja Henry Moore’i (1898–1986) eeskujul. Eelistatud on erinevates toonides kivimid, mille vormistus ja pinnatöötlus on kõrgetasemeline. On kuulunud kunstnike organisatsioonidesse, osalenud aktiivselt näituseelus USAs ja mujal ning pälvinud auhindu.
artists.ben: Adele Ulm-Augustas (1908–2000) graduated from the State School of Arts and Crafts in Tallinn in 1930. She studied sculpture at the Tallinn School of Applied Art from 1942 to 1944 and emigrated from Estonia to Sweden in 1944, moving on to the USA in 1949. In 1952 she graduated from the art school of the Boston Museum of Fine Arts, and in 1952, having moved to New York, she continued her studies at a design school there. She managed to fruitfully realise herself in exile, creating both figurative compositions and portraits, as well as abstract forms with a flowing formal language, following the example of Barbara Hepworth (1903–1975) and Henry Moore (1898–1986). She favoured rocks in various tones, whose finishing and surface treatment are of a high standard. She has belonged to artists' organisations, participated actively in exhibition life in the USA and elsewhere, and received awards.

artists.b: Tarbekunst. Loonud suuremõõtmelisi, jõulise kompositsiooni ja värvikäsitlusega köiteid ning objekte enda väljamõeldud käsiõmblus- ja paberreljeeftehnikas, kasutanud papjeemaðeed (köited "Armunud naise päevik" 1987, "Kaotatud paradiis" 1991, "Kurb kirjutaja" 1999, objekt "Neeger" 1995). illustreerinud raamatuid (E. Niidu "Onu ööbiku ööpäev" 1998). Avaldanud luulekogu "Tõsimäng" ja tarbekunstialaseid artikleid.
artists.ben: Applied art. Created large-scale bindings and objects with a forceful composition and colour treatment, in her own invented hand-sewing and paper-relief technique, used papier-mâché (bindings "Armunud naise päevik" 1987, "Kaotatud paradiis" 1991, "Kurb kirjutaja" 1999, object "Neeger" 1995). Illustrated books (E. Niit's "Onu ööbiku ööpäev" 1998). Published the poetry collection "Tõsimäng" and articles on applied art.

grp: member:Royal Swedish Academy of Fine Arts

artists.b: Elas ja töötas Tallinnas raamatupidajana. Arreteeriti 19.09.1945, tribunal toimus 07.12.45, karistus 10+5 aastat. Karistust kandis Komi ANSVs Uhtas Ust-Võmlagis, vabanes 18.01.1955. Asus elama Tallinna ja teenis elatist kunstnikuna.
artists.ben: He lived and worked in Tallinn as an accountant. He was arrested on 19.09.1945, the tribunal took place on 07.12.45, sentence 10+5 years. He served his sentence in the Komi ASSR in Ukhta, Ust-Vymlag, and was released on 18.01.1955. He settled in Tallinn and earned his living as an artist.

artists.b: Sündis Tallinnas voorimehe perekonnas, õppis kunsti 1903-1906 Ants Laikmaa ateljeekoolis ja 1910-1916 Peterburis Kunstide Edendamise Seltsi koolis Nikolai Roerichi ja Ivan Bilibini juures. Täiendas end 1910-1911 Pariisis ja 1913 Peterburis.
artists.ben: He was born in Tallinn into the family of a cabman, studied art in 1903–1906 at Ants Laikmaa's studio school and in 1910–1916 in St. Petersburg at the school of the Society for the Advancement of the Arts under Nikolai Roerich and Ivan Bilibin. He furthered his education in 1910–1911 in Paris and in 1913 in St. Petersburg.

artists.b: Anu-Leenu Uustalu sündis Tallinnas kooliõpetaja perekonnas. 1940–1941 tegutses ta vabakunstnikuna Tallinnas, 1944 põgenes Saksamaale, kus töötas Ameerika Punases Ristis kunstnikuna ning eesti algkoolis ja gümnaasiumis joonistusõpetajana. 1949 siirdus kunstnik koos õe Benita Uustaluga Ameerika Ühendriikidesse, Wisconsini osariiki Milwaukee linna. Ta töötas tehnilise joonestajana, 1977. aastast tegutses vabakunstnikuna. 1968. aastal hävis kogu tema varasem looming tulekahjus. 1979 kujundas A. Uustalu eesti rahvakultuuri tutvustava riideaida Milwaukee Public Museum'i püsiväljapanekus.
artists.ben: Anu-Leenu Uustalu was born in Tallinn into a schoolteacher's family. In 1940–1941 she worked as a freelance artist in Tallinn, in 1944 she fled to Germany, where she worked as an artist for the American Red Cross and as a drawing teacher at an Estonian elementary school and gymnasium. In 1949 the artist moved together with her sister Benita Uustalu to the United States, to the city of Milwaukee, Wisconsin. She worked as a technical draughtswoman, and from 1977 worked as a freelance artist. In 1968 all her earlier work was destroyed in a fire. In 1979 A. Uustalu designed a clothing display introducing Estonian folk culture in the permanent exhibition of the Milwaukee Public Museum.

artists.b: Maal leiti Viljandi Rajooni Riikliku Arhiivi töötajate poolt 1970. aastate lõpus hooletusse jäetuna Viljandi rajooni RSN Täitevkomitee hoone keldrist (hilisem Viljandi Maavalitsus, Vabaduse plats 2). Maali omandas Viljandi Rajooni Riiklik Arhiiv.
artists.ben: The painting was found neglected by employees of the Viljandi District State Archive in the late 1970s in the basement of the building of the Viljandi District RSN Executive Committee (later the Viljandi County Government, Vabaduse plats 2). The painting was acquired by the Viljandi District State Archive.

artists.b: Aastast 1919 Pallase õppejõud maali (1919-20) ja 1930-35 ka graafika alal, 1944-50 õppejõud Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis. 1953-56 graafika eksperimentaalateljee juhataja Tallinnas.
artists.ben: From 1919 a lecturer in painting (1919-20) at Pallas, and also in graphics 1930-35; 1944-50 lecturer at the Tartu State Art Institute. 1953-56 head of the graphic experimental studio in Tallinn.

artists.b: Kunti- ja arhitektuuriajaloolane, õppejõud, kunstnik, õppis A. Laikmaa ateljees ja Tartu ülikooli folosoofiateaduskonnas, mille lõpetas 1926 T. H. Kjellini õpilasena. Oma tegevuse kunstnikuna avalikustas 1980. aasatel.
artists.wdesc: Estonian art and architecture historian and teacher (1899-1999)
artists.ben: Art and architecture historian, lecturer, artist, studied at A. Laikmaa's studio and at the Faculty of Philosophy of the University of Tartu, which he completed in 1926 as a student of T. H. Kjellin. He made his activity as an artist public in the 1980s.

artists.b: Fotoseeria dokumenteerib ruumilist sekkumist Kumu kunstimuuseumi suures saalis näituse “Vabad hinged. Sümbolism Baltimaade kunstis” ruumikujundusse, mis eelnes näitusele “Gordon Matta-Clark: anarhitekt. Anu Vahtra: eemaldamise teel tervikuni”.
artists.ben:
Anu Vahtra (1982) is an artist working in the photo- and installation medium, and who focuses on exhibition format and specifics of exhibition space, initiated by architectural characters, and a historical and contextual background. Her installations play with the spectator’s memory and senses, grasping the whole space while altering it as the content and format of the work. Therefore Vahtra’s work is ephemeral in nature – it’s not possible to re-enact her exhibitions in the initial form. Vahtra’s work has been described as analytical archaeology.

One of Vahtra’s first works is “Dimensions Variable” (2009), in which she placed the depicted figure in-between a two and three dimensional space, so the space around the artwork became as important as the work itself. The same principle was used in photo-installation “17,9°” (2012). Exhibiting the work in a space with an ascending floor of 17,9 degrees in the Contemporary Arts Museum of Estonia, Vahtra focussed on the characteristics of the space. Practicing a contemporary

way of exhibiting, she structured and regulated the view of the spectator. Therefore the perspective of Vahtra’s work is not just aesthetical, but actually contributes to its meaning.

Vahtra also dealt with the physical properties of the aforementioned museum in the work “The Walls Stand, Speechless and Cold” (2015). In this photo installation she used a vacant space on the 2.

artists.b: J. Vahtra mobiliseeriti I maailmasõja ajal, Peterburi perioodil, sõjaväkke, rindele ei sattunud. Ta võttis aktiivselt osa Peterburi eesti üliõpilaste tegevusest, 1914-1915 aitas toimetada käsikirjalist kunstiajakirja “Ronk”, 1915-1916 kuulus kunsti-, muusika- ja kirjandushuviliste üliõpilaste ühendusse “Ritsikate ring”, kus tegutsesid ka kirjanikud Johannes Semper ja Karl Ast-Rumor. Peterburist siirdus Eestisse 1918. aasta juunis. 1923 oli Eesti Kunstnikkude Rühma asutajaliige (rühma liige kuni 1925). 1926 astus kunstiühingusse Pallas.
artists.ben: J. Vahtra was mobilised into the army during the First World War, during the St. Petersburg period, but did not end up at the front. He took an active part in the activities of Estonian students in St. Petersburg, in 1914-1915 he helped edit the handwritten art journal "Ronk", in 1915-1916 he belonged to the union of students interested in art, music and literature "Ritsikate ring", where the writers Johannes Semper and Karl Ast-Rumor were also active. He moved from St. Petersburg to Estonia in June 1918. In 1923 he was a founding member of the Estonian Artists' Group (member of the group until 1925). In 1926 he joined the art association Pallas.

artists.b: Silver Vahtre (s. 1953 Tartus) on graafik, disainer ja teatrikunstnik. Vahtre lõpetas 1977 disainierialal Eesti Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi ning on seejärel tegutsenud mitmetes ametites, sh Tartu linnakunstnikuna (1991-94). Vahtre on esinenud ca 30 isik- ja ühisnäitusega Eestis ja Soomes. Silver Vahtre on Eesti Kunstnike Liidu, Lavastuskunstnike Liidu, Kujundusgraafikute Liidu ja Tartu Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: Silver Vahtre (b. 1953 in Tartu) is a graphic artist, designer and theatre artist. Vahtre graduated in 1977 in the design speciality from the Estonian State Art Institute and has since worked in various positions, including as the town artist of Tartu (1991-94). Vahtre has taken part in ca 30 solo and joint exhibitions in Estonia and Finland. Silver Vahtre is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association, the Union of Stage Designers, the Union of Design Graphic Artists and the Tartu Artists' Union.

artists.b: Kunstnik Mall Valgu (aastani 1962 Mall Sooster) poolt valmistatud dekoratiivtaldrik. Ilmselt valmistatud õpingute ajal ERKIis (praegune Eesti Kunstiakadeemia), mille ta lõpetas 1961. aastal. Mall Sooster sündis 2. juunil 1935 Ühtri külas.
artists.ben: A decorative plate made by artist Mall Valk (until 1962 Mall Sooster). Apparently made during her studies at ERKI (the present Estonian Academy of Arts), which she graduated from in 1961. Mall Sooster was born on 2 June 1935 in the village of Ühtri.

artists.b: Sündinud 04.09.1901, Tartu; surnud 18.06.1983.

Matti Varik (1939–2011) kujunes 1960.–1970. aastail üheks silmapaistvamaks avalike skulptuuride ja monumentide loojaks Eestis, kuid sama novaatorlik oli ka tema 1970. aastate vabalooming. Ta tõi skulptuurinäitustele värvilisi figuure, eelistas materjalina pronksi, ent lõi ka suureformaadilisi figuure dolomiidist. Nõukogude ajal tema riiklike tellimustöödena valminud monumendid (näiteks fašismiohvrite monument Kuressaares, 1965, Tehumardi lahingu monument, 1967, mõlemad koos Riho Kullaga, Maarjamäe mälestuskompleksi skulptuuriosa, 1975) on lahendatud uuenduslikult ning tähistavad Eesti monumentaalkunstis pööret mõjusa lakoonilisuse suunas. Tema monumentaalloomingule on omane jõuline plastiline vorm, kompaktsus ja tasakaalustatud kompositsioon. Parimad selle perioodi teosed, näiteks V. I. Lenini mälestussammas Kotkas (1979), Ernst Särgava mälestussammas Tallinnas (1985) ja Berliini püstitatud avalik skulptuur „Perekond” (1984), kasutavad uudset vormikeelt ning kohanduvad õnnestunult oma keskkonnas. Ajastu ootustele vastanud monumentaallooming tõi 1970.–1980. aastail kaasa ühiskondliku tunnustuse. Pärast Eesti iseseisvumist lõi ta õnnestunud monumente nii kodu- kui välismaal.
artists.ben: Matti Varik (1939–2011) became one of the most prominent creators of public sculptures and monuments in Estonia during the 1960s-1970s, though his free creative work of the 1970s was equally innovative. He brought coloured figures to sculpture exhibitions, preferring bronze as a material, but also created large-format figures from dolomite. The monuments he created during the Soviet era as state commissions (for example the monument to the victims of fascism in Kuressaare, 1965, the monument to the Battle of Tehumardi, 1967, both together with Riho Kulla, the sculptural part of the Maarjamäe memorial complex, 1975) are resolved innovatively and mark a turn in Estonian monumental art towards effective laconicism. His monumental work is characterised by a forceful plastic form, compactness and balanced composition. The best works of this period, such as the monument to V. I. Lenin in Kotka (1979), the monument to Ernst Särgava in Tallinn (1985) and the public sculpture "Perekond" erected in Berlin (1984), employ a novel formal language and adapt successfully to their surroundings. His monumental work, which met the expectations of the era, brought him social recognition in the 1970s-1980s. After Estonia regained independence, he created successful monuments both at home and abroad.

artists.b: Tema peamised tellimustööd sellal olid San Luigi dei Francesis asuva Contarelli kabeli kaunistamine, mille jaoks ta maalis aastatel 1599–1600 Matteuse märtrisurma ja Matteuse kutsumise, ning Santa Maria del Popolos asuva Cerasi kabeli kaunistamine, millele ta lõi Pauluse pöördumise ja Peetruse ristilöömine.
artists.ben: His main commissioned works at that time were the decoration of the Contarelli Chapel in San Luigi dei Francesi, for which he painted the Martyrdom of Saint Matthew and the Calling of Saint Matthew in 1599–1600, and the decoration of the Cerasi Chapel in Santa Maria del Popolo, for which he created the Conversion of Saint Paul and the Crucifixion of Saint Peter.

artists.b: Maalija, graafik, eksliibrisekunstnik ja plakatist Lev Vassiljev sündis Venemaal Tuulas inseneri perekonnas. Pärast õpinguid Moskva kunstikeskkoolis siirdus 1950 Tallinna, kus õppis ERKI-s (EKA) skulptuuri, õppejõududeks Enn Roos, Aleksander Kaasik ja Martin Saks. Tegutses ka graafikuna (ofort ja akvatinta), tegi kollaaže ning assamblaaže. Tema tööde hulgas on poliitilise tooniga töid, samas oli kunstnik kiindunud mütoloogiasse ja literatuursetesse teemadesse.
artists.ben: Painter, graphic artist, ex libris artist and poster artist Lev Vassiljev was born in Tula, Russia, into an engineer's family. After studying at the Moscow Art School he moved in 1950 to Tallinn, where he studied sculpture at ERKI (EKA), his teachers being Enn Roos, Aleksander Kaasik and Martin Saks. He also worked as a graphic artist (etching and aquatint), made collages and assemblages. Among his works there are pieces of political tone, while at the same time the artist was fond of mythology and literary themes.

artists.b: Kuno Veeber sündis Adila mõisavalitseja kuuest pojast teisena. Ta õppis Tartu ülikoolis meditsiini ja osales velskrina Eesti Vabadussõjas. Kunstiõpingud algasid Ants Laikmaa ateljees, jätkusid Nikolai Triigi ja Jaan Koorti juures. 1922-1924 õppis Veeber kunstikoolis Pallas ja lõpetas selle esimeses lennus 1924. 1923 viibis ta Saksamaal, Dresdenis, elades kunstnik Magnus Zelleri juures. 1924-1926 täiendas end Pariisis Andre Lhote juures, olles tema ateljee vanemaks. Pariisis kujunes välja Kuno Veeberi stiil kunstnikuna. 1926 abiellus Agathe Kantoga (Veeber). 1927 oli Veeber kultuurkapitali stipendiumiga pool aastat Itaalias, kopeerides Veneetsia Doodžide palees Tintoretto seinamaali järgi. Kuno Veeber läks vabasurma 1. jaanuaril 1929, maetud Tallinna Rahumäe kalmistule. Hauamonument, mille valmistas Jaan Koort, on rüüstatud.

Seos sündmusega - Elupõline aadlik, sündis Kamenets-Podolski kubermangus. Lõpetas Kamenets-Podolski gümnaasiumi, kaks aastat kuulas loenguid Püha Vladimiri keiserliku ülikooli füüsika-matemaatika teaduskonnas Kiievis.

92. Petseri polgu teenistuses alates 16.04.1879. Sooritas ohvitseri auastme eksami Sankt-Peterburis junkrute jalaväe sõjakoolis ja pöördus polku tagasi. Osales Vene – Jaapani sõjas aastail 1904 - 1905. Vanuse tõttu erus alates 02.11.1913. Esimese maailmasõja algul pöördus teenistusse tagasi 92. Petseri polku. Haiguse tõttu saadeti erru 30.03.1917.
artists.ben:
Related to the event - A hereditary nobleman, born in the Kamenets-Podolsk Governorate. He graduated from the Kamenets-Podolsk gymnasium, attended lectures for two years at the Faculty of Physics and Mathematics of the Imperial St. Vladimir University in Kiev.

In service with the 92nd Pechora Regiment from 16.04.1879. He passed the officer's rank examination at the infantry cadet military school in St. Petersburg and returned to the regiment. He took part in the Russo-Japanese War in 1904–1905. Retired due to age from 02.11.1913. At the beginning of the First World War he returned to service with the 92nd Pechora Regiment. Due to illness he was discharged on 30.03.1917.

artists.b: Kunstnik sündis Tallinnas, lapsepõlve veetis Järvamaal. Hiiumaal Kassaris suvitanud alates 1960-ndate algusest ja sellest ajast alates on palju maalinud just Kassari loodust ja sealseid inimesi.
artists.ben: The artist was born in Tallinn, spent his childhood in Järvamaa. He has spent summers on Kassari, Hiiumaa, since the early 1960s, and since then has painted a great deal of the nature and people of Kassari.

artists.b: Sündis Paides, lõpetas Paide Gümnaasiumi 1941.a. Jätkas õpinguid 1942.a. Tallinna Kujutava ja Rakenduskunsti Koolis , 1943-44 "Pallases" ja a-st 1944 Tartu Rkl. Kunstiinstituudis, lõpetas selle 1948.a. J. Võerahansu õpilasena.
artists.ben: Born in Paide, graduated from Paide Gümnaasium in 1941. Continued studies in 1942 at the Tallinn School of Applied Art, 1943-44 at "Pallas" and from 1944 at the Tartu Rkl. Art Institute, graduated in 1948 as a student of J. Võerahansu.

artists.b: Edgar Viies (1931–2006) on üks 20. sajandi olulisemaid Eesti skulptoreid. Tema uuenduslikud vormiotsingud ja moodne materjalivalik (alumiinium, klinker, keevitatud raud, plekk ja betoon) tähistasid 1960. aastail Eesti skulptuuris modernse ajastu algust. Tema loominguga ilmus sõjajärgseil aastail esimest korda Eesti skulptuuri stiilipuhas abstraktne vormikultuur. Ta esines modernselt üldistatud portreeloominguga näitusesaalides juba 1950. aastate lõpul, äratades oma tavatult puhta siluetimõjuga tähelepanu ning mõjudes järgimakutsuvalt. Nii mitmestki tema 1960.–1980. aastate teosest on saanud Eesti kunsti klassika. Esteetilise problemaatika kõrval, mis oli Viiesele oluline eriti loomingu esimesel poolel, tuleb hinnatavaks pidada ka tema teoste elamuslikkust ning suhestatust üldinimliku vaimu- ja tundeeluga. Ta tõi 1960. aastate alguse võrdlemisi konservatiivsesse ja igavavõitu skulptuuri loomingulise eksperimendi, suunas skulptorite tähelepanu ruumi, vormi ja materjali seostele. Võib öelda, et just Edgar Viies andis tõuke tollal varjusurmas eksisteerivale dekoratiivskulptuurile. Tema arvukas vabalooming kuulub Eesti modernismi kullafondi. Viiese avalikud skulptuurid Tallinnas, Tartus ja Viljandis on meeliköitvad tänapäevani. Tuntumad neist on Johann Köleri (1976), Jaan Koorti (1983) ja Friedebert Tuglase (1986) ausambad, Viru väljakut kaunistav „Merineid” (1981) ning kõrgusse sööstev „Pegasus” (1963) Tallinna Harju tänava kohvikus, mis oli mitmele põlvkonnale tuttav esimene modernistlik interjööriskulptuur Eestis. Edgar Viies õppis aastatel 1951–1952 ENSV Riiklikus Kunstiinst.
artists.ben: Edgar Viies (1931–2006) is one of the most important Estonian sculptors of the 20th century. His innovative formal searches and modern choice of materials (aluminium, clinker, welded iron, sheet metal and concrete) marked the beginning of the modern era in Estonian sculpture in the 1960s. With his work, a stylistically pure abstract formal culture appeared in Estonian sculpture for the first time in the post-war years. He already appeared with modernly generalised portrait work in exhibition halls in the late 1950s, attracting attention with his unusually pure silhouette effect and having an inspiring influence. Quite a few of his works from the 1960s–1980s have become classics of Estonian art. Besides the aesthetic problematics, which were important to Viies especially in the first half of his oeuvre, the experiential quality of his works and their connection to universal human spiritual and emotional life should also be valued. In the early 1960s he brought creative experiment into a relatively conservative and rather dull sculpture scene, directing sculptors' attention to the relations of space, form and material. It can be said that it was precisely Edgar Viies who gave impetus to decorative sculpture, which at the time existed in a state of suspended animation. His numerous free works belong to the golden fund of Estonian modernism. Viies's public sculptures in Tallinn, Tartu and Viljandi remain captivating to this day. The best known of these are the monuments to Johann Köler (1976), Jaan Koort (1983) and Friedebert Tuglas (1986), the "Mermaid" (1981) adorning Viru Square, and the soaring "Pegasus" (1963) at the café on Harju Street in Tallinn, which was familiar to several generations as the first modernist interior sculpture in Estonia. Edgar Viies studied in 1951–1952 at the State Art Institute of the ESSR.

artists.b: Urmas Viik on lõpetanud Eesti Kunstiülikooli 1991. aastal graafika erialal. Ta on olnud Tallinna Ülikooli kunstiosakonna professor ja juhtinud pikka aega Eesti Kunstiakadeemia graafikaosakonda. Viik on illustreerinud kümneid lasteraamatuid ning tema kujundatud ja illustreeritud raamatud on korduvalt auhinnatud 25 kauneima Eesti raamatu ja 5 kauneima Eesti lasteraamatu konkursil.
artists.ben: Urmas Viik graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in 1991 in the field of graphic art. He has been a professor in the art department of Tallinn University and for a long time headed the graphic art department of the Estonian Academy of Arts. Viik has illustrated dozens of children's books, and the books he has designed and illustrated have repeatedly won awards in the competitions for the 25 Most Beautiful Estonian Books and the 5 Most Beautiful Estonian Children's Books.

artists.b: Lõpetas 1935.a Valga ühisgümnaasiumi ja 1941 J. Koorti nim. Riigi Rakenduskunsti Kooli. Töötas Tallinnas II maailmasõja ajal V. Tomassovi ja 1965-78 Arsi dekooriaateljees kujunduskunstnikuna. A-st 1939 EKL-i, a-st 1946 KL-i liige. Kujundas näitusi ja suurüritusi (sh. 1947 XII üldlaulupeo ning 1950. a-il Tallinna laulupäevi ja rongkäike). Viljeles portree- ja dekoratiivmaali ning plakatit.
artists.ben: Graduated from Valga Joint Gymnasium in 1935 and from the J. Koort State Applied Art School in 1941. Worked in Tallinn during World War II and in 1965–78 as a design artist in the decoration studio of Ars, together with V. Tomassov. Member of EKL from 1939, member of KL from 1946. Designed exhibitions and major events (incl. the 12th General Song Festival in 1947 and, in the 1950s, Tallinn song days and processions). Practised portrait and decorative painting as well as poster art.

artists.b: Photographer and installation artist on work, routine and the staged everyday.
artists.ben:
Sigrid Viir, A Sea of Gigs. Pigment print on acrylic, 62 x 60 cm, beech frame, series of 10 + 1 photos in a collage technique, glass, 110 x 80 cm, straps, 2021. The landscape photo used in the collages is from “The Sea”, Robert C. Miller, 1966, photo by: Ray Atkeson

Sigrid Viir (1979) is a photo and installation artist. Her work often addresses unspoken rules and morals, while also questioning the nature and limitations of the medium of photography. Viir has said that as an artist she values questioning things that are taken to be self-evident and examining behavioural patterns and the self in both a public and private context.

In her earlier work Viir explored unspoken rules, expectations or taboos in society, using the motif of family. In her photo series “Postcard for Grandparents” (2007) the artist examined a social stereotype and also highlighted her own unwillingness to adhere to it. The series, made up of pairs of images that juxtapose, on the one hand, a family sitting on the sofa at home and, on the other, a young woman (embodied by the artist), photographed in the same surroundings. With this Viir pointed to the societal expectation that at a certain age women should start a family. Presenting an alternative perspective was her protest against this expectation.

In 2009, together with Karel Koplimets and Taaniel Raudsepp, Viir founded the artist collective Visible Solutions LLC. The aim of the enterprise was to bring together the operating mechanics of art and economy, find new methods to create symbolic and real capital, and transgress that to the context of the creative economy. One of their more prominent works is performance- and photo-series “Hoisting the Banner”, in which the group members impose a new power relation with their theatrical composition. The banners always include a national flag and the “invisible hand”, referring to the philosopher and economist Adam Smith. In 2012 Visible Solutions LLC participated at the 9th Manifesta Biennial.

artists.b: Erna Viitol (1920–2001) alustas kunstiõpinguid 1939. aastal Rootsi siirdudes, õppides töö kõrval Viggbyholmi Örjansgårdeni vabakoolis. Pärast kodumaale naasmist alustas ta õpinguid Tallinna Rakenduskunsti Koolis ning lõpetas 1950. aastal Tallinna Riikliku Tarbekunsti Instituudi. 1960.–1970. aastail pühendus portreeloomingule ning lõi stiliseeritud vormiga dekoratiivseid skulptuure. Tema pärandis on üle 60 portree, parimad neist kasutavad õnnestunult vormiüldistust, kaotamata portreteeritava psühholoogilist isikupära. Viitol portreteeris palju oma perekonnaliikmeid ja lähedasi kultuuritegelasi nii Eestist, Soomest kui ka mujalt. Materjalidena kasutas ta keraamikat, epoksüvaiku, indoneesia puud, vaskplekki, klaasplasti. Osa teostest jäid kipsvalanditena materjali viimata.
artists.ben: Erna Viitol (1920–2001) began her art studies in 1939 upon moving to Sweden, studying alongside work at the Viggbyholm Örjansgården free school. After returning to her homeland she began studies at the Tallinn School of Applied Art and in 1950 graduated from the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art. In the 1960s–1970s she devoted herself to portraiture and created decorative sculptures with stylised form. Her legacy includes over 60 portraits, the best of which successfully use formal generalisation without losing the psychological individuality of the sitter. Viitol portrayed many members of her family as well as cultural figures close to her, from Estonia, Finland and elsewhere. As materials she used ceramics, epoxy resin, Indonesian wood, sheet copper, glass-reinforced plastic. Some of the works remained as plaster casts, without being executed in the final material.

artists.wdesc: Estonian dancer, choreographer, theatre director, painter (1941-2021)

artists.b: Õppis 1959-1962 Tartu Ülikoolis inglise filoloogiat ja 1963-1968 ERKI-s (EKA) klaasikunsti. On tegutsenud vabagraafiku, eksliibrisekunstniku, plakati- ja raamatukujundajana.

1898-1913 oli Moskva S. G. Stroganovi nim. Tööstuskunsti Instituudis õppejõud. Sai 1912 Peterburi KA akadeemikuks ja 1916 Kunstiakadeemia tegevliikmeks. Alates 1923 elas Riias.

Kuigi kuulus 1880-89 Rändnäituste Ühingusse, iseloomustab ta loomingut (eriti alates 1910. aastatest) siiski pigem Vene Kunstnike Liidu (VKL) impressionistlik laad. Ta oli ka selle ühingu asutajaliige (1903). Samas on teda nimetatud ka üheks tuntumaid peredvizhnikute rühmituse liikmeks.

Maalis zanristseene, portreid, interjööre ja maastikke enamasti heledas ja päikeselises vabaõhumaali stiilis. Parim osa ta loomingust sündis ajal, mil tegutses VKL-s.
artists.ben:
From 1898–1913 he was a lecturer at the S. G. Stroganov Moscow Institute of Applied Art. In 1912 he became an academician of the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts, and in 1916 a full member of the Academy of Arts. From 1923 he lived in Riga.

Although he belonged to the Society for Travelling Art Exhibitions (Peredvizhniki) from 1880–89, his work (especially from the 1910s onward) is nevertheless characterised rather by the impressionist manner of the Union of Russian Artists (VKL). He was also a founding member of this society (1903). At the same time, he has also been called one of the best-known members of the Peredvizhniki group.

He painted genre scenes, portraits, interiors and landscapes, mostly in a bright and sunny plein-air style. The best part of his work was created during the period when he was active in the VKL.

artists.b: Valeri Vinogradov (s. 1952) on maalikunstnik. Ta õppis Moskva lastekunstikoolis ja 1905. aasta nimelises kunstikoolis. Haridusteed jätkas ta 1980. aastal Eesti Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis. Ta on põhiliselt viljelenud tugeva üldistusjõuga abstraktset maali.
artists.ben: Valeri Vinogradov (b. 1952) is a painter. He studied at the Moscow children's art school and at the art school named after 1905. He continued his education in 1980 at the Estonian State Art Institute. He has mainly cultivated abstract painting with strong generalising force.

artists.b: Sündinud 25.04.1941, Rakvere.
artists.ben: Born 25.04.1941, Rakvere.

artists.b: Maara Vint on sündinud 31. oktoobril 1955. aastal Tallinnas Nõmmel teadlase Endel Vindi perekonnas. Kunstnike Tõnis ja Toomas Vindi õde on pärinud armastuse lillede vastu oma emalt Tamaralt.
artists.ben: Maara Vint was born on 31 October 1955 in Tallinn, Nõmme, into the family of the scientist Endel Vint. The sister of the artists Tõnis and Toomas Vint has inherited her love of flowers from her mother Tamara.

artists.b: Õppis 1962–1967 Eesti Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis klaasikunsti. Oli 1967-1970 Tallinna 46. keskkooli (Pelgulinna gümnaasiumi) kunstiõpetaja, pärast seda vabakutseline kunstnik. Loomingus on palju reiside ainest (Põhja-Aafrika, Egiptuses, Maroko, Lõuna-Itaalia, Malta, Türgi).
artists.ben:
Mare Vint (1942-2020) was a graphic artist whose work mostly focuses on the depiction of “ideal landscapes,” in an attempt to capture a perfect synthesis between nature and man-made structures. In her oeuvre, landscapes are represented as symbols through which she expressed a personal and generalised longing for a harmonic existence. Vint used photographs as a basis for her drawings, using them freely as a source of inspiration, rather than images to be reproduced, allowing her to create scenes which appear familiar to viewers, but which do not exist in reality. Vin

t’s works lack detail, and yet they present themes in tense, sharp displays of suggestions and compelling empty spaces. Lines are a fundamental element in Vint’s pictorial system – fine lines illustrate her works in a distinctively brittle but simultaneously strong figurative manner.

Vint’s emergence in the late 1960s coincided with changes in the strict political regime which also brought about a shift in the artistic group ‘ANK’. Even though Mare Vint was not a member of ANK, she was involved with the group, as a number of the members were her close friends. Vint made her first lithograph in 1973, and hereafter lithography became her predominantly used medium over colour pencils and Indian ink. Art historian Jüri Hain notes that Vint’s ‘

(1999-2000). During the 1990s, Vint expanded her oeuvre, beginning to use canvas alongside previously used  paper. It is also important to note that over time, Vint’s architectural objects have become increasingly simplified.

artists.b: Sündinud 05.03.1944. Haridus: 1962 - 1966 Tartu Ülikool bioloogia-geograafia teaduskond.
artists.ben: Born 05.03.1944. Education: 1962 - 1966 University of Tartu, Faculty of Biology and Geography.

artists.b: Ta on teinud tööd Tallinna reklaami ja raamatukujunduse alal. Oli aastatel 1971-1977 kujundaja almanahhi Kunst ja 1974-1980 ajakirja Kultuur ja Elu väljaannetes.
artists.ben: He has worked in the field of advertising and book design in Tallinn. In 1971-1977 he was the designer of the almanac Kunst and in 1974-1980 of the publications of the magazine Kultuur ja Elu.

artists.wdesc: Estonian theatre and film artist, director (1946-2019)

artists.b: Raamatugraafik, kirjakunstnik ja plakatist. Lõpetas 1931 tarbegraafikuna Riigi Kunsttööstuskooli. II ms ajal viibis Vene tagalas Jaroslavlis, kuulus 1945-1950 ENSV Kunstnike Liidu juhatusse, oli Kunstitoodete Kombinaadi organiseerijaid ja kunstiline juht, töötas 1949-1954 Eesti Riiklikus Kirjastuses.
artists.ben: Book graphic artist, calligrapher and poster artist. Graduated in 1931 as an applied graphic artist from the State School of Applied Art. During World War II was in the Russian rear in Yaroslavl, was a member of the board of the ESSR Artists' Union 1945-1950, was one of the organisers and artistic director of the Art Products Combine, worked at the Estonian State Publishing House 1949-1954.

artists.wdesc: social scientist and politician from Austria
Estonian musician, film director and politician (born 1957)

artists.b: Sündis Tartus kunstnkest abielupaari Benita ja August Vommi pojana Lapsena elas Rakveres. 1936.aastast Tallinnas. 1944.a. põgenes koos ema õega välismaale. Elas Venetsueelas, Caracases ja 1953.a. alates Kanadas Torontos.
artists.ben: Born in Tartu as the son of the artist couple Benita and August Vomm. Lived in Rakvere as a child. From 1936 in Tallinn. In 1944 fled abroad with his mother and sister. Lived in Venezuela, Caracas, and from 1953 in Toronto, Canada.

artists.b: Enne II Maailmasõda koosnes August Vommi looming valdavalt portreebüstidest ja kümnekonnast töömahukast hauasambast. Ta on kujutanud Ruts Baumani, Ants Lauterit, Hugo Lauri, Gustav Ernesaksa, Romulus Tiitust, Ferdi Sannameest jt. Ühena vähestest sõja-aastad kodumaal veetnud kunstnikest kohanes August Vomm uute nõudmistega kohe esimestel sõjajärgsetel aastatel. 1945 liitus ta skulptorite brigaadiga, luues Estonia teatri liiduvabariike sümboliseerivad reljeefid. 1947 valmis monument Viljandis Suures Isamaasõjas langenuile, 1952 avati jällegi brigaadimeetodil loodud Lenini monument Tartus ning koos Lagle Israeliga Nikolai Burdenko mälestusmärk Tartu Toomemäel. Tema loodud on tänaseks teisaldatud revolutsioonitegelaste Johannes Vares-Barbaruse ja Hans Pöögelmanni monumendid Tallinnas. Lenini juubelinäitusele 1970 lõi Vomm hiigelmõõtmetes tammepuidust V. I. Lenini portreebüsti, mille eest pälvis koos Elmar Kitse ja Avo Keerendiga riikliku preemia ja Eesti NSV teenelise kunstniku aunimetuse, samuti üleliidulise äramärkimise ajakirjanduses.
artists.ben: Before World War II, August Vomm's oeuvre consisted mainly of portrait busts and about a dozen labour-intensive gravestones. He depicted Ruts Bauman, Ants Lauter, Hugo Laur, Gustav Ernesaks, Romulus Tiitus, Ferdi Sannamees and others. As one of the few artists who spent the war years in his homeland, August Vomm adapted to the new demands right in the first post-war years. In 1945 he joined a brigade of sculptors, creating for the Estonia Theatre reliefs symbolising the union republics. In 1947 a monument to those fallen in the Great Patriotic War was completed in Viljandi, in 1952 a monument to Lenin, again created by the brigade method, was unveiled in Tartu, as well as, together with Lagle Israel, a memorial to Nikolai Burdenko on Toome Hill in Tartu. The monuments to the revolutionary figures Johannes Vares-Barbarus and Hans Pöögelmann in Tallinn, created by him, have since been relocated. For the Lenin jubilee exhibition in 1970, Vomm created a giant oak portrait bust of V. I. Lenin, for which, together with Elmar Kits and Avo Keerend, he was awarded the State Prize and the honorary title of Merited Artist of the Estonian SSR, as well as all-Union recognition in the press.

artists.b: 1926-1929 õppis "Pallases". Sai joonistusõpetaja kutse (A. Vabbe ateljee). 1944 läks Saksamaale, töötas 1945-48 Augsburgi eesti gümnaasiumis joonistusõpetajana. 1948 asus Venetsueelasse, Caracasesse. 1953. a-st elas Torontos. 1956 a-st EKKT liige. Abielus skulptor August Vommiga. Lapsed kunstnikud Ants Erik Vomm ja Mai Järve-Vomm. A-ni 1929 oli Mölder.
artists.ben: 1926-1929 studied at "Pallas". Received the qualification of drawing teacher (A. Vabbe's studio). In 1944 went to Germany, worked in 1945-48 as a drawing teacher at the Augsburg Estonian gymnasium. In 1948 moved to Venezuela, to Caracas. From 1953 lived in Toronto. Member of EKKT from 1956. Married to sculptor August Vomm. Children are artists Ants Erik Vomm and Mai Järve-Vomm. Until 1929 the surname was Mölder.

artists.b: 1930–1940 töötas algkooliõpetajana Aluveres ja Tartus. 1936 täiendas end Soomes, 1938 Rootsis, 1940 Itaalias. 1940–1941 oli Riikliku Kunstimuuseumi direktor. 1941 arreteeriti NKVD poolt ja küüditati Siberisse Krasnojarski kraisse. Viibis 1941–1951 vangilaagris, 1951–1956 asumisel. 1956–1965 Riikliku Projekteerimise ja Teadusliku Uurimise Instituudi "Eesti Ehitusmälestised" teadur, 1965–1982 peaspetsialist, 1982–1990 konsultant.
artists.ben: 1930–1940 he worked as a primary school teacher in Aluvere and Tartu. In 1936 he furthered his studies in Finland, in 1938 in Sweden, in 1940 in Italy. 1940–1941 he was director of the Riiklik Kunstimuuseum. In 1941 he was arrested by the NKVD and deported to Siberia, to Krasnoyarsk Krai. He was in a prison camp from 1941–1951, and in exile settlement from 1951–1956. 1956–1965 he was a researcher at the State Institute of Design and Scientific Research "Eesti Ehitusmälestised", 1965–1982 chief specialist, 1982–1990 consultant.

artists.b: Viive Väljaots (1948) on Eesti keraamik. Lõpetanud Eesti Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi keraamiku-konstruktorina (1974). Töötanud mitmes tehases disainerina ja Eesti Kunstiakadeemias õppejõuna, tegutseb vabakutselise keraamikuna. Viimane isikunäitus „Post Factum“ HOP galeriis (2020).
artists.ben: Viive Väljaots (1948) is an Estonian ceramicist. She graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute as a ceramicist-constructor (1974). She has worked as a designer in several factories and as a lecturer at the Estonian Academy of Arts, and works as a freelance ceramicist. Her latest solo exhibition "Post Factum" at HOP Gallery (2020).

artists.wdesc: Swedish photographer and photojournalist of Estonian origin (1936-2010)

artists.b: VÕERAHANSU, Johannes (1902, Keo, Raikküla vald – 1980, Tallinn). Johannes Võerahansut peetakse üheks silmapaistvaimaks eesti maastiku- ja olustikumaalijaks. 1930. aastate teises pooles valminud valgusküllase hõbedase koloriidiga Eesti eluolu ja loodust poetiseerivad maalid kuuluvad selle žanri tippteoste hulka. Loodust on kunstnik väljendusrikkalt kujutanud ka II maailmasõja ajal valminud maatööaineliste maalide taustana. Oma loometee algusest peale viljeles Võerahansu ka portreemaali, millest mitmed kuuluvad Eesti portreeklassikasse. 1960. – 1970. aastatel kaugenes ta maalist ning keskendus pigem joonistustele. Kunstihariduse omandas Võerahansu Ants Laikmaa ateljeekoolis ja Ado Vabbe käe all Pallase kunstikoolis. Hiljem töötas ta õppejõuna Kõrgematel Kujutava Kunsti Kursustel, Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis, Tartu Kunstikoolis ja professorina Eesti Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
artists.ben: VÕERAHANSU, Johannes (1902, Keo, Raikküla Parish – 1980, Tallinn). Johannes Võerahansu is considered one of the most outstanding Estonian landscape and genre painters. His paintings from the second half of the 1930s, with their light-filled, silvery colouring poeticising Estonian life and nature, are among the top works of this genre. The artist also expressively depicted nature as the background of paintings on the theme of fieldwork made during World War II. From the beginning of his creative path, Võerahansu also cultivated portrait painting, several of which belong to the classics of Estonian portraiture. In the 1960s–1970s he moved away from painting and focused more on drawings. Võerahansu received his art education at Ants Laikmaa's studio school and under Ado Vabbe at the Pallas Art School. He later worked as a teacher at the Higher Courses of Visual Art, at the Tartu State Art Institute, at the Tartu Art School, and as a professor at the Estonian State Art Institute. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.

artists.b: Õppis Peterburi Kunstide Akadeemias 1858-1861. Õpetajaks skulptor Peter Clodt von Jürgensburg. Siis sõitis Münchenisse, kus õppis Widemanni käe all. Oli sunnitudt tervislikel põhjustel skulptuurist loobuma ning hakkas maalima. Tegutses peamiselt Münchenis.
artists.ben: Studied at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Arts 1858-1861. Teacher was sculptor Peter Clodt von Jürgensburg. Then went to Munich, where he studied under Widemann. Was forced for health reasons to give up sculpture and began to paint. Worked mainly in Munich.

artists.b: Sündis Peterburis Tartust pärit kirurgi tütrena. Astus 17-aastasena Peterburi Kunstide Akadeemiasse. 1882 jätkas õpinguid Pariisis Courtois ja Collin'i käe all ning seejärel pr Skarbina juures Berliinis.
artists.ben: Born in St. Petersburg as the daughter of a surgeon from Tartu. Entered the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts at the age of 17. In 1882 continued her studies in Paris under Courtois and Collin, and thereafter under Mrs Skarbina in Berlin.

artists.b: Õppis Dresdeni Kunstiakadeemias. Tuli kirjanik August von Kotzebue kutsel 1809 Eestisse tema laste joonistusõpetajaks. Hiljem tegutses joonistusõpetajana Hageris pastor F. Ignatiuse asutatud kirikukoolis, alates 1815 Tallinna toomkoolis. Pensioneerus 1850, elas tütrele kuulunud Kaiu mõisas. Maalis enamasti altarimaale (Tallinna ja Kuressaare kirikuis, Ambla kirikus jm.), samuti portreid, temalt pärinevad Oleviste varemeid pärast 1820. a. tulekahju kujutavad joonistused, mille järgi tehti ka litograafilisi lehti. Asutas Tallinnas esimese litograafiatöökoja. Täitis ka Vene keisrite portreede, paraadportreede tellimusi.
artists.ben: Studied at the Dresden Academy of Art. Came to Estonia in 1809 at the invitation of the writer August von Kotzebue to be a drawing teacher for his children. Later worked as a drawing teacher in Hageri at the church school founded by pastor F. Ignatius, and from 1815 at the Tallinn Cathedral School. Retired in 1850, lived at Kaiu Manor, which belonged to his daughter. He mostly painted altarpieces (in the churches of Tallinn and Kuressaare, in Ambla Church, etc.), as well as portraits; drawings depicting the ruins of St Olaf's Church after the fire of 1820 originate from him, after which lithographic sheets were also made. He founded the first lithography workshop in Tallinn. He also carried out commissions for portraits of Russian tsars and ceremonial portraits.

artists.b: Sündis Dresdenis käsitöölise pojana, õppis Dresdeni kunstiakadeemias. Kirjanik August von Kotzebue kutsus ta Eestimaale oma laste koduõpetajaks, Walther tegutses Vardi mõisas ja Hageri pastoraadis praost Ignatiuse teenistuses, kes oli Kotzebue sugulane. 1812 asus Walther Tallinna ja sai 1815 Tallinna toomkooli kunstiõpetajaks. Tallinnas tegutses ta esimesena litograafina, maalis portreid ja kirikutele maale altariretaablitesse.1835 sai Walther Peterburi kunstiakadeemiast vabakunstniku nimetuse.
artists.ben: Born in Dresden as the son of a craftsman, studied at the Dresden Academy of Arts. The writer August von Kotzebue invited him to Estonia as a home tutor for his children; Walther worked at Vardi manor and at the Hageri parsonage in the service of Provost Ignatius, who was a relative of Kotzebue. In 1812 Walther moved to Tallinn and in 1815 became the art teacher at Tallinn Cathedral School. In Tallinn he was the first to work as a lithographer, painted portraits and paintings for church altarpieces. In 1835 Walther received the title of free artist from the Saint Petersburg Academy of Arts.

cit: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

artists.b: Töötas Lübeckis, Tallinnas, Göteborgis, Riias, Narvas ja Peterburis, oli alates 1701 Tallinna kodanik. 1715 töötas taas Göteborgis, seejärel Riias ja Narvas, kus maalis mitu portreed Peeter I tellimusel. Saabus 1725 Peterburi ja asus tööle õukonnas. Maalis kompositsioone ja portreid, oli tuntud hea kopistina. 1725 ostis Katariina I temalt neli usuteemalist ja allegoorilist maali ning tellis kuus portreed. Alates 1732 oli kadetikorpuses joonistusõpetaja, 1734-1736 samas maalija. Maalis keisrinna Anna Ivanovna tellimusel tema isa Ivan V, õdede Praskovja ja Jekaterina, tsaar Fjodor Aleksejevitši tütre Praskovja, Peeter I ja Katariina I portree. Üks tema varasemaid töid, Karl XII ratsaportree, asus Riia Mustpeade Vennaskonna majas.
artists.ben: He worked in Lübeck, Tallinn, Gothenburg, Riga, Narva and Saint Petersburg, and was a citizen of Tallinn from 1701. In 1715 he again worked in Gothenburg, then in Riga and Narva, where he painted several portraits commissioned by Peter I. He arrived in Saint Petersburg in 1725 and began working at the court. He painted compositions and portraits and was known as a good copyist. In 1725 Catherine I bought four religious and allegorical paintings from him and commissioned six portraits. From 1732 he was a drawing teacher at the Cadet Corps, and from 1734-1736 a painter there as well. Commissioned by Empress Anna Ivanovna, he painted portraits of her father Ivan V, her sisters Praskovya and Yekaterina, Praskovya, daughter of Tsar Fyodor Alekseyevich, and Peter I and Catherine I. One of his earlier works, an equestrian portrait of Charles XII, was housed in the House of the Brotherhood of Blackheads in Riga.

artists.b: Pärit kingsepa perekonnast. Töötas Erastveres tisleritöökojas. Pääses õppima Oderi-äärsesse Frankfurti, jätkas õpinguid Berliinis, Fr. R. Kreutzwaldi soovitusel Peterburis kujur A. F. von Bocki ateljees, 1865-1867 Peterburi Kunstide Akadeemias. Töötas Tartus, Berliinis, Münchenis ja 1873-1890 Roomas. Sai skulptuuri "Hamlet" eest Pariisi maailmanäituse auhinna. 1890-1914 elas ja töötas Peterburis, seejärel kuni surmani Tallinnas. Alates 1916 oli tegev linna kunstivarade järelevaatajana. Loomingu põhiosa moodustavad klassitsistlikud allegoorilised figuurid ning portreed. Kogu loometee jooksul, eriti aga Peterburi aastatel lõi ka keisrite ja keisrinnade portreid, 1890. aastatel osales mitmel valitsejate mälestussammaste võistlusel. Eriti populaarseks sai tema loodud Aleksander II marmorist portreebüst, sellest tegi kujur mitmeid kordusi. Portreteerinud ka teisi tema eluajal valitsenud keisreid ja keisrinnasid - Aleksander III-t ja Maria Fjodorovnat ning Nikolai II-t ja Aleksandra Fjodorovnat.
artists.ben: Came from a family of shoemakers. Worked in a joinery workshop in Erastvere. Was accepted to study in Frankfurt an der Oder, continued studies in Berlin, and on the recommendation of Fr. R. Kreutzwald, in St. Petersburg in the studio of sculptor A. F. von Bock, and 1865-1867 at the Imperial Academy of Arts in St. Petersburg. Worked in Tartu, Berlin, Munich, and 1873-1890 in Rome. Received the award of the Paris World Exhibition for the sculpture "Hamlet". From 1890 to 1914 he lived and worked in St. Petersburg, and thereafter until his death in Tallinn. From 1916 he served as overseer of the city's art treasures. The main part of his work consists of classicist allegorical figures and portraits. Throughout his career, but especially during his St. Petersburg years, he also created portraits of emperors and empresses, and in the 1890s participated in several competitions for monuments to rulers. The marble portrait bust of Alexander II that he created became especially popular, and the sculptor made several repetitions of it. He also portrayed other emperors and empresses who ruled during his lifetime - Alexander III and Maria Feodorovna, and Nicholas II and Alexandra Feodorovna.

artists.b: Gottlieb Welté sündis 1740. aastate lõpus Mainzi/Frankfurdi piirkonnas Saksamaal, 1782 saabus Eestisse, kus töötas Põltsamaa lossis, Tallinnas, Lohu mõisas ja mujal Suri 17. detsembril 1792. Lohu mõisas. Ta oli ofortist, freskomaalija ja muusik.
artists.ben: Gottlieb Welté was born in the late 1740s in the Mainz/Frankfurt region of Germany, arrived in Estonia in 1782, where he worked at Põltsamaa Castle, in Tallinn, at Lohu Manor and elsewhere. He died on 17 December 1792 at Lohu Manor. He was an etcher, fresco painter and musician.

artists.b: Elas Inglismaal, Prantsusmaal, Belgias ja 24 aastat Roomas. 1844 tuli Liivimaale, peatus Tallinnas ja Tartus, kus valmisid portreejoonistused, mis litografeeriti G. F. Schlateri poolt, külastas ka Tallinna. Hiljem elas Berliinis. Tema loomingust on teada žanrimaale ja portreid.
artists.ben: He lived in England, France, Belgium and for 24 years in Rome. In 1844 he came to Livonia, stayed in Tallinn and Tartu, where portrait drawings were made, which were lithographed by G. F. Schlater, he also visited Tallinn. Later he lived in Berlin. Genre paintings and portraits are known from his oeuvre.

artists.b: Eduard Wiiralt sündis 20. märtsil 1898. aastal Peterburi kubermangus Robidetsi mõisa toatüdruku Sophie-Elisabeth Asur'i ja mõisateenistuja Anton Wiralti pojana. 1909. aastal asus perekond elama Järvamaale Varangu mõisa lähistele. E. Wiiralt õppis Koeru haridusseltsi koolis ja Koeru saksa erakoolis. 1915. aasta sügisel astus ta Tallinna Linna Kunsttööstuskooli. E. Wiiralt võttis 1918. aastal osa Eesti Vabadussõjast. 1919. aastal esines ta esmakordselt Tallinnas Tütarlaste Kommertskooli ruumides peetud eesti kunsti ülevaatenäitusel nelja graafilise teosega. 1919. aasta sügisel astus Wiiralt äsjaavatud Pallase kunstikooli Tartus, kust suundus 1922. aasta kevadel Dresdeni Kujutava Kunsti Akadeemiasse stažeerima. 1923. aasta sügisel naasis kunstnik kodumaale ning lõpetas järgneva aasta kevadel Pallase kooli. 1924. aasta sügisel asus Wiiralt tööle Pallase graafikaateljee juhatajana, töötades samal ajal aktiivselt raamatugraafikuna. 1925. aasta kevadel sai Wiiralt Kujutavate Kunstide Sihtkapitali Valitsuselt stipendiumi Pariisi sõiduks, kuhu jõudis sama aasta sügisel ning jäi sinna elama. 1936. aasta sügisel, kunstniku võõrsil olles toimus Tallinna Kunstihoones Alfred Rõude eestvedamisel tema esimene personaalnäitus Eestis, eksponeeritud oli enam kui 300 teost. 1938. aasta suvel sõitis Wiiralt Prantsusmaalt Marokosse. 1939. aasta sügisel, II maailmasõja eel naasis kunstnik Pariisi kaudu Eestisse, kuhu jäi 1944. aastani. Viibinud põgusalt Viinis, Stockholmis ja rännanud Lapimaal, töötas Wiiralt oma elu viimasel kümnendil taas Pariisis, kus ta 8. jaanuaril 1954. aastal suri ning maeti Pariisi Père-Lachaise’i kalmistule.
artists.ben: Eduard Wiiralt was born on 20 March 1898 in Saint Petersburg Governorate, the son of Sophie-Elisabeth Asur, a maid at the Robidets manor, and Anton Wiralt, a manor employee. In 1909 the family moved to live near Varangu manor in Järvamaa. E. Wiiralt studied at the Koeru Education Society school and at the Koeru German private school. In the autumn of 1915 he entered the Tallinn City School of Applied Art. In 1918 E. Wiiralt took part in the Estonian War of Independence. In 1919 he appeared for the first time in Tallinn with four graphic works at a survey exhibition of Estonian art held at the premises of the Girls' Commercial School. In the autumn of 1919 Wiiralt entered the newly opened Pallas art school in Tartu, from where, in the spring of 1922, he went to the Dresden Academy of Fine Arts for further training. In the autumn of 1923 the artist returned to his homeland and, in the spring of the following year, graduated from the Pallas school. In the autumn of 1924 Wiiralt began working as head of the Pallas graphic art studio, while also being active as a book graphic artist. In the spring of 1925 Wiiralt received a scholarship from the Board of the Fine Arts Foundation for a trip to Paris, where he arrived in the autumn of that year and stayed to live. In the autumn of 1936, while the artist was abroad, his first solo exhibition in Estonia took place at the Tallinn Art Hall, organised by Alfred Rõude, with more than 300 works exhibited. In the summer of 1938 Wiiralt travelled from France to Morocco. In the autumn of 1939, before World War II, the artist returned to Estonia via Paris, where he stayed until 1944. Having briefly stayed in Vienna and Stockholm and travelled in Lapland, Wiiralt spent the last decade of his life again working in Paris, where he died on 8 January 1954 and was buried in the Père-Lachaise Cemetery in Paris.

artists.b: Kus kunstiõpetaja oli Alexander Schlater. 1870 ja 1875 viibis ravil Saksamaal ja Austrias. Õppis Tartu ülikooli keeleteaduskonnas 1879-1884 (cand phil), viibis samal aastal Šveitsis sanatooriumis, ka Prantsusmaal. 1889 alustas maali ja akvarelli õpinguid. Õpetajad: Hermann Eschke Berliinis, Charles Way Lausannes. 1891-1893 oli Winkler koduõpetaja Kehtna mõisas. 1893 tegi õpetaja eksami Peterburi KA juures. 1898 reisis Norras, 1901-1904 Dalmaatsias (Horvaatia) ja Itaalias, 1903 viibis Roomas. 1904 isiknäitus Tallinnas Kanuti gildi saalis. 1905 viibis Dresdenis. Elas aastast 1911 Tallinnas, kus juhatas akvarellikursusi. Suri Dresdenis 23.08.1911, maeti Tallinna lähedale Mõigu klamistule (haud pole säilinud)
artists.ben: Where his art teacher was Alexander Schlater. In 1870 and 1875 he was undergoing treatment in Germany and Austria. He studied at the Faculty of Linguistics of the University of Tartu 1879–1884 (cand phil), and in the same year stayed in a sanatorium in Switzerland, also in France. In 1889 he began studies in painting and watercolour. Teachers: Hermann Eschke in Berlin, Charles Way in Lausanne. In 1891–1893 Winkler was a home tutor at Kehtna Manor. In 1893 he took the teacher's examination at the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. In 1898 he travelled in Norway, 1901–1904 in Dalmatia (Croatia) and Italy, in 1903 he stayed in Rome. In 1904 a solo exhibition in Tallinn at the Kanuti Guild Hall. In 1905 he stayed in Dresden. From 1911 he lived in Tallinn, where he led watercolour courses. He died in Dresden on 23.08.1911, and was buried near Tallinn at Mõigu cemetery (the grave has not survived)

artists.ben: He received his art education in Moscow under academician Sherwood and worked in St. Petersburg under Premazzi and Shishtyakov. In 1870 he was granted the title of free artist and in 1874 he was named an honorary member of the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts.

artists.b: Sündis hilisema Valga erakoolipidaja Ferdinand Zeidleri tütrena. Sai hariduse Viiburis ja Valga eragümnaasiumis, lõpueksamid sooritas 1887 Tartus.1889-94 õppis Peterburis A. Stieglitzi kunsttööstuskooli, kooli stipendiaadina Pariisis portselanimaali ja Colarossi vaba-akadeemias joonistamist. 1908 täiendas end Londonis, Stuttgardis ja Viinis metallehistöö alal. Töötas 1897-1918 Petrogradi kunstikoolides õppejõuna. Asus 1918 Tallinna. Oli 1919-40 Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis metalli-, portselani-, akvarelli- ja joonistamise õppejõud. 1924-35 oli metallitöökoja juhataja ning arendas eriti filigraantehnikat. 1919-31 oli ka Tallinna saksa poeglaste eragümnaasiumis joonistusõpetaja. Asutas oma stuudio. 1920. aastail kuulus ARS-i, 1928-35 EKKKÜ-sse, 1938-39 EAKKK-sse, osales 1932 RaKü asutamsies. Siirdus 1940 Soome, 1941 Saksamaale, 1948 Rootsi.
grp: school:Saint Petersburg Stieglitz State Academy of Art and Design
artists.ben: She was born as the daughter of Ferdinand Zeidler, who later ran a private school in Valga. She was educated in Viipuri and at the Valga private grammar school, and passed her final examinations in Tartu in 1887. From 1889–94 she studied at A. Stieglitz's School of Technical Drawing in St Petersburg, and as the school's scholarship holder studied porcelain painting in Paris and drawing at the Académie Colarossi. In 1908 she furthered her studies in metalwork in London, Stuttgart and Vienna. She worked as a teacher at art schools in Petrograd from 1897–1918. In 1918 she settled in Tallinn. From 1919–40 she was a teacher of metal, porcelain, watercolour and drawing at the State School of Applied Art. From 1924–35 she was head of the metal workshop and particularly developed filigree technique. From 1919–31 she was also a drawing teacher at the Tallinn German private grammar school for boys. She founded her own studio. In the 1920s she belonged to ARS, from 1928–35 to EKKKÜ, from 1938–39 to EAKKK, and took part in the founding of RaKü in 1932. In 1940 she moved to Finland, in 1941 to Germany, and in 1948 to Sweden.

artists.b: (ZED) Eduard Zentsik on sündinud 26. detsembril 1975 Sillamäel, Eestis. Eduard Zentsik on viljakas ja mitmenäoline eesti kunstnik. Tal on kujunenud mitu erinevat kunstilist isiksust ning ta ei seo ennast ühegi konkreetse stiili, tehnika või teemaga. Selle asemel segab ta omavahel erinevaid meediume ja žanre ning kummutab mänguliselt traditsioone. Zentsiku looming on mitmekülgne ja mahukas. Mõned tema ettevõtmistest, näiteks mõnevõrra kõhedusttekitav art brut’ sari, keskenduvad ihu füüsilistele metamorfoosidele. Teised, näiteks sümbolistlikud sürrealistlikud maalid, rõhutavad Zentsiku filosoofia spirituaalseid aspekte. Siin-seal kasutab kunstnik Pollocklikke värvipritsmeid või katsetab digitaalsete meediumitega. Zentsiku maalid sisaldavad avatud ruumi, maagilist reaalsust, milles olemid, esemed ja mõisted näiliselt vabalt valitud ajastutest ja kultuuridest täidavad mõistatuslikke eesmärke. Mitte ükski mütoloogia ega esoteeriline õpetus pole immuunne kunstniku delikaatsete manipulatsioonide suhtes – Zentsiku töös käib Zen käsikäes Tao, Krishna, Kristuse ja Olümpose jumalatega. Tegu pole siiski intellektuaalse mänguga. Need, kes soovivad Zentsiku koodi dešifreerida, avastavad su.
artists.ben: (ZED) Eduard Zentsik was born on 26 December 1975 in Sillamäe, Estonia. Eduard Zentsik is a prolific and many-faceted Estonian artist. He has developed several different artistic personas and does not tie himself to any single style, technique or theme. Instead he mixes different media and genres and playfully overturns traditions. Zentsik's oeuvre is diverse and extensive. Some of his undertakings, for example the somewhat eerie 'art brut' series, focus on the physical metamorphoses of the flesh. Others, such as the symbolist surrealist paintings, emphasise the spiritual aspects of Zentsik's philosophy. Here and there the artist uses Pollock-like splashes of paint or experiments with digital media. Zentsik's paintings contain an open space, a magical reality in which beings, objects and concepts, seemingly freely chosen from various eras and cultures, fulfil enigmatic purposes. No mythology or esoteric teaching is immune to the artist's delicate manipulations – in Zentsik's work Zen goes hand in hand with Tao, Krishna, Christ and the gods of Olympus. Yet this is not an intellectual game. Those who wish to decipher Zentsik's code will discover su.

Jevgeni Zolotko (1983) is an artist whose work centres on the relationship between the verbal and the material. In his site specific installations Zolotko highlights the universal traits of human nature, intergenerational sensitivity passed on through culture and religion and suppressed subconscious. The artist digs deep into the past preceding our collective consciousness.

One of Zolotko's first large scale installations, “One day of the state archivist life” (2011) presents an eternal moment. The cellulose book-shaped pressed objects on shelves create a time scale that includes logs by the archivist. On the background of this static scene we can hear the whole-encompassing compositions of Bach's register. In a similar approach, a series of time-stilled moments were presented in his six-act exhibition “Things” (2012) in which Zolotko opened the attic of Tartu Art House to visitors, offering them different views on this static environment over the course of three months. Zolotko has said that he approached things and materials in that space without purpose, maintaining their incidental, neutral meaning. The only thing the artist added was a sound piece by Helena Tulve – everything else was already there.

Zolotko's solo show “Lukewarm” was based on the idea of childhood being a time of purity and openness, however, the exhibition was not autobiographical. In this installation Zolotko was interested in the idea of lukewarm as in-betweenness, neutrality and balance, and transferred these notions to a light grey tonality that has become one of the signature colours in his work.

Zolotko has mostly avoided explaining his work, as he dislikes the anchoring effect words have. He thinks that the overflowing mass of text that rules the world is a sign of the beginning of an apocalypse. The site-specific installation “It's time to take ceilings down” (2015) covered the wall of the exhibition space with a grey mass and consists of pulverised/ground-up books and newspapers, accompanied by a low-frequency pulsing sound. Also part of the work, are specks of paper under a magnifying glass that allows the viewer to look more closely.

artists.b: Ivan Zubaka on sündinud Lääne-Ukrainas ja elab ning töötab Eestis alates 1982. aastast. Ta on Eesti Kujurite Ühenduse liige alates 1993. aastast ning Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige alates 1997. aastast. Zubaka on loonud mitmeid avaliku ruumi teoseid, sealhulgas Igor Severjanini hauatähise, „Kaduviku mehed“ Rakvere teatri juures ja teostanud Tondipoiste mälestusmärgi taastamise. Zubaka on pälvinud mitmeid preemiaid, sealhulgas Tallinna ja Rakvere linna kunstipreemiad ning Viljandi linna teenetemärgi.
artists.ben: Ivan Zubaka was born in Western Ukraine and has lived and worked in Estonia since 1982. He has been a member of the Estonian Sculptors' Association since 1993 and a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1997. Zubaka has created several public space works, including the gravestone of Igor Severyanin, the "Men of Vanishing" ("Kaduviku mehed") near the Rakvere Theatre, and carried out the restoration of the Tondipoisid Memorial. Zubaka has received several awards, including art prizes from the cities of Tallinn and Rakvere and the Viljandi city medal of merit.
